Fact.Name: Has Schedule E rental real estate income
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports income or loss from rental real estate on Schedule E Part I. Gate for the rental intake; when true the `/rentalProperties` collection carries one item per property.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E rental income
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /hasScheduleERentalIncome is answered and true (IsComplete pattern, as /claimsScheduleCIncome). Unanswered resolves Complete false so returns without rental real estate still resolve. This remains the top-level gate on every rental AGGREGATE (it stays driven by /hasScheduleERentalIncome rather than being re-derived from the collection, so the ~150 non-rental scenarios that never populate /rentalProperties keep their aggregates Complete-0/false byte-identical; the collection is non-empty exactly when this is true, so the two are consistent).

Fact.Name: Rental real estate properties
Fact.Description: The collection of rental real-estate properties reported on Schedule E Part I — one item per property (Schedule E columns A/B/C). Introduces this collection; the demo migration carries exactly ONE item, reproducing the single-property model byte-identically. Each item holds the per-property line inputs (rents, expenses, basis, depreciation elections, at-risk facts) and the per-property derived chain.

Fact.Name: Rents received
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 3: total rents received for this rental property (was /writableRentalGrossIncome).

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this rental property
Fact.Description: The portion of Form 4797 line 35 recapture attributable to property whose section 179 deduction or depreciation was taken on this Schedule E rental property. This is a filer-supplied allocation, not a calculation of the Form 4797 recapture itself. Its amount is counted in the Form 4797 allocation reconciliation and, only when the return's line-35 allocation is complete, carried as Schedule E line 3 other income.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this rental property
Fact.Description: The answered ../writableForm4797Line35RecaptureAmount when this return claims Schedule E rental income; otherwise $0. This amount is counted in /scheduleEForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocatedTotal and is the value carried by ../form4797Line35RecaptureLeg when Form 4797 confirms the complete allocation.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture carried to this Schedule E property
Fact.Description:
../form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated only when form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated is TRUE. There is intentionally no fallback when the allocation is false or unanswered: the rental property's line 3, line 21, and the return stay Incomplete rather than filing without allocated recapture.
The "no fallback" sentence above described this fact as first written and is withdrawn. An unconfirmed allocation now contributes $0 to line 3 — which is the amount Schedule E line 3 carried before this leg existed, when line 3 was the bare ../grossIncome. A writable this campaign introduces may not turn a pre-existing return's resolved value into an Incomplete one (a standing dictionary rule), and this leg did exactly that: the committed witness scheduleE/form4797-line-35-schedule-e-deduction-has-no-addend-and-refuses moved /scheduleELine23aTotalRents from Complete 4,000.00 to Incomplete. NOTHING FILES THAT DID NOT FILE BEFORE. The refusal on an unallocated line 35 is not carried by this leg and never was: form4797:/hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture reads true, and the pre-existing Schedule 1 line 8z leg (income:/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg) has no fallback of its own, so /totalIncome is Incomplete and the return cannot be submitted — exactly as at base, where that same witness pinned line 23a 4,000.00 alongside an Incomplete /totalIncome. An ANSWERED and reconciled allocation still carries the whole recapture onto line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 3 income for this rental property
Fact.Description: Rents received (../grossIncome) plus the Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to this property (../form4797Line35RecaptureLeg). The recapture is reported as other income on line 3 with the required statement; this total is the Schedule E line 3 amount carried into this property's line 21 computation.

Fact.Name: Rental insurance expense
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 9: insurance (was /writableRentalInsurance). Enter the total for the whole property, not only the rental part. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the graph deducts only the rental part: ../insuranceExpense is this total times fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Rental management fees
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 11: management fees (was /writableRentalManagementFees). Enter the total for the whole property. This line is an expense of the rental activity alone, so it is deducted in full even when the property was also used for personal purposes (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Rental repairs expense
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 14: repairs (was /writableRentalRepairs). Enter the total for the whole property, not only the rental part. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the graph deducts only the rental part: ../repairsExpense is this total times fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Rental taxes expense
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 16: taxes (e.g., real estate / property taxes on the rental) (was /writableRentalTaxes). Enter the total for the whole property, not only the rental part. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the graph deducts only the rental part: ../taxesExpense is this total times fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Rental advertising expense
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 5: advertising for this rental property. OPTIONAL input: unanswered means the line is not claimed — the complete-safe wrapper ../advertisingExpense resolves it to 0, so every pre-existing scenario (which never answers it) is byte-identical. Enter the total for the whole property. This line is an expense of the rental activity alone, so it is deducted in full even when the property was also used for personal purposes (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Rental legal and other professional fees
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 10: legal and other professional fees for this rental property. OPTIONAL input: unanswered means the line is not claimed — the complete-safe wrapper ../legalProfessionalExpense resolves it to 0, so every pre-existing scenario (which never answers it) is byte-identical. Enter the total for the whole property. This line is an expense of the rental activity alone, so it is deducted in full even when the property was also used for personal purposes (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Depreciation override — taxpayer-supplied Schedule E line 18 figure
Fact.Description: OPTIONAL taxpayer-supplied depreciation figure for this property: when answered, it REPLACES the engine's computed line-18 depreciation (../depreciationExpense takes it as the whole line — building straight-line AND the 5-year personal-property path both yield to it); when unanswered. The precedence is an EXPLICIT Switch on presence (IsComplete), never a silent replacement — see the memo design note. World #1: the figure is the taxpayer's asserted number (e.g. from their own Form 4562 or prior preparer); the engine reports it, it does not validate the taxpayer's depreciation method. A ZERO override counts as answered (IsComplete) and zeroes line 18 — the fully-depreciated-property case. §179 scope: the §179 election facts are untouched, but because ../fiveYearDepreciation folds the §179 deduction into line 18, an override SWALLOWS any §179 amount out of line 18 while the display-only aggregate /rentalSection179Deduction (Form 4562 line 12) still reports it — a presentation mismatch, never a double deduction (that aggregate feeds no computation); the tax figure is exactly the taxpayer's asserted line 18.

Fact.Name: Rental building depreciable basis
Fact.Description: The depreciable basis of the building (land already excluded), supplied directly as an input — the building/land FMV split is not computed here. Drives the straight-line depreciation deduction (Form 4562 Part III → Schedule E line 18). Was /writableRentalBuildingBasis. Enter the basis of the whole building. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the depreciation figured on it is divided by fair rental days over total days used in ../depreciationExpense (IRC 280A(e)(1)).

Fact.Name: Rental building placed in service during the current tax year
Fact.Description:
True when the rental building was placed in service during 2025 (its first recovery year), which engages the MACRS mid-month convention first-year proration (Form 4562 Part III §B line 19i for residential rental property, line 19j for nonresidential real property). When false or unanswered, the building was placed in service in a prior year and 2025 is a full straight-line recovery year (the path). Was /writableRentalPlacedInServiceInCurrentYear.
CLASS-BLIND, and deliberately so. This gate selects the CONVENTION, not the recovery period: it forks ../buildingDepreciation's first-year arms for BOTH property classes, since Pub 946 applies the mid-month convention to nonresidential real property and residential rental property alike. The class itself is ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty, a separate answer.

Fact.Name: Month the rental building was placed in service
Fact.Description:
The calendar month (1 = January … 12 = December) the rental building was placed in service in the current tax year. Consulted only when ../placedInServiceInCurrentYear is true; it selects the first-year mid-month fraction (12.5 − month)/12 of a full straight-line year (Pub 527 Table 2-2d row). Domain 1–12. Was /writableRentalPlacedInServiceMonth.
THE FRACTION IS CLASS-BLIND; the year it is a fraction OF is not. The same (12.5 − month)/12 multiplies BOTH recovery periods in ../buildingDepreciation, which is why its two first-year divisors are the same product: 660 = 24 × 27.5 for residential rental property, 936 = 24 × 39 for nonresidential real property. So this month feeds a nonresidential building exactly as it feeds a residential one; only ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty moves the term.

Fact.Name: Rental building is NONRESIDENTIAL real property (39-year GDS, not 27.5-year)
Fact.Description:
The property-class attestation that drives the recovery period in ../buildingDepreciation: TRUE for section 1250 NONRESIDENTIAL real property — "an office building, store, or warehouse" that is neither residential rental property nor property with a class life under 27.5 years — which Pub 946's GDS table gives 39 years; FALSE for RESIDENTIAL rental property, a building 80% or more of whose gross rental income for the tax year comes from dwelling units, which the same table gives 27.5 years.
WHY THE UNANSWERED ARM IS FALSE AND NOT INCOMPLETE, reasoned rather than asserted. This intake is NEW to a module that has always computed line 18 at the 27.5-year residential term for every rental. Making the attestation obligatory would flip ../buildingDepreciation — and with it Schedule E line 18, line 21 and /totalIncome — to Incomplete on EVERY return that already carries a buildingBasis, i.e. it would break every committed rental scenario and every real filer mid-flow to fix a class that is the minority case. So the coalescing gate ../isNonresidentialRealProperty reads unanswered as FALSE, which is EXACTLY today's behaviour: an unanswered return depreciates over 27.5 years, byte for byte as before this fact existed. The safety is not free and is not hidden — an unanswered NONRESIDENTIAL rental still over-deducts. What that fill DID close is the "no refusal and no warning, and no way to say so" half: a filer who knows their building is commercial now has a place to say it, and saying it binds.
THE UNANSWERED ARM IS NO LONGER SUBMITTABLE, and the paragraph above is kept verbatim because it is still the right account of the VALUE. The complete-safe FALSE is unchanged and every dollar it produces is unchanged; what changed is that ../buildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown now fires on exactly the state that paragraph called a residue — positive basis, no class answer, no depreciation override — and /knockoutRentalBuildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown blocks submission on it. So the taxpayer- favourable default survives only inside an UNFINISHED return, which is the same bargain /formW2s/*/box12MedicareRegimeUnknown strikes: keep the value Complete, refuse the filing.
WHAT A BOOLEAN CANNOT SAY, so nothing is silently absorbed. This is a two-class attestation and MACRS has more than two real-property classes. The 31.5-year pre-May-13-1993 variant (Pub 946 footnote 4), 15-year land improvements, ADS's 40-year nonresidential / 30-year residential columns, and any class-life-under-27.5 property all sit OUTSIDE this Boolean. Answering TRUE means "39-year GDS", not "not 27.5" — a 15-year land improvement answered TRUE would be modeled at 39 and would be WRONG, so the ledger keeps carrying it. Reaching those classes needs an in-service YEAR (../placedInServiceInCurrentYear is a Boolean, not a year) and a class enum, neither of which exists.

Fact.Name: Rental building basis uses one of the modeled standard GDS recovery periods
Fact.Description: Answer Yes only when this building basis uses regular MACRS GDS residential rental property (27.5 years) or nonresidential real property (39 years), the two recovery periods represented by this Schedule E calculation. Answer No for property whose applicable period or method is not one of those two, including the pre-May-13-1993 31.5-year class, 15-year land improvements, ADS recovery periods, or another class-life property. This is a separate method/class attestation; it does not choose residential versus nonresidential — ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty does that. An answered No on a positive building basis, with no ../depreciationOverride supplying the whole line-18 amount, keeps the modeled depreciation value unchanged but blocks submission; see ../buildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown. An UNANSWERED attestation does not refuse, and it does not default either: on a positive basis with no override and no dated method, ../buildingDepreciation and Schedule E line 18 stay Incomplete until it is answered, so no building is computed at 27.5 or 39 years on silence. Ask it for every rental building with a positive basis.

Fact.Name: Rental has 5-year MACRS personal property placed in service this year
Fact.Description: True when the rental activity has a 5-year MACRS property item — an appliance, carpeting, or furniture used in the residential rental (Pub 527 Table 2-1) — placed in service during the current tax year (2025). Such property is depreciated MACRS GDS, 5-year recovery, 200% declining balance, half-year convention; the current (first) year deduction is cost basis × 20.00% (Pub 527 Table 2-2a, Year 1, half-year column). When false or unanswered, no 5-year property is claimed and only the building straight-line depreciation applies. Was /writableRentalHasFiveYearProperty.

Fact.Name: Rental 5-year property cost basis
Fact.Description: The depreciable cost (unadjusted basis) of the 5-year MACRS property (appliance / carpeting / furniture) placed in service in the rental this year, supplied directly as an input. Drives the first-year half-year-convention depreciation (cost × 20.00%). Consulted only when ../claimsFiveYearProperty is true. Was /writableRentalFiveYearPropertyBasis. Enter the basis of the whole 5-year property. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the depreciation figured on it before the section 179 deduction is divided by fair rental days over total days used in ../depreciationExpense (IRC 280A(e)(1)).

Fact.Name: Claims the special depreciation allowance (bonus) for the 5-year rental property
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer ELECTS the special depreciation allowance ("bonus depreciation", IRC §168(k)) for the rental's 5-year MACRS personal property (appliance / carpeting / furniture). When elected, the Year-1 rate on the post-§179 remaining basis (Form 4562 Part II line 14) depends on when the property was acquired (../writableFiveYearPropertyAcquiredAfterJan19_2025, P.L. 119-21): 100% for property acquired after January 19, 2025 (REPLACING the 20% half-year MACRS amount), or 40% of the remaining basis plus 20% half-year MACRS on what is left after that (52% total) for property acquired after September 27, 2017 and before January 20, 2025 — see that fact for the acquisition-date attestation and its unanswered posture. Modeled as an election-IN writable (default unanswered ⇒ not claimed ⇒ the 20%-MACRS path). When false or unanswered, no bonus is claimed. interpretation:provisional (the election-IN modeling is provisional). Was /writableRentalFiveYearBonusElection.

Fact.Name: 5-year rental property acquired after January 19, 2025 (bonus depreciation rate fork)
Fact.Description: Screen question: "Was this 5-year property (appliance / carpeting / furniture) acquired after January 19, 2025?" Help text: P.L. 119-21 (the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) restored the 100% special depreciation allowance for qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025; qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017 and before January 20, 2025 (the population most TY2025 rental personal property acquisitions fall into) is instead limited to a 40% special depreciation allowance, after which the remaining basis is depreciated under the ordinary 20% half-year MACRS rate for its first year — 52% total (i4562 (2025) p.1 lines 4-13, p.5 lines 358-376 and 394-403). ACQUISITION DATE, WHEN A BINDING CONTRACT PRECEDES DELIVERY: P.L. 119-21 §70301(a)(4) fixes the acquisition date at the CONTRACT date, not a later delivery/placed-in-service date — "property shall not be treated as acquired after the date on which a written binding contract is entered into for such acquisition" (26 U.S.C. 168, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title26-section168&num=0&edition=prelim). For this population (5-year rental personal property: appliances, carpeting, furniture) an advance binding purchase contract is an unlikely fact pattern, so this is a named, unmodeled edge rather than a population-wide gap: the screen asks for the acquisition date the taxpayer would state directly, and does not separately probe for a binding-contract date that precedes it. Asked when ../fiveYearBonusElection is answered true (the rate this fact selects matters only when bonus is claimed at all); otherwise not asked. UNANSWERED POSTURE, AND WHY THIS IS NOT THE ALIM/SLI/SCHF SILENT-DEFAULT VIOLATION CLASS: unanswered defaults to NOT after January 19, 2025, so ../fiveYearDepreciationBeforeSection179 applies the 52% rate rather than 100%. Those three rulings condemned an unanswered CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE (a binary gate where the deduction is $0 or granted in full) resolving silently on a claiming return. This fork is different in kind: it is a CONDITION OF AMOUNT choosing between two ALWAYS-NONZERO rates (100% vs. 52%), and the unanswered default is a provable FLOOR — 52% <= every possible true answer in the population this fact covers (100% >= 52% always), so it can only UNDER-allow, never over-allow. It mirrors the F8863 "still bars, never pays cash the statute withholds" pattern of a legitimately-safe complete default, not the ALIM/SLI/SCHF pattern of a claiming return silently getting the allowance it should have had to justify. Validation: Boolean, no default. Feeds ../fiveYearDepreciationBeforeSection179's bonus-elected arm, hence ../fiveYearDepreciation, this property's Schedule E line 20 total, and every downstream Schedule E and Form 1040 total income figure.

Fact.Name: More than 40 percent of this year's MACRS property basis was placed in service in the last 3 months
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked when a rental reports 5-year property placed in service this year: of all the MACRS property you placed in service this year (not counting residential rental or nonresidential real property, and property placed in service and disposed of in the same year), was more than 40 percent of the total depreciable basis placed in service in the last 3 months of the year? If so the mid-quarter convention replaces the half-year convention, and this return cannot yet figure it. Unanswered is read as No.

Fact.Name: This rental's 5-year property deduction uses the half-year convention rate
Fact.Description: True when ../fiveYearDepreciationBeforeSection179 is above $0 and it is not the 100 percent special allowance arm (../claimsFiveYearBonus with property acquired after January 19, 2025), so a first-year convention shapes the amount. False on the 100 percent arm, where the convention does not change the deduction.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the mid-quarter convention applies to a rental's 5-year property
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You told us more than 40 percent of the depreciable basis of the MACRS property you placed in service this year was placed in service in the last 3 months of the year. That requires the mid-quarter convention for your rental's 5-year property, and this return can only figure the half-year convention.
Fires when /writableMacrsMidQuarterConventionRequired is answered Yes and a recorded rental has ../fiveYearHalfYearConventionUsed true. Never fires on an unanswered question.

Fact.Name: Actively participated in the rental real estate activity
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer ACTIVELY PARTICIPATED in this residential rental real-estate activity within the meaning of §469(i) — the gate (aggregated up to /claimsRentalActiveParticipation) for the Form 8582 Part II $25,000 special allowance. Active participation is a less stringent standard than material participation: met if the taxpayer (owning at least a 10% interest) made management decisions in a significant and bona fide sense. When false or unanswered, the special allowance does NOT apply. interpretation:provisional (supplied as a direct taxpayer flag). Was /writableRentalActiveParticipation.

Fact.Name: Self-rental — property rented to a trade/business of the taxpayer (§469(c)(2))
Fact.Description: True when this rental property is a SELF-RENTAL: it is rented for use in a trade or business activity in which the taxpayer owns an interest (Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6), "Property rented to a nonpassive activity"). Combined with material participation in that lessee business (../materiallyParticipatesInLessee), a net rental PROFIT from this property is recharacterized NON-PASSIVE. Three-state: when false or unanswered the property is NOT a self-rental and the ordinary §8582 passive path applies unchanged (this preserves every existing golden byte-identical). interpretation:provisional (supplied as a direct taxpayer flag; this dictionary does not model the determination of whether the lessee is the taxpayer's trade/business).

Fact.Name: Materially participates in the lessee trade/business (self-rental gate, §469(c)(2))
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer MATERIALLY PARTICIPATES (within the meaning of §469(c)(1)/(h)) in the trade or business to which this self-rental property is rented (the LESSEE activity). This is the second condition of self-rental recharacterization: only when BOTH ../selfRental and this flag are true does a net rental PROFIT become non-passive. Supplied directly as a taxpayer flag — the same modeling precedent as ../activeParticipation and /formK1s/*/materiallyParticipated (this dictionary does not model the §469 seven-test material-participation determination). This is a NEW input distinct from the K-1 material-participation flag: it keys off material participation in the LESSEE business, not in this rental activity, so the existing K-1 flag cannot be reused. Three-state: false or unanswered ⇒ no recharacterization (the ordinary passive path applies). interpretation:provisional (supplied flag; the seven-test determination is not modelled).

Fact.Name: Fully at risk for the rental real estate activity (no Form 6198 needed)
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer is FULLY at risk for this residential rental real-estate activity within the meaning of IRC §465 — all investment in the activity is at risk, so no Form 6198 At-Risk Limitation applies and the entire activity loss is deductible at the at-risk step (subject only to the downstream §8582 passive limit). The typical case for a self-/recourse-financed rental. When false, the simplified Part II amount at risk (../amountAtRisk, Form 6198 line 10b) caps the deductible loss (Form 6198 line 21). When unanswered, the activity is treated as fully at risk (no limitation — three-state incompleteness; preserves the behavior for every scenario predating the at-risk model). interpretation:provisional. Was /writableRentalFullyAtRisk.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk in the rental activity (Form 6198 Part II line 10b)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's amount at risk in this residential rental real-estate activity from the SIMPLIFIED computation (Form 6198 Part II line 10b): adjusted basis on the first day of the year + increases − decreases, entered as not less than zero. Supplied directly as a single input — the line-by-line Part II build (and the detailed Part III) is not modelled. Consulted ONLY when ../fullyAtRisk is false. interpretation:provisional. Was /writableRentalAmountAtRisk.

Fact.Name: Rental 5-year property cost elected to expense under §179
Fact.Description: The cost of the rental's 5-year MACRS personal property that the taxpayer ELECTS to expense under IRC §179 (Form 4562 Part I line 6 column (c) "Elected cost"), supplied directly as an input. Must not exceed the property's cost basis (../fiveYearPropertyBasis). 0 or unanswered ⇒ NO §179 election (three-state incompleteness): the property is then depreciated entirely under the 20% half-year MACRS / 100% bonus path. PROVISIONAL TRADE-OR-BUSINESS ASSUMPTION (operator-directed): §179(d)(1) allows expensing ONLY for property used in the ACTIVE CONDUCT OF A TRADE OR BUSINESS — a higher bar than the §469 "active participation" standard. This unit models §179 on the rental on the PROVISIONAL ASSUMPTION that the rental rises to the level of a trade or business; a genuinely passive rental should claim NO §179. SECOND PROVISIONAL ASSUMPTION — NONCORPORATE-LESSOR GATE: Pub 946 ch.2 additionally bars §179 for a taxpayer OTHER THAN A CORPORATION on property PURCHASED AND LEASED TO OTHERS unless BOTH (a) the lease term is less than 50% of the property's class life AND (b) the first-12-month deductions on the property exceed 15% of its rental income. A residential-rental filer expensing appliances / carpet / furniture is a noncorporate lessor, but ytax collects no lease-term, class-life, or first-12-month-deduction fact, so this gate is UN-EVALUABLE and is NOT applied — DISCLOSED here rather than silently omitted (Pub 527 routes landlords to Pub 946 ch.2 with no carve-out). interpretation:provisional. Was /writableRentalFiveYearSection179ElectedCost.

Fact.Name: Prior years' unallowed passive loss carried into 2025 (Form 8582 Part I line 1c / Part IV col (c))
Fact.Description: The §469 prior years' UNALLOWED passive loss for THIS rental activity carried into 2025 — the activity's entry in Form 8582 Part IV column (c) "Prior years' unallowed losses", which totals to Part I line 1c and combines with the current-year income (line 1a) and loss (line 1b) at line 1d. Supplied directly as a per-property INPUT: the taxpayer reads it from last year's Form 8582 (this year's suspended loss, e.g. /rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss / /rentalSuspendedLoss, becomes next year's input), so NO multi-year carryover machinery is built. Entered as a POSITIVE amount (a prior loss). 0 or unanswered ⇒ no prior-year unallowed loss (three-state incompleteness): ../netAfterPriorLoss then equals ../atRiskAllowedNet and every scenario predating this fact is byte-identical. interpretation:provisional — this models the rental line-1c prior-year COMBINE only.

Fact.Name: Actively participated in this rental in the year the prior-year unallowed loss arose
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Did you actively participate in this rental real estate activity in the year (or years) in which the prior-year unallowed loss you entered arose?" HELP TEXT: "A prior-year unallowed loss can use the special allowance for rental real estate with active participation (up to $25,000) only if you actively participated in the activity both in the year the loss arose and in 2025. Active participation means you owned at least 10% of the property and made management decisions in a significant and bona fide sense, such as approving tenants, setting rents or approving expenditures. If you did not actively participate in the year the loss arose, the loss is still carried, but in Form 8582 Part V with your other passive activities." (2025 Instructions for Form 8582, Part IV column (c).) ASKED WHEN: this rental carries a prior-year unallowed loss above zero (../priorYearUnallowedLoss) and the filer actively participated in it in 2025 (../activeParticipation is Yes). UNANSWERED: REFUSED, not defaulted; the rental's Part IV and Part V figures (../activeEligibleNet, ../nonActiveNet) and every total they feed stay unresolved until it is answered, because either default misstates the passive loss allowed. VALIDATION: Yes or No; if the loss arose over several years with different answers, answer No and the filer's preparer splits it (one answer per rental). FEEDS: ../priorYearLossQualifiesForActiveParticipation, which decides whether the prior-year loss stays in the Part IV (active participation) figure or moves to Part V.

Fact.Name: This rental's prior-year unallowed loss may use the active participation special allowance
Fact.Description: True when this rental carries a prior-year unallowed loss above zero and the filer actively participated in the activity in the year the loss arose (../writableActivelyParticipatedWhenPriorYearLossArose); Form 8582 then enters that loss in Part IV column (c). False when the rental carries no prior-year loss, and when the filer did not actively participate in the year it arose, in which case the loss goes in Part V column (c) with the other passive activities. When a prior-year loss is entered and the question is unanswered this is Incomplete: it is read only on the active participation arms of ../activeEligibleNet and ../nonActiveNet and the professional-rental remainders, so the refusal reaches only a return that claims active participation and carries a prior-year loss.

Fact.Name: Rental depreciation uses the first-year mid-month convention
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate (IsComplete pattern): true only when ../placedInServiceInCurrentYear is answered AND true. Unanswered resolves Complete false, so prior-year assets keep the full-year straight-line path. Was /rentalUsesFirstYearConvention.

Fact.Name: Rental building is nonresidential real property (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe gate (IsComplete pattern, exact twin of ../usesFirstYearConvention above): true only when ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty is answered AND true. Unanswered resolves Complete FALSE, so a return that never saw the property-class question keeps the 27.5-year residential path in ../buildingDepreciation — today's behaviour, byte for byte. This gate, never the raw writable, is what ../buildingDepreciation depends on: taking the writable directly would make building depreciation INCOMPLETE for every rental that has not answered, which is every committed scenario.
When ../buildingDatedMethodSelected is true the ANSWERED method enum is authoritative for the class — gdsNonresidential39, gdsNonresidential315 and adsNonresidential40 are nonresidential; gdsResidential275, adsResidential30 and adsResidential40 are not — and the IsComplete gate below governs only the UNSELECTED population, unchanged. ../buildingDepreciation does not consult this fact on the dated route (it takes ../buildingDatedDepreciation whole), so the added arm moves no dollar today; it exists so the class reader cannot contradict an answered method.

Fact.Name: Nothing on this rental says which MACRS recovery period its building takes
Fact.Description:
True when this element has a depreciable building whose RECOVERY PERIOD the return does not determine: ../buildingBasis is answered and positive, and neither ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty (which would pick 27.5 or 39) nor ../depreciationOverride (which would replace the whole of line 18 with the taxpayer's own figure) is answered.
WHY IT EXISTS: IT IS THE FENCE ON A DEFAULT THAT POINTS THE WRONG WAY, and the shape is /formW2s/*/box12MedicareRegimeUnknown's exactly. ../isNonresidentialRealProperty is a complete-safe gate: unanswered resolves Complete FALSE, which keeps every return that has never seen the property-class question on the 27.5-year residential path. That default was the price of the nonresidential-class fill — making the attestation obligatory would have flipped ../buildingDepreciation, Schedule E line 18, line 21 and /totalIncome to Incomplete on every return already carrying a buildingBasis — and it was declared at the time rather than hidden. But it is a DEFAULT the dictionary chose, not a fact the filer stated, and for a genuinely nonresidential building it runs in the FALSE-ALLOWANCE direction: 1/27.5 of basis where the law allows 1/39, over-deducted every year of a long recovery period, on a broad population, fired by SILENCE rather than by any unusual answer. The fill measured one instance at $2,583 of excess deduction and ~$570 of tax on a single 240,900 office condo.
SO THE POPULATION IS REFUSED INSTEAD, and nothing about the arithmetic changes. This fact does not touch ../buildingDepreciation: the 27.5-year fallthrough still resolves, still Complete, still to the same dollar, so no incompleteness spreads into line 18, line 21, /totalIncome or AGI. What changes is that a return in that state may no longer be SUBMITTED (/knockoutRentalBuildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown). The wrong-direction default now survives only inside an unfinished return — precisely the bargain /formW2s/*/uncollectedMedicareTaxBox12FicaAddend strikes with its own unknown-regime fence.
WHY POSITIVE BASIS IS A CONJUNCT and not an oversight: at a basis of $0 both recovery periods produce $0 of depreciation, so the class decides nothing and refusing would be refusing over a question with no consequence. A fully-depreciated building entered at $0 files. Pinned by node test scheduleE/rental-building-class-zero-basis-does-not-refuse.
WHY THE OVERRIDE IS A CONJUNCT: ../depreciationExpense takes ../depreciationOverride as the WHOLE of line 18 when it is answered, and the modeled MACRS path — this class question included — is then never consulted. Refusing a return whose line 18 the taxpayer supplied themselves would refuse over a question the return does not ask. Pinned by scheduleE/rental-building-class-override-does-not-refuse.
WHAT THIS FACT IS NOT. It is not a judgment about the two-class Boolean's own coverage. The 31.5-year pre-May-13-1993 variant, 15-year land improvements and both ADS columns still have no representation, and a filer holding one still has no true answer available — but they can still ANSWER, so this guard does not catch them. This corrects the preceding limb-1-only statement that this guard does not catch the unsupported recovery classes. A second, affirmative method attestation is now also required: ../writableBuildingBasisUsesStandardGDS must be answered TRUE, confirming that the building basis belongs to one of the two recovery periods the calculation actually models (27.5-year residential or 39-year nonresidential standard GDS). An answered FALSE or an unanswered attestation on positive basis, with no line-18 override, now triggers this same refusal. This catches unsupported 31.5-year, 15-year land-improvement, ADS 30/40-year, and other recovery-period cases without pretending to calculate them. The existing class attestation remains independently required; answering standard GDS does not choose between 27.5 and 39 years. A complete depreciationOverride and zero basis remain exempt. The computed value itself is untouched.
The sentence above that reads "An answered FALSE or an unanswered attestation on positive basis, with no line-18 override, now triggers this same refusal" no longer describes this fact, and the posture it named was wrong. A refusal guard may never fire on an UNANSWERED intake (a standing dictionary rule): the method attestation was added in the same edit series as the guard, no interview asks it yet, and requiring it widened an existing refusal onto returns that answered the property class and filed. The method attestation is now read affirmatively only: an answered NO on positive basis, with no line-18 override, triggers the refusal; an UNANSWERED attestation leaves the original class fence governing, exactly as before the attestation existed, so a return that filed then files now. Three states: class unanswered leaves this fact true (unchanged); the attestation unanswered contributes nothing and only the class leg decides (unchanged); the attestation answered NO makes it true (the new catch). Witnesses: s3-standard-gds-affirmative (Yes, false), s3-standard-gds-no-refuses (No, true), s3-standard-gds-unanswered-depreciation-incomplete (unanswered with the class answered: false here, and ../buildingDepreciation Incomplete).
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-safe: the IsComplete guard on ../buildingBasis resolves without the basis being answered, and every conjunct inside it is itself complete-safe.
An ANSWERED dated method changes what this guard means for the population that selects one. When ../buildingDatedMethodSelected is true the two legs below are not consulted at all; instead the return refuses UNLESS ../depreciationOverride is complete, or ../buildingDatedDepreciation is Complete AND ../buildingDatedInputsValid is true. That is a refusal on a SELECTED but unresolved or unsupported dated schedule — an answered 30-year ADS on pre-2018 property, an answered 39-year term on a pre-May-13-1993 building, a missing in-service date, a missing unchanged-schedule confirmation, a carry-in above basis. It does NOT widen refusal onto any return that filed before: nothing in the corpus answers ../writableBuildingRecoveryMethod, so no return that filed then refuses now, and the lead ruling of 2026-09-12 (a refusal guard may never fire on an UNANSWERED intake) is untouched — the dated leg fires only on an ANSWERED method. The unselected population keeps the class leg and the answered-NO method-attestation leg exactly as the CORRECTION of 2026-09-13 left them. THE UNANSWERED ATTESTATION IS NOW FENCED BY INCOMPLETENESS, NOT BY THIS FACT. For ../writableBuildingBasisUsesStandardGDS the rejected alternative A of the authority comment below is the rule: on a positive basis with no override and no dated method, ../buildingDepreciation is Incomplete until the attestation is answered, so Schedule E line 18 never takes 27.5 or 39 years on silence. This fact still does not fire on the unanswered attestation (a refusal guard may never fire on an unanswered intake); it fires on the unanswered property class and on an answered No, as before.

Fact.Name: Claims a 5-year MACRS rental property item
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate (IsComplete pattern): true only when ../hasFiveYearProperty is answered AND true. Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every property that does not claim a 5-year asset keeps building-only depreciation. Was /claimsRentalFiveYearProperty.

Fact.Name: Claims the 100% bonus allowance for the 5-year rental property (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate (nested IsComplete pattern): true only when ../fiveYearBonusElection is answered AND true AND ../claimsFiveYearProperty is true (there must actually be a 5-year asset for bonus to apply). Unanswered or false resolves Complete false, so every property that does not elect bonus keeps the 20% half-year MACRS amount. interpretation:provisional. Was /claimsRentalFiveYearBonus.

Fact.Name: Property carries a non-straight-line depreciation intake (AMT line 2l/3 adjustment source)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe per-property gate (U-065a REVISION): true when this rental property carries a depreciation intake whose method is NOT the residential/nonresidential building straight-line path, so a Form 6251 line 2l / line 3 AMT depreciation adjustment could arise that U-065a does not model. Two sources: (1) ../claimsFiveYearProperty — a 5-year MACRS personal-property item (appliance / carpeting / furniture) depreciated 200% declining balance (AMT requires 150% DB), which also covers the bonus (../claimsFiveYearBonus) and §179 (../section179ElectedCostComplete) sub-elections since both REQUIRE claimsFiveYearProperty; and (2) IsComplete(../depreciationOverride) — a taxpayer-supplied line-18 figure of UNKNOWN method (World #1: cannot be PROVEN straight-line, so treated conservatively as a potential AMT adjustment). FALSE for a building-only rental (buildingBasis straight-line → NO AMT depreciation adjustment, which holds on EITHER real-property recovery period since the AMT adjustment turns on the METHOD, not the term) and for land. This sentence once read "27.5-/39-year", was corrected to "only 27.5 is modeled", and is now correct AGAIN in its original wording: the nonresidential-class fill gave ../buildingDepreciation a second arm, so both the 27.5- and the 39-year straight-line terms are modeled (driven by ../isNonresidentialRealProperty). The conclusion never moved, in any of the three states — the AMT adjustment turns on the method, and straight-line is straight-line at either term. Reduced up to /anyRentalHasAmtDepreciationAdjustment and consumed only by the AMT scope-out knockout (form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference). interpretation:provisional (a bonus-only or §179-only property has no AMT depreciation adjustment under §168(k)/§179, so treating claimsFiveYearProperty as the trigger OVER-refuses those in the AMT zone — the World-#1-safe direction; a future intake carrying the depreciation METHOD would refine this down).

Fact.Name: Claims active participation in the rental real estate activity (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate (IsComplete pattern): true only when ../activeParticipation is answered AND true. Unanswered resolves Complete false (treated as NOT actively participating). This per-property gate is reduced up to the taxpayer-level /claimsRentalActiveParticipation (true when ANY property actively participates). Was /claimsRentalActiveParticipation (now per-property; the top-level name is the aggregate).

Fact.Name: §179 dollar limitation after the threshold-cost phaseout (Form 4562 Part I line 5), per property
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 5, the §179 DOLLAR LIMITATION for the year AFTER the §179(b)(2) threshold-cost reduction, surfaced per element but measured against the TAXPAYER's line 2: max(0, $2,500,000 − max(0, /section179TotalCostPlacedInService − $4,000,000)). Line 1 is the $2,500,000 maximum and line 4 (reduction in limitation) = line 2 (total cost of §179 property placed in service, summed across EVERY rental element) − line 3 ($4,000,000 threshold), floored at 0. So this fact EQUALS the $2,500,000 maximum while the RETURN's aggregate cost is ≤ $4,000,000, shrinks dollar-for-dollar above it, and reaches $0 at $6,500,000. Consumed as the line-5 ceiling by ../section179ElectedCostComplete (the line-9 tentative deduction = smaller of line 5 or the elected cost) and ../section179Deduction (line 12). Gated on ../claimsFiveYearProperty; Incomplete when no 5-year property is claimed — referenced only inside that same gate, so no incompleteness propagates from that arm.
THE REBODY, stated first because it is what makes the OLD body wrong rather than merely narrow: this fact's line-2 input used to be the element's OWN ../fiveYearPropertyBasis. §179(b)(2) reduces the limitation by the amount by which "the cost of section 179 property placed in service during such taxable year" exceeds the threshold, and §179(b)(1) caps "the aggregate cost which may be taken into account"; both are TAXPAYER quantities, and the 2025 Form 4562 instructions say so in terms at Line 12 — "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity." MEASURED, not asserted: node test scheduleE/rental-179-nonelecting-sibling-caps-deduction-amt-refused puts $2,500,000 of five-year property in each of two elements, so the lawful line 5 is $1,500,000; before the rebody this fact handed the electing element $2,500,000 and Form 4562 line 12 came out $1,000,000 too high. The gap grows to the whole cap at $6,500,000 of aggregate cost.
WHY THE MULTI-ELECTOR KNOCKOUT DID NOT ALREADY REACH IT: /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities counts activities that ELECT, and the second element in that fixture need not elect at all — it only has to place five-year property in service. Exactly one activity elects, no knockout fires, and the over-deduction stood.
WHAT THE REBODY DOES NOT TOUCH: type, sign, rounding and the ../claimsFiveYearProperty gate are unchanged, and ../section179ElectedCostComplete and ../section179Deduction need NO edit — both already read this fact, and the swap is confined to its own subtrahend. A SINGLE-element return that claims Schedule E rental income is byte-identical, because there the aggregate IS the element's own basis: that covers every committed scenario and both clean-room nominations (all six of their fixtures are single-element and re-ran unchanged, and 0 resolved rows changed over the whole corpus). THE ONE EDGE WHERE EVEN A SINGLE ELEMENT DIVERGES, named so the sentence above is not read as unconditional: /section179TotalCostPlacedInService is gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome and falls back to $0 when that is false, so a return carrying a rental element with over $4,000,000 of five-year property while denying Schedule E rental income would now get the FULL $2,500,000 where the old body phased it down. That input state is self-contradictory rather than merely rare — the element exists only because the section was entered — and no fixture or scenario occupies it; it is recorded because the gate is real, not because the population is.
COMPLETENESS WIDENS — the one behaviour change here that is not a value, disclosed rather than left to be found. This fact used to be Incomplete only when THIS element's basis was unanswered; it is now Incomplete when ANY element claims five-year property with an unanswered basis, since /section179TotalCostPlacedInService cannot resolve until every claiming element has answered. That is the honest state — the taxpayer's line 2 genuinely is unknown — and it adds NO new incompleteness downstream: in that same shape the unanswered sibling's own ../section179Deduction was ALREADY Incomplete, so the return-level /rentalSection179Deduction was Incomplete before the rebody too. Pinned by node test scheduleE/rental-179-aggregate-incomplete-when-a-sibling-basis-unanswered.
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE (the shape a reader will ask about): making this fact a pass-through of /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit, which computes the same line 5 from the same aggregate. It yields identical numbers, but it would move the §179(b)(2) arithmetic that DTXV-NOM-U118's clean room independently re-derived OUT of the fact the nomination is attached to and into one tagged verified:ai-only. The dependency swap keeps the witnessed arithmetic where the witness points.
STILL NOT MODELED, and refused rather than guessed: the ALLOCATION of the single limit among two or more ELECTING activities (i4562 Line 12 makes it the filer's election — "you may allocate" — and no intake collects it; /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities blocks that return). Nor the MFS split of §179(b)(4), which halves both the dollar limit and the threshold between spouses; this fact applies the full $2,500,000 / $4,000,000 figures. interpretation:provisional. NON-CIRCULAR (property gate + the taxpayer line-2 aggregate + two literals; the aggregate's own cone is the per-element basis writables and their gates, never this fact).

Fact.Name: §179 elected cost, complete-safe (0 when unanswered or no 5-year property)
Fact.Description: The §179 elected cost (../fiveYearSection179ElectedCost) made three-state-safe AND capped at BOTH the property basis AND the §179 dollar LIMITATION: min(elected cost, ../fiveYearPropertyBasis, ../section179DollarLimit) ONLY when a 5-year property is claimed (../claimsFiveYearProperty) AND the elected cost is answered; otherwise 0. The basis cap enforces the Form 4562 line-6 rule that elected cost (col (c)) ≤ property cost (col (b)); the dollar-limitation cap enforces Form 4562 Part I line 9 — the tentative deduction is the smaller of line 5 (the dollar limitation) or line 8 (total elected cost), so an election above the line-5 cap cannot flow past it into either the deduction or the carryover. This fact IS Form 4562 line 9 (the tentative deduction). The line-5 cap was the flat $2,500,000 maximum until this unit swapped it for ../section179DollarLimit, which EQUALS $2,500,000 for basis ≤ $4,000,000 but shrinks under the §179(b)(2) threshold-cost phaseout above $4,000,000, reaching $0 at $6,500,000 (so line 9 = 0 and the whole basis stays in MACRS, not §179). Single source of the "elected cost" consumed by the §179 deduction (lines 9/12), the carryover (line 13), AND the basis reduction for the remaining bonus/MACRS depreciation; capping here at the dollar limitation makes all three faithful — the excess of an above-limit election returns to depreciable basis (not to §179), and the carryover (line 13) reflects only the business-income disallowance, never the dollar-limit excess (Form 4562 line 13 = 0 for a pure above-limit election). Like the sibling per-property line-5 cap in ../section179Deduction, this applies the taxpayer-AGGREGATE line-1/line-5 dollar figures per property (the single-element Schedule E model; multi-property allocation is oos-schedulee-multi-property-179-cap). interpretation:provisional. NON-CIRCULAR (writable + property gate + basis + dollar-limit fact). Was /rentalSection179ElectedCostComplete.

Fact.Name: §179 expense deduction allowed this year (Form 4562 Part I line 12), per property
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part I line 12, the §179 deduction ALLOWED for this property's 5-year personal property this year: the SMALLER OF the elected cost, the property basis, the line-5 dollar limitation (../section179DollarLimit), and the line-11 business-income limit. Gated on ../claimsFiveYearProperty (no 5-year asset ⇒ 0). Computed as min(../section179ElectedCostComplete, ../fiveYearPropertyBasis, ../section179DollarLimit, /rentalSection179IncomeLimit). The line-5 dollar cap and the line-11 wages limit are taxpayer-AGGREGATE (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit stays top-level). WHEN MORE THAN ONE ACTIVITY ELECTS AND this element's /rentalProperties/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow resolves, the minimum takes a fifth operand, ../section179AllocatedShare, this element's share of the one taxpayer cap out of the return level /section179AllocationByActivity. The arm engages on those two conditions only, so a single elector return and every return that never answers the allocation collection keep the expression above unchanged, value for value. See the block comment at /section179AllocationByActivity for which of the three shipping section 179 intakes survives as what and for why the cap has to bind on the CONSUMED share total rather than on the entered one. The Form 4562 lines 2-5 investment/phaseout reduction ($4,000,000 threshold for 2025) IS now modeled — the line-5 cap (../section179DollarLimit) is the $2,500,000 maximum reduced dollar-for-dollar above $4,000,000 of property placed in service, reaching $0 at $6,500,000. interpretation:provisional. Result rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: §179 carryover of disallowed deduction to 2026 (Form 4562 Part I line 13), per property
Fact.Description: Form 4562 Part I line 13, the §179 cost DISALLOWED this year by the business-income limitation and carried to next year = ../section179ElectedCostComplete − ../section179Deduction (= max(0, elected − line-11 limit)). §179(b)(3)(B) carries the disallowed amount to the first succeeding year; this single-year demo REPORTS it (aggregated to /rentalSection179CarryoverToNextYear) but does NOT apply it to a future year. interpretation:provisional. Result rounded to whole dollars. Was /rentalSection179CarryoverToNextYear (now per-property; the top-level name is the aggregate).

Fact.Name: This rental property elects §179 on its 5-year personal property (existence flag)
Fact.Description:
True exactly when this element's Form 4562 line-9 tentative deduction (../section179ElectedCostComplete) is POSITIVE — i.e. the element claims 5-year property AND answers a §179 elected cost AND that cost survives the basis and line-5 caps. Counted by /rentalSection179ElectingCount, which with the K-1-side count decides whether the return has more than one activity electing §179 (the multi-elector population is REFUSED, see /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities).
WHY THE CAPPED FIGURE AND NOT THE RAW WRITABLE, disclosed because the two differ in one corner: reading ../section179ElectedCostComplete means an element whose line-5 dollar limitation has already phased to $0 (over $6,500,000 of 5-year property placed in service) counts as NOT electing even though the filer wrote an elected cost. That element's §179 deduction is $0 either way, so treating it as a non-elector cannot let a second activity claim a cap the first one is using — there is no cap left to claim. The raw-writable reading would refuse that return for a conflict that cannot arise.

Fact.Name: The section 179 allocation row this rental element's share is entered on
Fact.Description:
The item of /section179AllocationByActivity that carries this rental element's share of the taxpayer's one section 179 dollar limit. FILER SUPPLIED, and it has to be: the split is an ELECTION ("if you have more than one business or activity, you MAY allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them"), not a formula, so neither the row nor its amount is derivable from the return's other answers.
WHY THE LINK POINTS THIS WAY. The allocation is return level because it spans two collections under one cap; the consumer that needs to know its own share is a collection element. A row cannot be found from the element it describes without a reverse lookup this engine does not express, so the element names its row, exactly as qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/linkedScheduleC names the Schedule C whose line 31 it reads.
UNANSWERED IS THE ORDINARY STATE and costs nothing: ../section179AllocationRowResolves is false, ../section179AllocatedShare is $0 and ../section179Deduction falls through to the expression it had before this unit, so every single elector return and every committed fixture is byte identical.

Fact.Name: This rental element's section 179 allocation link reaches an answered share
Fact.Description:
Whether ../linkedSection179AllocationRow actually reaches a row whose share this graph can read: the link is answered AND that row's ../writableElectedCostShare is answered. Both terms are needed. An unanswered CollectionItem dereferences to nothing, and a row that exists with an empty amount cell would otherwise hand the element a share of nothing and silently delete its deduction.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and that is load bearing rather than tidy. This fact is read in a Switch When by ../section179Deduction, and an Incomplete in a When clears the Switch's completeness flag, which would turn the deduction Placeholder on every return that answers a rental element. Both terms are IsComplete tests, so neither can be Incomplete. The same argument is written out at qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/scheduleCLinkResolves, which this fact copies.

Fact.Name: The share of the taxpayer's section 179 dollar limit allocated to this rental element
Fact.Description:
The amount on this element's allocation row when ../section179AllocationRowResolves, and $0 otherwise. Complete on every return. It is a CEILING on ../section179Deduction rather than the deduction itself: the elected cost, the property basis and the line 11 business income limitation still bind, and a filer who allocates more than an activity can use does not thereby deduct more.
NOT FLOORED AT $0 BY A GreaterOf, because the row's complete safe alias already returns $0 for an unanswered cell and a NEGATIVE entered share is an input contradiction rather than a quantity to clamp; it is reported by /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits through the consumed total, not silently repaired here.

Fact.Name: This rental element elects section 179 and has a resolving allocation row
Fact.Description: ../electsSection179 AND ../section179AllocationRowResolves: the per element half of /section179AllocationCoversEveryElectingRentalActivity, which counts the true items of this field against /rentalSection179ElectingCount. An electing element with no resolving row is the case in which the allocation is PARTIAL, and a partial allocation is not an allocation: the uncovered element would still take the whole taxpayer cap, which is the defect the refusal was put there to prevent.

Fact.Name: This element's contribution to Form 4562 Part I line 2 (total cost of §179 property placed in service)
Fact.Description:
This rental element's share of Form 4562 line 2, "Total cost of section 179 property placed in service": ../fiveYearPropertyBasis when the element claims 5-year property, else $0. Summed by /section179TotalCostPlacedInService into the taxpayer-level §179(b)(2) phaseout base.
THE GATE IS NOT DECORATION — it is what keeps a published-figure witness alive. Without it the CollectionSum reads ../fiveYearPropertyBasis on EVERY element, and that fact is a bare Writable (Incomplete when unanswered). The committed worked-example fixture tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleE/p527-property-changed-example carries two rental elements and answers the 5-year basis on ONE of them, so an ungated sum resolves Incomplete there and contaminates the module's strongest published-figure case. That case now asserts this fact 425.00 on the element that claims 5-year property and 0.00 on the one that does not.
THE GATE IS ../claimsFiveYearProperty ALONE, deliberately matching the per-element ../section179DollarLimit rather than adding an IsComplete guard on the basis itself. An element that claims 5-year property and leaves the basis unanswered resolves this Incomplete, and that Incompleteness is the honest state: the taxpayer's line 2 is not knowable until every claiming element has answered. Since the aggregate-cost rebody ../section179DollarLimit reads the sum this fact feeds, so the taxpayer-level limit and the per-element one have IDENTICAL completeness behaviour BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by coincidence, and neither is quietly more forgiving than the other. Pinned by node test scheduleE/rental-179-aggregate-incomplete-when-a-sibling-basis-unanswered.

Fact.Name: Rental 5-year property depreciation EXCLUDING §179 (bonus/MACRS on the remaining basis)
Fact.Description: The bonus / MACRS depreciation on the 5-year personal property's REMAINING basis (max(0, ../fiveYearPropertyBasis − ../section179ElectedCostComplete)) — i.e. ../fiveYearDepreciation WITHOUT its §179 term: when ../claimsFiveYearBonus, 100% × remaining for property acquired after January 19, 2025, or 40% × remaining PLUS 20% half-year MACRS on what is left after that — 52% × remaining, Rational 13/25 — for property acquired after September 27, 2017 and before January 20, 2025 (../writableFiveYearPropertyAcquiredAfterJan19_2025, P.L. 119-21; unanswered defaults to the 52% arm, the conservative reading); else 20% × remaining, else 0. Extracted so the §179 business-income limit (Form 4562 line 11, /rentalSection179IncomeLimit) can use a rental net figured WITHOUT the §179 deduction (Pub 946 ch.2: "figure taxable income ... without regard to ... the section 179 deduction") without a dependency cycle. Result rounded to whole dollars; 0 when no 5-year property is claimed (complete-safe).

Fact.Name: Rental 5-year property depreciation (first year, half-year convention)
Fact.Description: The current-year MACRS depreciation for this property's 5-year personal property (appliances / carpeting / furniture). 5-year property uses MACRS GDS, 200% declining balance, and the half-year convention; placed in service in the current year, so this is the FIRST recovery year (Pub 527 Table 2-2a half-year Year-1 = 20.00%). Year-1 deduction = §179 FIRST (../section179Deduction), then bonus/MACRS on the REMAINING basis = max(0, ../fiveYearPropertyBasis − ../section179ElectedCostComplete): when ../claimsFiveYearBonus is true, 100% × remaining; else 20% × remaining. §179 → bonus → MACRS ordering (i4562 Line 11/14). When §179 is NOT elected the §179 deduction is 0 and the remaining basis is the FULL basis. Resolves 0 when no 5-year property is claimed (complete-safe). Result rounded to whole dollars. Was /rentalFiveYearDepreciation. The bonus/MACRS-on-remaining term is now the extracted ../fiveYearDepreciationBeforeSection179 fact; this = §179 deduction + that, byte-identical to the prior single Round (the §179 deduction is whole dollars, so Round(int + x) = int + Round(x)).

Fact.Name: Rental building depreciation (27.5-yr or 39-yr S/L, mid-month) — building component only
Fact.Description:
The rental BUILDING's MACRS GDS straight-line, mid-month depreciation ONLY (the building component of Schedule E line 18) — the modeled path, NOT the ../depreciationOverride branch (that stays at ../depreciationExpense and replaces the whole modeled depreciation). Extracted from ../depreciationExpense so both the post-§179 depreciation and the before-§179 rental net (../depreciationExpenseBeforeSection179) reuse ONE mid-month formula instead of duplicating it.
FOUR arms now, on ../usesFirstYearConvention × ../isNonresidentialRealProperty (the recovery period used to be hardcoded at the residential 27.5 in both branches): (a) prior-year asset, residential — basis × 1/27.5 (= 2/55); (b) prior-year asset, NONRESIDENTIAL — basis × 1/39; (c) current-year, residential — first recovery year mid-month, basis × (25 − 2·month)/660; (d) current-year, NONRESIDENTIAL — basis × (25 − 2·month)/936. The mid-month numerator is shared because the convention itself is class-blind: Pub 946 applies it to nonresidential real property and residential rental property alike, allowing a one-half month for the month of placement. Only the recovery period moves, and the two divisors are the same product — 660 = 24 × 27.5, 936 = 24 × 39. STRUCTURALLY NON-NEGATIVE (the numerator is 23 at month 1 down to 1 at month 12, never zero or below across the declared 1–12 domain). Result rounded to whole dollars. ../fiveYearDepreciation is whole dollars, so Round(building) + fiveYearDepreciation = Round(building + fiveYearDepreciation).
BYTE-IDENTITY OF THE CLASS REBODY: the class fork reads ../isNonresidentialRealProperty, the coalescing gate, which resolves Complete FALSE when unanswered. Arms (a) and (c) are the pre-rebody expressions verbatim, so every return that does not answer the new attestation — which is every committed scenario and every pre-existing node-test fixture — resolves to the same dollar it did before. The value moves only where a taxpayer affirmatively attests nonresidential, which is the correction the fill asked for and is taxpayer-ADVERSE (a longer recovery period is a smaller annual deduction).
METHOD, and a choice this fill does NOT re-open: the arms compute the exact straight-line fraction rather than the optional-table percentage. On the 39-year full-year row the two agree (Table A-7a years 2–39 reads 2.564%, and 1/39 = 2.5641%); on the 39-year FIRST-year row they diverge slightly, because Table A-7a builds that row from a monthly rate rounded to 0.214% (its January cell reads 2.461% against the exact 23/936 = 2.4573%). Pub 946 names both methods and warns the no-table method "will generally result in a slightly different amount than using the tables"; the same reading is carried here from the 27.5-year arms.
A FIFTH arm now sits in front of the four above. When ../buildingDatedMethodSelected is true — that is, when ../writableBuildingRecoveryMethod is ANSWERED — this fact IS ../buildingDatedDepreciation, the dated-interval calculation over GDS 27.5/39/31.5 and ADS 30/40, and none of the four arms below runs. Because ../buildingDatedMethodSelected is IsComplete(../writableBuildingRecoveryMethod), it resolves Complete FALSE on silence, so the four arms below are byte-for-byte what they were: measured over the 31 committed scheduleE fixtures that seed ../buildingBasis, this fact, ../isNonresidentialRealProperty, ../buildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown and ../depreciationExpense resolve to the identical value AND completeness with and without this arm — 0 moves over 124 resolvable probes, and all 362 pre-existing scheduleE cases still pass. A complete ../depreciationOverride keeps its precedence at ../depreciationExpense over BOTH routes. The dated leg carries its own verification tag on ../buildingDatedDepreciation; the worksheet-verified tag in the authority comment below continues to cover the first-recovery-year mid-month path of the LEGACY arms only.
INCOMPLETE UNTIL THE STANDARD-GDS ATTESTATION IS ANSWERED. On the undated path (no dated method selected) with a positive ../buildingBasis, this fact resolves only once ../writableBuildingBasisUsesStandardGDS is answered; while it is unanswered the Switch runs off its end and the depreciation is Incomplete, never 27.5 or 39 years by default. A basis of $0 still resolves Complete $0 (neither period has a consequence), and an answered ../depreciationOverride replaces the whole of line 18 in ../depreciationExpense without reading this fact. An answered No keeps the 27.5 or 39 year value and refuses the return (../buildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown). The property class leg is unchanged: an unanswered ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty still computes 27.5 years, and that return is refused.

Fact.Name: Rental depreciation expense
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true this line prints ../worksheet51Line6e, the depreciation Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 allows (line 6e: the smaller of line 5 or line 6d, with line 6d the rental part of this year's depreciation before section 179, ../depreciationExpenseBeforeSection179, plus the line 6c carryover). A worksheet unit that elects section 179 is refused (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51Section179Unbuilt), so no section 179 deduction is added on that arm. Otherwise the body below applies, unchanged, and the rest of this Description describes it. The two cases are complements with no catch-all.
Schedule E line 18 (via Form 4562 Part III) for this property: the rental BUILDING depreciation (../buildingDepreciation) PLUS the 5-year personal-property depreciation (../fiveYearDepreciation) — or the taxpayer-supplied ../depreciationOverride when present, which replaces the whole modeled figure. Result rounded to whole dollars. The item's existence implies a claimed property, so no top-level claims gate is needed here (the aggregate /scheduleERentalNetIncome carries the claims gate). Was /rentalDepreciationExpense.
THE BUILDING TERM IS NOT 27.5 UNCONDITIONALLY, and this Description used to say it was. It read "the RESIDENTIAL rental BUILDING depreciation ... MACRS GDS, 27.5-year" and enumerated TWO arms on ../usesFirstYearConvention (basis × 2/55 and basis × (25 − 2·month)/660). The nonresidential-class fill made ../buildingDepreciation FOUR arms — that same pair for residential rental property, plus basis × 1/39 and basis × (25 − 2·month)/936 for NONRESIDENTIAL real property — forked on ../isNonresidentialRealProperty, and did not revisit this consumer's prose. So the fact that CARRIES THE LINE NUMBER this issue is about went on telling its reader that Schedule E line 18 knows only one recovery period. The arithmetic was never wrong here (this fact only adds and rounds); the statement of it was. Corrected rather than duplicated: the arms live on ../buildingDepreciation and are described there, once.
WHAT SILENCE STILL MEANS, restated here because line 18 is where a reader looks. The class gate is complete-safe, so a return that never answers ../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty is depreciated over 27.5 years. For a genuinely nonresidential building that is an OVER-deduction in the taxpayer's favour. THAT RETURN NO LONGER FILES: the value on this line is unchanged and still Complete, and /knockoutRentalBuildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown blocks submission until the class is answered. An answered ../depreciationOverride takes the branch above and is never refused — the class question decides nothing once the taxpayer supplies line 18 themselves.
THE RENTAL PART. When ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true (personal use days above 0) and no override is answered, the building depreciation and the 5-year depreciation before section 179 are figured on the whole property and multiplied by ../rentalUseFairDays over ../rentalUseAllocationTotalDays, rounded to whole dollars (IRC 280A(e)(1)); the section 179 deduction is then added undivided, because its elected cost is the business use cost. An answered ../depreciationOverride is the filer's own line 18 figure and is not divided.
The paragraph above that says the value "is unchanged and still Complete" describes the property class question only. The standard-GDS attestation works differently: while ../writableBuildingBasisUsesStandardGDS is unanswered on a positive basis with no override and no dated method, ../buildingDepreciation is Incomplete, and so is this line.

Fact.Name: Rental depreciation expense EXCLUDING the §179 deduction (Form 4562 line-11 limit)
Fact.Description: ../depreciationExpense computed WITHOUT the §179 deduction: the building depreciation (../buildingDepreciation) plus the 5-year bonus/MACRS on the remaining basis (../fiveYearDepreciationBeforeSection179); or the taxpayer-supplied ../depreciationOverride when present (an opaque figure that already stands in for the whole modeled depreciation, with no separable §179 — the same precedence as ../depreciationExpense). Equals ../depreciationExpense − ../section179Deduction, but built from inputs so /rentalSection179IncomeLimit (line 11) stays cycle-free. Feeds ../netBeforeSection179. Result rounded to whole dollars. THE RENTAL PART. When ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true and no override is answered, the same divided figure ../depreciationExpense uses before it adds the section 179 deduction, so the identity with ../depreciationExpense holds on a property used partly for personal purposes.

Fact.Name: Rental advertising expense (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 5 as it enters the line-20 total: ../advertising when answered, else 0 — the optional-input pattern, so a return that never saw the advertising question still totals its expenses (every pre-existing scenario is byte-identical apart from this new fact resolving 0).

Fact.Name: Rental legal and other professional fees (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 10 as it enters the line-20 total: ../legalProfessionalFees when answered, else 0 — the optional-input pattern (see ../advertisingExpense).

Fact.Name: Rental insurance expense, rental part (Schedule E line 9)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true (a dwelling unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more, whose rental expenses are more than its rents), this line prints the part of the rental expense Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 allows, as named in the Derived body; otherwise it prints ../insuranceRentalPart, the rental part of the whole-property intake, which is what the rest of this Description describes. The two cases are complements with no catch-all, so a unit whose worksheet test is undecided prints nothing rather than an unlimited figure.
Schedule E line 9 insurance for THIS rental property as it is printed and as the line 20 total and ../netBeforeSection179 add it: ../insurance (the total for the whole property) floored at $0, and, when ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true (personal use days above 0), times ../rentalUseFairDays over ../rentalUseAllocationTotalDays, rounded to whole dollars (IRC 280A(e)(1)); Incomplete while the fair rental days are unanswered. Incomplete when ../insurance is unanswered, as the line 20 total always was.

Fact.Name: Rental part of the Schedule E line 9 expense before the Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 limit
Fact.Description: The rental part of this property's Schedule E line 9 expense: the whole-property intake, divided by IRC 280A(e)(1) when personal use days are answered above 0. It is the body ../insuranceExpense carried before Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 was built, unchanged; ../insuranceExpense now prints it whenever the worksheet does not apply, and the worksheet reads it as its rental portion (Part I line F).

Fact.Name: Rental repairs expense, rental part (Schedule E line 14)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true (a dwelling unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more, whose rental expenses are more than its rents), this line prints the part of the rental expense Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 allows, as named in the Derived body; otherwise it prints ../repairsRentalPart, the rental part of the whole-property intake, which is what the rest of this Description describes. The two cases are complements with no catch-all, so a unit whose worksheet test is undecided prints nothing rather than an unlimited figure.
Schedule E line 14 repairs for THIS rental property as it is printed and as the line 20 total and ../netBeforeSection179 add it: ../repairs (the total for the whole property) floored at $0, and, when ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true (personal use days above 0), times ../rentalUseFairDays over ../rentalUseAllocationTotalDays, rounded to whole dollars (IRC 280A(e)(1)); Incomplete while the fair rental days are unanswered. Incomplete when ../repairs is unanswered, as the line 20 total always was.

Fact.Name: Rental part of the Schedule E line 14 expense before the Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 limit
Fact.Description: The rental part of this property's Schedule E line 14 expense: the whole-property intake, divided by IRC 280A(e)(1) when personal use days are answered above 0. It is the body ../repairsExpense carried before Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 was built, unchanged; ../repairsExpense now prints it whenever the worksheet does not apply, and the worksheet reads it as its rental portion (Part I line F).

Fact.Name: Rental taxes expense, rental part (Schedule E line 16)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true (a dwelling unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more, whose rental expenses are more than its rents), this line prints the part of the rental expense Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 allows, as named in the Derived body; otherwise it prints ../taxesRentalPart, the rental part of the whole-property intake, which is what the rest of this Description describes. The two cases are complements with no catch-all, so a unit whose worksheet test is undecided prints nothing rather than an unlimited figure.
Schedule E line 16 taxes for THIS rental property as it is printed and as the line 20 total and ../netBeforeSection179 add it: ../taxes (the total for the whole property) floored at $0, and, when ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true (personal use days above 0), times ../rentalUseFairDays over ../rentalUseAllocationTotalDays, rounded to whole dollars (IRC 280A(e)(1)); Incomplete while the fair rental days are unanswered. Incomplete when ../taxes is unanswered, as the line 20 total always was.

Fact.Name: Rental part of the Schedule E line 16 expense before the Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 limit
Fact.Description: The rental part of this property's Schedule E line 16 expense: the whole-property intake, divided by IRC 280A(e)(1) when personal use days are answered above 0. It is the body ../taxesExpense carried before Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 was built, unchanged; ../taxesExpense now prints it whenever the worksheet does not apply, and the worksheet reads it as its rental portion (Part I line F).

Fact.Name: Rental total expenses (per property)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 20 for this property: total expenses (add lines 5 through 19). ALL FIFTEEN PRINTED EXPENSE LINES ARE CARRIED: advertising (5, complete-safe), auto and travel (6, complete-safe), cleaning and maintenance (7, complete-safe), commissions (8, complete-safe), insurance (9), legal and other professional fees (10, complete-safe), management fees (11), mortgage interest paid to banks (12, complete-safe), other interest (13, complete-safe), repairs (14), supplies (15, complete-safe), taxes (16), utilities (17, complete-safe), depreciation (18, overridable ) and the line 19 other listed expense (complete-safe). Was /rentalTotalExpenses.
THE EIGHT COMPLETE-SAFE TERMS ADDED close a silent drop, not a rounding: lines 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 15, 17 and 19 had per property intakes that printed in the property column and reached NOTHING, so a filer who entered any of them deducted it on the printed page and not on the return (../propertyRawNet → /scheduleERentalNetIncome → /scheduleETotalIncome → /totalIncome). Each new term is a Switch on IsComplete of its intake defaulting to $0, so a return that never answered those questions totals exactly what it totalled before and every committed scenario is byte-identical; only a return that ANSWERED one of the eight moves, and it moves to the figure the form prints. /scheduleELine23eTotalExpenses, which sums this fact, becomes a true total of the printed line 20 cells for the same reason.
THE RENTAL PART: lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19 and the computed line 18 enter as the rental part of the whole-property totals (../cleaningAndMaintenanceExpense, ../insuranceExpense, ../mortgageInterestExpense, ../otherInterestExpense, ../repairsExpense, ../suppliesExpense, ../taxesExpense, ../utilitiesExpense, ../otherListedExpense and ../depreciationExpense), which equal the totals entered when no personal use days are answered above 0 (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Schedule E net rental real estate income (per property, pre-limitation)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1.
