When ../worksheet51Applies is true this is ../section280ALimitedNet, the unit's net after the IRC 280A(c)(5) limit, which equals line 3 less the printed line 20 of the limited lines; it is read from the worksheet's own net, not from the printed lines, so this figure and everything it feeds (Schedule E line 21, Schedule 1 line 5, AGI) never wait on the itemize election that only moves amounts between printed lines. Otherwise the body below, unchanged.
Schedule E line 21 body for this property: line 3 income (../scheduleELine3Income) minus total expenses (line 20, ../propertyTotalExpenses). The PRE-LIMITATION net; MAY be negative (a net loss). This is the per-property summand of the aggregate /scheduleERentalNetIncome (Schedule E line 21 total → Schedule 1 line 5). Was the body of the top-level /scheduleERentalNetIncome.

Fact.Name: Rental net income BEFORE the §179 deduction (Form 4562 line-11 business-income component)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true this is ../section280ALimitedNet: a worksheet unit may not elect section 179 (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51Section179Unbuilt), so the net before section 179 is the limited net itself, and the identity with ../propertyRawNet plus ../section179Deduction holds. That net is built from the depreciation before section 179, so the Form 4562 line 11 limit stays cycle-free. Otherwise the body below, now reading the rental-part facts (../insuranceRentalPart and its siblings), which are what the printed lines carry whenever the worksheet does not apply, so the value is unchanged.
This property's Schedule-E net figured WITHOUT the §179 deduction: ../scheduleELine3Income minus the line-20 expenses computed before §179 (every term of ../propertyTotalExpenses except depreciation — advertising, auto and travel, cleaning and maintenance, commissions, insurance, legal, management, mortgage interest, other interest, repairs, supplies, taxes, utilities and the line 19 other listed expense — with ../depreciationExpenseBeforeSection179 in place of the post-§179 ../depreciationExpense). THE EIGHT COMPLETE-SAFE TERMS ADDED TO ../propertyTotalExpenses ON 2026-08-30 ARE MIRRORED HERE DELIBERATELY: this fact's stated identity is "equals ../propertyRawNet + ../section179Deduction", and carrying a different expense list from the line 20 total would break it and over-state the Form 4562 line 11 business income limit by the whole of lines 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 15, 17 and 19. MAY be negative (a net loss). Equals ../propertyRawNet + ../section179Deduction, but built from inputs so the §179 business-income limit (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit, Form 4562 line 11) can depend on it WITHOUT a cycle through ../section179Deduction. The per-property summand of /rentalNetBeforeSection179. Result rounded to whole dollars. The insurance, repairs and taxes terms are ../insuranceExpense, ../repairsExpense and ../taxesExpense, the same rental parts line 20 adds, so the mirror with ../propertyTotalExpenses holds on a property used partly for personal purposes.

Fact.Name: Rental real estate loss before the at-risk limitation (Form 6198 line 5, positive)
Fact.Description: This property's current-year rental real-estate loss as a POSITIVE amount (Form 6198 Part I line 5 loss): when ../propertyRawNet is negative this is its absolute value; otherwise 0. The pre-at-risk loss magnitude — the input to the Form 6198 line-21 smaller-of test. Was /rentalRawLoss.

Fact.Name: The §465 at-risk limitation applies to the rental loss (Form 6198 required)
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when ../fullyAtRisk is answered AND false — i.e., the taxpayer is NOT fully at risk, so Form 6198 caps the deductible loss at the amount at risk. When ../fullyAtRisk is true OR unanswered (IsComplete false), this resolves false and NO at-risk limitation applies (the safe default preserving the behavior). Was /rentalAtRiskLimitationApplies.

Fact.Name: Rental at-risk-allowed (deductible) loss (Form 6198 line 21)
Fact.Description: This property's loss allowed under the §465 at-risk rules (Form 6198 Part IV line 21): the SMALLER of the line-5 loss (../rawLoss) or the line-20 amount at risk (../amountAtRisk) — but ONLY when the at-risk limitation applies (../atRiskLimitationApplies). When fully at risk OR unanswered, this equals the full raw loss (the behavior, byte-identical). Published i6198 line-21 examples: (a) loss $400, AR $1,000 → $400; (b) loss $1,600, AR $1,200 → $1,200; (c) loss $800, AR $0 → $0. Was /rentalAtRiskDeductibleLoss.

Fact.Name: Rental loss suspended by the §465 at-risk rules (per property, carryover)
Fact.Description: This property's rental real-estate loss DISALLOWED for 2025 by the §465 at-risk limitation = ../rawLoss − ../atRiskDeductibleLoss (Form 6198 line 5 − line 21). Under §465(a)(2) this carries to the first succeeding year; this single-year demo REPORTS it (aggregated to /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss) but does NOT apply it to a future year. DISTINCT from the §8582 passive suspended loss. 0 for profit cases and whenever fully at risk. Was /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss (now per-property; the top-level name is the aggregate).

Fact.Name: Rental at-risk-allowed net for this property (signed)
Fact.Description: Per-property SIGNED net AFTER the §465 at-risk limitation, summed up to the aggregate §8582 line-4 input: when ../propertyRawNet ≥ 0 (a profit) this is that profit unchanged; when it is a loss this is the at-risk-allowed loss expressed as a NEGATIVE amount (−../atRiskDeductibleLoss). The §465-suspended remainder (../atRiskSuspendedLoss) is excluded. CollectionSum over this field gives the aggregate at-risk-allowed net; max(0, −that sum) is the §8582 line-4 loss (/rentalRealEstateLoss).

Fact.Name: Per-property at-risk-allowed net after the prior-year unallowed passive loss (Form 8582 Part IV col (c) → Part I line 1d)
Fact.Description: This activity's signed at-risk-allowed net (../atRiskAllowedNet) COMBINED with its prior years' unallowed passive loss (../priorYearUnallowedLoss, Form 8582 Part IV col (c)): ../atRiskAllowedNet − ../priorYearUnallowedLoss. This is the activity's overall net that flows into the §8582 line-1d combine (line 1a current income + line 1b current loss + line 1c prior loss). MAY be negative; a prior loss reduces the net whether the current net is a profit (line 1a + 1c) or a loss (line 1b + 1c). Complete-safe (IsComplete guard): when ../priorYearUnallowedLoss is unanswered this equals ../atRiskAllowedNet unchanged. The active/non-active split (../activeEligibleNet / ../nonActiveNet) is taken on THIS net, so the prior loss flows through the §8582 special-allowance chain exactly like a current-year loss.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 1b code for this property is 7 (self-rental), complete-safe
Fact.Description: True only when ../writableLine1bPropertyTypeCode is answered AND equals 7, the printed self-rental code. Complete-safe: unanswered or any other code resolves false. Structural helper for ../recharacterizesSelfRental — the Instructions for Schedule E define code 7 by the same condition ../selfRental and ../materiallyParticipatesInLessee together assert, so an entered code 7 is the taxpayer's own complete attestation of both facts. RULING: when this fact is true, ../recharacterizesSelfRental does not read ../selfRental or ../materiallyParticipatesInLessee AT ALL — the code is the SOLE source of truth for a code-7 property, not a stand-in used only when a flag happens to be unanswered. This avoids resolving a filer-entered code against a separately-answered contradicting flag by silent precedence (this campaign's ALIM/SLI/SCHF doctrine): the corrected reading removes the premise that the code and the flags are two votes on the same question, so there is nothing for the code to "win" against.

Fact.Name: Self-rental recharacterization gate — net PROFIT rented to a materially-participated lessee (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when this property is a self-rental AND the taxpayer materially participates in the lessee AND this activity's net is a PROFIT (../netAfterPriorLoss > 0). RULING: when ../line1bCodeIsSelfRental is true, the code is the SOLE source of truth for this determination and ../selfRental / ../materiallyParticipatesInLessee are NOT READ AT ALL — not consulted, not overridden. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040se.pdf, page 5 defines code 7 BY the same conjunction the two flags assert ("Enter code '7' for self-rental if you rent property to a trade or business in which you materially participated"): entering code 7 on the printed line 1b is the taxpayer's own complete attestation of both facts, not a third vote alongside the two flags. This was previously implemented as the flags being read and the code winning on a tie/contradiction (an undocumented silent-precedence resolution this dictionary corrected per this campaign's ALIM/SLI/SCHF doctrine against resolving two contradicting filer answers by silent precedence); the corrected reading removes the premise instead of picking a winner — a code-7 return never reads the flags, so there is no second answer for the code to contradict. The two flags remain live and load-bearing for the population that does NOT enter code 7 (self-rental is a substantive §469(c)(2) fact, not solely a function of the printed code; a filer whose interview didn't force a code-7 selection can still assert self-rental directly). When true, the property's net rental income is recharacterized NON-PASSIVE per Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6): it LEAVES /rentalActiveNet / /rentalNonActiveNet (hence the §8582 pool AND /rentalLimitedNetIncome) and is re-routed to Schedule E line 26 through the Part I nonpassive channel (/rentalNonpassiveNet). The GreaterThan gate enforces the income-vs-loss ASYMMETRY: a self-rental LOSS (net <= 0) is NOT recharacterized and falls through to the ordinary passive path unchanged. Complete-safe: when code 7 is not entered and either flag is unanswered this resolves Complete false (no recharacterization), so every scenario predating this fact's code-7 wiring is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Per-property self-rental net recharacterized NON-PASSIVE (Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6))
Fact.Description: This property's net rental income that is recharacterized NON-PASSIVE under the self-rental rule = ../netAfterPriorLoss when ../recharacterizesSelfRental (self-rental AND materially participates in the lessee AND a net profit), else 0. Because the gate already requires ../netAfterPriorLoss > 0, this is always the (positive) profit — a self-rental LOSS is never recharacterized and yields 0 here (it stays on the ordinary passive path). CollectionSum over this field is /rentalNonpassiveNet, re-added to Schedule E line 26 through the Part I nonpassive channel. Complete-safe 0 when not recharacterized.

Fact.Name: Per-property at-risk-allowed net eligible for the §8582 special allowance (active participation only)
Fact.Description: Split of the per-property net for the §8582 Part II special allowance, which applies ONLY to rental real-estate activities in which the taxpayer ACTIVELY PARTICIPATED (Form 8582 Part II header). The net split here is ../netAfterPriorLoss (the at-risk-allowed net AFTER the prior-year unallowed loss, Form 8582 line 1d) rather than ../atRiskAllowedNet, so a prior-year carry-in flows through the special-allowance chain. This is ../netAfterPriorLoss when this property claims active participation (../claimsActiveParticipation), else 0. CollectionSum over this field gives the ACTIVE net (/rentalActiveNet) — the only net whose loss is eligible for the $25,000 allowance. When the prior loss is 0/unanswered, ../netAfterPriorLoss = ../atRiskAllowedNet. A new FIRST case: when this property's net is recharacterized non-passive under the self-rental rule (../recharacterizesSelfRental, Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6)) this emits 0, so the recharacterized PROFIT leaves /rentalActiveNet (hence the §8582 pool and /rentalLimitedNetIncome) and flows instead through the Part I nonpassive channel. SECTION 469(c)(7) ROUTING WRAPS THIS BODY. When ../repRoutingApplies is true the property's CURRENT net has left this bucket for the Part I nonpassive channel and only the prior passive remainder stays, as ../repRoutingActivePassiveRemainder. The two arms of the outer Switch are complements with no catch-all, so a live professional-rental branch with a missing boundary attestation leaves this fact Incomplete rather than handing back the pre-routing number. ../repRoutingApplies is Complete false on every return that answers no service log, so this is byte-identical to pre-routing for the whole existing population.

Fact.Name: Per-property at-risk-allowed net NOT eligible for the §8582 special allowance (no active participation)
Fact.Description: Complement of ../activeEligibleNet: this property's net when it does NOT claim active participation (NOT ../claimsActiveParticipation), else 0. CollectionSum over this field gives the NON-ACTIVE net (/rentalNonActiveNet); a non-active LOSS gets NO special allowance and is fully suspended (/rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss), while a non-active PROFIT flows to income. When the prior loss is 0/unanswered, ../netAfterPriorLoss = ../atRiskAllowedNet; for an all-active return this is 0 for every property. interpretation:provisional. The per-activity carryforward split remains pooled-ratable (provisional). A new FIRST case: when this property's net is recharacterized non-passive under the self-rental rule (../recharacterizesSelfRental, Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6)) this emits 0, so the recharacterized PROFIT leaves /rentalNonActiveNet (hence the §8582 pool and /rentalLimitedNetIncome) and flows instead through the Part I nonpassive channel. SECTION 469(c)(7) ROUTING WRAPS THIS BODY, on the same terms as the sibling ../activeEligibleNet: a routed property keeps only its prior passive remainder here, as ../repRoutingNonactivePassiveRemainder, and an unresolved routing flag leaves this fact Incomplete instead of falling through to the pre-routing number.

Fact.Name: §179 business taxable-income limitation (Form 4562 Part I line 11)
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 11, the §179 business-income limitation: the §179 deduction is capped at the taxpayer's aggregate taxable income from the ACTIVE CONDUCT of a trade or business, which "include[s] all wages, salaries, tips, and other compensation you earned as an employee (from Form 1040, line 1a)" (i4562 Line 11) and is figured by "totaling the net income and losses from all trades and businesses you actively conducted" (Pub 946 ch.2), floored at zero — the "(not less than zero)" of line 11 applied to the AGGREGATE, not per activity (i4562 Line 12: the limit applies "to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity"). = max(0, /wages + /scheduleCNetProfit + /k1NonpassiveActiveNet + /rentalNetBeforeSection179). Each business net is figured WITHOUT the §179 deduction itself (Pub 946 ch.2 "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction"), which is why the rental term is the pre-§179 /rentalNetBeforeSection179 (a POST-§179 net would create a §179 ↔ income cycle). A wages-only definition would not do: it over-states line 11 and over-allows §179 whenever an active business nets a loss (a rental / Sch C / nonpassive-K-1 loss that wages-only omits is a taxpayer-favorable over-deduction). This is a TAXPAYER-level limit (keeps it top-level); each property's section179Deduction references it. THE K-1 TERM IS LIKEWISE PRE-§179 since the K-1 §179 leg landed: /k1NonpassiveActiveNet now sums /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 rather than the post-§179 /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart, for the same Pub 946 reason the rental term is /rentalNetBeforeSection179. Byte-identical on every committed row (no committed scenario answers box 12); it is the MEANING that changes once one does. And it is not only a correctness point: measured with scripts/factdag.py, /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart was in this fact's upstream cone (81 paths) before the split, so a §179 subtrahend on it reading this limit would have closed a real cycle. RESIDUAL (honestly disclosed, NOT "conservative"): guaranteed payments (nonnegative ⇒ omission only under-allows §179, the safe direction; and its box-14 Incomplete would risk refusing returns) and Form 4797 §1231 gains/losses (a §1231 active-business LOSS omitted would over-allow §179 — bounded: no scenario combines a §1231 active-business loss with a §179 election, and §1231 recharacterization / capital-vs-ordinary is a follow-on) are not yet in line 11. ⚠ THE SCHEDULE C TERM STAYS THE COMBINED LINE 31 THROUGH A SECTION 931/933 EXCLUSION, and the unit that decided it moved every other money consumer of scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit onto the basis its own statute requires and left this one alone, because NO VENDORED SOURCE ANSWERS IT. Publication 570 chapter 4 names the deductions it apportions — the standard deduction, alimony, medical, charitable, real estate taxes, mortgage interest, the IRA contribution, the tips/overtime and vehicle-loan deductions — and the section 179 business-income limitation is not among them; Publication 946, the Form 4562 instructions and Publication 1321 say nothing about section 931 or 933 at all. So it is not knowable from the printed text whether "taxable income from the active conduct of a trade or business" is figured before or after the exclusion. DIRECTION IF THE READING IS WRONG: line 11 too HIGH by the excluded profit, section 179 over-allowed, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE — the riskier direction, which is why it is named here rather than left implicit. It is UNSOURCED, not deferred for convenience, and a unit that finds an authority should move it. The line-5 ceiling on line 11 is applied separately (the $2,500,000 cap inside section179Deduction), so line 11 here is the business-income figure. interpretation:provisional. Result rounded to whole dollars.
S202 (2026-09-12) correction to the historical equation above: the Schedule C term now reads scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfitBeforeSection179, which adds back each allowed section 179 deduction already included in that business's net profit. A Schedule C business must answer its per-business split (0 if none); an unanswered split leaves line 11 Incomplete rather than treating the mixed line-13 amount as all non-§179 depreciation. This add-back does not resolve the separate, still-provisional §931/§933 question recorded above.

Fact.Name: Schedule E net rental real estate income (total)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 21 / line 26 total across all rental properties (Parts II–V not applicable): CollectionSum of each property's pre-limitation net (/rentalProperties/*/propertyRawNet). This is the PRE-LIMITATION net and MAY be negative. It still EXPORTS as Schedule E line 21; what flows to total income is /rentalLimitedNetIncome (the §8582-limited amount).

Fact.Name: Aggregate rental net income BEFORE §179 (Form 4562 line-11 rental component)
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of each property's /rentalProperties/*/netBeforeSection179 — the total rental Schedule-E net figured WITHOUT the §179 deduction, the rental component of the Form 4562 line-11 §179 business-income limitation (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit). MAY be negative. Gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so non-rental returns resolve Complete-0 byte-identical (the /scheduleERentalNetIncome pattern). Result rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Aggregate NONPASSIVE (active) K-1 ordinary business net (Form 4562 line-11 K-1 component)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum of each K-1's /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 — the nonpassive (materially participated) share of Schedule E Part II ordinary business income or (loss). The actively-conducted K-1 component of the Form 4562 line-11 §179 business-income limitation (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit): a nonpassive K-1 profit RAISES line 11, a nonpassive K-1 LOSS REDUCES it. PASSIVE K-1 income/loss is deliberately EXCLUDED (a passive activity is not "actively conducted" for §179; §469). Guaranteed payments (/k1GuaranteedPayments) are also excluded here — omitting a nonnegative term only under-allows §179 (the safe direction), and wiring it would risk the box-14 Incomplete refusal. Gated on /claimsK1Income so non-K-1 returns resolve Complete-0 byte-identical (the /scheduleEPartIINetIncome pattern). Result rounded to whole dollars.
IT READS THE PRE-§179 TWIN, not /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart, since the K-1 §179 leg landed. That is the SAME rule the rental term already follows — Pub 946 ch.2 says to figure the line-11 taxable income "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction", which is why /rentalNetBeforeSection179 and not /scheduleERentalNetIncome is the rental addend. The values are byte-identical on every committed row (the §179 subtrahend is a complete-safe 0 with no box-12 amount answered); the change is what the fact MEANS once a box-12 amount exists.
THE OPERAND MOVED ONE STEP FURTHER, and the sentence above that needs reading with this one is the opening "CollectionSum of each K-1's /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179". It is now a CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/activelyConductedNetBeforeSection179, which IS that fact on every K-1 except a passive PTP, where it is $0. Nothing else in this Description changes: the pre-§179 rule the paragraph above argues is unaffected (the new fact reads the pre-§179 twin), and the values are byte-identical on every committed row that carries no passive PTP.
THE PARAGRAPH THIS DISCHARGES IS THIS FACT'S OWN. "PASSIVE K-1 income/loss is deliberately EXCLUDED (a passive activity is not 'actively conducted' for §179; §469)" was TRUE of every passive K-1 except one: a publicly traded partnership with an overall §469(k) gain, whose gain ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 admits as nonpassive income because the Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) print it so, "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 10). The Name and this Description claimed the exclusion; the body did not make it. That gap is why /formK1s/*/activelyConductedNetBeforeSection179 carries the argument and the citations.

Fact.Name: Claims active participation in any rental real estate activity (aggregate)
Fact.Description: Aggregate active-participation gate for the Form 8582 Part II $25,000 special allowance: true when the return claims rental income AND ANY property actively participates (Count of /rentalProperties/*/claimsActiveParticipation > 0). Gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so non-rental returns resolve Complete false. For the one-element collection this equals the single property's claims gate.

Fact.Name: Any rental property carries a non-straight-line depreciation intake (AMT scope-out gate)
Fact.Description: Aggregate AMT-depreciation-adjustment gate (U-065a REVISION): true when the return claims rental income AND ANY property carries a non-straight-line depreciation intake (Count(/rentalProperties/*/hasAmtDepreciationAdjustmentIntake) > 0) — a 5-year MACRS personal-property item (200% DB, incl. its bonus/§179 sub-elections) or an opaque-method depreciation override. This is the ONLY modeled source of a Form 6251 line 2l / line 3 AMT depreciation adjustment, so it is the narrowed trigger for the AMT scope-out knockout (form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference), replacing the former blanket "has any Schedule C or Schedule E rental income" trigger that over-refused building-only rentals and net-income business returns. Gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so the ~150 non-rental scenarios resolve Complete false byte-identical (the /claimsRentalActiveParticipation pattern). A building-only rental (straight-line 27.5-/39-year) resolves false → computes AMT (correctly, usually $0) rather than being refused.

Fact.Name: Aggregate at-risk-allowed net from actively-participated rental activities (§8582 line 4 input)
Fact.Description: The sum of the per-property at-risk-allowed nets that are ELIGIBLE for the §8582 Part II special allowance — i.e., only the activities with active participation: CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/activeEligibleNet), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. Signed (a net loss is negative). max(0, −this) is the §8582 line-4 loss (/rentalRealEstateLoss) eligible for the $25,000 allowance. For an all-active return this equals the all-property aggregate at-risk-allowed net.

Fact.Name: Aggregate at-risk-allowed net from NON-actively-participated rental activities
Fact.Description: The sum of the per-property at-risk-allowed nets that are NOT eligible for the §8582 special allowance (no active participation): CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/nonActiveNet), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. Signed. A net non-active loss gets NO special allowance; a POSITIVE sum (net non-active profit) flows to income. This signed net is now a direct input to the cross-activity §8582 pool (Form 8582 Part I line 2d, /otherPassiveNet): a net non-active loss is offset by passive income from OTHER activities when present (and its authoritative suspended figure is the pool's /passiveSuspendedLossTotal), else fully suspended (/rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss, retained for continuity). interpretation:provisional. The per-activity carryforward split remains pooled-ratable.

Fact.Name: Overall passive rental real-estate net (Form 8582 Part I line 3 = line 1d + line 2d)
Fact.Description: The §469 CROSS-PARTICIPATION passive net — Form 8582 Part I line 3 — the sum of the active-participation aggregate (line 1d, /rentalActiveNet) and the other-passive aggregate (line 2d, /rentalNonActiveNet): /rentalActiveNet + /rentalNonActiveNet, gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. Signed (a net loss is negative). This is the netting base that makes a NON-ACTIVE passive PROFIT offset an ACTIVE passive LOSS before the $25,000 special allowance: Form 8582 line 4 = the SMALLER of the line-1d loss and this line-3 loss (/rentalRealEstateLoss), and the amount that flows to total income is max(line 3, −allowed loss) (/rentalLimitedNetIncome). When there is no non-active passive income (/rentalNonActiveNet ≤ 0) line 3 ≤ line 1d so the line-4 smaller-of is unchanged; only when a non-active profit exists does the netting bite.

Fact.Name: Aggregate self-rental net rental income recharacterized NON-PASSIVE (Part I nonpassive channel)
Fact.Description: The total net rental income recharacterized NON-PASSIVE under the self-rental rule (Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6)) = CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/selfRentalRecharacterizedNet), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome (complete-safe 0 for a non-rental return). This is the Part I nonpassive channel that RE-ADDS the recharacterized self-rental PROFIT to Schedule E line 26 (/scheduleEPartINetIncome) — the same profit that the new first case of ../activeEligibleNet / ../nonActiveNet REMOVED from /rentalActiveNet / /rentalNonActiveNet. The split of channels is the point: the profit stays in TOTAL INCOME (via line 26) but no longer inflates /passiveIncomeTotal (the §8582 pool), so it can no longer absorb other passive losses. 0 (complete) for every scenario with no self-rental flag set, so this is a clean additive unit. This total is not self-rental only and is not always ≥ 0. It now sums ../repAwareNonpassiveNet, which is the self-rental recharacterized net for every property that is not routed under section 469(c)(7) and the professional-rental current net after its own prior passive offset for one that is. The two are alternatives per property, never addends, so a property that is both is counted once. The sign rule changes because a professional rental LOSS is nonpassive and is not limited by section 469: it reaches Schedule E line 26 in full, where a self-rental loss never could (only profits are recharacterized). The pre-routing value is preserved exactly for every return that answers no real estate professional service log, because ../repRoutingApplies is Complete false there.

Fact.Name: §179 expense deduction allowed this year (Form 4562 Part I line 12), total
Fact.Description:
The total §179 deduction allowed across all rental properties = CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/section179Deduction), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. (The $2.5M line-1 cap and the line-11 wages limit are taxpayer-aggregate; a genuine N-property allocation of the cap is a follow-on — the per-property deductions are value-identical to today for the single element.) interpretation:provisional.
DISPOSITION: EXPORTED as a CULMINATING fact. Re-measured on this trunk rather than inherited from the issue: no fact's depends_on in dictionary/manifest/facts-manifest.json names this path, no syndoc workbook lists it in a required VALUE_FACTS tuple, and no flow gate reads it — so it does terminate the computation, which is exactly what downstreamFacts asserts (js/src/TaxLogicTestCoverageReporter.ts reads that flag as `culminating`, a fact consumed downstream of the graph rather than by another fact). The claim is TRUE here because the value is a REAL OUTPUT and not an engine-internal fiction: Form 4562 Part I line 12 is a printed box on a form that is FILED with the return, and this fact's own Name already names that line. Two halves of one Part I block, one legible to a reader outside the graph and one not, was an asymmetry with no reason behind it.
mef is deliberately NOT claimed, on the Schedule H Worksheet 2 line: mef asserts that the IRS RECEIVES this element, which is an e-file/MeF schema question project invariant #7 excludes from this repo and which no vendored source in sources/ can settle (invariant #3). The sibling withholds it too. The Export changes no resolved value — it is metadata on the Fact element, absent from the manifest schema (whose per-fact keys are completeness/depends_on/module/rounding/type/writable) and from the baseline row shape (path/completeness/type/value). Witnessed by the 10 node-test cases pinning this path, three of them with more than one rental property, so the aggregation this fact performs is exercised beyond n=1, though the authority comment's cleanroom caveats above still speak to the single-rental nominations.

Fact.Name: §179 carryover of disallowed deduction to 2026 (Form 4562 Part I line 13, output), total
Fact.Description: The total §179 cost disallowed this year and carried to 2026 across all rental properties = CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/section179CarryoverToNextYear), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. Output only (single-year demo). interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Rental loss suspended by the §465 at-risk rules (carryover, output only), total
Fact.Description: The total rental real-estate loss disallowed for 2025 by the §465 at-risk limitation across all properties = CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/atRiskSuspendedLoss), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. §465(a)(2) carryover; output only (single-year demo). DISTINCT from the §8582 passive suspended loss.

Fact.Name: Rental real estate loss entering Form 8582 Part II line 4 (smaller of line 1d loss and line 3 loss, positive)
Fact.Description: The rental real-estate loss that enters Form 8582 Part II line 4 as a POSITIVE amount, gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome. Form 8582 line 4 is the SMALLER of (a) the active-participation loss on line 1d, max(0, −/rentalActiveNet), and (b) the OVERALL passive loss on line 3 after §469 cross-participation netting, max(0, −/rentalOverallPassiveNet): line 4 = min(activeLoss, overallLoss). Because a NON-ACTIVE passive PROFIT raises line 3 above the line-1d loss, the smaller-of caps the special-allowance-eligible loss at the post-netting amount — a non-active profit must offset an active loss before the $25,000 allowance applies. The special allowance still reaches only active-participation activities (Form 8582 Part II header), which is why line 1d (not line 3) is one arm of the min. At-risk (§465) still applies BEFORE §8582 (Form 6198 line-21 Note). A net-positive active or overall sum means no §8582 line-4 loss (= 0). Set this to the line-1d loss alone (max(0, −/rentalActiveNet)); when there is no non-active passive income overallLoss = activeLoss + (−/rentalNonActiveNet) ≥ activeLoss.

Fact.Name: Rental loss from non-active activities suspended (ineligible for the §8582 special allowance), output only
Fact.Description: The rental real-estate loss from NON-actively-participated activities that is DISALLOWED for 2025 because the §8582 Part II special allowance does not reach it: max(0, −/rentalNonActiveNet). DISTINCT from /rentalSuspendedLoss (the active-side §8582 carryforward) and from /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss (the §465 at-risk carryover). In scope there is no passive income to offset it, so the entire non-active loss is suspended; §469(b) carries it forward, but this single-year demo REPORTS it as an output only. 0 when every activity is active or when the non-active side is a net profit. interpretation:provisional — the full §469 netting is deferred (a later unit).

Fact.Name: Form 8582 line 6 MAGI adjustment reduction (excluding disregarded deductions)
Fact.Description: The Schedule 1 above-the-line adjustments that reduce Form 8582 line 6 modified AGI. Starts with taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra (Schedule 1 lines 11–19a, 23 and 25), then removes the deductible half of self-employment tax and section 501(c)(18)(D) pension contributions because the Form 8582 line-6 instructions say not to take those two deductions into account. IRA and student-loan deductions are already outside the starting subtotal, and the section 250 deduction is not in it. The income terms remain a separate cycle-free build. Unanswered optional Schedule 1 items contribute $0 through the source subtotal's complete-safe wrappers. Possession-exclusion allocation remains a successor; see the records overlay. Supplies the MAGI <Subtrahends> leg.

Fact.Name: Modified adjusted gross income for Form 8582 Part II (line 6)
Fact.Description:
Modified adjusted gross income for the §8582 special-allowance phaseout (Form 8582 Part II line 6): the sum of the income components that make up total income and are NOT excluded by line 6, floored at zero. §8582 line 6 MAGI is figured WITHOUT the taxable amount of social security benefits (i8582 line 6 excludes it; the published example computes $86,500 = $92,000 − $5,500), so /taxableSocialSecurityBenefits is EXCLUDED. REBODIED 2026-07-31 — SIX ADDENDS ADDED, AND WHAT THIS FACT IS NOW. This body used to carry eight of /totalIncome's twelve direct addends and describe itself as "/totalIncome MINUS the Schedule E rental term", which it was not: it dropped EVERY Schedule E component plus alimony and Form 4797 ordinary. Omitting income made MAGI too LOW, /rentalSpecialAllowance too LARGE, more passive rental loss allowed, and total income too LOW — a World-#1 under-statement on any return carrying a royalty, a REMIC residual, a farm rental, alimony or a Form 4797 ordinary gain TOGETHER WITH a rental loss inside the phaseout band. The six added terms and their individual sign rules are stated at each dependency in the body below; they are /royaltyNetIncome, /scheduleERemicResidualNet, /rentalNonpassiveNet (REPOINTED 2026-09-19 to /repAwareRentalNonpassiveMagiTotal, which is the same sum with a routed section 469(c)(7) professional-rental LOSS floored at zero — Form 8582 line 6 excludes any rental real estate loss allowed to a real estate professional, and IRC 469(i)(3)(E)(iv) excludes any loss allowable by reason of subsection (c)(7); a professional rental PROFIT is not excluded and stays. Identical to /rentalNonpassiveNet for every return that routes no professional rental), alimony:/taxableAlimonyReceived, form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome, and — the one that BRANCHED — /farmRentalNetIncome, profit in full and loss to zero.
THAT SIXTH ADDEND IS GONE AS OF 2026-08-03, and this paragraph is kept as history rather than rewritten, because the other five are unchanged. The /farmRentalPassivePoolParticipation fill made the Form 4835 farm rental a member of the Form 8582 Part I pool, so addend (8)'s single §469(d)(1) aggregate now carries it like every other passive activity, and a per-leg floor on top of that would double count the profit whenever the pool nets positive. The removal's full reasoning — including its taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, which is why it is argued rather than asserted — is at the deleted addend's site in the body below. FIVE added addends, not six, is the current count.
THE AUTHORITY IS INCLUSIVE BY DEFAULT, WITH A CLOSED EXCLUSION LIST. "To figure modified adjusted gross income, combine ALL the amounts used to figure adjusted gross income, except don't take into account" ten bullets (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8582.pdf, page 11), of which only three could ever reach a term here: any passive activity loss as defined in §469(d)(1), any rental real estate loss allowed to a real estate professional, and the taxable amount of social security and tier 1 railroad retirement benefits. The same rule is statutory at IRC §469(i)(3)(E) (26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section469&num=0&edition=2024), and the statute is why the sign rule reads the way it does: clause (iv) excludes "any passive activity LOSS", not passive amounts generally. Line 6 then states its INCLUDE side explicitly, which is the authority for three of the six: "Include in modified adjusted gross income any portfolio income and expenses that are clearly and directly allocable to portfolio income. Also include any income that's treated as nonpassive income, such as overall gain from a PTP and net income from an activity or item of property subject to the recharacterization of passive income rules" (lines 768-774).
ONE CONTRARY AUTHORITY, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN BURIED. Pub 925 (2025) renders the same rule with a broader bullet — "Passive activity income OR LOSS included on Form 8582" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p925.pdf, page 6) — under which a farm rental PROFIT would also drop out and MAGI would be lower still. This fact follows the statute and the form's own instructions (loss only), for three reasons: §469(i)(3)(E)(iv) is the controlling text and says LOSS; i8582's bullet cross-references §469(d)(1), which defines a loss; and the Pub 925 reading is the World-#1-riskier of the two (lower MAGI, larger allowance, less tax). Recorded so a later reader meets the conflict here instead of rediscovering it.
THE PASSIVE SIDE IS ONE FLOORED AGGREGATE, ADDEND (8) — corrected 2026-08-03 after the pre-PR fg-review (FINDING 2 and FINDING 5). Line 6 excludes "any passive activity loss AS DEFINED IN SECTION 469(d)(1)", and that definition is an aggregate across ALL passive activities, so the passive contribution to MAGI is max(0, aggregate passive income − aggregate passive losses) = GreaterOf(/overallPassiveNet, 0), Form 8582 Part I line 3 floored once. The first landing of the Part II/III fill instead floored each Schedule E Part separately and left the RENTAL passive legs out of line 6 altogether; both are corrected by this one addend. The full derivation is at addend (8). The Form 4835 farm rental was the last activity flooring on its own leg and it no longer does: addend (6) was DELETED 2026-08-03, when the farm rental became a member of the Part I pool, so the aggregate is now complete over every passive activity this dictionary models.
PARTS II AND III ARE IN AS ADDEND (7) — NONPASSIVE HALVES ONLY — AND THE CYCLE FINDING IS WHY THEY LOOK LIKE THAT. The rebody contract asserted that none of the five missing Schedule E terms is downstream of /rentalSpecialAllowance. THAT WAS FALSE FOR TWO OF THEM, verified with scripts/factdag.py on 2026-07-31 and RE-VERIFIED on this branch before anything was wired: /section8582Magi IS in the upstream cone of both /scheduleEPartIINetIncome (cone 819) and /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome (cone 812), so declaring either would close a real cycle. The loop runs through the §8582 suspension allocation (/k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated and /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated, cone 811 each), and that is not a coincidence: the term that closes the cycle IS the §469(d)(1) passive activity loss that bullet 1 tells line 6 to leave out. Both parts therefore enter as a DECOMPOSITION, not a dependency — /section8582MagiPartIIAndIIITerms, addend (7) below, which since the 2026-08-03 fg-review correction carries ONLY the NONPASSIVE halves; the passive side enters whole as addend (8), GreaterOf(/overallPassiveNet, 0), one floor over the entire Part I pool. The §469(d)(1) aggregate-versus-item-wise question is CLOSED BY THE PRINTED CROSS-REFERENCE, not provisional — see addend (8)'s derivation. The exposure this paragraph used to name — MAGI too LOW on a return with a K-1 plus a rental loss in the band — is CLOSED as of that fill.
interpretation:provisional — still omits the Schedule 1 ADJUSTMENTS side of AGI (the line-6 add-backs for the IRA deduction, student loan interest, the SE-tax deduction, and §250), which is a separate surface from the addend set this rebody corrected. The §135 savings bond exclusion is addend (9), below, and the adoption exclusion is already carried through the unnumbered base list's income:/employerIncomeSubtotalDisregardingSection137 and form8839:/adoptionLine23TotalEmployerBenefits pair; neither is part of this remaining gap.
The AGI-adjustment subtrahend is now wired below. Its cycle-free subtotal comes from taxCalculations:/adjustmentsExcludingStudentLoanAndIra, less the two deductions Form 8582 expressly disregards here (deductible half of SE tax and §501(c)(18)(D)); IRA and student-loan amounts were never in that subtotal, and §250 is outside it. This closes the domestic modeled adjustment path but not the possession-exclusion allocation: the source subtotal is unapportioned for §933, and its existing SE-health-insurance attribution still needs review. Exact successor: build a cycle-safe, territory-aware Form 8582 adjustment subtotal in taxCalculations/income, including the §933 allocation and §162(l) direct attribution, then point this fact at that export. Until then, this MAGI adjustment is partial for territory filers.
The subtrahend /section8582MagiEligibleAboveLineAdjustments takes $0 ONLY when scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction, the operand it bottoms out in, is Incomplete (a Schedule C return that answers no Schedule SE intake); on that return this fact is the income Add alone, value and completeness. Whenever that deduction resolves, the subtrahend is subtracted as it resolves: Complete, or Placeholder with its value, the Placeholder tier carried through (i8582 line 6 "combine all the amounts used to figure adjusted gross income", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8582.pdf, page 11, with Form 8582 line 6 and line 8 at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8582.pdf, page 1; the HSA or educator deduction is not on its exclusion list). Residue: a return whose /selfEmploymentTaxDeduction is itself Placeholder still takes $0. The reasoning, the witnesses and the alternative that was rejected are on the Subtrahends in the body below.

Fact.Name: Form 8582 line 6 MAGI — the Schedule E Part II and Part III NONPASSIVE terms (a DECOMPOSITION, not a dependency)
Fact.Description:
The Part II (line 32) and Part III (line 37) contributions to /section8582Magi, built from the pieces of those lines rather than from the lines themselves. This is the remaining half of the 2026-07-31 line-6 rebody, and it is a separate fact because the obvious construction — declaring /scheduleEPartIINetIncome and /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome as dependencies of /section8582Magi — CLOSES A REAL CYCLE.
THE CYCLE, re-measured on this branch with scripts/factdag.py rather than trusted from the contract. /section8582Magi is in the upstream cone of /scheduleEPartIINetIncome (cone 819) and of /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome (cone 812). It enters through exactly ONE term per part: the §8582 suspension allocation, /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated and /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated (cone 811 each), both of which read the special allowance that MAGI itself determines. Every other term is clean — /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart (12), /k1GuaranteedPayments (10), /k1PassiveNet (14), /estatePassiveNet (11), /estateTrustNonpassivePart's inputs /writableEstateTrustK1Income (1), /estateTrustK1LossIsPassive (2), /estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss (8), and both gates (2 each); NONE has /section8582Magi in its cone. The coincidence is the answer rather than an obstacle: the term that closes the cycle IS the §469(d)(1) passive activity loss that line 6's first exclusion bullet tells us to leave out. Excluding it is required by the instructions and required by the graph, for the same reason.
SO THE SUSPENSION ALLOCATIONS ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT, not forgotten. And so, after the 2026-08-03 review correction below, ARE BOTH PASSIVE LEGS. What is included here is only the NONPASSIVE halves: Part II = CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart) + /k1GuaranteedPayments; Part III = /estateTrustNonpassivePart. They enter SIGNED, because a nonpassive loss is not reached by bullet 1 — the same rule addends (2) and (5) of /section8582Magi already state.
THE CONE SIZES ABOVE ARE AS MEASURED ON 2026-07-31 and one of them has since grown: the section 179 split gave /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart a section 179 column-(j) subtrahend, so its cone is no longer 12. THE CONCLUSION IS RE-MEASURED AND HOLDS — /section8582Magi is NOT in the upstream cone of /rentalSection179IncomeLimit (scripts/factdag.py up, 0 hits), which is the only new path the subtrahend reaches, so no term here has acquired a cycle. And the post-§179 figure is the RIGHT one for line 6 rather than merely a harmless one: the line-6 exclusion list (i8582 lines 744-767) names passive activity losses, real-estate-professional rental losses, social security, IRA and 501(c)(18) contributions, the SE-tax deduction, savings-bond and adoption-assistance exclusions, student loan interest, and the FDII/GILTI deduction — it does NOT name the section 179 deduction, so a nonpassive one stays subtracted in MAGI exactly as it is in AGI.
CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (pre-PR fg-review, FINDING 2), and the correction is the whole point of this paragraph. As first landed, this fact ALSO carried the two passive legs, each floored inside its own Part: GreaterOf(/k1PassiveNet, 0) and GreaterOf(/estatePassiveNet, 0). Its Description defended that by declaring §469(d)(1)'s AGGREGATE definition controlling. THE TWO CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT, and the review said so: §469(d)(1) aggregates across ALL passive activities, not within a Schedule E Part, and the rental legs were not in the sum at all. Flooring per Part excludes MORE than the PAL whenever one activity's loss could have been absorbed by another's income, and no printed text licenses that. The reading was not rescued; the implementation was changed. The passive side of line 6 is now ONE floored aggregate over the whole Form 8582 Part I pool, /section8582Magi addend (8), where the derivation is written out. There is NO interpretive choice left on this axis — the instruction's own cross-reference settles it — so the aggregate-versus-item-wise "provisional" this fact used to carry is GONE rather than reworded. The residue this paragraph named — the Form 4835 farm rental still flooring on its own leg because it was not a pool member — is ALSO gone as of 2026-08-03: that contract is filled, the farm rental is a pool member, and addend (6) is deleted. What is provisional on this axis now is only the Part IV/Part V routing itself, which is derived rather than printed and is tagged at /farmRentalActiveParticipation.
COMPLETENESS CONTAGION — AUDITED, NOT ASSUMED, per term. Every input here is ALREADY upstream of /totalIncome through /scheduleEPartIINetIncome or /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, both of which Export downstreamFacts into it. /k1GuaranteedPayments is the one that can genuinely refuse (Result.Incomplete when a guaranteed payment lacks its box-14 SE assessment) — and on exactly those returns /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, and therefore /totalIncome, was ALREADY Incomplete. So no return that used to compute stops computing, which is the same audit addend (5) records for form4797:/form4797OrdinaryIncome.
VALUE-MOVING, AND THE DIRECTION IS NOT UNIFORM — measured, not predicted. MAGI moves BOTH WAYS. On a K-1 reporting nonpassive INCOME, MAGI RISES, the allowance FALLS, less passive rental loss is allowed and tax goes UP — the World-#1 correction the 2026-07-31 rebody opened its account on, and the reason this half was contracted rather than dropped. On a K-1 reporting a NONPASSIVE LOSS, MAGI FALLS (e.g. 100,000 → 70,000 where a 30,000 nonpassive loss enters), the allowance can RISE, and that is the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction. The second direction is not an oversight and is not optional: a nonpassive loss IS an amount used to figure adjusted gross income and is NOT a passive activity loss, so no line-6 bullet reaches it, and excluding it would be inventing an exclusion the instructions do not contain. It is exactly the signed treatment addends (1), (2), (4) and (5) already give the royalty, REMIC, alimony and Form 4797 legs, each of which can also be negative. The PASSIVE side moves separately and in one place, at addend (8). TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, signed (the nonpassive legs may be negative), unrounded here — /section8582Magi applies the single Round and the floor at zero, so a return whose components net below zero still reports MAGI 0 rather than a negative.

Fact.Name: Rental real estate special allowance (Form 8582 Part II line 8)
Fact.Description: The maximum special allowance after the MAGI phaseout (Form 8582 Part II line 8), FILING-STATUS-AWARE: line 8 = min(cap, 50% × max(0, threshold − /section8582Magi)), where the threshold and cap depend on filing status — (i) single / HoH / QSS / MFJ → $150,000 / $25,000; (ii) MFS lived APART all year (/livedApartAllYear) → $75,000 / $12,500; (iii) MFS lived WITH spouse → $0 (not eligible). THE THREE CASES ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AND THERE IS NO CATCH-ALL, deliberately. Eligibility under IRC 469(i)(5)(B) is an AFFIRMATIVE condition on the MFS filer: the subsection does not apply to a married individual filing separately who does not live apart from the spouse at all times during the year. So when filers:/livedApartAllYear is UNANSWERED for an MFS filer, none of the three Whens is true, the Switch runs off the end of its case list, and this fact resolves INCOMPLETE rather than guessing. That shape is load-bearing and both halves of it are: the Switch evaluator does NOT stop at a case whose When is Incomplete, it only clears the accumulated completeness and keeps scanning, so the FIRST later true When supplies the value as a Placeholder. Case (ii) was once a bare /isFilingStatusMFS test and case (iii) a bare True, and the pair handed an MFS filer with an unknown cohabitation answer a Placeholder 12,500.00 - the full lived-apart allowance for someone whose allowance may be 0. Tightening only case (ii) is WORSE, not better: the bare True then matches and returns the single filer 25,000.00 as a Placeholder. Both, or neither. This now agrees with form8582:/form8582Line8SpecialAllowanceCap, which is Incomplete on the same return; the two facts are the same line 8 and must not disagree. Pinned by the node tests scheduleE/rsa-mfs-cohabitation-unanswered-is-incomplete (Incomplete), scheduleE/rsa-nonmfs-single-cohabitation-unanswered-stays-complete (the non-MFS population stays COMPLETE when the cohabitation question was never asked, because case (i) is a false All and case (iii) is a Complete Not), scheduleE/rsa-nonmfs-mfj-non-mfs-branch-still-supplies-the-value (an MFJ return still takes case (iii) and still carries the 25,000-cap body, 15,000.00 at that MAGI; its Placeholder comes from /section8582Magi, which is Placeholder on that fixture for a reason upstream of this fact and present before this change), scheduleE/rsa-mfs-lived-apart-cap-binds, scheduleE/rsa-mfs-lived-apart-half-binds and scheduleE/rsa-mfs-lived-with-spouse-zero.

Fact.Name: Rental loss allowed by the special allowance (Form 8582 Part II line 9)
Fact.Description: The passive rental real-estate loss allowed for 2025 under the special allowance (Form 8582 Part II line 9): when the taxpayer actively participated (/claimsRentalActiveParticipation), the smaller of the loss (line 4, /rentalRealEstateLoss) or the phased-out allowance (line 8, /rentalSpecialAllowance); otherwise 0. The portion of the rental loss that reduces nonpassive income (flows, as a negative, through /rentalLimitedNetIncome to total income).

Fact.Name: Rental loss suspended (disallowed / carryforward), output only
Fact.Description: The passive rental real-estate loss DISALLOWED for 2025 = /rentalRealEstateLoss − /rentalAllowedLoss (Form 8582 line 4 minus line 9). §469(b) carries it forward; this single-year demo REPORTS it as an output only. 0 for profit cases and fully-allowed losses.

Fact.Name: Total passive rental loss suspended for 2025 under §469 cross-participation netting (authoritative), output only
Fact.Description: The AUTHORITATIVE combined passive rental real-estate loss DISALLOWED for 2025 after §469 cross-participation netting and the §8582 special allowance: max(0, overallLoss − /rentalAllowedLoss), where overallLoss = max(0, −/rentalOverallPassiveNet) is the Form 8582 line-3 loss. §469(b) carries it forward; this single-year demo REPORTS it as an output only. This supersedes the per-category split (/rentalSuspendedLoss + /rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss), which is KEPT for continuity but is only an approximation once a non-active passive PROFIT nets against an active passive loss (the netting moves loss off the active line-4 path). When there is no non-active passive income (/rentalNonActiveNet ≤ 0) line 3 ≤ line 1d so the line-4 smaller-of is unchanged; only when a non-active profit exists does the netting bite.

Fact.Name: Schedule E net rental income after the §8582 limitation (flows to total income)
Fact.Description: The rental real-estate amount that flows to total income (Schedule 1 line 5 → Form 1040 line 8) after the §8582 passive-loss limitation. Under FULL cross-activity §469 netting this is /rentalActiveNet + /rentalNonActiveNet + /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated (gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome): the rental SIGNED net (line 1d + line 2d) plus the rental share of the pool suspended total (the plug, which adds back the portion of the rental loss DISALLOWED by §469). When no passive K-1/estate activity is present, /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated reduces to the rental-only suspended loss and this equals max(/rentalOverallPassiveNet, −/rentalAllowedLoss). The pool facts (/passiveAllowedLossTotal etc.) are the authoritative cross-activity figures; the rental-only chain (/rentalAllowedLoss, /rentalSuspendedLoss, /rentalTotalSuspendedLoss) is retained for continuity and is the line-1d/3 rental view. SUPERSEDED PRIOR TEXT: this was max(/rentalOverallPassiveNet, −/rentalAllowedLoss): • When the OVERALL passive net (Form 8582 line 3, /rentalOverallPassiveNet) is ≥ the negated allowed loss, the overall net flows — i.e. a net passive PROFIT (line 3 ≥ 0) flows in full, and a net passive loss that is ENTIRELY allowed by the special allowance flows as that (negative) overall net. • Otherwise the special allowance caps the deductible loss, so only −/rentalAllowedLoss flows and the remainder is suspended (/rentalTotalSuspendedLoss). This single expression lets a non-active passive profit offset an active passive loss; summing an active side and a non-active side would suspend such a loss even when passive income existed to absorb it (the §469 gap). When there is no non-active passive income (/rentalNonActiveNet ≤ 0) line 3 ≤ line 1d so the line-4 smaller-of is unchanged; only when a non-active profit exists does the netting bite. For an all-active return /rentalNonActiveNet = 0 and /rentalOverallPassiveNet = /rentalActiveNet. The AUTHORITATIVE combined suspended loss under netting is /rentalTotalSuspendedLoss; the per-category split (/rentalSuspendedLoss + /rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss) is retained for continuity but is an approximation when non-active income nets against an active loss. interpretation:provisional — the per-activity allocation (Form 8582 Worksheets 4-7) is deferred.

Fact.Name: Has Schedule E royalty income
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports royalty income on Schedule E Part I (line 4) — royalties from oil, gas, or mineral properties (not operating/working interests), copyrights, patents, or name-image-likeness (NIL) rights, held for INVESTMENT (not in the active conduct of a trade or business). Gate for the royalty intake (twin of /hasScheduleERentalIncome). When true, /writableRoyaltyIncome and /writableRoyaltyExpenses carry the single royalty activity's line-4 income and ordinary deductible expenses.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E royalty income
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /writableHasRoyaltyIncome is answered AND true (IsComplete pattern, as /claimsScheduleERentalIncome). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so returns without royalty income still resolve and /royaltyNetIncome is 0. Gates the royalty net so the ~325 non-royalty scenarios keep /royaltyNetIncome Complete-0 byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Royalties received
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 4: the gross amount of royalty income received for the royalty property (oil/gas/mineral, copyright, patent, or NIL), entered even if state or local taxes were withheld from oil or gas payments (those withheld taxes are deducted on line 16 / included in /writableRoyaltyExpenses). Consulted only when /claimsRoyaltyIncome is true.

Fact.Name: Royalty ordinary deductible expenses (Schedule E lines 5-19 total, ex-depletion)
Fact.Description:
The total ordinary and necessary deductible expenses for the royalty property (Schedule E lines 5 through 19, summed to line 20), supplied directly as a single input — e.g. taxes withheld by the producer (line 16), management / other professional fees (line 11 / 10), and other ordinary expenses. DEPLETION (line 18) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED and deferred to a follow-on unit (cost vs percentage/15% depletion forks on royalty type). Consulted only when /claimsRoyaltyIncome is true. THE "SCOPED SO THAT INCOME ≥ EXPENSES" CLAIM THIS DESCRIPTION USED TO CARRY IS RETIRED, and it is printed here rather than deleted because it outlived nothing — it was never true. This writable is Min-0 with NO MAXIMUM, so a filer could always type expenses above income, and /royaltyActivityNet has no floor: a probe at income 10,000 / expenses 25,000 reduced /totalIncome by 15,000 with no refusal. From 2026-08-17 a net loss was REFUSED, by /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss.
WHAT IS TRUE NOW, corrected 2026-08-30 on the PROJECT OWNER'S DIRECTION of that date that the at-risk refusal be corrected and BUILT rather than knocked out: an expense figure above income is COMPUTED, not refused. It produces a net loss on Schedule E line 21 that reaches lines 25 and 26 and Schedule 1 line 5, limited under section 465 to /writableRoyaltyAmountAtRisk when the filer answers /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk FALSE, with the disallowed remainder carried out as /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss. The guard is narrowed to the population that has a loss and has not answered that attestation at all. This writable stays Min-0 with no maximum, which is correct: the ceiling is not on the expense, it is on the deductible loss.

Fact.Name: Royalty cost depletion (Schedule E line 18), taxpayer-supplied input
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 18 ("Depreciation expense or depletion"): the COST depletion (§611/§612) for the royalty property, supplied directly as a taxpayer-computed input. Cost depletion is a unit-of-production allowance (adjusted basis ÷ recoverable units × units sold) that needs multi-year basis tracking the single-year engine cannot hold, so the taxpayer computes it EXTERNALLY and enters the result here. Note: ytax now COMPUTES the PERCENTAGE depletion side (/royaltyPercentageDepletion, 15% for oil/gas/geothermal); /royaltyNetIncome deducts the GREATER of this cost input and that computed percentage figure, the depletion being non-elective (Pub 5652 §VII.D.10(8)). A separate line-18 deduction beyond the ordinary deductible expenses in /writableRoyaltyExpenses (lines 5-19 ex-depletion). Complete-safe: 0 / unanswered ⇒ greater-of falls back to the percentage figure (or 0). Consulted only when /claimsRoyaltyIncome is true. SINCE THE ROYALTY SECTION 465 AT-RISK GATE WAS BUILT, a cost-depletion figure that drives the activity to a loss is COMPUTED — the loss reaches Schedule E lines 21, 25 and 26, capped at the amount at risk when the filer says some investment is not at risk. The node test boundary-royalty-cost-depletion-drives-the-loss is the case that exercises this input on the loss side.

Fact.Name: Royalty is an oil, gas, or geothermal property (eligible for 15% percentage depletion)
Fact.Description: Whether the royalty property is an oil, gas, or geothermal deposit — the property classes eligible for PERCENTAGE depletion at the 15% rate (IRC §613A(c)(1); geothermal per §613(e)). Copyright, patent, and name-image-likeness (NIL) royalties are NOT depletable natural resources and get no percentage depletion (only cost recovery / amortization). When true, /royaltyPercentageDepletion computes 15% of gross royalty income (capped at net property income), and the depletion deducted on Schedule E line 18 is the GREATER of that and any taxpayer-supplied cost depletion (/writableRoyaltyDepletion). Absent/false ⇒ no percentage depletion. Consulted only when /claimsRoyaltyIncome is true.

Fact.Name: Royalty percentage depletion (15% of gross, capped at net property income) — Schedule E line 18
Fact.Description:
The percentage-depletion deduction for an oil/gas/geothermal royalty (Schedule E line 18): 15% of gross royalty income (IRC §613A(c)(1)), capped at /royaltyPercentageDepletionPropertyIncomeCap — 100% of net property income (gross royalty − ordinary expenses ex-depletion, §613(a)) for oil and gas, 50% for a geothermal deposit (§613(e)(2)) — floored at 0. Gated on /claimsRoyaltyIncome AND /writableRoyaltyIsOilGasGeothermal — complete-safe 0 when the royalty is not oil/gas/geothermal or none is claimed, so every non-oil/gas scenario keeps /royaltyNetIncome byte-identical. This is the PERCENTAGE side; /royaltyNetIncome deducts the GREATER of this and the taxpayer-supplied cost depletion (/writableRoyaltyDepletion), the deduction being non-elective (Pub 5652 §VII.D.10(8)). The 65%-of-taxable-income cap (§613A(d)(1)) + carryforward is deferred (multi-year state). Result rounded to whole dollars.
The percentage amount below is the pre-§613A(d)(1) operand. The 65% cap itself is a return-level taxable-income circularity, not a multi-year computation; only the disallowed-amount carryforward requires multi-year state. The pre-cap amount and the corresponding line-18/pre-depletion operands are exported under explicitly named facts below. No §613A cap is applied here; /royaltyIsGeothermal now separates a geothermal deposit, which takes the §613(a) 50% limit and is outside §613A.

Fact.Name: Royalty taxable income from the property before depletion
Fact.Description: Gross royalty income less the ordinary royalty expenses, before any depletion: the taxable income from the property that the IRC 613(a) percentage-depletion limit is measured against. Can be negative; every reader floors the depletion result, not this operand.

Fact.Name: Percentage-depletion limit on the taxable income from the royalty property
Fact.Description: The IRC 613(a) limit on percentage depletion: 100 percent of /royaltyNetPropertyIncomeBeforeDepletion for an oil and gas property, and 50 percent for a geothermal deposit, which IRC 613(e)(2) says shall in no case be treated as a gas well. The geothermal arm applies when /writableRoyaltyIsGeothermal is answered Yes. Unanswered or No keeps the 100 percent limit.

Fact.Name: The oil, gas or geothermal royalty is a geothermal deposit
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked when /writableRoyaltyIsOilGasGeothermal is Yes: is this royalty from a geothermal deposit (natural heat stored in rock, water or steam) rather than an oil or gas well? Both get percentage depletion at 15 percent of gross income, but the deduction for a geothermal deposit cannot be more than 50 percent of the taxable income from the property, while an oil or gas property's limit is 100 percent. Unanswered is read as oil or gas, the limit this return applied before the question existed.

Fact.Name: The percentage-depletion royalty is a geothermal deposit (complete safe)
Fact.Description: True only when /royaltyIsOilGasGeothermalCompleteSafe is true and /writableRoyaltyIsGeothermal is answered Yes; false otherwise, including unanswered.

Fact.Name: Royalty percentage depletion before the separate §613A(d)(1) taxable-income limit
Fact.Description: The existing Schedule E percentage-depletion result from /royaltyPercentageDepletion, exported under an explicit name for the §613A(d)(1) shadow taxable-income successor. It retains the §613(a) limit on the taxable income from the property (100% for oil and gas, 50% for a geothermal deposit) and the 15% rate. No 65%-of-taxable-income limit is applied in this Schedule E-only fact. The fact is not itself a final §613A-eligible amount: a geothermal deposit (/royaltyIsGeothermal) is outside §613A, so the successor must exclude it before applying the 65% cap.

Fact.Name: Modeled Schedule E line 18 depletion before the §613A(d)(1) taxable-income limit
Fact.Description: The larger of the scalar royalty's cost-depletion input and its §613(a)-limited percentage-depletion amount, before the separate §613A(d)(1) taxable-income limit. The complete-safe cost-input arm is $0 when unanswered, matching /royaltyActivityNet. This is an operand for a later shadow calculation, not a claim that the return-level cap or multi-year disallowed-depletion carryforward is complete. K-1 royalties and their underlying property depletion are not represented by this scalar line-18 amount.

Fact.Name: Modeled Schedule E royalty net before its scalar property's depletion deduction
Fact.Description: /royaltyActivityNet plus /royaltyLine18DepletionBeforeSection613AIncomeLimit: the current modeled royalty line-21 net with this scalar property's line-18 depletion added back. It is a pre-depletion operand for a later §613A(d)(1) shadow taxable-income computation, not the taxpayer's final taxable income. K-1 royalty boxes remain included as their current pass-through net in /royaltyActivityNet; K-1 property-level depletion and the geothermal/oil-gas classification split are not represented. The future return-level cap therefore needs additional Schedule K-1/property axes and must exclude cost as well as percentage depletion from the statutory base.

Fact.Name: Royalty depletion: the AMT adjustment for Form 6251 line 2d
Fact.Description:
SCREEN SPEC (the application builds this screen from this Description and opens no IRS document).
QUESTION AS ASKED: "Your royalty depletion for the Alternative Minimum Tax. Enter the difference between the depletion you deducted for the regular tax on Schedule E, line 18 and the depletion allowed for the Alternative Minimum Tax. This is the amount that goes on Form 6251, Part I, line 2d. If the AMT depletion is the larger of the two, enter the difference as a negative number."
WHAT THE FILER IS COPYING FROM: not a printed box on a statement she was mailed - this is her OWN royalty property, so the figure is one she or her preparer computes. The two numbers it is built from are one she can read off her own return and one she must refigure: the REGULAR-TAX depletion is the amount printed on her Schedule E LINE 18, which is the GREATER OF the cost depletion she entered (/writableRoyaltyDepletion) and the percentage depletion this dictionary computed (/royaltyPercentageDepletion) - the deduction is non-elective and /royaltyNetIncome takes the larger of the two, never their sum. The tax destination is Form 6251, Part I, line 2d, "Depletion (difference between regular tax and AMT)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1) - see the RENDER caveat under WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS, which qualifies what the PRINTED 2d box shows today.
HELP TEXT: "For the AMT, your depletion deduction for mines, wells and other natural deposits under section 611 is limited to the property's adjusted basis at the end of the year, refigured for the AMT. Enter the amount by which your regular-tax depletion exceeded that limit. ONE EXCEPTION COVERS MOST FILERS: if you are an independent producer or royalty owner claiming PERCENTAGE depletion for OIL AND GAS wells under section 613A(c), that limit does not apply to you - enter 0. The exception is for oil and gas only; it does NOT cover geothermal deposits, coal, or any other mineral, so if your royalty is one of those the limit applies and you may have an amount to enter here." Paraphrased from the 2025 Instructions for Form 6251, "Line 2d - Depletion" ("Refigure your depletion deduction for the AMT ... your depletion deduction for mines, wells, and other natural deposits under section 611 is limited to the property's adjusted basis at the end of the year, as refigured for the AMT, unless you are an independent producer or royalty owner claiming percentage depletion for oil and gas wells under section 613A(c). Figure this limit separately for each property. ... Enter the difference between the regular tax and AMT deduction. If the AMT deduction is more than the regular tax deduction, enter the difference as a negative amount."); https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i6251.pdf, page 3.
ASKED WHEN: /royaltyReportedOnScheduleE is true - that is, the return claims royalty income (/claimsRoyaltyIncome) AND the royalty is NOT an oil-or-gas working interest (/royaltyIsNotWorkingInterest). The working-interest filer is not asked, and the block comment above this fact states why in full: her section 57(a)(1) answer would be $0 by the 613A(c) carve-out, but her return still carries the section 57(a)(2) intangible drilling cost preference (Form 6251 line 2t), for which this dictionary holds no SOURCE-SIDE intake - only the filer-typed whole-line attestation form6251:/writableAmtLine2tIntangibleDrillingCosts, and a blank attestation is not an attestation of absence - so a 57(a)(1) answer alone could not release her from form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference and asking would be a question with no consequence. A follow-on unit that pairs a 57(a)(1) question with a "was the source answered" predicate over that attestation WOULD release her; it is buildable today and is not foreclosed.
UNANSWERED POSTURE: BLANK ON THE RETURN, and the return is still REFUSED for the prior-year-minimum-tax-credit claimant. /royaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment resolves a Complete $0 when this is unanswered, so Form 6251 line 2d and AMTI are exactly what they were before this field existed and no committed scenario moves. The refusal is the point: /royaltyMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems stays TRUE while this is unanswered, so arm 1 of form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference keeps blocking submission for the MTC claimant who holds a royalty. An unanswered field is NOT read as "no preference" - a blank royalty AMT box is exactly the state this dictionary cannot distinguish from an unstated one, which is the coarser-instrument trap the Schedule C absence attestation already records.
VALIDATION: Dollar. SIGNED - no Min and no Max, deliberately. Section 57(a)(1) itself is an excess and cannot be negative, but the PRINTED LINE 2d is a difference between a regular-tax figure and an AMT figure and the instruction says in terms to enter a negative when the AMT deduction is the larger (a taxpayer whose AMT-refigured section 613(a) taxable-income-from-the-property limit is higher than the regular-tax one has exactly that case). Flooring this at $0 would silently delete a legitimate AMTI REDUCTION, which is taxpayer-adverse. This matches the sign posture of the K-1 siblings form6251:/formK1s/*/amtDepletionAdjustmentFromThisK1 and form6251:/formK1s/*/amtDepreciationAfter1986FromThisK1, both "SIGNED, no floor" for the same printed reason. Whole dollars; no cents expected.
WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: /royaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment (the complete-safe wrapper), which form6251:/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment adds to the Schedule K-1 box 17 / box 15 code C rows to make Form 6251 Part I line 2d, a summand of form6251:/amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold and thus of alternative minimum taxable income. It ALSO answers /royaltyAmtDepletionAnswered, which demotes the filer-typed whole-line attestation form6251:/writableAmtLine2dDepletionAdjustment to a fallback so the same money is never stated twice, and drives /royaltyMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems, which narrows arm 1 of form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference.
INTERACTION THE APPLICATION MUST HANDLE: answering this field DEMOTES the whole-line attestation form6251:/writableAmtLine2dDepletionAdjustment COMPLETELY - the typed amount is discarded, not netted. A filer who typed the whole line because it covered this royalty AND a depletion difference this dictionary does not surface separately (Schedule C, farm rental, a partnership figure) would silently lose that other component. Either suppress the whole-line screen once this is answered, or reword it as "any OTHER depletion difference, not counting the royalty amount you already gave us". The same caveat applies to the Schedule K-1 box 17 / box 15 code C slots, which demote it the same way; this unit did not create that behaviour but it does enlarge the population that meets it.
WHERE THE MONEY ACTUALLY LANDS, AND A RENDER CAVEAT. The amount reaches Form 6251 LINE 4, alternative minimum taxable income, through form6251:/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment and form6251:/amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold. The PRINTED line 2d box still renders form6251:/writableAmtLine2dDepletionAdjustment (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS6251/en/configuration.yml, the f1_8[0] row), so a filer who answers this field WITHOUT also typing the whole-line attestation gets the amount inside AMTI and a BLANK printed 2d, and the printed Part I does not foot. That is a PRE-EXISTING render mapping shared by printed lines 2j, 2k and 2l whose boxes point at their attestations while line 4 takes the computed legs. It is dictionary/pdf/ work, outside this unit's grant, and it is HANDED UP rather than fixed here.
NOT A REGULAR-TAX FIGURE. This does not touch /royaltyNetIncome, /royaltyActivityNet, Schedule E line 18 or anything else on the regular return. It exists only for Form 6251. Artifact (3) of the records contract form6251:/amtAdjustmentItemIntakeSurface.

Fact.Name: Was the royalty Form 6251 line 2d field actually answered
Fact.Description:
The "was the source answered" predicate for the royalty AMT depletion adjustment: true exactly when the royalty is reported on Schedule E Part I (/royaltyReportedOnScheduleE, itself All(/claimsRoyaltyIncome, /royaltyIsNotWorkingInterest)) AND /writableRoyaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment has been answered.
IT TESTS THE RAW WRITABLE'S IsComplete AND NEVER /royaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment, which is complete-safe by construction and whose IsComplete is therefore always true - the trap the brief names and the same discipline form6251:/formK1s/*/reportsAmtDepletionAdjustment uses on its own leaves. It is an EXISTENCE test, never a magnitude test, because the line 2d entry is signed: a filer whose AMT depletion exceeds her regular-tax depletion answers a NEGATIVE amount and must select the computed arm exactly as a positive answer does, and an answer of $0 is a real answer ("I checked; the carve-out applies") rather than an absence.
COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: both conjuncts are complete-safe Booleans on this module's existing royalty chain and IsComplete always resolves, so a return that never opened the royalty section, a working-interest return and a partially answered royalty all resolve Complete false rather than Placeholder. Nothing downstream of this can be made Incomplete by it.
CONSUMERS: /royaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment (which arm to take), /royaltyMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems (whether arm 1 of form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference still refuses), and form6251:/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment (whether the filer-typed whole-line attestation form6251:/writableAmtLine2dDepletionAdjustment is demoted to a fallback, so the same money is not stated twice).

Fact.Name: Royalty share of Form 6251 line 2d (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
/writableRoyaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment when /royaltyAmtDepletionAnswered is true, else a Complete $0: this return's ROYALTY share of the Form 6251 Part I line 2d depletion adjustment, "Depletion (difference between regular tax and AMT)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f6251.pdf, page 1).
SIGNED, NO FLOOR, for the reason its writable's Description gives at length: the printed line is a difference and the instruction says to enter a negative when the AMT deduction is the larger. Not rounded here - the filer enters whole dollars and form6251:/amtiWithoutRegardToAtnold rounds the combine.
COMPLETE-SAFE: the Switch's else arm is a literal $0, so this resolves Complete on every return, including one that claims no royalty, one whose royalty is an oil-or-gas working interest and one that left the field blank. That is what lets form6251:/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment add this term unconditionally inside its answered arm without any committed scenario moving: on every return that existed before 2026-09-02 this fact is $0 and the sum is byte-identical.
WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a regular-tax deduction and it touches nothing on Schedule E: /royaltyNetIncome, /royaltyActivityNet, /royaltyPercentageDepletion and /writableRoyaltyDepletion are all unchanged by it. ONE QUANTITY, ONE FACT: this is the royalty leg of line 2d and the ONLY one; the Schedule K-1 legs are form6251:/formK1s/*/amtDepletionAdjustmentFromThisK1 (box 17 / box 15 code C) and the filer-typed whole-line fallback is form6251:/writableAmtLine2dDepletionAdjustment. The three are alternatives and terms, never duplicates: the typed whole-line attestation is DEMOTED whenever this fact's source was answered. Artifact (3) of the records contract form6251:/amtAdjustmentItemIntakeSurface.

Fact.Name: The royalty may still carry an AMT item this dictionary does not model
Fact.Description:
The NARROWING INSTRUMENT for the royalty conjunct of arm 1 of form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference, and the exact sibling of scheduleC:/anyScheduleCMayCarryUnmodeledAmtItems on the Schedule C side. TRUE - keep refusing - unless /royaltyAmtDepletionAnswered is true.
WHAT THE GUARD USED TO SAY AND WHY IT SAID IT. Arm 1 fires on a Form 8801 prior-year minimum tax credit claim beside an intake whose AMT adjustment this dictionary does not model, because Form 8801 line 23 IS Form 6251 line 9: an understated AMTI understates line 23, overstates line 24 and hence the credit, at 26-28 cents per dollar of missing add-back, in exactly the zone where the AMT itself is $0 on both the modeled and the true AMTI. The royalty was on that list for one named reason - the guard's own words, "scheduleE:/claimsRoyaltyIncome (residual (c): section 57(a)(1) percentage depletion, and the oil/gas WORKING-INTEREST fork of the royalty activity rides the same intake)".
WHAT ANSWERING THE FIELD CHANGES. Once /writableRoyaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment is answered, the section 57(a)(1) amount is no longer unmodeled: it is stated by the filer, it reaches Form 6251 line 2d through /royaltyAmtDepletionAdjustment and form6251:/amtLine2dDepletionAdjustment, and it is inside AMTI.
