The understatement arm 1 protects against cannot occur through this intake for that filer, so this fact goes FALSE and the royalty alone no longer holds the arm open.
COMPLETE-SAFE TRUE, and every way of failing to answer keeps today's refusal: a royalty with no AMT answer, an unanswered royalty section, a return in the middle of being filled, and - deliberately - a royalty that IS an oil-or-gas working interest. The working interest keeps refusing not because its section 57(a)(1) answer would be unknown (it is $0 by the section 613A(c) carve-out) but because that activity carries the section 57(a)(2) INTANGIBLE DRILLING COST preference, Form 6251 line 2t, for which this dictionary holds no SOURCE-SIDE intake - only the filer-typed whole-line attestation form6251:/writableAmtLine2tIntangibleDrillingCosts, and a blank attestation is not an attestation of absence, exactly as a blank K-1 box 17 is not. The line 2t attestation ships at form6251:/writableAmtLine2tIntangibleDrillingCosts, reaches AMTI. A follow-on unit pairing a 57(a)(1) question with a "was the source answered" predicate over that attestation would release the working-interest filer, and is NOT foreclosed. Releasing the working-interest MTC claimant on a 57(a)(1) answer alone would be a real World-#1 exposure, and /royaltyReportedOnScheduleE - the gate inside /royaltyAmtDepletionAnswered - is what keeps her held ONCE SHE HAS ATTESTED THE WORKING INTEREST. THE HOLD IS EXACTLY THAT STRONG AND NO STRONGER: /royaltyIsNotWorkingInterest resolves TRUE on every return that never answered /writableRoyaltyIsWorkingInterest, so a filer who simply SKIPS that attestation is treated as a Schedule E royalty owner throughout this module and is asked this question like any other. That is the module's existing posture - the royalty-to-Schedule-C routing depends on the same attestation - and it is not something this unit changes.
THIS IS A NARROWING, NOT A RETIREMENT, and the surviving refusal is named rather than waved at. form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference keeps BOTH arms and keeps refusing the MTC claimant who holds (i) a Schedule C that has not attested absence of the Form 6251 items - residual (b), still open, and the Schedule C depreciation-METHOD detail is artifact (1) of the records contract and NOT this unit's work; (ii) a Schedule K-1 or an estate/trust K-1 - the AMT-item fields for those SHIP (form6251.xml, on the /formK1s and /form1041K1s collections) but a BLANK box 17 / box 15 / box 12 is not an attestation of absence, and codes D and E stay intake-only by design, so narrowing those two conjuncts needs an instrument this unit did not build and hands up; (iii) Form 4835 farm rental, which enters as an attested NET with the same collapse Schedule C has; (iv) a royalty that is an oil-or-gas working interest, per the paragraph above; and (v) everyone arm 2 refuses. The reason for every one of those is still "not modeled", not "not modelable" - the same honest wording the four prior narrowings used.
ONE RELEASED RESIDUE THIS NARROWING DOES NOT COVER, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT. /writableRoyaltyExpenses is "Schedule E lines 5-19 total, ex-depletion", and Schedule E line 18 is captioned "Depreciation expense OR depletion" - only the DEPLETION half is carved out of that writable. So a royalty whose collapsed expense figure contains POST-1986 DEPRECIATION carries a section 56(a)(1) / Form 6251 line 2l adjustment with no intake of its own, and once this fact goes FALSE that filer is released. The population is thin (a pure royalty owner rarely holds depreciable property) and the collapse is pre-existing; it is a named gap. Closing it belongs with the Form 4835 and Schedule C attested-net collapse work, not here.

Fact.Name: The royalty is a working (operating) interest in an oil or gas well
Fact.Description: Whether the royalty activity reported through /writableHasRoyaltyIncome is a WORKING (operating) interest in an oil or gas well that the taxpayer holds directly, or through an entity that does not limit the taxpayer's liability — as opposed to the investment royalty (a non-operating mineral, copyright, patent or NIL interest) the rest of this Part I chain is built for. Answering TRUE re-routes the activity's net off Schedule E line 4 and onto Schedule C, where it becomes self-employment income; the Schedule E line-4 instruction excludes operating interests from that line in terms (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040se.pdf, page 6). Consulted only when /claimsRoyaltyIncome is true. UNANSWERED IS TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR EXACTLY: every royalty is treated as investment royalty, so every committed return is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: The royalty activity is a working interest (complete-safe gate)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate for the working-interest fork: true only when a royalty is claimed AND /writableRoyaltyIsWorkingInterest is answered AND true. The All/IsComplete shape is the one /royaltyPercentageDepletion already uses on this chain, for the same reason — an unanswered attestation must resolve Complete false rather than making its consumers Incomplete. Unanswered or false ⇒ the royalty stays on Schedule E Part I and every downstream value is exactly what it was before this fork existed.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 7 royalties
Fact.Description: This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's royalties: box 7 as recorded (../writableK1065Box7Royalties), or $0 when this item did not answer that box. Complete-safe, so a /formK1s item recorded for its ordinary income alone contributes a Complete $0 and the CollectionSum over the collection stays Complete. NON-NEGATIVE by construction: the box reports GROSS royalties received, which the partner instructions send straight to Schedule E line 4, and line 4 is a gross receipts line with no loss arm.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 4 - the royalties passed through on Schedules K-1
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded Schedule K-1's box 7 royalties, which the partner instructions route to Schedule E line 4 ("Report royalties on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 4"). A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/royaltyIncomeForScheduleE behind an IsComplete guard on the /formK1s collection root, because a CollectionSum over a collection the return never opened does not resolve; a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0.
A SECOND ADDEND, NOT A FALLBACK, and the distinction is the reason this is safe. /writableRoyaltyIncome is the gross royalty of the filer's OWN royalty property (its own Description: "the gross amount of royalty income received for the royalty property (oil/gas/mineral, copyright, patent, or NIL)"), gated behind /claimsRoyaltyIncome and paired with /writableRoyaltyExpenses and /writableRoyaltyDepletion for that one property. A partnership's box 7 royalty is a DIFFERENT activity's receipts, so the two are different money and /royaltyActivityNet adds them rather than choosing between them.
THE TERM SITS OUTSIDE THE /claimsRoyaltyIncome GATE inside /royaltyActivityNet, deliberately and for the reason form4797:/netSection1231GainOrLoss gives for its own line 3, 4 and 5 addends: a partner whose only royalty is a K-1 box 7 amount has no royalty property of their own and would never answer /writableHasRoyaltyIncome, so a term inside the gate would leave exactly the population this fills at $0.
NO DEPLETION AND NO EXPENSES ARE TAKEN AGAINST IT HERE, stated rather than left implied. The line 18 depletion and line 20 expenses this module computes belong to the filer's own royalty property and are measured against /writableRoyaltyIncome; a partner's share of the partnership's royalty deductions arrives on other K-1 boxes (box 13 and box 20) that this dictionary does not read. The figure is therefore an OVER statement of the partner's net royalty by whatever those boxes carry, which is the same posture the module already takes for a K-1 whose deductions it does not model, and it is reported to the lead as a named gap.

Fact.Name: This K-1 is recorded as a partnership Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)
Fact.Description:
True only when ../entityType is ANSWERED and answers partnership. It is the gate every Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 11 code keyed leg in this module fires behind, because /formK1s holds both K-1 layouts and the box 11 code table is the partnership one.
THE SHAPE IS All(IsComplete(../entityType), Equal(../entityType, partnership)) and the IsComplete guard is what makes the flag resolve at all: Equal() over an unanswered Enum is Incomplete, so without the guard every consumer would hang on a K-1 that never recorded its entity type. WITH it the flag is Complete FALSE there, because AllOperator returns Complete(false) as soon as any member is Complete false, head or tail. That reasoning is not new here; it is written out at length on ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership in this same file, which uses the identical shape for its sCorp arm, and this fact deliberately mirrors it.
AN UNANSWERED entityType RESOLVES FALSE, which withholds the leg rather than guessing. "I did not say what kind of K-1 this is" is not a statement that it came from a partnership. The withholding is reported by ../codeSlotAnsweredWithoutEntityType.

Fact.Name: This K-1 is recorded as an S corporation Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)
Fact.Description:
True only when ../entityType is ANSWERED and answers sCorp. The twin of ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership, and the gate every Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 10 code keyed leg in this module fires behind. Same All(IsComplete, Equal) shape and same reason: an unanswered entityType resolves Complete FALSE and withholds the leg instead of guessing.
THE TWO FLAGS ARE NOT COMPLEMENTS, deliberately. Both are FALSE on a K-1 whose entity type was never recorded, so a code row answered on such a K-1 is read by NEITHER code table. That is the whole point: /k1EntityTypeOptions offers exactly two options, but the field is three state, and the third state is "unrecorded", not "the other one".

Fact.Name: DIAGNOSTIC: this K-1 answered an other income code slot but never recorded its entity type
Fact.Description:
DIAGNOSTIC, NOT A REFUSAL AND NOT A TAX FIGURE. True when this K-1 answered at least one row of the "other income (loss)" coded box (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 11, which the Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 10 share, plus the 1120-S box 10) AND ../entityType is UNANSWERED.
WHY IT EXISTS. The two instruction books disagree about what those letters mean. Code E is cancellation of debt on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), which the partner instructions route to Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8c, and section 951A(a) GILTI on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S), which the shareholder instructions route to no named line at all. Because the two layouts share one row list, a code letter alone cannot say which table to read. The standing policy is that a code keyed leg fires only on an ANSWERED entity type, so on the population this flag identifies EVERY code keyed leg in this cluster is WITHHELD: the amount stays a faithful record of the printed document and reaches no line. That is deliberately an under statement of income rather than a guess at the wrong line, and this fact is how the graph says so out loud instead of failing silently.
SCOPE, and it is narrow on purpose. Only this one coded box is covered. The other coded K-1 boxes this dictionary reads (Form 1065 box 13 with Form 1120-S box 12, box 18 with box 16, box 20 with box 17) have code tables that AGREE letter for letter on every code routed, so the legs over them run ungated and a return with an unanswered entity type computes them correctly. Extending this flag over those boxes would flag returns that have nothing wrong with them.
WHAT THE LEAD MUST DECIDE. Whether the withheld population deserves a knockout instead. It is not one today, and a unit does not mint one on its own.

Fact.Name: DIAGNOSTIC: some recorded K-1 answered an other income code slot with no entity type
Fact.Description:
True when at least one recorded /formK1s item is flagged by /formK1s/*/codeSlotAnsweredWithoutEntityType, i.e. when this return carries a Schedule K-1 whose box 11 (or Form 1120-S box 10) code rows were transcribed but whose entity type was never recorded, so every code keyed leg over that document is withheld.
Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s COLLECTION ROOT, the idiom /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities and scheduleD:/collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered use over this same collection, because a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete. A return with no K-1 reads Complete false.
IT DOES NOT BLOCK SUBMISSION. It is exported for the lead, who owns the decision whether the withheld population should be refused instead of quietly under stated. OPERATOR RULING: this STAYS a diagnostic, not a refusal - the withheld legs only under-state on an incoherent intake state, and the fix is the application screen ordering (entity type asked before the code rows), not a knockout.

Fact.Name: This K-1's other income code A amount, for Schedule E line 38 column (d)
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1's code A "other portfolio income (loss)" amount from the other income coded box, routed to the Schedule E (Form 1040) Part IV line 38 column (d) REMIC taxable income column. SIGNED and with no floor: the printed column (d) caption is "Taxable income (net loss)" and the box itself is "other income (LOSS)", so a negative row is a real negative term.
TWO ARMS PER ROW, WRITTEN PER CODE TABLE. Each row of ../otherIncomeEntries is read by ../otherIncomeEntries/*/otherPortfolioIncomeForRemicColumnDFromThisRow twice, once behind ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership reading the Form 1065 box 11 table and once behind ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp reading the Form 1120-S box 10 table. The two flags are mutually exclusive, so no row can contribute twice. The two tables happen to AGREE on code A (both books print the identical REMIC paragraph), so the two arms have the same destination today; they are still written separately, because that is what makes the leg survive a future divergence and what makes the lead's answered entity type policy visible in the XML rather than only in prose.
COMPLETE SAFE: a row contributes only when its CODE and its AMOUNT are both answered, the code is A, and the entity type is answered; otherwise the Switch tail gives $0. A K-1 that answered no row, or answered rows without an entity type, contributes a Complete $0.
THE DESTINATION, and the residual it leaves. Both instruction books say the same thing about code A: the entity "will report portfolio income other than interest, ordinary dividend, royalty, and capital gain (loss) income", and then, "if the partnership held a residual interest in a real estate mortgage investment conduit (REMIC), it'll report on the statement your share of REMIC taxable income (net loss) that you report in column (d) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 38". Column (d) is the ONLY line number either book names for a code A amount. THE RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: a code A amount from an entity that held NO REMIC residual interest is ordinary other portfolio income whose destination is a Schedule 1 line 8z write in, not Schedule E line 38, and the split between the two lives in an attached STATEMENT that no intake in this dictionary collects. Routing all of code A to column (d) is therefore right on the line number only for the REMIC half. It is taken anyway because the magnitude reaching Form 1040 total income is the SAME either way: Schedule E line 39 feeds line 41, which feeds Schedule 1 line 5, and Schedule 1 line 8z feeds Schedule 1 line 9; both land in Schedule 1 line 10 and Form 1040 line 8. Only the printed line differs, and $0 (the status quo before this fact) is wrong by the whole amount. Flagged for the lead as a REVIEW item: if the lead prefers, this leg is demoted to reference only by deleting the Dependency that /scheduleERemicResidualNet takes on /k1RemicColumnDTaxableIncome.
COLUMN (c) IS NOT A DESTINATION HERE, deliberately. The same paragraph routes the entity's share of any "excess inclusion" to column (c), but a code A row carries ONE number and the column (c) share arrives on the same unread statement. /writableRemicExcessInclusion, which is column (c), is untouched by this leg, and Schedule E line 39 excludes column (c) anyway by the form's own instruction. Summed over the collection by /k1RemicColumnDTaxableIncome.

Fact.Name: This K-1's other income code A amount, for Schedule E line 38 column (d): this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/otherIncomeEntries as /formK1s/*/k1OtherPortfolioIncomeForRemicColumnD reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is A and both the code and the amount are answered, read on the code table of the K-1's answered entity type (one arm behind /formK1s/*/k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership, one behind /formK1s/*/k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp; the two flags are mutually exclusive, so a row contributes at most once); otherwise $0. Complete on every row.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 38 column (d) - the REMIC taxable income passed through on Schedules K-1
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded Schedule K-1's code A other portfolio income, the amount both instruction books route to column (d) of Schedule E (Form 1040) line 38. A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/k1OtherPortfolioIncomeForRemicColumnD behind an IsComplete guard on the /formK1s collection root, because a CollectionSum over a collection the return never opened does not resolve; a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0. UNROUNDED: it is a term of /scheduleERemicResidualNet, which rounds once at the top, the shape interest:/k1TaxExemptInterest uses inside /taxExemptInterest.
A SECOND ADDEND OF LINE 39, OUTSIDE THE /claimsRemicResidualInterest GATE, and that placement is the load bearing choice. /writableRemicResidualNet and the two printed column intakes describe the filer's OWN Schedules Q; a partner or shareholder whose only REMIC exposure is the pass through has no Schedule Q of their own and would never answer /writableClaimsRemicResidualInterest, so a term inside the gate would leave exactly the population this fills at $0. It is the same argument /k1RoyaltyIncomeTotal makes for sitting outside /claimsRoyaltyIncome, and the same one form4797:/netSection1231GainOrLoss makes for its line 3, 4 and 5 addends. It is NOT put inside /remicColumnsDAndENet, which sits behind BOTH that gate and /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered and would strand the leg on every K-1 only return.
A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING so it is not read as a defect: on a K-1 only return, Schedule E line 39 now prints a figure while the line 38 columns above it print nothing, because line 38 is a per REMIC table this dictionary fills only from the filer's own Schedules Q. The same foot mismatch already exists for the K-1 royalties on line 4 and is the accepted posture of this module: the computed total is right and the detail table is short.
Complete safe, and no committed value moves. Every term is $0 unless a K-1 answers a code A row AND records its entity type, and no committed fixture or scenario answers /formK1s/*/entityType on a K-1 that also answers a box 11 or box 10 code row.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 11 code E cancellation of debt (Schedule 1 line 8c)
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1's cancellation of debt income: the total of the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 11 rows whose printed letter code is E, which the partner instructions route to Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8c ("Generally, this cancellation of debt (COD) amount is included in your gross income (Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8c)").
PARTNERSHIP ONLY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THIS FACT. The rows are read only behind ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership. Code E on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 10 is NOT cancellation of debt at all: it is a section 951A(a) GILTI inclusion, and the 1120-S box 10 code table contains no cancellation of debt code anywhere. Because the two layouts share one row list (../otherIncomeEntries), an ungated code E leg would route an S corporation shareholder's GILTI to Schedule 1 line 8c, which is the wrong line and the wrong character of income. A K-1 whose entity type is unanswered contributes $0 and is reported by ../codeSlotAnsweredWithoutEntityType.
COMPLETE SAFE: a row contributes only when its code and its amount are both answered, the code is E, and the entity type answers partnership; otherwise $0. NO FLOOR: the box is "other income (loss)" and the instructions print no sign rule for the row, so the recorded figure is taken as transcribed. Cancellation of debt income is gross income under IRC 61(a)(11); the section 108 exclusions and the section 108(b)(5) basis reduction election the code E paragraph mentions are NOT modelled by this leg and are a named gap: a partner who qualifies for an exclusion has no way here to say so, so this figure is the pre exclusion amount the K-1 printed. Summed over the collection by /k1CancellationOfDebtTotal.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 11 code E cancellation of debt (Schedule 1 line 8c): this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/otherIncomeEntries as /formK1s/*/k1CancellationOfDebtIncome reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is E, both the code and the amount are answered and only when /formK1s/*/k1EntityTypeAnsweredPartnership holds; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8c - the cancellation of debt passed through on Schedules K-1 (Form 1065)
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded partnership Schedule K-1's box 11 code E cancellation of debt. A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/k1CancellationOfDebtIncome behind an IsComplete guard on the /formK1s collection root, so a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0. Rounded once here, because its consumer is a Schedule 1 line and not another Round.
ITS CONSUMER LIVES IN ANOTHER MODULE AND IS NOT WIRED BY THIS UNIT. Schedule 1 line 8c is income:/schedule1Line8cIncomeOrZero (the complete safe wrapper over income:/writableSchedule1Line8cCancellationOfDebt), and income.xml belongs to a different author this round. This fact carries an Export so it is reachable, and the one line Add that must be made in income.xml is owed in income.xml. UNTIL THAT ADD LANDS the amount is recorded and totalled but reaches no printed line, which is the same posture the module already takes for a figure whose destination is another owner's file.
A SECOND ADDEND, NOT A FALLBACK, when it does land. income:/writableSchedule1Line8cCancellationOfDebt is the filer's own attested canceled debt (a Form 1099-C the filer received); a partnership's box 11 code E share is different money on a different document, so line 8c adds them rather than choosing between them. The scope carve that keeps the two from overlapping has to be written on the income.xml writable, and is requested in the report.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 10 code E section 951A(a) GILTI inclusion (Schedule 1 line 8o)
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)'s section 951A(a) inclusion: the total of the box 10 rows whose printed letter code is E. Global intangible low taxed income, the inclusion a United States shareholder of a controlled foreign corporation takes into income.
S CORPORATION ONLY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. Every row of ../otherIncomeEntries is read, but only behind ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp. Code E on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 11 is CANCELLATION OF DEBT, an entirely different item with an entirely different line, and the two boxes share one row list, so an ungated code E leg would send a partner's COD to Schedule 1 line 8o. /formK1s/*/k1CancellationOfDebtIncome is the mirror image of this fact and reads the same rows behind the partnership flag; between them the two legs partition the rows and neither can fire on a K-1 whose entity type is unanswered.
THE DESTINATION IS A LINE THE FORM NAMES, NOT A GUESS, and the reasoning is worth stating because the shareholder instructions do not name it. They say only "Report this amount on your Form 1040, Form 1040-SR, or relevant income tax return". Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 8o IS the printed line for a section 951A(a) inclusion — income:/writableSchedule1Line8oSection951AInclusion carries exactly that caption — so the quantity and the line match one to one. Line 8n, the section 951(a) inclusion, is a DIFFERENT line and the two "are not interchangeable" (that writable's own Description); codes F and G go there through /formK1s/*/k1Section951Inclusion instead.
COMPLETE SAFE: a row contributes only when its code and its amount are both answered, the code is E, and the entity type answers sCorp; otherwise $0.
A DISCLOSED OVERLAP RISK, since line 8o already has an attestation. A shareholder who typed their GILTI on income:/writableSchedule1Line8oSection951AInclusion AND recorded the K-1 box 10 code E row would state the same money twice once the income.xml Add lands. The scope carve that closes it has to be written on the income.xml writable, and is requested there. Summed by /k1Section951AInclusionTotal.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 10 code E section 951A(a) GILTI inclusion (Schedule 1 line 8o): this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/otherIncomeEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Section951AInclusion reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is E, both the code and the amount are answered and only when /formK1s/*/k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp holds; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8o - the GILTI passed through on Schedules K-1 (Form 1120-S)
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded S corporation Schedule K-1's box 10 code E section 951A(a) inclusion. A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/k1Section951AInclusion behind an IsComplete guard on the /formK1s collection root, so a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0. Rounded once here, because its consumer is a Schedule 1 line.
ITS CONSUMER LIVES IN income.xml AND IS NOT WIRED BY THIS UNIT: Schedule 1 line 8o is income:/schedule1Line8oIncomeOrZero, another module's file. The Export makes this fact reachable and the one line Add is owed there. Until it lands the amount is recorded and totalled but reaches no printed line.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 10 code F and code G section 951(a) inclusions (Schedule 1 line 8n)
Fact.Description:
THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)'s section 951(a) inclusions: the total of the box 10 rows coded F (inclusions of subpart F income, section 951(a)(1)(A)) or G (section 951(a)(1)(B) inclusions). ONE fact for the two codes because they are one printed Schedule 1 line between them — line 8n is captioned "Section 951(a) inclusion" and both codes are section 951(a) inclusions — and because the module's rule is one quantity, one fact.
S CORPORATION ONLY, behind ../k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp, for the same reason every leg in this cluster is gated: rows are shared with the Form 1065 box 11 leaves, where code F means "section 743(b) positive income adjustments" and codes G and H are reserved for future use. An ungated leg would read a partner's section 743(b) adjustment as a subpart F inclusion.
THE LINE IS MATCHED ON THE CAPTION, as it is for the GILTI twin: the shareholder instructions say only "Report this amount on your Form 1040, Form 1040-SR, or relevant income tax return", and Schedule 1 line 8n is the printed line for a section 951(a) inclusion. THE CAUTION THE BOOK PRINTS IS NOT MODELLED and is a named gap: where Regulations section 1.958-1(d) applies the corporation provides no box 10 code F or G at all and puts the information in Part V of Schedule K-3 instead, which this dictionary does not read; and income:/writableSchedule1Line8nSection951Inclusion notes that a filer who made a section 962 election reports tax on Form 1040 line 16 rather than entering the inclusion here, a fork this leg does not enforce either.
COMPLETE SAFE, and the same disclosed overlap with the line 8n attestation that the GILTI leg has with line 8o. Summed by /k1Section951InclusionTotal.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 10 code F and code G section 951(a) inclusions (Schedule 1 line 8n): this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/otherIncomeEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Section951Inclusion reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is F or G, both the code and the amount are answered and only when /formK1s/*/k1EntityTypeAnsweredSCorp holds; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Schedule 1 line 8n - the section 951(a) inclusions passed through on Schedules K-1 (Form 1120-S)
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded S corporation Schedule K-1's box 10 code F and code G section 951(a) inclusions. A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/k1Section951Inclusion behind an IsComplete guard on the /formK1s collection root, so a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0. Rounded once here.
ITS CONSUMER LIVES IN income.xml AND IS NOT WIRED BY THIS UNIT: Schedule 1 line 8n is income:/schedule1Line8nIncomeOrZero, another module's file. The Export makes this fact reachable and the one line Add is owed there.

Fact.Name: The royalty activity's net, before the working-interest routing fork
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 4 (/writableRoyaltyIncome) minus the line-20 ordinary deductible expenses (/writableRoyaltyExpenses) minus the line-18 depletion deduction (the GREATER of the taxpayer-supplied cost depletion /writableRoyaltyDepletion and the computed /royaltyPercentageDepletion, non-elective per Pub 5652 §VII.D.10(8)). Complete-safe: 0 when no royalty is claimed.
A SECOND INCOME TERM JOINS THIS FACT. /k1RoyaltyIncomeTotal, the Schedule K-1 box 7 royalties the partner instructions route to Schedule E line 4, is added OUTSIDE the /claimsRoyaltyIncome gate, because a partner whose only royalty is a pass through never answers /writableHasRoyaltyIncome and a term inside the gate would leave that population at $0. It is complete safe and non negative, so every committed scenario stays byte-identical and the fork identity below still holds: /royaltyNetIncome + /workingInterestNetProfit still equals this fact, now over a base that includes the K-1 royalties.
THIS IS THE FORMER BODY OF /royaltyNetIncome, MOVED UNCHANGED, and that is the point: it is the single figure the fork routes, so /royaltyNetIncome + /workingInterestNetProfit equals this fact on every return. Splitting it out is what makes "the working-interest fill is a RE-ROUTE, not a re-computation" a structural property rather than a claim — nothing here can drift away from what Schedule E used to report. Result rounded to whole dollars, at the same place in the tree the Round sat before the split.
THE FORK NO LONGER READS THIS FACT DIRECTLY. The section 465 at-risk cap now sits between this fact and the fork, on /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet, so the conservation identity stated above moves one step down and reads /royaltyNetIncome + /workingInterestNetProfit == /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet. The difference between the two is exactly /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss, the section 465(a)(2) carryover, which is REPORTED rather than lost. This fact is unchanged and is still the PRE-limitation figure - Schedule E line 21 before Form 6198 - which is why the cap chain and /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss both keep testing it. Built on the project owner's direction of 2026-08-30: the at-risk refusal should not be a knockout, it should be corrected and built.

Fact.Name: All amounts invested in the royalty activity are at risk (the Form 6198 gate)
Fact.Description:
The section 465 attestation for the royalty activity: TRUE means every amount invested in the activity is at risk, so no Form 6198 is needed and a royalty loss is deductible in full; FALSE means some investment is not at risk, which makes the amount at risk (/writableRoyaltyAmountAtRisk, the Form 6198 Part II line 10b simplified single input) cap the deductible loss. It is the negation of the second bullet in the Schedule E line 21 instruction ("Amounts in the activity for which you are not at risk"), and it is the Schedule C line 32a checkbox in Part I clothing.
BUILT 2026-08-30 on the PROJECT OWNER'S DIRECTION of the same date: the at-risk refusal "should not be a knockout, correct it and build it". It takes the gating shape: one quantity, one fact. form4835's print only pair (/writableForm4835AllInvestmentAtRisk with /form4835SomeInvestmentNotAtRisk) is the outlier the project owner still owes a ruling on; nothing here reads it and nothing here changes it.
WHAT UNANSWERED MEANS, and it is deliberately NOT the scheduleF answer. Mechanically the gate below resolves FALSE when this is unanswered, so no limitation runs and every existing return is untouched. But an unanswered attestation on a return that HAS a royalty loss is not a filer saying "I am fully at risk", it is a filer who was never asked - so /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss is narrowed rather than retired, to fire ONLY on that population (a royalty loss with this Boolean still unanswered). Answering it, either way, is what frees the return. The narrowing is the lead's edit, not this unit's.
interpretation:provisional. Full Form 6198 (Parts I and III, the mid year changes, the recapture in section 465(e)) is not modelled here, exactly as on all five sibling instances.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk in the royalty activity (Form 6198 Part II line 10b)
Fact.Description:
The filer's amount at risk in the royalty activity from the SIMPLIFIED computation (Form 6198 Part II line 10b), supplied as a single input. Consulted ONLY when /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk is answered AND false. Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/amountAtRisk, /formK1s/*/amountAtRisk, /writableEstateTrustAmountAtRisk, scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/writableAmountAtRisk and scheduleF:/writableScheduleFAmountAtRisk; the line by line Part II build and the detailed Part III are not modelled there and here.
BUILT 2026-08-30 on the PROJECT OWNER'S DIRECTION of the same date that the at-risk refusal be corrected and built rather than kept as a knockout. A filer who answers the attestation FALSE and leaves this blank leaves /royaltyAtRiskDeductibleLoss Incomplete, which is the family's prompt posture and not a refusal: the form asks for the figure and the return waits for it. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The section 465 at-risk limitation applies to the royalty activity's loss
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk is answered AND false - the filer said some investment is not at risk, so the amount at risk caps the deductible loss. When the attestation is answered true OR is unanswered this resolves false and NO limitation applies. The inverted IsComplete guard, mirroring /rentalProperties/*/atRiskLimitationApplies, /formK1s/*/atRiskLimitationApplies, scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/atRiskLimitationApplies and scheduleF:/scheduleFAtRiskLimitationApplies. Built on the owner's direction to correct and build the at-risk refusal rather than keep it as a knockout.

Fact.Name: Royalty activity loss before the at-risk limitation, as a positive amount (Form 6198 line 5)
Fact.Description: The royalty activity's current year loss as a POSITIVE magnitude: the absolute value of /royaltyActivityNet when that is negative, and $0 otherwise. It is the input to the Form 6198 line 21 smaller of test, which is stated in positive terms ("treat the loss on line 5 as a positive number"). Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/rawLoss and scheduleF:/scheduleFRawLoss. Complete safe: $0 on every profit or breakeven return, which is every committed scenario. Built 2026-08-30 on the project owner's direction of the same date to correct and build the at-risk refusal.

Fact.Name: Royalty at-risk-allowed (deductible) loss (Form 6198 line 21)
Fact.Description:
The royalty activity's loss allowed under the section 465 at-risk rules (Form 6198 Part IV line 21): the SMALLER of the line 5 loss (/royaltyRawLoss) and the line 20 amount at risk (/writableRoyaltyAmountAtRisk) - but ONLY when the limitation applies (/royaltyAtRiskLimitationApplies). When the filer is fully at risk, OR has not answered the attestation, this equals the full raw loss and nothing is capped. Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/atRiskDeductibleLoss, whose published i6198 line 21 examples fix the arithmetic: (a) loss $400, amount at risk $1,000 gives $400; (b) loss $1,600, amount at risk $1,200 gives $1,200; (c) loss $800, amount at risk $0 gives $0.
WHEN THE LIMITATION APPLIES AND THE AMOUNT AT RISK IS BLANK this is Incomplete, on purpose: the filer told the return that some investment is not at risk and the form then asks for the figure. That is the same posture /rentalProperties/*/atRiskDeductibleLoss and scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss take, and it is a prompt, not a refusal. Built 2026-08-30 on the project owner's direction of the same date to correct and build the at-risk refusal rather than keep it as a knockout.

Fact.Name: Royalty loss suspended by the §465 at-risk rules (carryover, output only)
Fact.Description:
The royalty activity loss DISALLOWED for 2025 by the section 465 at-risk limitation = /royaltyRawLoss minus /royaltyAtRiskDeductibleLoss (Form 6198 line 5 minus line 21). Under section 465(a)(2) it is treated as a deduction allocable to the activity in the first succeeding taxable year; this single year demo REPORTS it and does NOT apply it to a future year, exactly as /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss and /rentalProperties/*/atRiskSuspendedLoss do for the rental side. DISTINCT from any section 469 passive suspended loss: royalty income is portfolio income and Form 8582 is not completed for royalty properties.
$0 on every profit or breakeven return and whenever the filer is fully at risk or has not answered the attestation, so every committed scenario carries $0 here. It covers BOTH arms of the fork, because the cap it records is applied to /royaltyActivityNet before the working interest split. Export only: nothing in the fact graph reads it, which is the same posture /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss and /rentalNonActiveSuspendedLoss take for their carryovers. Built 2026-08-30 on the project owner's direction of the same date to correct and build the at-risk refusal rather than keep it as a knockout.

Fact.Name: The royalty activity's net after the §465 at-risk limitation, signed, before the working-interest fork
Fact.Description:
The royalty activity's SIGNED net AFTER the section 465 at-risk limitation, and the figure the working interest fork now routes: when /royaltyActivityNet is a profit or breakeven this is that amount unchanged; when it is a loss this is the at-risk allowed loss expressed as a NEGATIVE amount (minus /royaltyAtRiskDeductibleLoss). The suspended remainder (/royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss) is excluded and carried out instead. Mirrors /rentalProperties/*/atRiskAllowedNet and scheduleF:/scheduleFNetProfitOrLoss's loss arm. The cap can only SHRINK the magnitude of a loss; it can never turn a loss into a profit and it never touches a profit at all, which is what the Form 6198 line 21 TIP and the Schedule F line 36 TIP both say in their own words.
THE CONSERVATION IDENTITY MOVES ONE STEP DOWN AND STILL HOLDS: /royaltyNetIncome + /workingInterestNetProfit == THIS FACT, on every return. It used to be stated against /royaltyActivityNet, and the difference between the two is exactly /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss - which is reported, not lost. Putting the cap HERE, before the fork, is what stops a working interest loss from reaching scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit uncapped: that Dependency joins OUTSIDE the /scheduleCs collection, after /scheduleCs/*/atRiskLimitationApplies has already run, so a royalty side cap applied any later would leave the section 465 machinery scheduleC ships bypassed on that arm.
COMPLETE SAFE: when the attestation is unanswered /royaltyAtRiskLimitationApplies is false, /royaltyAtRiskDeductibleLoss is the full raw loss, and this equals /royaltyActivityNet exactly - so no committed scenario moves. Built on the owner's direction: the at-risk refusal should not be a knockout, it should be corrected and built.

Fact.Name: Working-interest oil/gas net profit routed to Schedule C (line 31 / Schedule SE line 2)
Fact.Description:
The working-interest half of the fork: /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet when the activity is a working interest in an oil or gas well, else $0. Consumed by scheduleC as a SECOND Schedule C business's line 31 — combined into /scheduleCNetProfit (Schedule 1 line 3) and into /primaryFilerScheduleCNetProfit (that filer's Schedule SE line 2), which is what finally subjects the activity to self-employment tax.
WHY IT JOINS AT LINE 31 AND NOT AT LINE 29, the choice the coupled contract asked the fill to make and state. Line 29 was the contract's first-named shape, and it is the wrong one: Schedule C line 29 is the gross-income limitation base for the home-office deduction and the figure the §465 at-risk cap measures, so folding an unrelated activity into it would widen ANOTHER business's home-office allowance and blend two activities' at-risk postures. Joining at line 31 is also the more form-faithful reading the contract offered as the alternative: a second trade or business files its own Schedule C, and it is the two line 31s that combine at Schedule 1 line 3 and Schedule SE line 2.
THE SOURCE FACT CHANGED FROM /royaltyActivityNet TO /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet, and that re-point is the whole reason the section 465 build put its cap BEFORE the fork. This Dependency joins scheduleC at /scheduleCNetProfit from OUTSIDE the /scheduleCs collection, i.e. after /scheduleCs/*/atRiskLimitationApplies has already run on the modeled Schedule C business, so an uncapped working interest loss arriving here would walk straight past the at-risk machinery that module ships. Reading the capped net closes it. A profit is untouched: the cap only ever shrinks a loss. Consumer certification (c) of that contract - this arm into Schedule C line 31, then Schedule SE line 2, then QBI - is pinned by the node test scheduleE/royalty-working-interest-loss-at-risk-capped-into-schedule-c.
ATTRIBUTED TO THE PRIMARY FILER, always, and stated rather than left to inference. The royalty surface carries no owner intake at all (/writableRoyaltyIncome is a return-level scalar), so there is nothing to attribute FROM; the primary filer is the same back-compat posture /scheduleCFiler takes when unanswered. The consequence is deliberate: on a return whose modeled Schedule C belongs to the SPOUSE, this amount still lands on the PRIMARY's Schedule SE rather than inheriting her attribution — which is why scheduleC's two per-filer terms were re-pointed at /scheduleCBusinessNetProfit in this same commit instead of being left to read the now-combined line 31. interpretation:provisional — a working-interest owner intake is the fact that would retire this default.
RESIDUAL, disclosed not claimed away: only ONE Schedule C business is modeled per return. A return carrying BOTH an attested Schedule C business and a working interest reports two businesses' figures on one printed line 31 and gives QBI one blended per- business component. The tax RESULT is right — total income, self-employment tax and the §179 business-income limit are all return-level sums — and the two figures that are not separately representable are the printed detail and QBI's per-business split, the same single-business conflation /scheduleCNetProfit's own Description already carries.

Fact.Name: Net royalty income (Schedule E line 26 royalty portion → Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description:
The net royalty income from the single INVESTMENT royalty activity — the section 465 at-risk-allowed activity net (/royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet, which caps the loss arm of /royaltyActivityNet: Schedule E line 4 minus the line-20 ordinary deductible expenses minus the line-18 depletion deduction) — i.e. the royalty contribution to Schedule E line 21 / line 26 (Total rental real estate and royalty income → Schedule 1 line 5). NONPASSIVE / PORTFOLIO: investment royalty income is NOT subject to the §469 passive-loss limitation (Schedule E line 22 / Form 8582 is not completed for royalty properties), so it flows to total income without passing through the /rentalProperties §8582 chain.
It is subject to the §465 at-risk rules: Schedule E line 21 points a royalty loss straight at Form 6198 on the printed form. The §465 chain this fact rides is its own (/royaltyAtRiskLimitationApplies, /royaltyRawLoss, /royaltyAtRiskDeductibleLoss, /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss, /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet), separate from the /rentalProperties one — separate chain, same statute.
Complete-safe: 0 when no royalty is claimed (/claimsRoyaltyIncome false), which keeps every non-royalty scenario byte-identical. A NET ROYALTY LOSS IS BUILT, not refused, on the owner's direction: the at-risk refusal "should not be a knockout, correct it and build it". This fact now reads /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet, the activity net AFTER the section 465 limitation, so a royalty loss reaches Schedule E line 21, line 25, line 26 and Schedule 1 line 5 as a NEGATIVE amount — capped at the amount at risk when the filer answers /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk FALSE, and uncapped when the filer answers it TRUE. The disallowed remainder leaves as /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss, the section 465(a)(2) carryover. /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss is NARROWED rather than retired, to the population that has a loss and has not answered the attestation at all; the narrowing itself is the lead's edit and this unit did not touch that fact.
The guard that limits an at-risk royalty loss is /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss, placed on /royaltyActivityNet (before the working-interest fork) so one refusal covers both arms; its Description carries the printed Schedule E line 21 / Form 6198 grounds. The §465 limitation this fact rides is the real fix and is in the tree at the same place the guard sits, so one gate still covers both arms.
THE WORKING-INTEREST FORK: $0 when /royaltyIsWorkingInterest — an oil or gas working (operating) interest is a trade or business, so Schedule E line 4 excludes it by its own instruction ("royalties from oil, gas, or mineral properties (not including operating interests)") and the activity's net is routed to Schedule C through /workingInterestNetProfit instead. The income does not vanish and is not doubled: the two arms partition /royaltyActivityNet exactly. The paragraph that used to sit here calling the working-interest regime "deferred" is retired by this fill, not merely amended — the fork it deferred is the fork above.
interpretation:provisional — the nonpassive / portfolio treatment stated here holds for INVESTMENT royalties, which after this fill is exactly the population this fact reports. Result rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Has Schedule E Part II partnership / S-corporation K-1 income
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports income or loss from a partnership or S corporation on Schedule E Part II (line 28) via a Schedule K-1 (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 1 / Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 1). Gate for the Part II K-1 intake (twin of /hasScheduleERentalIncome and /writableHasRoyaltyIncome). When true the /formK1s collection carries one item per K-1 (/formK1s/*/ordinaryIncome, /formK1s/*/materiallyParticipated, the basis / at-risk inputs, and a stable /formK1s/*/label); the collection is non-empty exactly when this is true (so the ~190 non-K-1 scenarios that never populate /formK1s keep every K-1 aggregate Complete-0/false byte-identical, exactly as /hasScheduleERentalIncome gates /rentalProperties).

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E Part II K-1 income
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /writableHasK1Income is answered AND true (IsComplete pattern, twin of /claimsRoyaltyIncome and /claimsScheduleERentalIncome). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so returns without a partnership / S-corp K-1 still resolve and /scheduleEPartIINetIncome is 0. Gates the Part II net so every non-K-1 scenario keeps /scheduleEPartIINetIncome Complete-0 byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Partnership / S-corporation Schedule K-1s (Schedule E Part II)
Fact.Description: The collection of partnership / S-corporation Schedule K-1s reported on Schedule E Part II (line 28) — one item per K-1 (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) / Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)). Introduces this collection (faithful 1:1 input: each physical K-1 is its own item, never a pre-summed scalar); the demo migration carries exactly ONE item, reproducing the single-K-1 model byte-identically. Each item holds the per-K-1 box-1 ordinary income/loss, the material-participation flag, the basis / at-risk loss-limitation inputs, and a stable label. Populated exactly when /writableHasK1Income is true.

Fact.Name: K-1 entity type options
Fact.Description: The entity types a Schedule E Part II K-1 can come from: a partnership (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)) or an S corporation (Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)). Both flow box-1 ordinary business income identically to Schedule E Part II line 28, so the type is a faithful-record field, not a computation input.

Fact.Name: K-1 label (stable identity)
Fact.Description: A stable, human-referenceable label for this K-1 item — e.g. the entity name or payer EIN. The collector preserves this identity across intake sessions so adding / replacing / removing a K-1 touches exactly one item. Play no part in any computation; a faithful record field. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered leaves the item unlabeled and changes no tax value.

Fact.Name: K-1 entity type (partnership or S corporation)
Fact.Description:
Whether this K-1 is from a partnership (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)) or an S corporation (Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)) — a faithful-record field. Box-1 ordinary income flows to Schedule E Part II line 28 identically for both. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered leaves the type unrecorded.
This Description used to end the sentence above with "so this does not change any tax value". THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE and the correction rides with the fill that made it false. ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership now reads this field: an ANSWERED sCorp resolves item D to FALSE without asking the filer, because Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) has no publicly-traded checkbox — its own Part I item D is "Corporation’s total number of shares". So on a K-1 that elects a box-12 §179 amount, or answers a box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount, or carries a passive box-1 figure, this field decides whether the §469(k) and §199A chains compute at all. It is still a faithful-record field for its OTHER purpose; it is no longer inert. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY, which is deliberate: only an ANSWERED sCorp is load-bearing. An answered "partnership" and an UNANSWERED entityType behave identically — both still require item D to be answered — because a missing entity type is not a statement that the K-1 came from an S corporation.

Fact.Name: K-1 recipient (which filer received this K-1)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer who received this Schedule K-1 — the primary filer or, on an MFJ return, the spouse. Mirrors /formW2s/*/filer (the established per-form attribution pattern). Schedule SE and the box-14A self-employment leg are PER-INDIVIDUAL (IRC 1402; "If you and your spouse are both partners, each of you must complete and file your own Schedule SE"), so a K-1 must be attributable to a specific filer. This field partitions the box-14A earnings per filer (/primaryFilerK1SeEarnings, /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings), which scheduleSE.xml's two per-filer chains consume — so an MFJ return with nonzero box 14A now COMPUTES (each spouse's earnings against that spouse's own OASDI wage base) instead of being knocked out. Unanswered defaults to the PRIMARY filer (the /formW2s/*/filer back-compat posture): a single-filer return has no spouse to attribute to, and an existing MFJ K-1 item that pre-dates this field keeps its prior primary-filer attribution, so no resolved value changes. interpretation:provisional — the default-to-primary attribution is the load-bearing reading NOW that the chain split is live: an MFJ K-1 whose filer is left unanswered is computed on the PRIMARY's Schedule SE. Rejected alternative: REFUSE an unanswered MFJ K-1, rejected because it would knock out every pre-existing MFJ K-1 item — a value/completeness change to committed returns imposed to guard a case the intake flow can simply require an answer for. Revisit if a real intake ever writes an MFJ K-1 without a filer.

Fact.Name: K-1 belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: This K-1 was received by the primary filer. Like /formW2s/*/belongsToPrimaryFiler, but COMPLETE-SAFE on the unanswered default: /formW2s scenarios answer ../filer, whereas ../filer is NEW on /formK1s and every existing K-1 leaves it unanswered (resolving to its primary-filer Placeholder). A bare Equal(../filer, /primaryFiler) would then be Result.Placeholder and cascade incompleteness into /k1SeEarnings → Schedule SE → total tax. So this reads ../filer only when it is actually ANSWERED (IsComplete-first, the established pattern used by ../seEarnings): an unanswered filer defaults to the primary filer as a COMPLETE true, preserving the prior whole-collection completeness and value. interpretation:provisional (default-to-primary attribution).

Fact.Name: K-1 belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: This K-1 was received by the secondary (MFJ spouse) filer. COMPLETE-SAFE mirror of /formW2s/*/belongsToSecondaryFiler (see ../belongsToPrimaryFiler): reads ../filer only when ANSWERED (IsComplete-first); an unanswered filer defaults to NOT-secondary as a COMPLETE false, so /secondaryFilerK1s is empty and /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings is a complete 0 on every existing return. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Partnership / S-corp K-1 ordinary business income or (loss) (Schedule K-1 box 1)
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part II line 28 column (h)/(k) (income) or column (g)/(i) (loss): the ORDINARY business income OR (loss) from this partnership / S-corporation K-1 (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 1 / Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 1). SIGNED: positive is box-1 income, NEGATIVE is a box-1 loss. A LOSS is deductible only to the extent of basis (704(d)/1366(d)) via ../ordinaryLoss, ../basis and ../basisAllowedLoss, then 465 at-risk and 469 passive. Was /writableK1OrdinaryIncome.

Fact.Name: Materially participated in the partnership / S-corporation activity
Fact.Description:
True when the taxpayer MATERIALLY PARTICIPATED in this partnership / S-corporation trade or business (469(h)) — the activity is then NONPASSIVE. When answered FALSE the activity is PASSIVE. Decisive only for a K-1 LOSS (routes a passive loss through Form 8582); for a K-1 profit the flag does not change line 32. Was /writableK1MateriallyParticipated. interpretation:provisional.
WHEN IT IS UNANSWERED the classification is taken by ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption, and there are TWO answers rather than one. On an item-D PTP held as a LIMITED partner the activity is PASSIVE, because IRC 469(h)(2) presumes no material participation in a limited partnership interest held as a limited partner. Everywhere else — a general-partner PTP, and every non-PTP K-1 — it is NONPASSIVE, the module's completeness convention.
UNANSWERED IS NOT REFUSED, with one exception, named so it is not discovered: a K-1 that elects a box-12 §179 deduction on an item-D PTP held by a GENERAL partner still blocks submission through /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp, because the box-12 fork chooses between two regimes on this answer and 469(h)(2) supplies no presumption for a general partner.

Fact.Name: Partnership / S-corporation adjusted basis before the K-1 loss (704(d)/1366(d))
Fact.Description: The partner's adjusted basis in the partnership interest (704(d)) / shareholder's stock+debt basis (1366(d)) BEFORE the current-year box-1 loss — the ceiling on a deductible K-1 loss. Consulted ONLY when this K-1 reports a loss (../ordinaryLoss > 0); for a profit it is never read. 0 or unanswered ⇒ 0 basis ⇒ the whole loss suspends. Was /writableK1Basis. interpretation:provisional (1366(d) S-corp ceiling applied by analogy to the 704(d) partnership rule).

Fact.Name: Fully at risk for the K-1 activity (465; no Form 6198 needed)
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer is FULLY at risk (465) for this partnership / S-corporation activity, so no Form 6198 applies and the basis-allowed loss survives the at-risk step. When FALSE, ../amountAtRisk (Form 6198 line 20) caps the deductible loss. When UNANSWERED, treated as FULLY AT RISK. Was /writableK1FullyAtRisk. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk in the K-1 activity (465; Form 6198 line 20)
Fact.Description: The simplified amount at risk in this partnership / S-corporation activity (Form 6198 Part II -> Part IV line 20), entered not less than zero. Consulted ONLY when ../fullyAtRisk is answered AND false. Was /writableK1AmountAtRisk. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss magnitude (Schedule K-1 box 1 loss)
Fact.Description: The MAGNITUDE of this K-1's box-1 ordinary loss = max(0, -../ordinaryIncome): the loss when box 1 is negative, else 0. The pre-limitation loss the 704(d)/1366(d) basis rule caps. No claims gate (item existence ⇒ a claimed K-1). Was /k1OrdinaryLoss — the top-level /k1OrdinaryLoss is now the CollectionSum aggregate.

Fact.Name: K-1 loss and deduction items competing for one basis pool (basis worksheet line 15s, column C)
Fact.Description: ../ordinaryLoss + ../section179Elected — the total of the loss and deduction categories this dictionary carries for a single K-1, which is what the partner's basis worksheet compares the remaining basis against before deciding whether a pro rata allocation is needed at all. TWO CATEGORIES, NOT ALL OF THEM. The printed block runs 15a through 15t and includes capital losses, section 1231 losses, charitable contributions, EBIE and more; this dictionary models the box-1 ordinary loss (line 15a) and the box-12 section 179 deduction (line 15i) and no others, so the total is over those two. A K-1 carrying an unmodeled category would allocate too much basis to these two — NAMED, not silently absorbed: it is the same residue oos-schedulee-part-ii-followons already owns ("separately-stated K-1 items"), and it is unreachable today because no other category has an intake to answer. COMPLETE-SAFE: ../section179Elected is the 0-default alias, so this resolves for every K-1 item whether or not box 12 was answered.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss allowed by the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation (basis worksheet line 15a, column D)
Fact.Description: The portion of this K-1's ordinary loss deductible after the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation, consulted only when ../ordinaryLoss > 0 (else 0 WITHOUT reading ../basis). Was /k1BasisAllowedLoss. interpretation:provisional (1366(d) by analogy). REBODIED FROM min(../ordinaryLoss, ../basis) TO THE WORKSHEET'S TWO-ARM COLUMN D: the whole loss when ../basis covers ../basisCompetingItemsTotal, and its PRO RATA share of ../basis when it does not. See the block comment above for the reassembled instruction and for why this is byte-identical on every K-1 with no box-12 section 179 amount — which is every fixture and every scenario in the committed corpus, including the clean-room witness.

Fact.Name: K-1 section 179 deduction allowed by the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation (basis worksheet line 15i, column D)
Fact.Description: The box-12 section 179 amount this K-1's basis can absorb: the whole of ../section179Elected when ../basis covers ../basisCompetingItemsTotal, and otherwise whatever basis the box-1 loss leg did not take — ../basis minus ../basisAllowedLoss, floored at $0. THE REMAINDER RATHER THAN A SECOND ROUNDED RATIO, and the choice is forced by the printed cap: "The total allocation amount reported in column D of line 15s can't exceed the amount report[ed] on Part II, line 14." Two independently rounded pro rata shares can sum to a dollar above basis; a remainder cannot. It also leaves ../basisAllowedLoss rounding exactly as it did before this unit, which is what the clean-room witness and the section 465/469 chain downstream of it are entitled to. AND THIS FACT CARRIES NO Round OF ITS OWN, deliberately, where every sibling in the block does: rounding the remainder would re-open the very gap the remainder closes. Basis 15,999.99 against a 4,000 loss and a 12,000 election rounds the loss leg UP to 4,000, so a ROUNDED remainder of 11,999.99 would become 12,000 and the column-D total would exceed basis by a cent — which is exactly what the printed cap forbids. The cents stop here: ../section179ColumnJ wraps its own Round, so the figure that reaches Schedule E column (j) is whole dollars either way. WHEN ../basis IS UNANSWERED this resolves $0 — and the return is refused anyway by ../section179WithoutSufficientBasis, which after this fill is exactly that unanswered arm. The $0 is therefore never a silently withheld deduction; it is the value on a return that cannot be filed. COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 for any K-1 that elects nothing, without reading ../basis.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss suspended by the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation (carryforward)
Fact.Description: The portion of this K-1's ordinary loss disallowed because it exceeds basis = ../ordinaryLoss - ../basisAllowedLoss; suspended and carried forward (704(d)/1366(d)). Was /k1BasisSuspendedLoss. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The 465 at-risk limitation applies to this K-1 loss (Form 6198 required)
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when ../fullyAtRisk is answered AND false — Form 6198 caps the deductible loss at the amount at risk. When ../fullyAtRisk is true OR unanswered (IsComplete false), false and NO at-risk limit applies. Was /k1AtRiskLimitationApplies.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss allowed by the 465 at-risk limitation (Form 6198 line 21)
Fact.Description:
The basis-allowed loss (../basisAllowedLoss) deductible after the 465 at-risk limit (Form 6198 line 21): the SMALLER of the basis-allowed loss or ../amountAtRisk when ../atRiskLimitationApplies, else the full basis-allowed loss. Was /k1AtRiskAllowedLoss. interpretation:provisional.
A LEADING PER ACTIVITY CASE. When this K-1 carries a usable box 22 statement (../atRiskActivitySharesUsable), the cap is LesserOf(../basisAllowedLoss, ../atRiskActivityAllowedLossTotal): each activity has already been capped against its OWN amount at risk by ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedLoss, and this line only holds the result under the item level 704(d)/1366(d) ceiling. IRC 465(a)(1) allows a loss "only to the extent of the aggregate amount with respect to which the taxpayer is at risk ... for such activity" and IRC 465(c)(2) makes each activity separate, so the single ../amountAtRisk is the wrong grain on this population and is not consulted there.
THE ORDERING WAS REFINED BY THE BASIS-BY-ACTIVITY RULE THE UNIT D6 PARAGRAPH ANTICIPATED. That paragraph read: "The basis limit is a limit on the PARTNERSHIP INTEREST (704(d)) and the at-risk limit is a limit per ACTIVITY (465), and nothing vendored allocates a partially binding basis across the activities of one K-1. This fact therefore applies the per activity at-risk caps first and the whole item basis ceiling second, which can never allow more than either limit standing alone. A future unit that allocates basis by activity would refine, not reverse, this." Something vendored DOES allocate a partially binding basis, at the CATEGORY grain: the partner basis worksheet's column D pro rata rule. Unit C5 applies it across the activities inside the box 1 loss category, so ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityBasisAllowedLossShare now carries the basis limit INTO each activity and ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedLoss caps THAT rather than the raw share, which is the printed basis-then-at-risk ordering ("After applying the basis rules, the loss you report on Schedule E may be further reduced by the at-risk rules", Instructions for Schedule E (2025)).
IT REFINED RATHER THAN REVERSED. This line's BODY IS UNCHANGED; the LesserOf still holds the per activity sum under ../basisAllowedLoss, and it now also absorbs any rounding oversum from N independently rounded pro rata shares. The answer can only be the same or SMALLER than before — smaller exactly when basis BINDS and the shares are USABLE, a population no committed fixture reached before scheduleE/k1-box22-basis-binds-across-two-activities. On that witness this line moves 1,000 to 750, which is the correct figure: 1,000 of basis pro rated 750/250 across a 1,500/500 loss split leaves activity A capped by its 500 at risk and activity B's 250 fully at risk. The old 1,000 silently allocated the scarce basis to whichever activity happened to be fully at risk — a taxpayer election no printed rule grants.
WHAT REMAINS AN INTERPRETATION: the pro rata rule is printed for CATEGORIES of loss, not for the activities inside one category, so the allocation stays ai-only and provisional.
BYTE IDENTICAL WHERE BOX 22 IS BLANK. ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable is complete safe false on every return that leaves box 22 unchecked, so the leading case never fires and the two original cases are reached unchanged; the cleanroom-verified i6198 example (b) figure is re-proved by scheduleE/i6198-line21-k1-example after the rewire.
ON THE USABLE-SHARES POPULATION THE ITEM-LEVEL ../amountAtRisk IS NOT CONSULTED — including when it was ANSWERED (measured: item amountAtRisk 500 answered, footing shares 1500/500 at-risk 1500/500 -> allowed 2000, where the old path gave 500). That is the correct grain: 465(a)(1) measures the amount at risk FOR SUCH ACTIVITY, 465(c)(2) makes each activity separate, and Form 6198 is filed per activity with no line summing the line-20s, so no item-level cross-check is owed; the single amountAtRisk is the single-activity path's modelling artifact. The application screen for the shares should say the per-activity amounts REPLACE the single item-level answer on a box-22 K-1 (INTAKE-GROUPS.md, the at-risk group).
A MIXED-SIGN STATEMENT NETS ITS INCOME SHARES AGAINST THE CAPPED LOSS SHARES. On a usable statement the per activity sum is reduced by ../atRiskActivityIncomeShareTotal before it meets ../basisAllowedLoss: IRC 465(d) measures each activity's loss net of that activity's own income, and an earning activity's income is never capped, so the K-1's loss after the at-risk rule is the capped loss shares less the untouched income shares. On every statement with no income share the subtrahend is $0 and the arm is unchanged. The GreaterOf floor never binds on a usable statement, because ../atRiskActivitySharesMixedSignResidue refuses the statement whose capped loss falls below its income; it is a sign guard.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss suspended by the 465 at-risk limitation (carryover)
Fact.Description: The basis-allowed loss disallowed by the 465 at-risk limit = ../basisAllowedLoss - ../atRiskAllowedLoss (Form 6198 line 5 - line 21). Carries to the succeeding year (465(a)(2)); this single-year demo REPORTS it. Was /k1AtRiskSuspendedLoss. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This K-1 is a publicly traded partnership interest held as a LIMITED partner (IRC 469(h)(2) scope)
Fact.Description:
Gate: true when item D is checked (../isPubliclyTradedPartnership) AND this partner is not a general partner (../partnerIsGeneralPartner false). ONE gate fact rather than the same conjunction spelled twice, so IRC 469(h)(2)'s scope is drawn in exactly one place — the shape ../appliesPtpSection469 already uses for the §469(k) regime boundary.
WHAT IT SELECTS. IRC 469(h)(2) provides that, except as regulations provide, no interest in a limited partnership as a limited partner is treated as an interest with respect to which the taxpayer materially participates. On THIS population an unanswered ../materiallyParticipated therefore defaults to FALSE (passive) instead of taking the module's usual "unanswered means nonpassive" convention. The default itself lives in exactly one fact, ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption; this one is only its scope. IT READS THE RAW ITEM-D ALIAS, NOT ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived, and the choice is load-bearing rather than stylistic. ../appliesPtpSection469 gates the §469(k) per-PTP regime on the RAW checkbox alias. Keying this fact on the DERIVED one would make a K-1 that answers a box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount with item D UNCHECKED passive WITHOUT also putting it inside §469(k) — so its passive loss would join the general Form 8582 pool and net against other activities' passive income, which is exactly what "a net passive loss from a PTP may not be deducted from other passive income" forbids. The presumption and the regime must turn on TOGETHER, so both read the same alias. The item-D split that leaves standing is the one ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived already discloses in its own NAMED GAP paragraph (§199A reads the derived fact, §469 reads the checkbox), a named gap this fact neither widens nor closes.
THE GENERAL-PARTNER CONJUNCT IS THE RULE'S OWN CARVE-OUT, not a softening of it: for purposes of the material participation tests a partner is not treated as a limited partner if they were also a general partner in the partnership at all times during the partnership's tax year. A general partner's PTP interest keeps today's behaviour exactly, and what that costs is stated rather than hidden — see ../section179OnPtp, which still refuses a general-partner PTP whose participation answer is missing and a box-12 §179 amount is elected.
AN UNANSWERED ITEM G COUNTS AS LIMITED HERE, and that is a READING of rather than a quotation of it. This fact reads the complete-safe alias ../partnerIsGeneralPartner, whose FALSE default already covers an unanswered item G and whose own Description calls that default the taxpayer-ADVERSE one. Three things carry the reading. (a) Presuming passivity on silence is taxpayer-adverse in the SAME direction — a loss suspends instead of being deducted in full — so the two defaults agree rather than compound. (b) A publicly traded partnership's traded units ARE limited partner interests; item D checked with item G silent points at "limited" on the facts, not merely on the convention. (c) Read as answered-false-only it would exempt the ORDINARY PTP, since no committed fixture and no committed scenario answers item G at all, and the unit would discharge nothing. The alternative reading is one operand away if it is ever ruled the other way.
COMPLETENESS, AND IT IS NOT SIMPLY COMPLETE-SAFE. ../partnerIsGeneralPartner is a complete-safe FALSE-defaulting alias; ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership is NOT — it is INCOMPLETE on a partnership K-1 that has not answered the checkbox. The truth table: item D TRUE, item G not general partner -> true item D TRUE, item G general partner -> false item D FALSE (answered, or an sCorp K-1) -> false (All() returns Complete(false) on a Complete-false head, so item G is not even read) item D UNANSWERED on a partnership K-1 -> INCOMPLETE, unless item G is answered TRUE, in which case Not(../partnerIsGeneralPartner) is Complete(false) and All() still returns Complete(false). That exception is worth naming rather than rounding off: a K-1 that has declared itself a GENERAL-PARTNER interest is outside 469(h)(2) whatever item D says, and the member ordering of All() is what lets the engine see it. The consequence for the presumption is that it cannot fire on an unanswered item D — the classification does not compute at all rather than defaulting either way.

Fact.Name: Material participation for this K-1, after the IRC 469(h)(2) PTP limited-partner presumption
Fact.Description:
The participation answer the passive/nonpassive classification reads: ANSWERED, it is the answer; UNANSWERED on a PTP interest held as a limited partner (../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner), FALSE, because IRC 469(h)(2) presumes no material participation there; UNANSWERED anywhere else, TRUE, which is the module's pre-existing "unanswered means NONPASSIVE" convention restated as a value rather than changed. ../lossIsPassive is Not() of this fact and nothing else.
THE THIRD ARM IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE FILER PARTICIPATED. It returns TRUE so that ../lossIsPassive returns FALSE, which is byte-for-byte what an unanswered ../materiallyParticipated produced on every non-PTP K-1 and every general-partner PTP before this fact existed. The truth table is the whole argument, and only the third row moves: answered true -> true (was: Not(true) = lossIsPassive false) answered false -> false (was: Not(false) = lossIsPassive true) unanswered, PTP + limited partner -> FALSE (was: lossIsPassive false) , PTP + general partner -> true (was: lossIsPassive false) unanswered, not a PTP -> true (was: lossIsPassive false) unanswered, ITEM D UNANSWERED -> Placeholder true, i.e. NOT COMPLETE. When ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership is Incomplete, ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner is Incomplete, so the SECOND arm's When has no value; the Switch falls to the third arm with its accumulated completeness already false, and Expression.switches returns that arm's value asPlaceholder. ../lossIsPassive is then Placeholder false and ../appliesPtpSection469 is Incomplete outright. The row is listed because a five-row table that omits it reads as a claim that this fact always resolves, which is the claim the paragraph below used to make. ANSWERED item D is a precondition for every row above it. On an sCorp K-1 item D resolves FALSE off ../entityType and the table applies unchanged (the "not a PTP" row).
WHAT THE MOVED ROW COSTS THE FILER, said plainly because it is a tax INCREASE in the year it fires: that K-1's items become passive, so a box-1 LOSS stops being deducted in full on Schedule E line 28 column (i) and is suspended per-PTP under §469(k) to be carried forward (../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut), and a box-1 GAIN becomes §469(k) nonpassive income in column (k) at the same dollar figure. That direction is the point: reading silence as material participation is wrong in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction, and 469(h)(2) is the reason it is wrong.
AND IT IS NOT ADVERSE IN EVERY DIRECTION — ONE CORNER REDUCES TAX, named because a Description that only lists the increases is selling the ruling rather than describing it. A presumed-passive PTP with an OVERALL GAIN enters the §469(k) regime, and "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income. In addition, the nonpassive income is included in investment income to figure your investment interest expense deduction." So ../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome becomes that gain instead of $0, Form 4952 line 4h grows, and a filer with investment interest can deduct MORE under §163(d) than the old nonpassive reading allowed. That is not a defect and not a loophole: IRC 469(h)(2) is the statutory baseline, and this is simply what the correct classification does on that corner. It is disclosed here so nobody reads the tax-increase paragraph above as the whole effect.
THE PRESUMPTION IS REBUTTED BY ANSWERING TRUE — there is no separate rebuttal fact and none is needed, because the first arm already wins. The application asks the question with the limited-partner test set (items 1, 5 and 6 of the material participation standards).
THE IDIOM IS IsComplete/Switch, never a Not() over an unanswered Boolean, which would resolve Incomplete and drag the classification with it — that shape is what keeps an unanswered ../materiallyParticipated from being the thing that breaks this fact. IT IS NOT COMPLETE-SAFE END TO END, and that is worth keeping separate from the idiom claim: ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership carries no FALSE default, so ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner is Incomplete on a partnership K-1 whose item D is unanswered, and this fact is a PLACEHOLDER true there rather than a Complete one.
NOT MODELED, disclosed rather than implied: the presumption is applied ONLY to an item-D PTP. IRC 469(h)(2) reaches every limited partnership interest held as a limited partner, and this dictionary holds item G on non-PTP partnership K-1s too — so an unanswered participation answer on a NON-PTP limited-partner K-1 still reads nonpassive. Scopes the change to PTPs ("General-partner PTP interests and all non-PTP K-1s keep today's behaviour") and this fact does not exceed its ruling; widening it is a change to every partnership K-1's classification and needs its own decision.

Fact.Name: This K-1 ordinary loss is a 469 passive-activity loss (not materially participated)
Fact.Description:
Gate: true exactly when the activity is PASSIVE, so the at-risk-allowed loss is subject to the 469 passive limit. Not() of ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption and nothing else. The participation-based gate classifies BOTH income and loss (used by ../passiveNet). Was /k1LossIsPassive. interpretation:provisional.
The prior text read "true only when ../materiallyParticipated is answered AND false — the activity is PASSIVE and the at-risk-allowed loss is subject to the 469 passive limit. When ../materiallyParticipated is true OR unanswered (IsComplete false), false (NONPASSIVE, no 469 limit)", and the body was the IsComplete/Switch over ../materiallyParticipated directly. That is still what happens on every K-1 EXCEPT one cell: an item-D PTP held as a LIMITED partner whose participation answer is UNANSWERED is now PASSIVE, because IRC 469(h)(2) presumes no material participation in a limited partnership interest held as a limited partner. The whole of that change — the presumption, its scope, and the unchanged default everywhere else — lives in ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption and ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner, which is why this body is now a single Not(). Values are byte-identical on all four other rows of the truth table; the moved row is pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleE/k1-ptp-participation-*.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss allowed as NONPASSIVE (Schedule E line 28 column (i))
Fact.Description:
The at-risk-allowed loss (../atRiskAllowedLoss) that flows to Schedule E Part II because the activity is NONPASSIVE = ../atRiskAllowedLoss when NOT ../lossIsPassive, else 0 (a passive loss does not flow; it suspends via ../passiveSuspendedLoss). Was /k1NonpassiveAllowedLoss. interpretation:provisional.
A §469(g)(1)(A) DISPOSITION RELEASE IS ALSO NONPASSIVE: when ../dispositionReleaseApplies, this column reports ../dispositionReleasedLoss instead of the ordinary "passive, so 0" outcome — the statute's own words are "treated as a loss which is not from a passive activity", which is exactly this column's definition. Leading case, ahead of the box-23 arm: dispositionReleaseApplies already excludes a usable box-23 statement as one of its conjuncts, so the two cases can never both fire on the same K-1.

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss suspended by the 469 passive limitation (isolated; superseded by the pool allocation)
Fact.Description:
This K-1's at-risk-allowed loss suspended by the 469 limit IN ISOLATION = ../atRiskAllowedLoss when ../lossIsPassive, else 0. The AUTHORITATIVE suspended amount once a cross-activity pool exists is the ratable /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated; retained for continuity. Was /k1PassiveSuspendedLoss. interpretation:provisional.
