NOT BOX-23-AWARE, AND THAT IS FINE: this fact and its CollectionSum /k1PassiveSuspendedLoss are a genuine dead end — no other fact in dictionary/ty2025/*.xml depends on either path, and no PDF field binds them (a grep of both confirms zero consumers), unlike ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss, which is bound to Schedule E line 28 column (i) and DID need the leading case above.

Fact.Name: Prior-year unallowed passive loss from THIS publicly traded partnership (§469(k) carry-in)
Fact.Description:
The passive loss from THIS PTP that prior years suspended and carried forward, supplied directly as an attested input. Step 1 of the partner instructions' PTP procedure combines it with the current year: "Combine any current-year income, gains, and losses, and any prior-year unallowed losses to see if you have an overall gain or loss from the PTP."
PER PTP, NOT PER RETURN, and that is the whole point of §469(k) rather than an implementation choice: a suspended PTP loss is "carried forward to be applied against passive income from the SAME PTP in later years", so pooling these across PTPs would re-create exactly the netting the section forbids. Hence a per-item writable on /formK1s rather than a top-level one.
WHY IT IS AN ATTESTED WRITABLE: this is cross-year state, and ytax resolves one tax year. The established shape for that is a filer-stated carry-IN — the same shape qbi:/writableQualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear, qbi:/writableQualifiedBusinessNetLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear, form4952:/writableInvestmentInterestCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear and scheduleD:/writableLongTermLossCarryoverFromPriorTaxYear already use. Its PRODUCER now ships: ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut is the exported amount a 2026 return's carry-in should be handed, on the SAME positive-magnitude convention as this writable. The pair is closed on this repo's side; it stays an ATTESTED writable because ytax still resolves one year at a time, so nothing here reads that export back.
SIGN — STORED AS A POSITIVE MAGNITUDE AND SUBTRACTED, matching the four siblings named above. A prior-year UNALLOWED LOSS can only be a loss, so the magnitude convention makes the normal entry positive and the dangerous entry (a negative, which subtracted would invent a gain and could flip a suspended loss into nonpassive income on Schedule E line 28) unenterable. The Min $0 Limit is what enforces that mechanically; the gate auto-covers declared Limits.
OPTIONAL: unanswered means no carry-in, via the complete-safe ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss. Answer it only on a K-1 whose item D is checked; on any other K-1 it is inert, because ../appliesPtpSection469 is false and nothing reads the alias.

Fact.Name: Prior-year unallowed PTP loss, complete-safe
Fact.Description: ../writablePtpPriorYearUnallowedLoss when answered, else $0 (the IsComplete-guard pattern). A $0 default is the conservative one here: a carry-in only ever REDUCES an overall gain, so defaulting it to zero can never manufacture a suspension the filer did not claim, and it keeps every pre-existing /formK1s item resolving.

Fact.Name: The §469(k) per-PTP regime governs this K-1
Fact.Description:
True when item D is checked (../isPubliclyTradedPartnership) AND this K-1's items are PASSIVE (../lossIsPassive). One gate fact rather than the same conjunction spelled three times, so the regime's boundary is defined in exactly one place.
WHY ../lossIsPassive IS PART OF IT, since §469(k) names no such condition: §469(k)(1) applies "this section" separately per PTP, and this section — the passive activity loss rules — only reaches PASSIVE activities in the first place. A partner who MATERIALLY PARTICIPATES has no passive activity for §469(k) to partition, and the K-1's income or loss is already nonpassive and fully deductible on Schedule E line 28. Both errors this regime corrects also live only in the passive branch: a passive PTP loss netted against other activities' passive income, and a passive PTP gain absorbing other activities' passive losses.
THE HOLE THIS LEAVES, disclosed rather than glossed, because it is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE: ../lossIsPassive is false when ../materiallyParticipated is answered-true OR UNANSWERED, and "unanswered" is a completeness convention, not a claim of material participation. So a PTP K-1 whose participation question has not been answered keeps the NONPASSIVE path — its box-1 loss is deducted in full this year rather than suspended. Two committed fixtures sit in exactly that state (scheduleE/ptp-item-d-selects-code-z, box 1 of $5,000, and form8995/ptp-k1-below-threshold-divergence, $20,000; both are income cases, so nothing is over-deducted there today). This is a PRE-EXISTING property of ../lossIsPassive's default that this unit deliberately does not change: narrowing it is a change to every K-1's passive classification, not a §469(k) question.
The paragraph above is kept verbatim as the record of what this regime shipped with. IRC 469(h)(2) now supplies the missing claim: on an item-D PTP held as a LIMITED partner (../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner) an unanswered participation answer resolves PASSIVE through ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption, so ../lossIsPassive is TRUE there and THIS REGIME NOW GOVERNS that K-1. Both named fixtures were in that population and both moved: their item is now inside §469(k), and because both are INCOME cases at a $0 carry-in the dollars they assert are unchanged (an overall gain is nonpassive income in column (k) at the same figure). What is NOT closed is the general-partner PTP, where 469(h)(2) has its own carve-out and the hole stands exactly as written above. This fact can now be INCOMPLETE. ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership lost its FALSE default, so on a partnership K-1 whose item D is unanswered the first operand of the All is Incomplete and this fact does not resolve — and neither does anything it gates: ../ptpCurrentYearNet, ../ptpSection469Net, ../passiveNet, ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179, ../partIINonpassivePart and, through the collection sums, /scheduleEPartIINetIncome and /scheduleETotalIncome. Most of those come out as PLACEHOLDER values rather than bare Incompletes, because each is a Switch whose LATER arm matches with the accumulated completeness already false — a distinction worth naming, since a Placeholder carries a number that is right for the arm it took and wrong about whether the arm was the right one. Two things did NOT move and both are load-bearing: ../section179OnPtp and ../hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD each test IsComplete on the answer that would matter (the box-12 election, the box 20 code Z amount) BEFORE reading item D, so a K-1 with neither answered keeps them Complete FALSE and stays out of both refusal chains.
NOT BOX-23-AWARE, AND THAT IS FINE: a usable box-23 statement always has ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership false, one of ../passiveActivitySharesUsable's own conjuncts, so this fact is already false for the whole population that statement can express — no rewire needed.

Fact.Name: This PTP's CURRENT-year signed amount (§469(k) step 1, the current-year half)
Fact.Description:
The current-year half of step 1's combination for a PTP whose items are passive: +../ordinaryIncome when box 1 is income (>= 0), else -../atRiskAllowedLoss, plus this PTP's box 2 and box 3 rental income (../k1RentalRealEstateRentalIncome) on both arms. $0 when ../appliesPtpSection469 is false, which is every non-PTP and every nonpassive K-1.
IT IS THE AT-RISK-ALLOWED LOSS, not the raw box-1 loss, and that ordering is the same one ../passiveNet already uses: §704(d)/§1366(d) basis and §465 at-risk come BEFORE §469, so the amount §469(k) partitions is what survives them. A loss disallowed by basis or at-risk is suspended by those sections, not by this one, and is already tracked by ../basisSuspendedLoss and ../atRiskSuspendedLoss.
BOX 1 AND THE INCOME SIDE OF BOXES 2 AND 3 ARE IN IT, because step 1 says to combine "any current-year income, gains, and losses". The box 2 and box 3 rental INCOME of this PTP (../k1RentalRealEstateRentalIncome, floored at zero) is added on both arms, so a box 1 loss is allowed against the same PTP's rental income and a box 1 income and a rental income form one overall gain; /k1RentalRealEstateIncomeTotal leaves that PTP income out, so it is counted once. A box 2 or box 3 LOSS is not added: the basis, at-risk and passive limits on a second activity of the same K-1 are not modelled (see ../k1RentalRealEstateNet), so the loss stays off the return, the over-tax direction. A PTP's section 1231 / Form 4797 gains and losses and its credits remain outside the combination: the instructions' own worked example combines a Schedule E income with a Form 4797 prior-year loss, and this dictionary intakes no PTP Form 4797 amount.
THIS IS THE PRE-SECTION-179 TWIN (closure, 2026-08-21). Its post-section-179 twin is ../ptpCurrentYearNetAfterSection179 = this less ../ptpSection179Allowed, and that is what step 1's combination, Schedule E column (k), Form 4952 line 4h and the carry-out all read. THIS fact keeps the PRE-section-179 role and may not move: ../ptpSection469Net and ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 read it, and /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums the latter into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation, which Pub 946 ch.2 and i4562 Line 11 both figure "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction". scripts/factdag.py measures that limitation's upstream cone at 124 paths containing no post-section-179 fact.

Fact.Name: This PTP's overall §469(k) gain or loss, applied separately from every other activity
Fact.Description:
Step 1 of the partner instructions' PTP procedure, as a signed dollar amount: ../ptpCurrentYearNet less ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss. POSITIVE is an overall GAIN, NEGATIVE an overall LOSS, $0 when ../appliesPtpSection469 is false. From this one signed result the whole routing follows, which is why it is a fact and not an expression inlined twice.
WHAT IT DECIDES. Overall GAIN: "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income" — ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 reports it on Schedule E Part II line 28 column (k), and ../partIINonpassivePart carries it to line 32 through its own subtraction. Overall LOSS: the loss is suspended in full, so it reaches NOTHING this year — ../passiveNet is $0 for every PTP, honouring "Don't report passive income, gains, or losses from a PTP on Form 8582", and the nonpassive arm floors at zero.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES, in both directions, because a PTP K-1 previously flowed through ../passiveNet exactly like any other partnership. (1) A PTP's passive LOSS was netted against other activities' passive income and deducted this year, which "a net passive loss from a PTP may not be deducted from other passive income" forbids — tax was UNDER-stated, a false allowance. (2) A PTP's passive GAIN entered the same pool, where it absorbed OTHER activities' passive losses and released them — tax was OVER-stated for those activities. Both arms need their own witness and both have one; see the node tests named below.
WHAT IS NOT IN THE COMBINATION, and each of these is a real hole rather than a formality: (a) the §1231 / Form 4797 leg the instructions' own worked example uses (that example combines a $12,000 Schedule E loss with a $7,200 Form 4797 gain and carries $4,800 forward), because this dictionary intakes no PTP 4797 amount — the example is cited for the COMBINATION RULE, not reproduced; (b) K-1 rental real estate (box 2), which has no fact in this module at all; (c) the low-income housing and rehabilitation credits, which §469(k)(1) expressly carves OUT of the separate application and which this chain does not carry; (d) item 4's rule for a partner who disposes of the entire PTP interest, which releases the suspended loss.
THE INVESTMENT-INTEREST LEG NOW SHIPS TOO: "In addition, the nonpassive income is included in investment income to figure your investment interest expense deduction." ../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome is the positive part of this fact, summed by /k1PtpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome into form4952:/section163dInvestmentIncome — Form 4952 LINE 4h, the unfloored investment-income fact, and not line 6 (/section163dNetInvestmentIncome) as this paragraph previously said. Line 6 no longer carries the 4h sum itself, so entering at 4h is what keeps one definition of that line; the contract behind this fill named a form4952:/investmentIncome that module never declared, and both re-derivations are recorded rather than silently applied. That leg RAISES the §163(d) ceiling, so unlike the rest of this chain its direction is tax-reducing and it rests on the printed sentence above.
THE CARRY-OUT NOW SHIPS as ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut: the amount this fact suspends is what next year's ../writablePtpPriorYearUnallowedLoss should carry, and the pair is closed on this repo's side. It is EXPORTED, never read here, so it moves no 2025 figure.

Fact.Name: This PTP's suspended loss carried OUT to next year (§469(k) carry-out)
Fact.Description:
This fact is now the ALIAS of ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179, which is max($0, minus ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179). The opening formula below, "max($0, minus ../ptpSection469Net)", is the RETIRED body and is kept because every paragraph after it argues the quantity rather than the expression. The AMOUNT changed: once a passive PTP's box-12 section 179 share is a term of step 1's combination, an overall loss is deeper and more of it suspends — node-test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-income-limit-caps-the-179-term carries $0 before that closure and $50,000 after. max($0, minus ../ptpSection469Net): the part of this PTP's overall §469(k) result that suspends. "Instead, a passive loss from a PTP is suspended and carried forward to be applied against passive income from the same PTP in later years" — and because the regime allows NOTHING of an overall loss in the current year, the amount suspended is the whole negative part of step 1's signed result. An overall GAIN suspends nothing, which is what the floor says.
IT IS THE PRODUCING HALF OF A CARRY-OUT PAIR. ../writablePtpPriorYearUnallowedLoss is the consuming half — the attested carry-IN a filer types from the prior year — and this fact is what a 2026 return's carry-in should be handed. It is stored on the SAME convention that twin uses: a POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, never a signed loss. The two halves agreeing on sign IS the closure claim; a signed spelling here would be subtracted by next year's chain and invent a gain out of a loss.
WHAT A CONSUMER IS PROMISED, stated narrowly because an export is a commitment to a reader outside this repo (invariant #7 — the application owns the surface that would carry it into next year's intake). This is the §469(k)-SUSPENDED amount for THIS PTP and nothing else. It is NOT "everything this PTP carries forward": a box-1 loss disallowed by §704(d)/§1366(d) basis or by §465 at-risk never reaches ../ptpCurrentYearNet in the first place, because that fact reads ../atRiskAllowedLoss — the amount that SURVIVES those sections — so basis- and at-risk-suspended losses are tracked separately by ../basisSuspendedLoss and ../atRiskSuspendedLoss. The three amounts are disjoint by that ordering and may be added; reading this one ALONE as the PTP's whole carryforward would UNDER-state it. Naming which one this is, is the point of the sentence.
PER PTP, NEVER POOLED, for the same reason the carry-in is: §469(k)(1) applies the section separately to each PTP's items, so pooling suspended losses across PTPs re-creates exactly the netting it forbids. Two PTPs, one with an overall gain and one with an overall loss, carry out $0 and the full loss — never a single netted figure. Pinned by scheduleE/ptp-469-two-ptps-applied-separately, where pooling would give $1,000 and the shipped answer is $0 and $4,000.
EXPORTED, AND READ BY NOTHING THIS YEAR — re-verified, not assumed: it sits downstream of ../ptpSection469Net and upstream of nothing in this dictionary, so it closes no cycle and moves no 2025 figure. It is complete wherever ../ptpSection469Net is, adding no Incomplete surface, and it is $0 on every K-1 the regime does not govern because that fact is $0 there. READ THE TWO CLAUSES ABOVE AGAINST ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179, which is what the alias resolves through: this fact sits downstream of that one and is complete wherever it is. EXPORTED AND READ BY NOTHING THIS YEAR is unchanged, and so is the $0-off-regime property: the post-section-179 net re-applies ../appliesPtpSection469 in its own Switch exactly as its pre-section-179 twin does.

Fact.Name: This PTP's overall gain, as §163(d) investment income (Form 4952 line 4a component)
Fact.Description:
THE FIGURE: the positive part of the smaller of ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179 (the Schedule E-side result) and ../ptpSection469NetWithSection1231 (the result with the box 10 section 1231 amount combined). A passive box 10 LOSS of the same PTP makes the combined result the smaller, and the net gain portion that step 2 makes nonpassive is that combined result; the income the loss is allowed against is passive income (Schedule E column (h)), outside investment income under IRC 163(d)(4)(D). A box 10 GAIN makes the Schedule E-side result the smaller: that part of the PTP's overall gain is a net gain from the disposition of property, which Form 4952 routes to line 4d ("Also include on line 4a (or 4d, if applicable)" and "Don’t include on line 4a any net gain from the disposition of property held for investment"), a filer-entered line in this dictionary (form4952:/writableNetGainFromInvestmentPropertyDispositions), so it is not added here.
The rest of this Description is the history of the addend. GreaterOf(../ptpSection469Net, $0) — the second half of a two-sentence printed rule whose first half already ships. "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income. In addition, the nonpassive income is included in investment income to figure your investment interest expense deduction." Sentence one is ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179's §469(k) arm; sentence two is this fact, and the AMOUNT is the same amount — the sum across PTP K-1s (/k1PtpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome) becomes an addend of form4952:/section163dInvestmentIncome.
WHY 4h AND NOT 4a, since the printed phrase is "investment income" and Form 4952 collects gross investment income on line 4a. The two are the same number here, and the chain is worth stating rather than assuming: line 4c is 4a less 4b (qualified dividends), and a PTP's overall §469(k) gain is ordinary income, never a qualified dividend, so it survives 4b intact into 4c. Lines 4f and 4g now ship as independent addends; adding the PTP amount at 4h remains arithmetically identical to adding it at 4a because a PTP's overall operating gain is not a gain from the disposition of investment property and is not part of the election.
THE DIRECTION IS TAX-REDUCING, stated plainly because it is the opposite of the deferral it replaces. Line 6 is max($0, line 4h minus line 5) and line 8 is the smaller of line 3 and line 6, so a larger 4h can only RAISE the §163(d) ceiling and ALLOW MORE investment interest expense. While this leg was unbuilt the omission was taxpayer-ADVERSE and could not under-state tax; now that it ships, correctness rests on the printed instruction rather than on a safe direction. Witnessed end-to-end by form4952/ptp-gain-raises-the-163d-ceiling, where the same return's line 8 moves from $0 to $2,000 and its line-7 carryforward from $3,000 to $1,000.
NO GATE OF ITS OWN, deliberately: ../ptpSection469Net re-applies ../appliesPtpSection469 inside its own Switch and is $0 on every K-1 the regime does not govern, so the floor here is already $0 off-regime and a second gate would be dead weight pretending to be a safeguard.
AND IT IS NOT ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179, which carries the identical value on a PTP: that fact ALSO carries ordinary nonpassive box-1 income on every non-PTP K-1, and that is the wrong income. §163(d)(5)(A)(ii) includes a trade-or-business interest in "property held for investment" only when it is "(I) … not a passive activity, and (II) with respect to which the taxpayer does not materially participate" — so a MATERIALLY-PARTICIPATED business interest is excluded by the statute's own second condition, and reading that fact here would sweep every active partner's business income into the §163(d) ceiling. The two arms agree only inside the regime, and only this fact is confined to it.
PER PTP, NEVER POOLED: the aggregate below sums the POSITIVE PARTS, not the positive part of the pooled net. Two PTPs, one +$3,000 and one −$4,000, contribute $3,000, not $0 — pinned by scheduleE/ptp-469-two-ptps-applied-separately.

Fact.Name: Total PTP overall gain entering §163(d) investment income (Form 4952 line 4a component)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum of each K-1's /formK1s/*/ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome — the return-level addend form4952:/section163dInvestmentIncome (Form 4952 line 4h) reads. It lives here rather than as an inline CollectionSum inside form4952 for the reason /k1NonpassiveActiveNet does: the §469(k) quantity is defined once, in the module that owns the regime, and Form 4952's line-4h Add stays a list of NAMED addends.
THE SUM OF THE POSITIVE PARTS, never the positive part of the sum, and the difference is the whole of §469(k)(1): a PTP with an overall loss contributes $0, it does not cancel another PTP's gain. Pinned by scheduleE/ptp-469-two-ptps-applied-separately.
GATED ON /claimsK1Income, the /k1NonpassiveActiveNet and /scheduleEPartIINetIncome pattern, so a return with no K-1 collection at all resolves Complete-$0 rather than dragging an Incomplete into Form 4952 line 4h — and through it into line 6, line 8 and Schedule A line 9. That is the one real hazard in wiring a collection aggregate into an existing chain, and the gate is how this fact answers it; form4952/form4952-unanswered-complete-safe is the case that holds it, on a fixture that declares no /formK1s key whatsoever.
Rounded to whole dollars, which changes nothing: every summand is already whole, because /formK1s/*/ptpSection469Net is itself Rounded. Form 4952 line 4h applies no rounding of its own and this addend does not give it one.

Fact.Name: This PTP's box-12 §179 share after the Form 4562 Part I taxpayer-level limits
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 12 as it falls on THIS K-1's box-12 share, for a K-1 that is an item-D publicly traded partnership whose items are PASSIVE (../appliesPtpSection469): the SMALLER of the amount this K-1's §704(d)/§1366(d) basis can absorb (../basisAllowedSection179), the return's line-5 dollar limitation (/section179TaxpayerDollarLimit) and the line-11 business-income limitation (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit, taxpayer-level despite its rental-era name). It is the SAME three-way minimum ../section179ColumnJ takes, on the same three operands, because the partner instruction that forks on item D forks only on the DESTINATION of the amount, never on its size: "Report the amount from Form 4562, Part I, line 12, allocable to a passive activity using the Instructions for Form 8582. If the amount isn't a passive activity deduction, report it in column (j) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28. However, if the box in item D of Schedule K-1 is checked, report this amount following the rules for PTPs under Publicly traded partnerships, earlier." Form 4562 Part I is completed once for the taxpayer and its line 12 is the figure both destinations start from.
THE ORDER OF THE SWITCH IS LOAD-BEARING, not tidiness. The FIRST arm returns $0 for a K-1 that elects nothing and the SECOND for a K-1 the §469(k) regime does not govern, and both arms sit AHEAD of any read of the two taxpayer-level limits. LesserOf evaluates BOTH operands, and /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit CAN be Incomplete — a rental element that claims five-year property and leaves its basis unanswered makes the aggregate line-2 base Incomplete. Without those two arms that Incompleteness would reach every /formK1s item on such a return, including items with no box-12 amount and items that are not PTPs at all. Pinned by the node tests scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-does-not-contaminate (no election) and scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-refuses-an-electing-k1 (an ELECTING non-PTP K-1, where ../section179ColumnJ is Incomplete and this fact is a Complete $0 because the regime gate fires first).
IT DOES NOT READ ../section179OnPtp OR ../section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited, and that is a decision rather than an omission. Those two flags are exactly the refusals the closure retires on these facts; gating on them would make this fact $0 on the entire population it exists for, and the closure would have to re-body it. The refusals stay standing meanwhile, so no return files on this number today.
NAMED GAP — THE MULTI-ELECTOR RETURN. When a second activity anywhere on the return also elects, /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit and /rentalSection179IncomeLimit are ONE cap the two activities must share, and no allocation intake exists; that population is refused by /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities, which this fact does NOT read and does not retire. The value it computes there is the un-apportioned minimum, which can over-state this K-1's share. The successor is /section179AllocationByActivity, and the pro rata allocation is the sibling draft slice k1-s179-draft-passive-fold's work, not this one's.
NAMED GAP — THE AT-RISK LEG. A K-1 that is not fully at risk must cap the activity's loss INCLUDING this §179 share under §465 before §469 reaches it; ../atRiskAllowedLoss caps exactly one class today, the ordinary box-1 loss. This fact takes no at-risk operand, so on a not-fully-at-risk PTP it can allow more §179 than §465 permits. That population is refused by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited, and the at-risk leg is the sibling draft slice's work.
COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 on every K-1 that elects nothing and on every K-1 the §469(k) regime does not govern, which today is every committed row.
WIRED. REBODIED ONTO ../atRiskAllowedSection179, which COLLAPSES this fact and ../section179AllocatedShare into one computation and closes BOTH named gaps above. The three-way minimum this fact used to take independently is exactly what ../section179AllocatedShare takes - allocated pro rata to box 12 across the return's electing activities, so THE MULTI-ELECTOR GAP is gone - and ../atRiskAllowedSection179 then caps it at what is left of ../amountAtRisk after the box-1 leg, so THE AT-RISK GAP is gone too. What survives of this fact is the REGIME GATE and the name: a $0 for every K-1 the section 469(k) regime does not govern, so a non-PTP share cannot leak into a PTP combination. Byte-identical to the retired expression on a single electing, fully-at-risk PTP. THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE beginning "IT DOES NOT READ ../section179OnPtp OR ../section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited" still holds and is now the reason the closure works: neither flag is read here, the first is narrowed to the unanswered-participation PTP and the second has been removed. Narrower still - the first now holds only the GENERAL-PARTNER unanswered-participation PTP, and the LIMITED-partner half reaches this fact through ../appliesPtpSection469 exactly as an answered-false PTP does.

Fact.Name: This PTP's CURRENT-year signed amount WITH the box-12 §179 share in it (§469(k) step 1)
Fact.Description:
../ptpCurrentYearNet less ../ptpSection179Allowed: the current-year half of step 1's combination once the box-12 §179 share is one of its terms. Step 1 says to "Combine any current-year income, gains, and losses, and any prior-year unallowed losses to see if you have an overall gain or loss from the PTP." and to "Include only the same types of income and losses you would include in your net income or loss from a non-PTP passive activity"; the Form 8582 instructions define that inclusion set as the activity's PASSIVE ACTIVITY DEDUCTIONS — "Passive activity deductions include all deductions from activities that are passive activities for the current tax year" — and a §179 share allocable to a passive activity is one of them. So the share reduces an overall gain or deepens an overall loss; it is not a column (j) entry on a passive PTP, which is what the two standing guards protect until the closure unit retires them.
THIS IS THE POST-§179 TWIN. ../ptpCurrentYearNet is the PRE-§179 one and KEEPS THAT ROLE UNCHANGED — it is what ../ptpSection469Net, ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179, /k1NonpassiveActiveNet and through them the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation read, because Pub 946 ch.2 and i4562 Line 11 both say to figure that taxable income "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction". THE NAMING IS ASYMMETRIC and it is recorded rather than repaired: the module's other twin pair spells the pre-§179 half explicitly (../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 against ../partIINonpassivePart), while here the UNQUALIFIED name is the PRE-§179 half. Renaming the shipping fact would be a fact deletion, which owes four allowlists and a completeness-probe baseline regeneration and moves every committed baseline row for no change in meaning.
NO GATE OF ITS OWN, deliberately, and the reason is specific: BOTH operands re-apply ../appliesPtpSection469 inside their own Switches, so this fact is $0 on every K-1 the regime does not govern without testing the gate a third time.
THE AT-RISK ORDERING GAP IS INHERITED, not introduced. ../ptpCurrentYearNet already carries the box-1 loss AFTER §704(d) basis and §465 at-risk; the §179 share subtracted here has had basis applied (../basisAllowedSection179) but not at-risk. On a not-fully-at-risk PTP this fact therefore subtracts more than §465 allows. That population is refused today by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited and the at-risk leg belongs to the sibling draft slice k1-s179-draft-passive-fold. SPENT IN BOTH HALVES. The at-risk leg landed in that slice and this closure wired it - ../ptpSection179Allowed now reads ../atRiskAllowedSection179, so the subtrahend here IS section 465-capped and the gap this paragraph names is closed. /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited, which could no longer fire, has been removed. Witness: node-test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-at-risk-limited-share-capped.

Fact.Name: This PTP's overall §469(k) gain or loss WITH the box-12 §179 share in the combination
Fact.Description:
Step 1's signed overall result with the §179 term inside it: ../ptpCurrentYearNetAfterSection179 less ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss, $0 when ../appliesPtpSection469 is false. POSITIVE is an overall GAIN, NEGATIVE an overall LOSS — the same reading ../ptpSection469Net carries, on the same two operands, with the current-year half replaced by its post-§179 twin.
THE GATE IS RE-APPLIED HERE for the reason the shipping twin gives in its own comment: a carry-in answered on a K-1 that is not a passive PTP must not leak a negative overall result through ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss, which is complete-safe but not regime-gated.
WHAT IT WILL DECIDE, once the closure unit wires it. An overall GAIN is nonpassive income reported in Schedule E Part II column (k); an overall LOSS is suspended in full and carried forward against income from the SAME PTP. Both routes exist today off ../ptpSection469Net; this fact is the figure they should read once the §179 term is part of the combination.
READ BY NOTHING TODAY, stated as a measured property rather than an intention: it is downstream of ../ptpCurrentYearNetAfterSection179 and upstream of nothing in this dictionary, so it closes no cycle and moves no 2025 figure. In particular ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 and ../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome (Form 4952 line 4h) still read the PRE-§179 ../ptpSection469Net. Leaving 4h on the pre-§179 net OVER-states §163(d) investment income by the §179 share once this term ships, which is taxpayer-favourable, so it is named here as an open decision for the closure unit rather than settled by a draft.
WIRED. THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE HEADED "READ BY NOTHING TODAY" IS SPENT. Three facts read this one now: ../partIINonpassivePart takes GreaterOf(this, $0) as its leading section 469(k) arm, which is Schedule E Part II column (k); ../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome takes the same positive part for Form 4952 line 4h; and ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179 takes the negative part, which ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut then exports. The open decision that paragraph named IS SETTLED, the way it leaned: line 4h moved to this net, because the printed rule ties both destinations to ONE quantity ("If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income. In addition, the nonpassive income is included in investment income to figure your investment interest expense deduction"). ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 still reads the PRE-section-179 ../ptpSection469Net, and MUST: it is the Form 4562 line-11 base.

Fact.Name: This PTP's suspended loss carried OUT with the box-12 §179 share in the combination
Fact.Description:
max($0, minus ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179): the post-§179 twin of ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut. Because the §469(k) regime allows NOTHING of an overall loss in the current year, the amount suspended is the whole negative part of step 1's signed result — and once the §179 share is a term of that combination, a passive PTP's §179 deduction DEEPENS the suspension rather than reaching column (j). The same K-1 carries $20,000 out on the pre-§179 twin and $25,000 here.
SAME STORAGE CONVENTION as the shipping twin: a POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, never a signed loss, so it pairs with ../writablePtpPriorYearUnallowedLoss.
NO Export DECLARED, and that is deliberate rather than forgotten. ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut already carries Export downstreamFacts="true"; declaring a second export for the same PTP would hand a consumer TWO carry-out figures for one partnership with nothing on the surface to say which is the filed one. Which of the two is the export is the closure's decision, made when the term is actually wired into the filed return. ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut keeps the Export and is this fact's ALIAS; there is exactly one exported carry-out per PTP, and it is the post-section-179 amount.
DISJOINT FROM THE OTHER TWO CARRYFORWARDS, the same way its twin is: a box-1 loss disallowed by §704(d) basis or §465 at-risk never reaches ../ptpCurrentYearNet at all and is tracked by ../basisSuspendedLoss and ../atRiskSuspendedLoss. Reading this one alone as the PTP's whole carryforward would UNDER-state it.
THE BOX 10 TERM IS NOW INSIDE IT. The operand is ../ptpSection469NetWithSection1231, which is ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179 plus the box 10 net section 1231 amount step 1 combines. The partner instructions' own example states the identity: a 12,000 Schedule E loss beside a 7,200 Form 4797 gain carries forward 4,800. A K-1 with no box 10 answer, or one outside the regime, adds $0, so its carry-out is unchanged.

Fact.Name: This PTP's box 10 net section 1231 amount, as a term of its own section 469(k) combination
Fact.Description:
The box 10 (box 9 on Form 1120-S) net section 1231 gain or loss that step 1 of the partner instructions' PTP procedure combines with the rest of this PTP's items: "Combine any current-year income, gains, and losses, and any prior-year unallowed losses to see if you have an overall gain or loss from the PTP." The instructions' own example puts a Form 4797 gain inside that combination.
FIVE ARMS. Box 10 unanswered: $0, Complete, so a K-1 recorded without box 10 adds nothing and every total over /formK1s stays as complete as it was. A K-1 outside the section 469(k) regime (../appliesPtpSection469 false): $0; its box 10 amount reaches Form 4797 by the general rule alone. A GAIN under the regime: the gain. A LOSS under the regime answered as from a passive activity (../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity Yes): the loss. Any other loss (answered nonpassive, or unanswered): $0, because a nonpassive loss is admitted on Form 4797 in full and is not a passive item, and an unanswered one already refuses the return through Form 4797.
IT DOES NOT MOVE THE AMOUNT ONTO SCHEDULE E. The gain stays on Form 4797 line 2 in full, as the example says ("Report the $7,200 gain on the appropriate line of Form 4797"); this term only decides how much of the PTP's Schedule E loss the gain lets through (../ptpSection1231AllowedScheduleELoss) and how much is carried forward (../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179). Counting it on Schedule E as well would count box 10 twice.

Fact.Name: This PTP's overall section 469(k) result with its box 10 section 1231 amount combined
Fact.Description:
Step 1 of the partner instructions' PTP procedure with every term in it: ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179 (box 1, the box 2 and 3 rental income, the box 12 section 179 share and the prior-year unallowed loss) plus ../ptpSection1231AmountInCombination (the box 10 net section 1231 amount). POSITIVE is an overall GAIN, NEGATIVE an overall LOSS, $0 on every K-1 the regime does not govern, because both operands are $0 there.
WHAT IT DECIDES. An overall LOSS: "the losses are allowed to the extent of the income, and the excess loss is carried forward", so the negative part of this figure is the carry-out (../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179). Where the income is a box 10 gain, the loss it lets through is ../ptpSection1231AllowedScheduleELoss. The instructions' example: a 12,000 Schedule E loss and a 7,200 Form 4797 gain give an overall loss of 4,800.
A PASSIVE BOX 10 LOSS beside a Schedule E-side GAIN: the loss is allowed to the extent of that income (../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncome, entered on Form 4797 through ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedOnForm4797), the income it is allowed against prints in column (h), and a positive combined result is the net gain portion that column (k) and Form 4952 line 4h carry.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DECIDE. On a PTP whose box 10 GAIN is larger than its Schedule E loss, the combined overall gain sits on Form 4797 as section 1231 gain, a net gain from the disposition of property; Form 4952 routes such a gain to line 4d, which the filer enters, so line 4h keeps the Schedule E-side result (../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome).

Fact.Name: This PTP's Schedule E loss allowed against its own box 10 section 1231 gain
Fact.Description:
The part of this PTP's overall Schedule E loss that its own box 10 net section 1231 gain lets through this year, as a positive amount: the smaller of the Schedule E-side loss (minus ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179) and the box 10 gain (../ptpSection1231AmountInCombination), floored at $0. The instructions' example: "On Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28, report $7,200 of the losses as a passive loss in column (g)" beside a 7,200 Form 4797 gain and a 12,000 Schedule E loss.
$0 whenever there is nothing to allow: a Schedule E-side gain, a box 10 loss or no box 10 answer, or a K-1 outside the regime (both operands are $0 there). It is Complete $0 when box 10 is unanswered, so a K-1 without box 10 adds nothing to the totals that read it.
WHERE IT GOES. Schedule E line 28 column (g) for this row (../line28ColumnGPassiveLossAllowed), the line 29b column (g) total (/k1Line29bColumnGPassiveLossAllowedTotal), and line 32 (/scheduleEPartIINetIncome, subtracted through /k1PtpSection1231AllowedScheduleELossTotal). The gain itself stays on Form 4797 through form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797; nothing here adds it to Schedule E. Column (k) and the Form 4562 line 11 base are untouched: this is a passive loss, not nonpassive income.

Fact.Name: Total PTP Schedule E loss allowed against the same PTPs' box 10 section 1231 gains
Fact.Description: The sum over every recorded K-1 of ../ptpSection1231AllowedScheduleELoss, as a positive amount: the passive PTP losses Schedule E line 28 column (g) reports because the same PTP's box 10 gain absorbed them. Subtracted in /scheduleEPartIINetIncome and added to /k1Line29bColumnGPassiveLossAllowedTotal. Each PTP is its own figure before the sum; a gain from one PTP never allows another PTP's loss. $0 when /formK1s is not complete.

Fact.Name: This PTP's passive box 10 section 1231 loss allowed against the same PTP's Schedule E-side income
Fact.Description:
The part of a passive box 10 (box 9 on Form 1120-S) net section 1231 LOSS that this publicly traded partnership's own Schedule E-side income absorbs, as a positive amount: the smaller of the loss and the positive part of ../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179. Step 3 of the partner instructions' PTP procedure allows an overall loss "to the extent of the income", and where the combination is an overall gain the loss is allowed in full; both are this one figure.
WHY THE PER-FORM NET. The Form 8582 instructions allocate an activity's unallowed loss among the forms that carry its losses by each form's net loss (the loss less any net income on the same form). A Schedule E side above $0 carries no net loss, so the whole unallowed part of the PTP's loss falls on the Form 4797 amount and the allowed part is exactly the Schedule E-side income; a Schedule E side at or below $0 leaves no income to allow against, and the whole box 10 loss is carried forward inside ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179.
WHERE IT GOES. It is the passive income that the allowed loss offsets, so Schedule E line 28 column (h) prints it (../line28ColumnHPassiveIncome) and column (k) prints only the rest of the Schedule E-side income (../partIINonpassivePart), as the instructions' example does: 8,000 of Schedule E income beside a 3,500 Form 4797 loss prints 4,500 in column (k) and 3,500 in column (h). Line 32 adds it back through /k1PtpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncomeTotal, so line 32 still carries the whole Schedule E-side income.
$0, Complete, on every K-1 this does not describe: no box 10 answer, a box 10 gain or zero, a loss answered nonpassive, a passivity question unanswered, or a K-1 the section 469(k) regime does not govern or cannot yet decide (../appliesPtpSection469 not Complete true).

Fact.Name: This PTP's passive box 10 section 1231 loss allowed this year, for Form 4797 line 2
Fact.Description:
The allowed part of a passive box 10 net section 1231 LOSS of a publicly traded partnership, as a positive amount; form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 enters it negated on Form 4797 line 2. Two arms, keyed on the entire disposition of the partner's interest (../ptpEntireDispositionApplies), with no catch-all.
NOT DISPOSED: ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncome, the loss allowed to the extent of the same PTP's Schedule E-side income; the rest is carried forward.
DISPOSED of the entire interest in a fully taxable transaction: the whole loss, because the PTP's losses are not limited by the passive loss rules in that year. The Schedule E side then releases only its own net loss (../ptpDispositionReleasedLoss subtracts this amount), so the box 10 loss is deducted once, on Form 4797, where the instructions report it.
$0 on every K-1 that has no passive box 10 loss under the section 469(k) regime. Incomplete while the disposition question of such a PTP is undecided, so Form 4797 line 2 waits for it rather than taking either arm.

Fact.Name: Total PTP Schedule E-side income that the same PTPs' passive box 10 losses absorb (Schedule E line 28 column (h))
Fact.Description: The sum over every recorded K-1 of ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncome: the publicly traded partnership income that Schedule E line 28 prints as passive income in column (h) because the same partnership's passive box 10 loss is allowed against it on Form 4797. Added to Schedule E line 32 (/scheduleEPartIINetIncome) and to the Part II term of the Form 8582 line 6 modified adjusted gross income (/section8582MagiPartIIAndIIITerms), where the allowed Form 4797 loss already enters through Form 4797. Each PTP is its own figure before the sum. $0 when /formK1s is not complete.

Fact.Name: You disposed of your ENTIRE interest in this partnership/S-corp activity in 2025 (§469(g))
Fact.Description: Did you sell, exchange, or otherwise dispose of your ENTIRE interest in this partnership or S corporation's activity during 2025 — not merely a partial interest or a distribution? Screen text: "Did you dispose of your entire interest in [this K-1's activity] this year?" Help text: entire disposition of a passive (or former passive) activity interest can release suspended and current-year losses from the §469 passive-activity limitation in full (IRC 469(g)(1)(A)); a partial disposition does not (Pub. 925 (2025), "Partial disposition of an activity"). Asked when a recorded K-1 exists; most K-1s answer No or leave it unanswered. Unanswered defaults to No (../disposedEntireInterest, complete safe) — the conservative direction, since silently assuming a disposition happened would invent a benefit nobody claimed. Answering Yes leads to the qualifying-transaction question below, which IS a condition of allowance and does NOT default. Feeds ../dispositionReleaseApplies and, through it, ../dispositionReleasedLoss.

Fact.Name: Disposed of entire interest, complete safe
Fact.Description: ../writableDisposedEntireInterest when answered, else false. The safe default for a question almost no K-1 needs: unanswered means "no disposition claimed", so every existing K-1 item resolves exactly as it did before this fact existed.

Fact.Name: The disposition was a single fully-taxable sale to an unrelated party (§469(g)(1)(A)/(B))
Fact.Description: On the disposition you just described, was ALL of your realized gain or loss recognized in ONE transaction (not an installment sale), to a person who is NOT related to you under the section 267(b)/707(b)(1) family and common-control tests? Screen text: "Was this a single sale in which you reported all of your gain or loss, to someone who is not related to you?" Help text: both conditions must be true for the loss release; an installment sale releases losses only in the same proportion as the gain you report each year (Pub. 925 (2025), "Installment sale of an entire interest" — not modeled here, so answer No if this was an installment sale) and a sale to a related party (a family member, or an entity you or your family control) suspends the loss until an unrelated party later acquires the interest (IRC 469(g)(1)(B)) — also not modeled, so answer No there too. Asked only when ../disposedEntireInterest is true. CONDITION OF ALLOWANCE: unanswered here is Incomplete, never defaulted — ../dispositionReleaseConditionUnanswered refuses the return rather than guessing either direction. Answering No (or leaving the return with a knockout standing) simply forgoes the release; the loss stays suspended under the ordinary §469 rules. Feeds ../dispositionReleaseApplies.

Fact.Name: Disposition claimed but the qualifying-transaction condition is unanswered (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True exactly when ../disposedEntireInterest is true (the filer claims an entire-interest disposition) and ../writableDispositionFullyTaxableToUnrelatedParty is unanswered. Kleene-safe: when ../disposedEntireInterest is false the All() short-circuits on that operand and never looks at the second, so a K-1 that never claims a disposition can never set this flag regardless of the other writable's state. IsComplete is legal here because its operand is the raw Writable.

Fact.Name: A recorded K-1 claims an entire-interest disposition with the qualifying condition unanswered (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when at least one recorded /formK1s item is flagged by ../formK1s/*/dispositionReleaseConditionUnanswered. Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s collection root, the idiom /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities and its siblings use over this same collection: a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete, and a return with no K-1 has nothing to claim a disposition on. Keys /knockoutK1DispositionReleaseUnanswered.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a K-1 claims an entire-interest disposition with the qualifying condition unanswered
Fact.Description:
A recorded Schedule K-1 answers ../formK1s/*/writableDisposedEntireInterest TRUE (the filer claims they disposed of their entire interest in this partnership or S corporation's activity in 2025) but leaves ../formK1s/*/writableDispositionFullyTaxableToUnrelatedParty unanswered. IRC 469(g)(1)(A)/(B) makes both the entire-interest disposition AND the fully-taxable/unrelated-party conditions prerequisites of the loss release; without an answer this dictionary cannot tell a qualifying sale from an installment sale or a related-party transfer, either of which forfeits or defers the release. Refusing rather than defaulting either direction is the correct posture for a condition of allowance on a return that is already claiming the benefit: defaulting to Yes would invent an unearned release, and defaulting to No would silently decide against a filer who may in fact qualify.
NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION: only a K-1 that affirmatively claims a disposition reaches this guard; every other K-1 (the overwhelming majority) resolves ../disposedEntireInterest to false and is untouched. Answering the second question, either way, clears the refusal — Yes computes the release (../dispositionReleasedLoss, wired into ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss); No leaves the loss suspended under the ordinary §469 rules exactly as if no disposition had been claimed.
A K-1 that answers both questions Yes has its release figured (../dispositionReleasedLoss, the PTP twin ../ptpDispositionReleasedLoss, the former passive ../formerPassiveDispositionReleasedLoss), except a box 22 or 23 statement or a passive non-PTP section 179 elector, which /knockoutPassiveEntireDispositionReleaseNotBuilt refuses. It is a flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member.

Fact.Name: Prior-year unallowed passive loss from this K-1's activity (non-PTP §469 carry-in)
Fact.Description: The passive loss from THIS K-1's activity that prior years suspended and carried forward under IRC 469(b), supplied as an attested input, entered not less than zero. Screen text: "How much of this partnership or S corporation's passive loss was suspended (not deductible) in a prior year and carried forward to 2025?" Help text: this is the running total Form 8582 would have tracked in Part IV column (c) for this activity across every prior year; leave blank if none. Asked when this K-1's activity is passive this year (../lossIsPassive) or was disposed of (../disposedEntireInterest). On a passive, non-PTP K-1 it enters the Form 8582 pool with the current-year result (../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLossInPool); on a disposition it feeds the release. Unanswered defaults to $0 via ../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss (complete safe) — the conservative direction, since a carry-in can only ever ENLARGE the released loss, never shrink it, so defaulting it to zero never manufactures a benefit the filer did not attest to. SAME SHAPE AS ../writablePtpPriorYearUnallowedLoss (positive magnitude, subtracted/added rather than signed, Min $0 Limit) — the general non-PTP twin of that PTP-only carry-in.

Fact.Name: Prior-year unallowed passive loss, complete safe
Fact.Description: ../writablePriorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss when answered, else $0 — the same IsComplete-guard idiom as ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss, and the same reasoning: a carry-in only ever enlarges the released loss, so zero is the safe default.

Fact.Name: This K-1's prior-year unallowed passive loss entering the Form 8582 pool this year
Fact.Description: ../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss for a passive, non-PTP K-1 whose activity was not disposed of with the release (../dispositionReleaseApplies false, no statement or section 179 refusal): Form 8582 combines the activity's current income or loss with its prior-year unallowed loss (Part V column (c)), so the carry-in reduces this K-1's pool contribution (../passiveNetAfterSection179). $0 otherwise: a PTP carries its own (../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss), and a released disposition already folds it in.

Fact.Name: This K-1's activity was disposed of entirely to an unrelated person in a fully taxable transaction
Fact.Description: True when the filer says the entire interest in this K-1's activity was disposed of (../disposedEntireInterest) and answers Yes to the fully taxable, unrelated-party question. Complete false otherwise, including while that question is unanswered (the unanswered case is refused by /knockoutK1DispositionReleaseUnanswered).

Fact.Name: A former passive activity's prior-year unallowed loss released by the entire disposition
Fact.Description: For a K-1 whose activity is NOT passive this year (a former passive activity), with a qualifying entire disposition and no box 22 or 23 activity statement: the whole prior-year unallowed passive loss carried in (../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss plus the PTP carry-in ../ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss). Section 469(f)(1)(A) allows it against this year's income from the activity and section 469(g)(1)(A) releases the rest on the disposition, so the whole carry-in is deductible, as a nonpassive loss, either way. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: The entire interest in this passive publicly traded partnership was disposed of in a fully taxable transaction
Fact.Description: True when ../entireDispositionQualifies and this K-1 is a passive PTP under the section 469(k) regime (../appliesPtpSection469). The PTP's losses are released on the entire disposition of the partner's interest in the PTP: ../ptpDispositionReleasedLoss.

Fact.Name: A disposed publicly traded partnership's overall loss released as nonpassive
Fact.Description: When ../ptpEntireDispositionApplies: the PTP's overall loss left after the section 469(k) combination (current-year items, the box 12 section 179 share, the box 10 section 1231 amount and the prior-year unallowed loss), less the passive box 10 loss that Form 4797 deducts in full on the disposition (../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedOnForm4797), floored at $0: max($0, minus ../ptpSection469NetWithSection1231 minus that Form 4797 amount). What remains is the Schedule E side's own net loss, the amount ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOutAfterSection179 would otherwise carry out for it; on the entire disposition it is allowed as a loss that is not from a passive activity. A box 10 GAIN adds nothing to the Form 4797 amount, so there the release is the combined overall loss, as before. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: This K-1 claims a fully taxable disposition of an entire passive interest whose loss release this return does not figure
Fact.Description: True when this K-1's activity was disposed of entirely in a fully taxable transaction to an unrelated person (../entireDispositionQualifies), carries a prior-year unallowed passive loss or a current-year loss, and is one of the two sub-cases the release does not figure: (1) a K-1 with a usable box 22 or box 23 activity statement, whose items split into several activities while the carry-in is asked once for the whole K-1, so the per-activity overall gain or loss the Form 8582 instructions combine cannot be formed from the answers; (2) a passive, non-PTP K-1 that passes through a box 12 section 179 deduction, whose release decision would depend on the section 179 share while that share depends, through the Form 4562 line 11 business income limitation, on the release. The return is refused (/knockoutPassiveEntireDispositionReleaseNotBuilt; TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-63). Complete false when any answer is missing.

Fact.Name: Disposed of the entire interest in this rental property in 2025
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Did you sell or otherwise dispose of your entire interest in this rental property during 2025?" HELP TEXT: "Answer Yes if you no longer own any part of this rental activity at the end of 2025. If you sold it to an unrelated person in a transaction in which all gain or loss is recognized, its prior-year unallowed losses and this year's loss are no longer limited by the passive activity rules." ASKED WHEN: the rental carries a prior-year unallowed loss or a current-year loss. UNANSWERED POSTURE: read as No (no release), the conservative direction. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../entireDispositionQualifies.

Fact.Name: This rental's entire disposition was fully taxable and to an unrelated party
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Was the disposition a sale or exchange to someone not related to you in which all your gain or loss was recognized (not an installment sale, a gift, a like-kind exchange or a transfer at death)?" ASKED WHEN: ../writableDisposedEntireInterest is Yes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: refused (/knockoutRentalDispositionReleaseUnanswered). WHAT IT FEEDS: ../entireDispositionQualifies.

Fact.Name: This rental was disposed of entirely to an unrelated person in a fully taxable transaction
Fact.Description: True when both disposition answers on this rental are Yes. Complete false when either is unanswered or No.

Fact.Name: This rental claims an entire disposition with the fully taxable question unanswered
Fact.Description: True when ../writableDisposedEntireInterest is Yes and ../writableDispositionFullyTaxableToUnrelatedParty is unanswered. Read by /knockoutRentalDispositionReleaseUnanswered.

Fact.Name: This disposed rental has an overall loss that leaves Form 8582
Fact.Description: True when ../entireDispositionQualifies and the rental's overall result, its at-risk-allowed current net less its prior-year unallowed loss (../netAfterPriorLoss), is a loss. The Form 8582 instructions combine the activity's income, losses and prior-year unallowed losses; an overall loss is not entered on Form 8582 and is deducted in full (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-62). Then the rental contributes nothing to the Form 8582 pool (../activeEligibleNet and ../nonActiveNet are $0) and its overall loss is its nonpassive Part I net (../repAwareNonpassiveNet). An overall gain stays on Form 8582 as usual.

Fact.Name: This rental's at-risk-allowed loss that enters the Form 8582 pool
Fact.Description: ../atRiskDeductibleLoss, or $0 when ../dispositionReleasesOverallLoss (a disposed rental with an overall loss is not on Form 8582). The per-property numerator of the line 22 ratable suspended share.

Fact.Name: Total of the rental at-risk-allowed losses that enter the Form 8582 pool
Fact.Description: The collection sum of /rentalProperties/*/atRiskDeductibleLossInPool: the denominator of the per-property ratable line 22 suspended share, leaving out a disposed rental whose overall loss is deducted in full. Equals /rentalAtRiskDeductibleLossTotal on a return with no such disposition. $0 when the rental list is not answered.

Fact.Name: A rental claims an entire disposition with the fully taxable question unanswered (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when the return claims Schedule E rentals and at least one rental is flagged by /rentalProperties/*/dispositionReleaseConditionUnanswered. Keys /knockoutRentalDispositionReleaseUnanswered.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a rental claims an entire disposition with the fully taxable question unanswered
Fact.Description: We can't file this return yet. You told us you disposed of your entire interest in a rental property. Tell us whether it was a fully taxable sale or exchange to someone not related to you: only then are its prior-year unallowed losses released. Fires when /hasRentalWithUnansweredDispositionReleaseCondition. The twin of /knockoutK1DispositionReleaseUnanswered: defaulting Yes would release losses an installment sale or a related-party transfer does not release, defaulting No would decide against a filer who may qualify.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a disposition of an entire passive interest whose loss release this return does not figure
Fact.Description: We can't file this return yet. You disposed of your entire interest in a partnership or S corporation activity that has losses, and its Schedule K-1 either carries a statement splitting it into several activities (box 22 or box 23) or passes through a section 179 deduction on a passive activity. This return cannot yet figure the release of that activity's losses. Fires when any K-1 has ../entireDispositionReleaseNotBuilt. Guarded by IsComplete on /formK1s. Every other disposed passive activity (a rental, a PTP, a K-1 beside other passive activities, a former passive activity) has its release figured (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-62, IN-63). NOT COVERED: an estate or trust K-1 and a Form 4835 farm rental, which have no disposition question on this return.

Fact.Name: This rental property carries the royalty code 6 on Schedule E line 1b
Fact.Description: True when ../writableLine1bPropertyTypeCode is answered 6 (royalties). Royalty property is reported in the royalty activity (line 4, /writableRoyaltyIncome and its siblings), not as rents on line 3, and royalty income not derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business is portfolio income that the passive activity rules leave out. A rental property coded 6 would put royalties into rents and into the Form 8582 pool, so the return is refused (/knockoutRentalPropertyCodedAsRoyalty). Complete false when the code is unanswered or another code.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a rental property is coded 6 (royalties) on Schedule E line 1b
Fact.Description: We can't file this return yet. One of your rental properties is marked as royalty property (code 6). Royalties are reported in the royalty section of Schedule E, not as rents, and are not passive income. Enter the royalty as royalty income instead, or choose the property's type code. Fires when the return claims Schedule E rentals and any rental property has ../codedAsRoyaltyProperty.

Fact.Name: The §469(g)(1)(A) entire-interest disposition release applies to this passive, non-PTP K-1 this year
Fact.Description:
Ten conjuncts: (1) ../disposedEntireInterest, (2) ../writableDispositionFullyTaxableToUnrelatedParty is answered, (3) and TRUE, (4) ../lossIsPassive (the activity is classified passive this year — a former-passive activity's release, IRC 469(f), is a further unbuilt residue), (5) NOT ../appliesPtpSection469 (the PTP leg is its own item-4 procedure inside the per-PTP pool, a separate residual), (6) NOT ../passiveActivitySharesUsable (a usable box-23 per-activity statement reclassifies this item below the whole-item grain this release computes at — unbuilt), (7) NOT ../electsSection179 (a section-179 electing K-1's ../passiveNet feeds ../section179PassiveActivityDeduction's own subtraction chain, which the leading zero-out case below would corrupt — unbuilt), and OTHER passive activities on the return (rentals, estate or trust K-1s, farm rentals, other K-1s) no longer keep the release out: the Form 8582 instructions combine only THIS activity's income, losses and prior-year unallowed losses, and an overall loss leaves Form 8582 entirely (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-62). A fully taxable entire disposition that conjuncts (6) and (7) keep out (a box 22 or 23 statement), or a passive non-PTP section 179 elector, with a loss to release, is refused (../entireDispositionReleaseNotBuilt, /knockoutPassiveEntireDispositionReleaseNotBuilt) rather than left suspended. Kleene-safe: conjunct (1) being false short-circuits the whole All() before conjunct (2)'s IsComplete or conjunct (3)'s raw writable are read, so a K-1 that never claims a disposition is never made Incomplete by an unanswered qualifying-transaction question it was never asked. This fact never resolves Incomplete.
OTHER PASSIVE ACTIVITIES DO NOT MATTER. Section 469(g)(1)(A)(ii) measures the release against the net income of all other passive activities, but the Form 8582 instructions figure it by combining only THIS activity's income, losses and prior-year unallowed losses: an overall loss is not entered on Form 8582 and is deducted in full, and the other activities go through Form 8582 as usual. The two reach the same taxable income (the part the statute leaves passive is absorbed by the other activities' net income it is measured against), so neither this fact nor ../dispositionReleasedLoss reads another activity (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-62).
An additional box-22 statement guard now prevents this whole-K-1 release when ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable is true, because the statement splits the K-1 into activity-level at-risk amounts below this release's grain. The ten historical conjuncts above are otherwise unchanged.

Fact.Name: The §469(g)(1)(A) released loss from this K-1's activity (nonpassive, Schedule E line 28 col (i))
Fact.Description:
$0 unless ../dispositionReleaseApplies. When it applies: max(0, ../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss − CURRENT_YEAR_NET), where CURRENT_YEAR_NET = ../ordinaryIncome when ≥ 0, else −../atRiskAllowedLoss — the SAME signed current-year-net idiom ../ptpSection469Net already uses (that fact = ptpCurrentYearNet − ptpPriorYearUnallowedLoss; this fact is the same subtraction, floored at $0 because IRC 469(g)(1)(A) only ever RELEASES a loss, never manufactures a negative one). ORDERING (adversarial review MUST FIX 1, 2026-09-09): the disposed activity's OWN current-year result absorbs its own carry-in FIRST; only the excess loss releases. A prior build used LOSS_FOR_YEAR = priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss + max(0, −ordinaryIncome), which never let a current-year GAIN reduce the carry-in and over-released whenever the disposed K-1 also had current-year income — not exercised by Carter's own example (ordinaryIncome = $0 there), caught by the review reading the fact against its own sibling ../ptpSection469Net. Fixed here; see the two new node-test witnesses below.
OTHER PASSIVE ACTIVITIES ON THE RETURN (a second passive K-1, a rental, an estate or trust, a farm rental) do not change this figure: the Form 8582 instructions combine only this activity's own items (TAX-INTERPRETATIONS IN-62). Witnessed by node-test scheduleE/k1-disposition-release-beside-a-second-passive-k1-releases and scheduleE/k1-disposition-release-beside-a-rental-overall-loss.
CARTER'S EXAMPLE, PINNED (Pub. 925 (2025) p.17-18): priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss $2,000, CURRENT_YEAR_NET $0 (ordinaryIncome $0, the example states no current-year operating result, only the carryover), no other K-1 at all. Released = max(0, 2,000 − 0) = $2,000, matching "Carryover losses allowable ... 2,000" exactly. (The example's separate $3,000 allowable CAPITAL loss on the sale itself is a Schedule D/Form 8949 computation, outside this module.)
ROUTES TO ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss (Schedule E line 28 column (i)) — IRC 469(g)(1)(A)'s own text, "treated as a loss which is not from a passive activity", is exactly a column-(i) nonpassive loss.

Fact.Name: This passive K-1's signed net entering the 8582 pool (Form 8582 line 2d component)
Fact.Description:
This K-1's SIGNED contribution to the cross-activity 8582 passive pool (Form 8582 Part I line 2d), AFTER the 704(d)/1366(d) basis and 465 at-risk limits and BEFORE 469. Only a PASSIVE K-1 (../lossIsPassive — participation-based, classifies income and loss) enters: a passive LOSS contributes -../atRiskAllowedLoss; passive INCOME (box 1 >= 0) contributes +../ordinaryIncome; a NONPASSIVE K-1 contributes 0. CollectionSum over this field gives the top-level /k1PassiveNet. Was the top-level /k1PassiveNet body. interpretation:provisional. ONE HOP LONGER NOW. CollectionSum over this field is /k1PassiveNetAfterSection179 — taken over ../passiveNetAfterSection179, which is THIS fact less ../section179PassiveActivityDeduction — and /k1PassiveNet is that aggregate's alias. This fact keeps its PRE-section-179 meaning and every witness above rides it unchanged, because a K-1 with no box-12 amount has a $0 deduction and the two nets are equal there.
AND A PUBLICLY TRADED PARTNERSHIP CONTRIBUTES 0, whichever sign its items carry. IRC 469(k)(1) applies the passive activity rules "separately with respect to items attributable to each publicly traded partnership", and the partner instructions turn that into an instruction about this very form: "Don't report passive income, gains, or losses from a PTP on Form 8582." A PTP is its own pool of one, resolved by ../ptpSection469Net; the leading ../appliesPtpSection469 case is what keeps it out of this one. BEFORE that case a PTP's passive LOSS was netted against other activities' passive income and deducted this year — the thing "a net passive loss from a PTP may not be deducted from other passive income" forbids — and a PTP's passive INCOME absorbed other activities' passive losses. The first error under-stated tax and the second over-stated it; both are gone.
AND A §469(g)(1)(A) DISPOSITION RELEASE CONTRIBUTES 0: when ../dispositionReleaseApplies, the whole activity's current-year and suspended loss is released as NONPASSIVE (../dispositionReleasedLoss, routed to ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss) rather than entering this pool at all — the statute's own words are "treated as a loss which is not from a passive activity". THAT IS THE OVERALL-LOSS CASE ONLY. When the activity's current-year box 1 income is larger than its carry-in (../priorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss), the combined result is an overall gain, nothing is released, and the Instructions for Form 8582 report the income, losses and prior-year unallowed losses as an ordinary passive activity. This fact then contributes the overall gain, max(0, ../ordinaryIncomeCompleteSafe less the carry-in), as passive income, so the income reaches Schedule E column (h) and line 32 net of the carry-in allowed against it; on an overall loss that maximum is $0 and the release carries the whole result.

Fact.Name: Total box-12 §179 elected by this return's K-1s (the allocation ratio's denominator)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/section179Elected), gated on /claimsK1Income so a non-K-1 return resolves Complete $0. This is box 12 AS PRINTED, before any partner-level limitation, and it exists to be the DENOMINATOR of the pro rata allocation below.
WHY BOX 12 AND NOT THE BASIS-LIMITED FIGURE, since the sibling /k1Section179BasisAllowedTotal is what Form 4562 line 8 actually carries. States the allocation "pro rata to box 12", and the two denominators differ only when a K-1's own §704(d) basis cannot absorb its whole share — in which case the per-item cap below (the LesserOf against ../basisAllowedSection179) removes the excess and the shares sum to LESS than the allowed total. That under-allocation is the conservative direction and it is named on ../section179AllocatedShare rather than engineered away, because engineering it away means re-allocating a basis-blocked partner's share to the other partners, which no printed rule authorises.
COMPLETE-SAFE: ../section179Elected is the $0-default alias, so every /formK1s item contributes whether or not box 12 was answered.

Fact.Name: The K-1 leg's Form 4562 Part I line 8 total elected cost, net of §704(d) basis
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/basisAllowedSection179), gated on /claimsK1Income. Form 4562 line 8 is "Total elected cost of section 179 property. Add amounts in column (c), lines 6 and 7", and a K-1 share is a line-6 column (c) entry; the shipping ../section179ColumnJ already takes ../basisAllowedSection179 as that entry, "net of the section 704(d)/1366(d) allocation", so this aggregate takes the same figure rather than a second reading of the same line.
NO Round, deliberately, matching ../basisAllowedSection179's own reason: that fact keeps cents so two independently rounded column-D shares cannot sum a cent above the partner's basis, and rounding the sum here would re-open the gap the remainder closes.
THE RENTAL LEG IS NOT IN IT, and that is the named boundary of this whole slice: a return where a rental element ALSO elects has a second competitor for the same line-5 and line-11 limits, and /k1Section179AllowedTotal below does not subtract it. That population is refused by /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities, which this slice does not touch. The rental competitor is now subtracted one level down, in /formK1s/*/section179AllocatedShare, by the filer's own row share of /section179AllocationByActivity; this total and /k1Section179AllowedTotal are unchanged, and the population computes when every electing activity has a resolving row.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 Part I line 12 as it falls on this return's K-1 leg (taxpayer level)
Fact.Description:
The section 179 deduction the K-1 leg of this return may take in total, before it is allocated to the individual K-1s: LesserOf(/k1Section179BasisAllowedTotal, /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit, /rentalSection179IncomeLimit). Form 4562 line 9 is the smaller of line 5 and line 8 and line 12 caps that at line 11, and both line 5 and line 11 "apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity" — which is exactly why this quantity is computed ONCE here and then divided, rather than per K-1.
THE FIRST ARM IS A COMPLETENESS GUARD, not an optimisation, and it is the same one ../section179ColumnJ documents: LesserOf evaluates BOTH operands, and /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit CAN be Incomplete when a rental element claims five-year property and leaves its basis unanswered. Without the arm that Incompleteness would reach every K-1 on such a return, including K-1s with no box-12 amount at all. Pinned by node-test scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-does-not-contaminate.
AND WHEN A K-1 DOES ELECT ON SUCH A RETURN THIS FACT IS Incomplete, deliberately and by the same reasoning ../section179ColumnJ gives: the line-5 limitation genuinely cannot be figured from a phaseout base the filer has not finished answering, and the return is already refused by that same missing answer. Pinned by scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-refuses-an-electing-k1, where this fact is Incomplete and ../section179PassiveActivityDeduction is nevertheless a Complete $0.
Rounded to whole dollars, matching ../section179ColumnJ, which is the same line 12 taken for a single nonpassive K-1 — and node-test scheduleE/k1-179-nonpassive-flows-column-j asserts both at the same figure so the two readings of line 12 cannot drift apart.

Fact.Name: This K-1's share of the return's allowed §179 deduction, pro rata to box 12
Fact.Description:
The §179 allocation: when /k1Section179AllowedTotal covers /k1Section179BasisAllowedTotal there is nothing to divide and this K-1 takes its whole basis-allowed amount; otherwise it takes the allowed total times this K-1's box 12 over /k1Section179ElectedTotal, capped at its own ../basisAllowedSection179. $0 for a K-1 that elects nothing, and that arm comes FIRST so such a K-1 never reads the taxpayer-level total.
THE RATIO IS A CONVENTION, NOT A PRINTED RULE, and this is the load-bearing disclosure of the whole slice. Form 4562's Line 12 instruction says the limitations "apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity. Therefore, if you have more than one business or activity, you MAY allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them" (emphasis ours), and then prints only the MECHANISM — a "Summary" Form 4562 for the totals, and "On line 12 of the Form 4562 you prepare for each separate business or activity, enter the amount allocated to the business or activity from the 'Summary.'" WHICH amounts is the filer's election, and no intake in this dictionary collects it. Pro rata to box 12 is the default standing in for that election; it is not transcription and is tagged accordingly. The population is refused meanwhile by /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities, which this slice does not read and does not retire, so no return files on this number today.
THE BASIS CAP IS APPLIED AFTER THE RATIO, NOT INSIDE IT, and the consequence is stated rather than hidden: when one K-1's §704(d) basis cannot absorb its pro rata share, the shares sum to LESS than the allowed total. Re-allocating the blocked partner's remainder to the other partners would allow more in total, and no printed rule authorises it, so the under-allocation stands as the conservative direction. It is unreachable today because the multi-elector population is refused.
NO Round, for /formK1s/*/basisAllowedSection179's reason: N independently rounded shares can sum above the one taxpayer-level cap, which is the thing an allocation may never do. The cents stop at the consumers — ../passiveNetAfterSection179 wraps its own Round. Note that a SINGLE electing K-1 never reaches the Divide at all: the covering arm returns ../basisAllowedSection179 whole.
IT IS THE SAME QUANTITY AS ../ptpSection179Allowed ON A SINGLE-ELECTOR RETURN, which is why node-test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-passive-gain-reduced-by-the-179-share asserts both at $15,000. They diverge only where more than one activity elects — and collapsing the two into one fact belongs to the closure, which is what will decide whether the PTP term reads this allocation. COLLAPSED, and the divergence is what settled it. ../ptpSection179Allowed is now Switch(Not(../appliesPtpSection469) -> $0; else ../atRiskAllowedSection179), so on a multi-elector PTP return it takes the APPORTIONED share instead of the un-apportioned minimum, which is the correct one. One computation, two named entry points: this fact for the allocation, that one for the section 469(k) regime gate.
THE FILER'S ROW SHARE IS NOW A CEILING ON THIS SHARE (the K-1 arm of /section179AllocationByActivity). When more than one activity elects AND ../section179AllocationRowResolves, a leading arm takes the smaller of the pro rata share described above and ../section179AllocationRowShare, the amount the filer allocated to this K-1 on its row of the return level allocation. That is the "subtraction of the rental competitor from the K-1 leg's limits" the records contract owed: the K-1 leg's pro rata division still hands out the whole line 5 and line 11 limits within the K-1 leg, and the row share is what stops that whole from being taken beside a rental element taking its own share. The election stands in for the pro rata default wherever the filer made one; the default survives untouched where they did not. Every route downstream (../atRiskAllowedSection179, column (j), the Form 8582 fold, the PTP combination) reads this fact, so the cap is applied once. "The population is refused meanwhile" above is no longer the whole truth: a return whose every electing activity has a resolving row and whose shares fit the limits now files on this number. Witness: scheduleE/j3-179-allocation-two-electing-k1s-share-the-cap (37,500 / 12,500 pro rata, capped to the filer's 30,000 / 10,000).

Fact.Name: This K-1's allocated §179 share allowed by the §465 at-risk limitation
Fact.Description:
../section179AllocatedShare capped at what is left of ../amountAtRisk once the box-1 loss leg has taken its own bite: LesserOf(share, max($0, ../amountAtRisk - ../atRiskAllowedLoss)) when ../atRiskLimitationApplies, else the whole share. The at-risk rules "generally limit the amount of loss and other deductions that you can claim to the amount you could actually lose in the activity. These losses and deductions include a loss on the disposition of assets and THE SECTION 179 EXPENSE DEDUCTION" — so §465 caps the ACTIVITY, not one class within it, and the box-1 loss and the §179 share compete for one pool exactly as they already compete for one basis pool.
THE REMAINDER RATHER THAN A SECOND RATIO, and it is the same choice ../basisAllowedSection179 made on the basis pool, for the same reason: two independently computed shares of one pool can sum above it, a remainder cannot.
