The PRIORITY — box-1 loss first, §179 second — is THIS REPO'S CONVENTION and not a printed rule; Form 6198 prints no allocation between classes, and the partner instructions name the §179 deduction as one of the deductions §465 reaches without saying which yields first. The direction is disclosed: giving the box-1 loss priority never changes the TOTAL allowed (it is capped at the amount at risk either way), only which class carries the suspension, and the two suspensions are tracked separately by ../atRiskSuspendedLoss and ../atRiskSuspendedSection179.
IT IS NOT A REBODY OF ../atRiskAllowedLoss, deliberately. That fact is cleanroom-verified and is read by ../passiveNet and ../ptpCurrentYearNet; folding the §179 share into it while this chain also folds the share in would count the deduction TWICE. AN ARM OF ITS OWN FOR A K-1 THAT ELECTS NOTHING, RESTORED 2026-08-22 (Fable review B1). The paragraph that stood here read: "NO ARM OF ITS OWN FOR A K-1 THAT ELECTS NOTHING, and the omission is deliberate rather than an oversight: ../section179AllocatedShare is already a complete-safe $0 there and is the only value the first arm below returns, so an elects-nothing arm here would be an arm no mutation could distinguish from its absence." IT WAS WRONG, and wrong in a way worth keeping visible: the claim is true of the NOT-AT-RISK-LIMITED arm, whose only operand is ../section179AllocatedShare, and false of the LAST arm, which reads ../amountAtRisk. So a K-1 that elects nothing but answered ../fullyAtRisk FALSE and left ../amountAtRisk blank reached an unanswered input, and this fact - and through it /scheduleEPartIINetIncome - went Incomplete on a return that resolves at base. The arm is mutation-distinguishable after all; the three node tests named in its comment are what distinguish it.
IT IS NOT GATED ON PARTICIPATION, and that matters: §465 comes BEFORE §469 and applies to a NONPASSIVE K-1 too. Node-test scheduleE/k1-179-not-at-risk-refused pins exactly that — a nonpassive K-1 with box-1 INCOME (so ../atRiskAllowedLoss is $0 and the whole at-risk amount is still available), where a $12,000 share is cut to the $5,000 at risk and $7,000 suspends.
COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 for a K-1 that elects nothing, because ../section179AllocatedShare is.
THE PER ACTIVITY ARM (filling the records contract /formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySection179Share): on a box 22 K-1 whose statement is usable (../atRiskActivitySharesUsable, which since this unit requires the 179 column to foot to box 12 whenever the K-1 elects), the single ../amountAtRisk is the wrong grain and this fact reads ../atRiskActivityAllowedSection179Total instead, the sum over the statement of each activity's basis aware 179 share capped at what is left of that activity's own amount at risk after its loss share, held under ../section179AllocatedShare. The remainder rule and the box-1-first priority are unchanged; they are applied per activity. ../atRiskSuspendedSection179 is unchanged in body and agrees with the sum of the per activity suspensions up to rounding. Witnesses: scheduleE/j3-box22-179-column-foots-and-computes-per-activity (share 300 split 200/100 against remaining at-risk 0/4,500: 100 allowed, 200 suspended, where the whole item remainder 5,500 less 2,000 would have allowed all 300) and j3-box22-179-basis-binds-across-two-activities (704(d) before 465, per activity).

Fact.Name: This K-1's allocated §179 share suspended by the §465 at-risk limitation (carryover)
Fact.Description:
../section179AllocatedShare less ../atRiskAllowedSection179: the part of the §179 share §465 disallows this year. "Any loss from an activity to which this section applies not allowed under this section for the taxable year shall be treated as a deduction allocable to such activity in the first succeeding taxable year" — this single-year model REPORTS the amount and applies no carryover, exactly as its sibling ../atRiskSuspendedLoss does for the box-1 leg.
DISJOINT FROM ../atRiskSuspendedLoss BY CONSTRUCTION, which is the point of splitting them: the box-1 leg's suspension is measured against ../basisAllowedLoss and this one against the §179 share, and the two together are what the activity carries out of §465. Adding them is correct; reading either alone as the activity's whole at-risk carryover under-states it.
NO GATE OF ITS OWN: both operands are $0 for a K-1 that elects nothing, so this resolves Complete $0 there without a third test.
EXPORTED, AND READ BY NOTHING IN THIS DICTIONARY, which is the same shape as ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut and is deliberate rather than a loose end: IRC 465(a)(2) makes this a deduction allocable to the activity in the FIRST SUCCEEDING taxable year, and puts a cross-year carryover outside a per-year dictionary. Its box-1 twin ../atRiskSuspendedLoss is consumed by the return-level /k1AtRiskSuspendedLoss instead; no such aggregate is added here, because a section 179 carryover is reported per activity (IRC 179(b)(3)(B)) rather than as one taxpayer figure.

Fact.Name: This K-1's §179 share as an ordinary passive-activity deduction of its own activity
Fact.Description:
../atRiskAllowedSection179 when this K-1's items are PASSIVE and it is NOT a publicly traded partnership; $0 otherwise. After the taxpayer-level Form 4562 Part I limits and the §465 at-risk limitation, a box-12 §179 share allocable to a passive activity is one of that activity's PASSIVE ACTIVITY DEDUCTIONS — "To figure your overall gain or overall loss from all passive activities or any passive activity, take into account only passive activity deductions", and "Passive activity deductions include all deductions from activities that are passive activities for the current tax year". There is no separate §179 class in the Form 8582 pool and none is needed.
THE FORM 8582 PLACEMENT, NAMED IN THE 2025 FORM'S OWN VOCABULARY. A K-1 trade-or-business activity the partner does not materially participate in is a "Passive trade or business activity", which the 2025 instructions route to PART V — "Use Part V to figure the amounts to enter on Part I, lines 2a through 2c" — where column (a) takes the activity's current year net INCOME and column (b) its current year net LOSS. And the unit brief both call these "Worksheet 1 / Worksheet 3"; that was the PRE-2025 name for the same tables, and the 2025 form renames Worksheet 1 to Part IV (rental real estate with active participation) and Worksheet 3 to Part V (all other passive activities). The rename is recorded rather than silently substituted, because a reader checking the decision against the printed form would otherwise find no worksheet by that name.
TWO $0 ARMS AND EACH IS A DIFFERENT POPULATION. A NONPASSIVE K-1, whose share is not a passive activity deduction at all and stays a Schedule E line 28 column (j) entry through the shipping ../section179ColumnJ — "If the amount isn't a passive activity deduction, report it in column (j) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28." And a PASSIVE PTP, whose share is already a term of its own §469(k) step-1 combination through ../ptpSection179Allowed (draft slice 1); without that arm the same deduction would be folded TWICE, once into the PTP combination and once into the cross-activity pool the PTP is forbidden to join. Node-test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-passive-gain-reduced-by-the-179-share asserts this fact at $0 on a PTP that carries a $15,000 share, which is what pins the no-double-fold property.
AT-RISK BEFORE PASSIVE, which is why the operand is ../atRiskAllowedSection179 and not ../section179AllocatedShare: "losses after taking into account first the at-risk limitations and then the passive loss limitations (this form)".
NOT BOX-23-AWARE, AND THAT IS FINE: a usable box-23 statement always has ../electsSection179 false, one of ../passiveActivitySharesUsable's own conjuncts, so no K-1 this fact's leading arm reaches ever has a usable box-23 statement to route around — no rewire needed.

Fact.Name: This passive K-1's Form 8582 Part V net WITH its §179 share folded in
Fact.Description:
../passiveNet less ../section179PassiveActivityDeduction: the activity's current year net as Form 8582 Part V should carry it once the box-12 §179 share is one of its passive activity deductions. A POSITIVE result is a Part V column (a) net income, a NEGATIVE one a column (b) net loss, and the column totals reach Form 8582 Part I lines 2a and 2b.
THIS IS THE POST-§179 TWIN. ../passiveNet is the PRE-§179 one and keeps that role unchanged; it is what /k1PassiveNet, and through it the whole shipping §8582 chain, still reads. The naming follows draft slice 1's: the unqualified name is the pre-§179 half, and renaming the shipping fact would be a fact DELETION owing four allowlists and a completeness-probe baseline regeneration.
NO GATE OF ITS OWN: ../section179PassiveActivityDeduction is already $0 on every K-1 this fold does not reach — non-electing, nonpassive, and PTP — so this fact equals ../passiveNet there without testing any of those three a second time.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated because a reader will look for it: the cross-activity consequences of a deeper passive loss are NOT built here. /overallPassiveNet, the $25,000 special allowance in Form 8582 Part II, the ratable suspended-loss allocation (/k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated) and Schedule E line 32 all still read the pre-§179 chain. Wiring them is the closure's work, and doing it in a draft would move a filed number while both guards still refuse the population.
WIRED. THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE HEADED "WHAT IT DOES NOT DO" IS SPENT, and it was closed by ONE operand change rather than the five it anticipated: /k1PassiveNet - which /overallPassiveNet, /passiveIncomeTotal, /passiveLossTotal, /k1PassiveLoss (and through it /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated and the Form 8582 Part II $25,000 special allowance) and /scheduleEPartIINetIncome all read - is now the alias of /k1PassiveNetAfterSection179, the CollectionSum over THIS field. Every consumer that paragraph listed therefore carries the section 179 share without one of them being edited.

Fact.Name: Aggregate passive K-1 net WITH the §179 shares folded in (Form 8582 line 2 twin)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/passiveNetAfterSection179), gated on /claimsK1Income: the post-§179 twin of /k1PassiveNet, which is the Part II K-1s' aggregate signed contribution to the cross-activity Form 8582 pool. Rounded to whole dollars, matching its pre-§179 twin, and every summand is already whole because ../passiveNetAfterSection179 Rounds.
READ BY NOTHING TODAY, stated as a measured property rather than an intention: it is downstream of ../passiveNetAfterSection179 and upstream of nothing in this dictionary, so it closes no cycle and moves no 2025 figure. /overallPassiveNet, /otherPassiveNet and the whole Form 8582 Part I chain still read /k1PassiveNet. Switching them is the closure unit's work.
WIRED. THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS SPENT AND ITS SECOND SENTENCE IS NOW BACKWARDS: /k1PassiveNet is the ALIAS of this fact, so the whole Form 8582 Part I chain reads this one through that name. The NAME did not move - five facts read /k1PassiveNet and it carries the module's Export and its clean-room nominations - the COMPUTATION did.

Fact.Name: This K-1's NONPASSIVE Schedule E Part II contribution, BEFORE the §179 deduction
Fact.Description:
The nonpassive part of this K-1's Schedule E Part II line-32 contribution, figured WITHOUT the section 179 deduction: when box 1 is INCOME (../ordinaryIncome >= 0) it is the income if NONPASSIVE (not ../lossIsPassive) else 0; when box 1 is a LOSS it is -../nonpassiveAllowedLoss (the nonpassive-allowed loss, 0 for a passive activity). The passive part joins the pool via ../passiveNet (and the pool's suspended allocation). Was the inline first summand of /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, then the whole body of ../partIINonpassivePart until the section 179 split separated the two.
WHY THE SPLIT EXISTS, and it is a CORRECTNESS reason before it is a graph-shape one: this fact is what /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation, and Pub 946 says to figure that taxable income "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction". The rental term of the same limit has always been the pre-section-179 /rentalNetBeforeSection179 for exactly this reason; the K-1 term now matches it. The graph-shape consequence is that the cycle this would otherwise close does not exist: measured with scripts/factdag.py before the split, ../partIINonpassivePart WAS in the upstream cone of /rentalSection179IncomeLimit (cone 81), so a column-(j) subtrahend reading that limit would have closed a real loop.
CollectionSum over this field is /k1NonpassiveActiveNet. The AFTER-section-179 figure that reaches Schedule E line 32 is ../partIINonpassivePart.
THE SECTION 469(k) ARM is the leading case, ahead of the box-1-sign test: when ../appliesPtpSection469 this fact is GreaterOf(../ptpSection469Net, 0). "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income" — so an overall gain lands here, in column (k), instead of in the Form 8582 pool it used to join. An overall LOSS is suspended in full, so the arm floors at zero rather than reporting a nonpassive loss: a PTP loss is not deductible against anything this year, which is exactly what makes it different from the ordinary nonpassive case below.
IT IS THIS TWIN AND NOT ONLY ../partIINonpassivePart, deliberately: this fact is the term /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation. Rebodying only the post-section-179 twin would leave Schedule E line 32 and that limitation disagreeing about the same PTP. ../partIINonpassivePart inherits the arm through its own subtraction and needs no edit; its section 179 subtrahend is $0 for the whole population THIS ARM touches, because the arm requires ../appliesPtpSection469 — a PASSIVE PTP — and a passive K-1 that elects section 179 is refused by /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp and, independently, by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited. RESTATED: the sentence used to claim the subtrahend was $0 on ANY PTP, which stopped being true when /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp narrowed to the passive and unanswered-participation PTP. A materially participating PTP partner now takes a real column (j) deduction — but ../appliesPtpSection469 is false there, so this arm is not what carries that K-1.
RESTATED AGAIN (closure), and the sentence that needed it is "../partIINonpassivePart inherits the arm through its own subtraction and needs no edit; its section 179 subtrahend is $0 for the whole population THIS ARM touches". BOTH halves ended. That fact now carries a section 469(k) arm OF ITS OWN, GreaterOf(../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179, $0), because the figure Schedule E column (k) must print is the POST-section-179 one; and the population is no longer refused - the passive item-D PTP FILES, /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited has been removed and /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp is narrowed to the unanswered-participation PTP alone narrower again - the GENERAL-PARTNER half of that alone; the limited-partner half now computes. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and is the reason the split exists, is THIS fact: it stays PRE-section-179 because /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums it into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation, and scripts/factdag.py measures that limitation's upstream cone at 124 paths containing no post-section-179 fact.
THIS FACT IS UNCHANGED AND STOPS BEING THE LINE-11 TERM, which is a correction to the two paragraphs above that argue it must be. "IT IS THIS TWIN AND NOT ONLY ../partIINonpassivePart, deliberately: this fact is the term /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation" and the closing "WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE ... is THIS fact: it stays PRE-section-179 because /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums it into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation" both stay TRUE AS TO THE PRE-§179 ROLE, which is why this fact is not rebodied; what ends is the identity of the summand. /k1NonpassiveActiveNet now sums ../activelyConductedNetBeforeSection179, which is this fact on every K-1 except a passive PTP.
THE REASON IS THAT LINE 11 AND SCHEDULE E PART II ASK DIFFERENT QUESTIONS OF THE SAME K-1, and the paragraph above that reads "Rebodying only the post-section-179 twin would leave Schedule E line 32 and that limitation disagreeing about the same PTP" was right about ITS worry (a §179 timing mismatch) and must not be read as forbidding THIS divergence. Schedule E Part II asks whether the income is PASSIVE, and the Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) answer, "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 10), so it belongs in column (k) and this fact keeps it. Form 4562 line 11 asks whether the taxpayer ACTIVELY CONDUCTED the trade or business (IRC 179(b)(3)(A); i4562 Line 11), and Publication 946 answers that one by participation - "A mere passive investor in a trade or business does not actively conduct the trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 109). A §469 recharacterisation is not a finding of active conduct. The two answers differ for exactly one population, the passive PTP partner with an overall gain, and the divergence is the correct reading of two different statutes rather than an inconsistency. Direction of the defect it closes: taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, an inflated line 11 allowing more §179 than the statute does.
THE CONE CLAIM ABOVE HOLDS AS A PROPERTY: the new path reads only this fact and ../appliesPtpSection469, both already in that cone and both PRE-section-179, so the limitation's cone still contains no post-section-179 fact and the cycle the split exists to avoid is still not closed.

Fact.Name: This K-1's contribution to the Form 4562 line-11 ACTIVELY CONDUCTED base, before the §179 deduction
Fact.Description:
ADDED as the actively-conducted base. $0 when ../appliesPtpSection469, else ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179. /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums THIS fact into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation; ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 keeps its own role unchanged and still carries the §469(k) gain into Schedule E Part II.
WHY THE TWO PARTED, and it is one term answering two different statutory tests. Form 4562 line 11 is "the total taxable income from any trade or business you actively conducted" (i4562 Line 11, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4562.pdf, page 5), and IRC 179(b)(3)(A) is the statute behind it: the deduction "shall not exceed the aggregate amount of taxable income of the taxpayer for such taxable year which is derived from the active conduct by the taxpayer of any trade or business" (26 U.S.C. 179, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section179&num=0&edition=2024). Publication 946 defines that test by PARTICIPATION - "Generally, you are considered to actively conduct a trade or business if you meaningfully participate in the management or operations of the trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 19) - and its glossary states the exclusion in terms: "A mere passive investor in a trade or business does not actively conduct the trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p946.pdf, page 109, the LEFT column of a three-column extraction, reassembled before quoting).
../appliesPtpSection469 is All(../isPubliclyTradedPartnership, ../lossIsPassive), so this fact uses the §469 passive determination as the active-conduct proxy, exactly as the non-PTP arm already does through Not(../lossIsPassive). The Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) treat such a partner's overall gain as nonpassive, "If you have an overall gain from a PTP, the net gain is nonpassive income" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 10); IRC 469(k)(1) (26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section469&num=0&edition=2024) is the rule that section 469 is applied separately to the items of each publicly traded partnership. The instructions' nonpassive label is a section 469 CHARACTERISATION and not a finding of active conduct, and no participation changes when the label does. A materially participating PTP partner has ../appliesPtpSection469 FALSE, takes ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179's ordinary box-1 case, and stays in this base unchanged - which is why no new attestation intake is needed to tell the two apart.
THE DEFECT THIS CLOSES: a passive PTP's overall gain raised the line-11 limitation by its own amount, so a return could take more §179 than IRC 179(b)(3)(A) allows (taxpayer-FAVOURABLE). NO NEW ROUNDING BOUNDARY: both arms are already whole-dollar - the $0 literal and ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179's own Round - so this fact carries no Round of its own, which also keeps it byte-identical to its operand on every non-PTP K-1.
A PASSIVE NON-PTP K-1 NEEDED NO ARM: ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 already contributes $0 there (its income case requires Not(../lossIsPassive) and its loss case reads ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss, which is $0 for a passive activity). The §469(k) arm was the only route by which a passive activity reached this base. The box-23 per-activity arm ahead of it cannot collide: ../passiveActivitySharesUsable carries Not(../isPubliclyTradedPartnership).

Fact.Name: This K-1's §179 expense deduction reaching Schedule E line 28 column (j)
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 12 for this K-1's box-12 share, routed to Schedule E Part II line 28 column (j) "Section 179 expense deduction from Form 4562".
REBODIED (closure): the operand is now ../atRiskAllowedSection179, and a PASSIVE K-1 routes $0 from an arm of its own because its share is a passive-activity deduction rather than a column (j) entry. ../atRiskAllowedSection179 IS the three-way minimum this paragraph describes - allocated pro rata across the return's electing K-1s and then capped by IRC 465 - so this fact is byte-identical on a single electing, fully-at-risk, nonpassive K-1, and differs only where an allocation or an at-risk cap was previously REFUSED rather than computed. The retired expression is kept below because the paragraphs that follow argue it and because its clean-room and completeness arguments still hold of the operand that replaced it. IT READ: the SMALLER of the amount the K-1's basis can absorb (../basisAllowedSection179 — line 6 column (c) and so line 8, net of the section 704(d)/1366(d) allocation), the return's line-5 dollar limitation (/section179TaxpayerDollarLimit) and the line-11 business-income limitation (/rentalSection179IncomeLimit, taxpayer-level despite its rental-era name). THE FIRST OPERAND IS NOW ../section179Elected to ../basisAllowedSection179. It is not an extra cap bolted on: section 704(d)/1366(d) is a PARTNER-level limitation on what the partner may report at all, and the partner's own basis worksheet says to include the section 179 share on line 15i "even if you can't deduct all of it due to limitations" and then allocate column D pro rata. So column (j) was reading the pre-limitation figure. It made no difference before, because a basis too small to absorb the deduction REFUSED the return (../section179WithoutSufficientBasis, now narrowed to its unanswered-basis arm) — the change is what makes that narrowing safe rather than a silent over-claim. Subtracted by ../partIINonpassivePart, because Schedule E line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) as the LOSS side of line 32.
$0 WHENEVER ANY OF THE FOUR REFUSALS IS UP, and that is not belt-and-braces: a knockout in this dictionary blocks submission without an Incomplete cascade, so the resolved value stays visible. Leaving a computed deduction visible on a refused return would be a number the graph does not stand behind. Routing $0 instead means the printed return neither claims the deduction nor pretends the question was never asked, exactly as /formK1s/*/qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss drops an amount its own knockout refuses. The four are ../section179WithoutSufficientBasis, ../section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited, ../section179OnPtp and /hasMultipleSection179ElectingActivities. THREE, not four. ../section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited, Complete FALSE on every input, was removed and is not in the Any below rather than left as a dead disjunct. ../section179OnPtp survives NARROWED to the unanswered-participation PTP. The other two are unchanged, and a PASSIVE K-1 now routes $0 from an arm of its own rather than from a refusal. ../section179OnPtp narrowed once more, to the GENERAL-PARTNER unanswered-participation PTP. The LIMITED-partner half is now PASSIVE, so it routes $0 from the ../lossIsPassive arm below rather than from this refusal - the same substitution the closure made for the answered-false PTP. The third disjunct is now the GUARD /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities rather than the population flag /hasMultipleSection179ElectingActivities. The records discharge block said "whichever unit does that owes the column-(j) leg the same treatment", and this is it: on a multi elector return whose every electing activity has a resolving allocation row and whose shares fit, the guard is down, this arm does not fire, and column (j) prints ../atRiskAllowedSection179, which is now capped at the filer's row share. On a refused multi elector return the guard is up and $0 routes exactly as before.
WHAT IS NOT MODELLED, disclosed rather than left to be discovered: a section 179 amount disallowed by the line-11 business-income limitation is carried to the next year under section 179(b)(3)(B), and this fact reports no such carryover for the K-1 leg. The rental leg does report one (/rentalProperties/*/section179CarryoverToNextYear) but only reports it — this is a single-year model that never applies a carryover — so the omission costs no TY2025 tax and no TY2025 line. It is a legibility gap, not a computation gap, and it is the reason the K-1 leg ships without a carryover twin.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, not by argument: the FIRST arm of the Switch returns $0 for any K-1 that elects nothing, so such an item never reads either taxpayer-level limit. That matters because LesserOf evaluates both operands and /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit CAN be Incomplete — a rental element that claims five-year property and leaves its basis unanswered makes the aggregate line-2 base Incomplete, exactly as it already makes the shipping per-element ../section179DollarLimit Incomplete. Without the guard that Incompleteness would propagate to ../partIINonpassivePart and /scheduleEPartIINetIncome on a K-1 with no section 179 amount at all. Pinned by node-test scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-does-not-contaminate.
AND WHEN THE K-1 DOES ELECT ON SUCH A RETURN, this fact IS Incomplete, deliberately: the line-5 dollar limitation genuinely cannot be computed from a phaseout base the filer has not finished answering, and inventing a $0 or an unphased $2,500,000 would both be numbers the graph cannot stand behind. That return is already refused by the same missing answer through the rental chain (/rentalProperties/*/section179DollarLimit and /scheduleETotalIncome are Incomplete on it too), so the Incompleteness here adds a Part II line to a refusal that already exists rather than creating one. Pinned by node-test scheduleE/k1-179-unanswered-rental-basis-refuses-an-electing-k1.
NOT BOX-23-AWARE, AND THAT IS FINE: a usable box-23 statement always has ../electsSection179 false, one of ../passiveActivitySharesUsable's own conjuncts, so this fact's own PASSIVE arm never fires on a K-1 that statement can express — no rewire needed.

Fact.Name: This K-1's NONPASSIVE contribution to Schedule E Part II line 32
Fact.Description:
../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 less ../section179ColumnJ: the K-1's nonpassive column (i)/(k) amount net of its column (j) section 179 expense. Schedule E line 30 adds columns (h) and (k), line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) as a bracketed LOSS total, and line 32 combines them — so the section 179 expense is a SUBTRAHEND here, not an addend. CollectionSum over this field is the nonpassive summand of the top-level /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, and it is also the Part II term of /section8582MagiPartIIAndIIITerms (Form 8582 line 6 MAGI), where the post-section-179 figure is the right one: the line-6 exclusion list does not add the section 179 deduction back, and a nonpassive section 179 deduction does reduce adjusted gross income.
ADDITIVE ON EVERY COMMITTED ROW: ../section179ColumnJ is a complete-safe $0 on any K-1 with no box-12 amount, and no committed scenario or pre-existing node-test fixture answers box 12, so this fact's value is byte-identical to its pre-split body everywhere committed. The clean-room nominations this fact carries (DTXV-NOM-I6198K1 and the /scheduleEPartIINetIncome ones that read it) were all taken on K-1s with no section 179 amount and are unaffected; the section 179 subtrahend itself carries NO clean-room witness and is tagged ai-only on ../section179ColumnJ.
NO EDIT AT THE SECTION 469(k) REBODY, stated so a reader does not go looking for one: the PTP arm went into ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179, and this fact reads that twin, so an overall PTP gain reaches Schedule E line 32 through the existing subtraction. The subtrahend is $0 for the whole population that arm touches — the arm runs only on a PASSIVE PTP, and a passive K-1 electing section 179 is refused both by /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp and by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited — so this fact equals its twin there. RESTATED: the claim used to be "$0 on any PTP in any case", which the narrowing of /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp ended; a materially participating PTP partner now carries a real column (j) subtrahend through this fact, exactly as any other nonpassive K-1 does, and ../appliesPtpSection469 is false on that K-1. The DTXV-NOM-I6198K1 witness is untouched either way: that K-1's item D is unanswered, so it is not a PTP here at all.
DISCHARGED. THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE HEADED "NO EDIT AT THE SECTION 469(k) REBODY" IS SPENT: this fact NOW carries a leading section 469(k) arm of its own, GreaterOf(../ptpSection469NetAfterSection179, $0). Both its premises ended. The claim that "the subtrahend is $0 for the whole population that arm touches ... because a passive K-1 electing section 179 is refused both by /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp and by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited" ended when this closure freed that population; and reading ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 alone would now print the PRE-section-179 gain in column (k) while the Form 8582 side and Form 4952 line 4h carried the post-section-179 one. The twin still may not move - /k1NonpassiveActiveNet sums it into the Form 4562 line-11 business-income limitation, figured "without regard to ... the section 179 deduction" - so the arm lands HERE, which is exactly the role the section 179 split created for this fact. The non-PTP arm is untouched and every clean-room witness above rides it.
A PASSIVE BOX 10 LOSS OF THE SAME PTP. Step 2 of the partner instructions makes only "the net gain portion (total gain minus total losses)" nonpassive; the rest of the income is passive income against which the loss is allowed. So the section 469(k) arm also subtracts ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncome, which column (h) prints and line 32 adds back. The instructions' example: 8,000 of Schedule E income and a 3,500 Form 4797 loss put 4,500 here (column (k)) and 3,500 in column (h).

Fact.Name: Guaranteed payments for services (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 4a)
Fact.Description: Box 4a of this partnership K-1: guaranteed payments to the partner for services, determined without regard to partnership income. Partnership K-1s only (an S corporation makes no guaranteed payments; leave unanswered on an sCorp item). OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../guaranteedPaymentsServices downstream. Entering a nonzero amount requires ../writableSeEarnings to be answered (services GP is SE income for every partner, 1402(a)(13)); an unanswered box 14 alongside GP REFUSES the return via ../guaranteedPayments (never a silent SE omission). Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 4a (Guaranteed payments for services).

Fact.Name: Guaranteed payments for services (box 4a), complete-safe
Fact.Description: Box 4a of this K-1, defaulting to $0 when unanswered.

Fact.Name: Guaranteed payments for capital (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 4b)
Fact.Description: Box 4b of this partnership K-1: guaranteed payments other than for services, such as for the use of capital or attributable to section 736(a)(2) payments. Partnership K-1s only. OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../guaranteedPaymentsCapital downstream. Entering a nonzero amount requires ../writableSeEarnings answered (the SE-assessment gate), and a return carrying capital GP with MAGI above the Form 8960 threshold is REFUSED (/knockoutK1CapitalGuaranteedPaymentsNiit) because its NIIT character depends on partner classification the model does not represent. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 4b (Guaranteed payments for capital).

Fact.Name: Guaranteed payments for capital (box 4b), complete-safe
Fact.Description: Box 4b of this K-1, defaulting to $0 when unanswered (complete-safe alias of ../writableGuaranteedPaymentsCapital).

Fact.Name: Item G, this partner is a general partner or LLC member-manager (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) Part II item G)
Fact.Description:
Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) Part II item G, the printed partner-type checkbox pair: TRUE for "General partner or LLC member-manager", FALSE for "Limited partner or other LLC member". Partnership K-1s only (a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) has no item G, so leave this unanswered on an sCorp item). OPTIONAL writable; use the complete-safe ../partnerIsGeneralPartner downstream.
WHAT IT SELECTS. FIRST, whether this K-1's box 4b guaranteed payment for capital can be excluded from net investment income. A general partner's box 14A carries the payment into SECA and IRC 1411(c)(6) excludes SECA-taxed income from NII, so the character of the payment is determinable and the return computes. See ../capitalGuaranteedPaymentNiitUndeterminable. SECOND, whether IRC 469(h)(2)'s limited-partner presumption reaches an item-D PTP on this K-1: see ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner and ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption.
THE UNANSWERED CASE IS DELIBERATELY TAXPAYER-ADVERSE, and that is the point of the default rather than an accident of it: ../partnerIsGeneralPartner defaults FALSE, which keeps /knockoutK1CapitalGuaranteedPaymentsNiit firing. Treating silence as "general partner" would exclude the payment from NII on a return where nobody said so, which UNDER-computes NIIT.
THE PRINTED FIELD IS A CHECKBOX PAIR AND THIS IS A BOOLEAN, which collapses one reading and the collapse is stated rather than hidden: "LLC member-manager" reads TRUE (it shares item G's left box with "general partner") and "other LLC member" reads FALSE. The two boxes are printed as a mutually exclusive pair, so the only third state is unanswered.
NOT MODELED, disclosed: item G is the PRINTED classification, NOT the section 1402(a)(13) test. The partner instructions say plainly that "whether a partner qualifies as a limited partner for purposes of self-employment tax depends on whether the partner is considered a limited partner under section 1402(a)(13)", so an LLC member whose K-1 marks item G "limited" can still be a general partner for SE purposes. This dictionary transcribes the box; it does not re-derive that test and holds no facts from which it could. interpretation:provisional. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box G (General partner or LLC member-manager / Limited partner or other LLC member).

Fact.Name: Item G, complete-safe
Fact.Description:
Whether this K-1's item G marks the partner a GENERAL partner (or LLC member-manager), defaulting to FALSE when unanswered (complete-safe alias of ../writablePartnerIsGeneralPartner, the IsComplete-guard-per-member pattern that keeps every pre-existing /formK1s item resolving).
THE FALSE DEFAULT IS THE TAXPAYER-ADVERSE ONE HERE, which is the opposite of the usual reason for a false default: it WITHHOLDS the IRC 1411(c)(6) exclusion rather than inventing it, so an unanswered item G lands in the same arm as an answered "limited partner" and the NIIT refusal survives.
A SECOND CONSUMER, and it makes the same default do a second job in the same direction: ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner reads this fact to decide whether IRC 469(h)(2)'s limited-partner presumption reaches this K-1. False here — answered "limited partner" OR unanswered — puts an item-D PTP inside the presumption, so an unanswered participation answer resolves PASSIVE. That is taxpayer-ADVERSE too (a loss suspends rather than being deducted in full), so the two consumers agree about what silence costs rather than pulling in opposite directions.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 4b capital guaranteed payment has undeterminable NII character (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True exactly when THIS K-1 reports a box 4b guaranteed payment for capital (../guaranteedPaymentsCapital > $0) AND this partner is not established as a general partner (../partnerIsGeneralPartner false, which covers both an answered "limited partner or other LLC member" and an unanswered item G).
WHY BOTH CONJUNCTS ARE PER-ITEM. The section 1411 character of a section 707(c) capital payment is a property of the PARTNER's relationship to THAT partnership, so a return with two K-1s can have one determinable and one not. Reading the classification across every item, or reading the taxpayer-level /k1GuaranteedPaymentsCapital total here, would let an unanswered item G on a K-1 that reports NO capital guaranteed payment keep the whole return refused, which is the ordinary shape of most returns.
WHAT IS FREED, AND WHAT IS NOT. A GENERAL partner's capital guaranteed payment is carried into SECA by box 14A and excluded from net investment income by IRC 1411(c)(6), so this flag is false and the return computes. The LIMITED partner's above-threshold case stays refused: its answer depends on the substitute-for-interest reading of Reg. 1.1411-4(g), which is not published as an irs.gov artifact, so under invariant 3 there is nothing this repo may cite for it. That arm is blocked on a SOURCE this repo cannot obtain, not on a build.
COMPLETE-SAFE: built only from this item's own 0-default and false-default aliases, so an item with nothing answered resolves Complete false (the lesson).

Fact.Description: The qualified dividends reported on this K-1 (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 6b / Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 5b) — the subset of box 6a/5a ordinary dividends eligible for the preferential QDCGT rates, reported on Form 1040 line 3a. Flows to Form 1040 line 3a and the QDCGT worksheet; the box-6b-le-box-6a subset relation is taxpayer-input GIGO, not machine-enforced (interpretation:provisional — consciously matching the 1099-DIV box 1a/1b posture).

Fact.Name: K-1 self-employment earnings (loss) (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A)
Fact.Description: Box 14 code A of this partnership K-1: the partner's net earnings (loss) from self-employment as COMPUTED BY THE PARTNERSHIP. SIGNED as printed (a loss is negative). A POSITIVE (or zero) box 14A is taken AS ENTERED per Schedule SE line 2 ("and Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code A"); the model does not re-derive the SE base from boxes 1/4, because that derivation is partner-classification-dependent (general vs limited, 1402(a)(13)) and, while ../writablePartnerIsGeneralPartner now records the PRINTED item-G classification, it deliberately does not re-derive the section 1402(a)(13) test that derivation would need. A NEGATIVE value is NOT consumed raw: it is consumed only through the partner's own already-limited figure, ../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss, and is REFUSED when that figure is unanswered or self-contradictory — see ../seEarningsAllowed and /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings. WHY A NEGATIVE IS NOT TAKEN RAW: the partner instructions say "If the amount in this box is a loss, enter only the DEDUCTIBLE amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040). See Limitations on Losses, Deductions, and Credits" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 22) — the deductible amount depends on 704(d) basis, 465 at-risk and 469 passive state that this SINGLE-YEAR graph does not fully hold (there is no carryforward of suspended amounts), so the engine cannot compute it. Taking the printed loss RAW would UNDER-state SE tax whenever the loss is wholly or partly suspended (e.g. a box-1 loss fully suspended by zero basis, alongside Schedule C profit). The honest posture is therefore to INTAKE the figure the partner already computed off the return, and to refuse when they have not stated it. Partnership K-1s only (an S-corp K-1 reports no SE earnings; leave unanswered). NOT MODELED, disclosed: the general-partner instruction to reduce 14A by section 179 / unreimbursed partnership expenses / oil-and-gas depletion before Schedule SE (no such intake exists) — entering the printed value OVERstates SE tax in that case, never understates. HONEST LIMIT of the GP/SE gate (../seAssessmentSatisfied): it forces the box-14 QUESTION to be ANSWERED, and 0 is an accepted answer. It is a PROMPT, not a proof: a taxpayer with services guaranteed payments who answers 0 gets $0 SE tax on them, which is wrong (1402(a)(13) carves services GP INTO SE income for every partner type). No hard invariant is derivable here — the correct SE base is not a function of any facts the graph holds — so this is stated rather than enforced. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 (Self-employment earnings (loss)).

Fact.Name: K-1 box 14 code A amount read out of the printed slots
Fact.Description:
The box 14 amount this partnership K-1 printed beside a row coded A, the net earnings (loss) from self-employment, read out of the box 14 rows: the sum over the rows of ../selfEmploymentEarningsEntries/*/codeAAmountFromThisRow, where a row contributes its amount only when the row's code AND its amount are both answered and the code is A, and $0 otherwise. COMPLETE SAFE, so an item that recorded no box 14 row resolves a Complete $0.
SIGNED, because box 14 code A is signed: the printed label is "Self-employment earnings (loss)" and a loss is negative. A negative arriving through this route is NOT taken raw onto Schedule SE — ../hasNegativeSeEarnings was widened on 2026-08-30 to fire on a row-sourced negative exactly as it fires on the code-keyed writable, so the same "state the deductible amount or be refused" machinery (../deductibleSeEarningsLossStated, ../seEarningsLossUndeterminable, /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings) governs both routes. Wiring the row into ../seEarnings WITHOUT that widening would have let a row-typed loss reach Schedule SE line 2 in full and UNDERSTATE SE tax, which is why the two edits are one edit.
IT IS THE SECOND ROUTE TO ONE QUANTITY, NOT A SECOND QUANTITY. ../writableSeEarnings is the code-keyed intake and remains the OVERRIDE: ../seEarnings reads it first and only falls back here.

Fact.Name: K-1 box 14 code A amount read out of the printed slots: this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/selfEmploymentEarningsEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeASlotAmount reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is A, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: A box 14 slot on this K-1 is coded A and answered
Fact.Description:
True when at least one row of this partnership K-1's printed box 14 has an answered letter code equal to A and an answered amount. This is the "was the source answered" predicate that lets the printed ROW leaves feed ../seEarnings without retiring the code-keyed intake ../writableSeEarnings, and it is an IsComplete on the RAW row leaves, never on the complete safe ../k1Box14CodeASlotAmount (which is always Complete and would make the predicate vacuously true on every K-1).
THREE FACTS READ IT, and they must move together. ../seEarnings takes the row amount when the code-keyed writable is unanswered; ../hasNegativeSeEarnings treats a row-sourced figure as an ANSWERED box 14 so a row-typed loss runs the refusal path; and ../seAssessmentSatisfied accepts a row answer as the box 14 assessment a K-1 with guaranteed payments owes.

Fact.Name: A box 14 slot on this K-1 is coded A and answered: this row
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/selfEmploymentEarningsEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered reads it: True when this row passes the test /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered applies to every row (code A); otherwise False. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: K-1 box 14 code B amount read out of the printed slots
Fact.Description:
The box 14 amount this partnership K-1 printed beside a row coded B, the partner's share of GROSS farming or fishing income, read out of the box 14 row list ../selfEmploymentEarningsEntries by testing each row's code. Same code-keyed per-row sum and the same complete safe $0 as ../k1Box14CodeASlotAmount.
GROSS, and a DIFFERENT QUANTITY FROM CODE A. Box 14 carries three codes on one printed box: A is net earnings (loss) from self-employment, B is this gross farming or fishing figure and C is gross nonfarm income, which this dictionary still does not consume. A row coded C contributes $0 here rather than being mistaken for a farm figure.
WHERE IT GOES: ../grossFarmingFishingIncome, and from there /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome and Schedule E line 42 (/scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation). Line 42 is a reconciliation line the form does not combine into line 41, so nothing here moves an income total. UNFLOORED, for the reason ../writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome records at length: no floor is printed at the intake and the one nearby printed floor sits downstream at Schedule SE line 15.
IT IS THE SECOND ROUTE TO ONE QUANTITY, NOT A SECOND QUANTITY: ../writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome is the code-keyed intake and remains the OVERRIDE.

Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/selfEmploymentEarningsEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeBSlotAmount reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is B, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: A box 14 slot on this K-1 is coded B and answered
Fact.Description: True when at least one row of this partnership K-1's printed box 14 has an answered letter code equal to B and an answered amount — the "was the source answered" predicate behind ../grossFarmingFishingIncome's row arm, on the raw row leaves rather than on the complete safe ../k1Box14CodeBSlotAmount for the reason ../k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered records.
