Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/selfEmploymentEarningsEntries as /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeBSlotAnswered reads it: True when this row passes the test /formK1s/*/k1Box14CodeBSlotAnswered applies to every row (code B); otherwise False. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: K-1 self-employment earnings as DECLARED (box 14 code A), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
This K-1's box 14 code A SE earnings exactly as declared (signed), defaulting to $0 when unanswered. COMPLETE-SAFE and never refused — this is the LEGIBILITY alias, aggregated into /k1SeEarningsDeclared so a refused return can still say WHY.
TWO ROUTES SINCE: the code-keyed ../writableSeEarnings when it is answered, and otherwise the printed ROW ../k1Box14CodeASlotAmount when a box 14 row is coded A and answered (../k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered). The code-keyed intake is the OVERRIDE and every committed fixture reaches it, so nothing moved; before that date a filer who typed 14A into the printed row moved no SE tax at all. ../hasNegativeSeEarnings and ../seAssessmentSatisfied were widened in the same edit so a row answer counts as an ANSWERED box 14 for the negative-loss refusal and for the guaranteed-payment assessment. say WHY.
The value that actually reaches Schedule SE is ../seEarningsAllowed, which for a declared negative carries the partner's stated deductible amount (../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss) and refuses when that amount is unstated or self-contradictory. The 0-default does not silently zero an SE obligation for guaranteed payments (an item with GP and an unanswered box 14 is refused upstream via ../guaranteedPayments) but it DOES leave a hole open for a BOX-1-ONLY item: a general partner with box-1 income and no 14A entry still gets no SE tax. That hole is PRE-EXISTING and it is NOT fine — it is an OPEN World-#1 gap. It was formerly described as "awaiting the partner-type field"; that field now exists (../writablePartnerIsGeneralPartner) and the gap did NOT close with it, because the missing piece is a box-1 SE leg, not the classification. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Box 14 self-employment earnings row 1 of this K-1, addressed by position
Fact.Description: Row 1 of ../selfEmploymentEarningsEntries (position 0), hoisted so the box 14 print projection can read the code and amount the K-1 prints on its printed line 1. The engine has no operator that gives a collection item its own position; IndexOf with a constant index is the inverse lookup (the form2210:/form2210Line1bSlot1 precedent). With fewer than 1 rows, or with the row table unanswered, it is Incomplete, and so is every field read through it, exactly as an unanswered printed row was.

Fact.Name: Box 14 self-employment earnings row 2 of this K-1, addressed by position
Fact.Description: Row 2 of ../selfEmploymentEarningsEntries (position 1), hoisted so the box 14 print projection can read the code and amount the K-1 prints on its printed line 2. The engine has no operator that gives a collection item its own position; IndexOf with a constant index is the inverse lookup (the form2210:/form2210Line1bSlot1 precedent). With fewer than 2 rows, or with the row table unanswered, it is Incomplete, and so is every field read through it, exactly as an unanswered printed row was.

Fact.Name: Both printed box 14 slots have either both fields answered or neither
Fact.Description: Structural check for the first two rows of this Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 (../selfEmploymentEarningsRow1 and ../selfEmploymentEarningsRow2), the two the form prints. False flags a half-answered pair; the print consumer must not use the normalized projection unless this is true. The rows themselves remain unchanged.

Fact.Name: The effective box 14 code-A value fits in the two printed slots
Fact.Description: True when the current code/amount row values can carry the effective code-A amount without losing another printed code: an answered ../writableSeEarnings can replace an existing code-A row, or occupy either unfilled row. False when the answered code-A value cannot fit without dropping a code, or when a raw code/amount pair is malformed. When ../writableSeEarnings is unanswered the original rows remain the print source. This is a representability check only; ../box14PrintedSlotsAreWellFormed separately refuses a half-answered raw pair.

Fact.Name: The code-A override is assigned to printed box 14 slot 1
Fact.Description: When ../writableSeEarnings is answered, code A stays in its first existing row; otherwise it uses the first unfilled row. If both rows already contain other codes, ../box14PrintIsRepresentable is Complete false. False when the code-A writable is unanswered, because then the two raw printed rows remain authoritative.

Fact.Name: The code-A override is assigned to printed box 14 slot 2
Fact.Description: When ../writableSeEarnings is answered, code A stays in its second existing row if rows has another code, or uses rows when that is the only available position. False when rows is selected or the code-A writable is unanswered. If both rows already contain other codes, ../box14PrintIsRepresentable is Complete false.

Fact.Name: Normalized Form 1065 box 14 printed code, slot 1
Fact.Description: The print projection for box 14. If the code-keyed ../writableSeEarnings is answered and ../box14PrintIsRepresentable is true, this places code A here only when this is the selected row. Otherwise it preserves the raw code1 intake, including when the transform cannot represent an additional code A. The original writable leaves are never modified; an unanswered raw row remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Normalized Form 1065 box 14 printed amount, slot 1
Fact.Description: The amount paired with ../box14PrintedCode1. An answered ../writableSeEarnings takes precedence only when rows is selected by the representable print projection; otherwise this preserves the raw amount1 intake. An unanswered raw row remains Incomplete, including an unrepresentable print state.

Fact.Name: Normalized Form 1065 box 14 printed code, slot 2
Fact.Description: The print projection for box 14, paired with ../box14PrintedAmount2. It places the code-keyed code A here only when rows is the selected position in a representable projection. Otherwise it preserves the raw code2 intake. The original row leaf is retained unchanged; an unanswered raw row remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Normalized Form 1065 box 14 printed amount, slot 2
Fact.Description: The amount paired with ../box14PrintedCode2. An answered ../writableSeEarnings takes precedence only when rows is selected by the representable print projection; otherwise this preserves the raw amount2 intake. An unanswered raw row remains Incomplete, including an unrepresentable print state.

Fact.Name: This K-1 declares a NEGATIVE box 14 code A (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True exactly when ../writableSeEarnings is ANSWERED and NEGATIVE — the case the partner instructions route through "enter only the DEDUCTIBLE amount on Schedule SE ... See Limitations on Losses, Deductions, and Credits", a deductibility determination this single-year graph cannot make (704(d)/465/469 suspension state is not carried). Raises /hasK1NegativeSeEarnings, the legibility flag for "this return declares an SE loss at all", and SELECTS ../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss as the value ../seEarningsAllowed reads. It does not key the knockout by itself: that is ../seEarningsLossUndeterminable -> /hasK1UndeterminableSeEarningsLoss -> /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings, which fires only when the deductible amount is unstated or self-contradictory. Either way a raw negative can never reach Schedule SE and under-state SE tax. COMPLETE-SAFE: reads only this item's own raw writables (IsComplete-first, so an unanswered box 14 resolves Complete-false rather than cascading — the lesson). WIDENED: "ANSWERED" now means the code-keyed ../writableSeEarnings is answered OR a printed box 14 row is coded A and answered (../k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered), because ../seEarnings now reads the row as its fallback. Without this widening a row-typed LOSS would have passed straight through ../seEarningsAllowed arm 1 onto Schedule SE line 2 and UNDERSTATED SE tax — the exact failure the code-keyed route exists to prevent. The comparison itself already read ../seEarnings, so it follows the effective figure, and ../deductibleSeEarningsLossStated compares its answer against ../seEarnings too and therefore needed no edit.

Fact.Name: The DEDUCTIBLE part of a box 14 code A loss, as the partner computed it off the return
Fact.Description:
When this K-1's box 14 code A is a LOSS, the amount of that loss the partner is actually allowed to enter on Schedule SE, SIGNED the same way box 14A is signed (a loss is NEGATIVE, and $0 is a valid answer meaning the whole loss is suspended). Asked only on a K-1 whose ../writableSeEarnings is answered and negative; on any other K-1 leave it unanswered and ../seEarningsAllowed takes the printed figure as entered.
THIS IS A TRANSCRIPTION, NOT A COMPUTATION, and the printed instruction is what makes it one: "If the amount in this box is a loss, enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE (Form 1040). See Limitations on Losses, Deductions, and Credits, earlier." The partner arrives having already applied the 704(d) basis, 465 at-risk and 469 passive limits OFF the return. The dictionary does not re-derive that figure and could not: the suspension state those limits turn on is cross-year and this single-year graph does not carry it. Same ground on which this repo accepted Form 4797 line 26a and Schedule E's cost-depletion attestation.
IT IS A SEPARATE FACT FROM ../writableSeEarnings ON PURPOSE. The return still wants the PRINTED box 14A for the rest of Schedule SE's reconciliation and for ../seEarnings / /k1SeEarningsDeclared, so collapsing the two would lose the filer's own entry. Both survive: ../seEarnings echoes the printed loss, ../seEarningsAllowed carries the deductible one.
IT IS BOUNDED AT BOTH ENDS RATHER THAN CLAMPED, and the difference matters: an entry outside [printed box 14A, $0] is an input CONTRADICTION, not a number to silently rewrite. A deductible loss cannot be larger in magnitude than the loss it comes from, and a "deductible amount" of a LOSS cannot be positive. Either violation leaves ../deductibleSeEarningsLossStated false, which keeps ../seEarningsAllowed Result.Incomplete and keeps /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings firing. There is deliberately NO Limit element here: a Min or Max clamp would rewrite the filer's contradictory entry into a plausible one, which is the wrong-looking-right failure the refusal exists to prevent.
NOT MODELED, disclosed, and each is a DIFFERENT population from this one. (1) The general-partner instruction to reduce a POSITIVE box 14A by section 179 expense, unreimbursed partnership expenses and oil-and-gas depletion before Schedule SE: no such intake exists, and that gap sits on ../writableSeEarnings, not here. (2) Options-dealer and commodities-dealer partnerships (section 1402(i)) and investment clubs (Rev. Rul. 75-525): narrow special cases printed in the same instruction block, with no status intake anywhere in this module. (3) The fuller successor, carrying 704(d)/465/469 suspended-loss state ACROSS years, is deprioritised rather than retired by this intake; a later unit that builds it supersedes this field rather than the other way round.
NOT AN INPUT TO THIS FIELD, stated because the neighbouring machinery invites the mistake: ../basis, ../amountAtRisk and ../fullyAtRisk apply the same three statutes to ../ordinaryLoss (the box-1 loss) only. Box 14A has its own, different base, and this field is the partner's already-limited figure rather than anything derived from those three. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This K-1's deductible box 14A loss is stated and internally consistent
Fact.Description:
True exactly when ../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss is ANSWERED and lies within [../seEarnings, $0] inclusive: not positive, and not larger in magnitude than the printed box 14A loss it comes from. BOTH ends are fenced, and the inclusive ends are both real populations: $0 is a wholly suspended loss, and a deductible equal to the printed loss is a wholly allowed one.
THE IsComplete GUARD IS A Switch, NOT A LEADING CONJUNCT, deliberately: comparing an unanswered Dollar is Result.Incomplete, and only a Switch guarantees the comparison is never reached on an unanswered field. Complete-safe: false when nothing is answered, which is what keeps an unanswered deductible amount REFUSING rather than falling through to a silent $0.
NOT A DEDUCTIBILITY TEST. This checks the filer's entry against itself; it does not verify the 704(d)/465/469 arithmetic behind it, which is off-return by construction (see ../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss).

Fact.Name: This K-1 declares a box 14A loss whose deductible amount is not stated (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True exactly when this K-1 declares a NEGATIVE box 14 code A (../hasNegativeSeEarnings) AND its deductible amount is not validly stated (../deductibleSeEarningsLossStated false, i.e. unanswered, positive, or more negative than the printed loss). This is the narrowed successor of the blanket "any declared negative refuses" rule: it raises /hasK1UndeterminableSeEarningsLoss -> /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings and makes ../seEarningsAllowed Result.Incomplete, so a raw negative can still never reach Schedule SE and under-state SE tax. COMPLETE-SAFE: both conjuncts are complete-safe Booleans over this item's own writables.

Fact.Name: K-1 SE earnings ALLOWED onto Schedule SE line 2 (box 14 code A, non-negative only)
Fact.Description:
The box 14 code A amount that may reach Schedule SE, in three arms. (1) NOT a declared negative: ../seEarnings, taken as entered. (2) A declared negative WITH a validly stated deductible amount (../deductibleSeEarningsLossStated): ../writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss, the partner's own already-limited figure, which MAY be negative and is what the printed instruction asks for. (3) Otherwise Result.Incomplete.
WHAT ARM 3 STILL COVERS, since it is the narrowed remnant of the former blanket refusal: a declared negative box 14A whose deductible amount is unanswered, positive, or more negative than the printed loss. The deductible amount is a function of 704(d) basis / 465 at-risk / 469 passive suspension state the single-year graph does not hold, so the dictionary cannot supply it and taking the printed loss RAW would UNDER-state SE tax whenever any part of it is suspended (the representable failure: box-1 loss fully suspended by zero basis + Schedule C profit, SE tax wrongly reduced to 0). Only the filer can state it. So the return is REFUSED (the Incomplete cascades /k1SeEarnings -> /netEarningsFromSelfEmployment -> /selfEmploymentTax -> total tax) and legibly knocked out via /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings.
THIS FACT MAY NOW BE NEGATIVE, which it never was before the fill: arm 2 carries a signed, still-negative allowed loss through to Schedule SE line 2, which is exactly what "enter only the deductible amount" instructs. ../seEarnings keeps echoing the PRINTED figure unchanged. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The SE-tax assessment for this K-1's guaranteed payments is satisfied (a PROMPT, not a proof)
Fact.Description: True when this item either reports NO guaranteed payments (boxes 4a+4b both absent/0) or has box 14 code A ANSWERED (any value, INCLUDING 0) — which since 2026-08-30 means the code-keyed ../writableSeEarnings is answered OR a printed box 14 row is coded A and answered (../k1Box14CodeASlotAnswered). The widening is a LOOSENING: a filer who transcribed box 14 into the printed rows has answered the question this gate asks, and refusing them for using the other field would have been a false refusal. False exactly when guaranteed payments are present but box 14 is unanswered. HONEST LIMIT: this forces the box-14 QUESTION to be answered; it does NOT verify the answer. Answering 0 alongside services guaranteed payments yields $0 SE tax on them, which is WRONG (1402(a)(13) carves services GP into SE income for every partner type) — the gate cannot catch it, because the correct SE base is not a function of any facts the graph holds. What the gate does buy: the unanswered-box-14 case (the one where the engine would otherwise default silently to 0) is refused rather than computed. COMPLETE-SAFE and built ONLY from this item's own raw writables via their 0-default aliases (the lesson: an item gate must never cascade incompleteness into a return without the item). interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports guaranteed payments without an SE assessment (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: The negation of ../seAssessmentSatisfied: true when this item reports guaranteed payments (box 4a/4b) but box 14 SE earnings is unanswered. Raises the taxpayer-level /hasK1GuaranteedPaymentsWithoutSeAssessment flag so the refusal (Result.Incomplete on ../guaranteedPayments) is legible rather than silent (the refuse-and-flag pattern).

Fact.Name: This K-1's guaranteed payments flowing NONPASSIVE to Schedule E Part II (line 28 col (k))
Fact.Description: Boxes 4a + 4b of this partnership K-1, flowing to Schedule E Part II line 28 column (k) as NONPASSIVE income per the partner instructions (guaranteed payments are never passive income and never enter the Form 8582 pool, regardless of ../materiallyParticipated). Defined ONLY when ../seAssessmentSatisfied; for an item reporting GP with box 14 unanswered this resolves Result.Incomplete (single-case Switch with no default), which propagates through /k1GuaranteedPayments and /scheduleEPartIINetIncome to /totalIncome and REFUSES the return rather than flow GP income with its SE tax silently omitted. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 gross farming or fishing income (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code B)
Fact.Description:
Box 14 code B of this partnership K-1: the partner's share of the partnership's GROSS farming or fishing income. The partner instructions state both of its uses verbatim: "If you're an individual partner, enter the amount from this line, as an item of information, on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 42. Also use this amount to figure net earnings from self-employment under the farm optional method on Schedule SE (Form 1040), Part II." OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../grossFarmingFishingIncome downstream.
GROSS, not net, and therefore NOT the code A figure. Box 14 carries three codes on one printed box: code A is net earnings (loss) from self-employment (../writableSeEarnings), code B is this gross farming or fishing figure, and code C is gross NONFARM income. They are different quantities and this dictionary models code A and now code B; code C has no intake.
SIGN, and what is NOT proven. No floor is printed at this intake: the code B instruction carries none, the Schedule E line 42 instruction carries none, and the box's own printed label on the K-1 face is "Self-employment earnings (loss)". The one printed floor anywhere near this figure is Schedule SE line 15, "Enter the smaller of: two-thirds (2/3) of gross farm income (not less than zero) or $7,240" — and that floor governs the COMPOSITE its own footnote defines, "From Sch. F, line 9; and Sch. K-1 (Form 1065), box 14, code B". An earlier unit proved the OTHER member of that composite negative-capable (Schedule F line 8 prints the gain OR LOSS on commodity futures contracts, and line 9 sums it), which explains the printed floor entirely without any claim about code B. So this writable is UNFLOORED BY CHOICE, not by proof: a Min limit would REJECT a printed entry whose impossibility no vendored source establishes, and the printed law's own floor sits downstream at Schedule SE line 15 where a consumer applies it to the composite. The portfolio intakes on this collection (boxes 5, 6a, 6b) do carry Min 0; their printed labels name receipts with no loss form at all, which is the asymmetry rather than a stronger rule.
Partnership K-1s only. Schedule E line 42's other two K-1 legs are Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F, and neither of those K-1s exists as an item collection in this dictionary, so an entityType other than partnership leaves this unanswered. The S CORPORATION half of that sentence is wrong. /k1EntityTypeOptions in this same file already offers "sCorp" beside "partnership" and /formK1s/*/entityType is already a live enum over it, so the 1120-S leg needs a per-item FIELD on THIS collection — the shape this fact already is — and not a new collection. Only the Form 1041 leg needs an entity type that does not exist yet. What actually blocks both is SOURCE ACQUISITION rather than modelling: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1120ssk.pdf is the form and its box 17 prints only "Other information", the code letters being in the Shareholder's Instructions, which are not vendored; nothing for Form 1041 is vendored at all. Invariant 3 forbids citing a code from a document we do not hold, so the vendoring is the first unit. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 farming and fishing income — Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN
Fact.Description:
An S CORPORATION K-1's box 17 code AN amount, as declared. The S-corporation sibling of ../writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome, which is the PARTNERSHIP box 14 code B figure, and the second of the four legs Schedule E line 42 names.
A SEPARATE WRITABLE RATHER THAN A SHARED ONE, on the faithful-record principle: the two amounts arrive on different forms, in different boxes, under different code letters, and a filer transcribing a 1120-S K-1 is reading "17 AN" while a filer transcribing a 1065 K-1 is reading "14 B". They are the same QUANTITY for line 42's purposes and are summed as such, but recording them in one field would make the stored return unable to say which printed box a figure came off.
THE PRINTED WORDING DIFFERS AND IS NOT SMOOTHED OVER: the 1065 instruction says "Gross farming or fishing income", the 1120-S instruction says "Farming and fishing income" with no "gross". This fact's Name follows its own source. Nothing downstream turns on the difference — line 42 collects both as items of information — but a successor comparing the two intakes should know the asymmetry is the IRS's and not a transcription slip.
WHICH ENTITY TYPE THIS BELONGS TO: /formK1s/*/entityType already offers "sCorp" beside "partnership" (see /k1EntityTypeOptions), so no new collection and no new enum option was needed — a correction to three earlier passes that described this leg as requiring a K-1 collection this dictionary does not model. NOT GATED on that enum here: the intake is a faithful record of what the filer transcribed, and gating a writable on another writable would make a mistyped entity type silently discard an answered figure. The entity type is the reader's guide to which box was read, not a validity rule.
UNANSWERED IS UNANSWERED — the complete-safe default lives on ../farmingFishingIncomeSCorp, the same split the box 14 code B pair uses. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 farming and fishing income (Form 1120-S box 17 code AN), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
This K-1's box 17 code AN amount exactly as declared, defaulting to $0 when unanswered — the complete-safe alias of ../writableFarmingFishingIncomeSCorp, character for character the IsComplete/Switch shape ../grossFarmingFishingIncome uses for the partnership leg. Reads only this item's own raw writable, so an unanswered box 17 AN never makes any consumer Incomplete.
THE 0 DEFAULT IS SAFE FOR THE SAME REASON IT IS SAFE ON THE PARTNERSHIP TWIN: nothing in this dictionary computes tax, AGI or any threshold from this figure — Schedule E line 42 remains a filer attestation until all four of its legs exist — so a K-1 whose code AN is blank contributes 0 to a total nobody reads. Whoever eventually wires line 42 inherits the question of whether a blank 17 AN on a farming S corporation's K-1 should be answered rather than defaulted. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 gross farming or fishing income (box 14 code B), complete-safe
Fact.Description:
This K-1's box 14 code B amount, defaulting to $0 when unanswered. TWO ROUTES: the code-keyed ../writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome when it is answered, and otherwise the printed ROW ../k1Box14CodeBSlotAmount when a box 14 row is coded B and answered (../k1Box14CodeBSlotAnswered). The code-keyed intake is the OVERRIDE and every committed fixture reaches it, so nothing moved; before that date a filer who typed 14B into the printed row reached Schedule E line 42 with nothing. Reads only this item's own raw writable, so an unanswered box 14B never makes any consumer Incomplete.
THE 0 DEFAULT IS SAFE HERE in a way the box 14A default is not. Nothing in this dictionary computes tax, AGI or any threshold from this figure — see /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome for the full consumer statement — so a K-1 whose code B is left blank contributes 0 to a total nobody reads. When Schedule E line 42 or the Schedule SE farm optional method is eventually built on it, whoever wires it inherits the question of whether a blank 14B on a farming partnership's K-1 should be answered rather than defaulted. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Item D — this K-1 is from a publicly traded partnership (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) item D)
Fact.Description:
Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) item D, the printed checkbox "Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)". Partnership K-1s only: a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) has no item D and an S corporation is never a PTP, so leave this unanswered on an sCorp item — the derivation answers FALSE there off ../entityType without asking. OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership downstream.
A SCHEDULE K-1 (FORM 8865) ITEM IS ASKED TOO. That K-1 is a partnership item on /formK1s (../writableLine28cForeignPartnership TRUE) and prints no item D, but IRC 469(k)(2) defines a publicly traded partnership as ANY partnership whose interests are traded on an established securities market or are readily tradable on a secondary market, foreign partnerships included, so the question stays and ../itemDUnanswered keeps the item unfinished until it is answered. the application asks it in the statute's words for such an item: "Are interests in this partnership traded on an established securities market, or readily tradable on a secondary market?"
IT IS THE ONLY INPUT FOR ITEM D, and the sentence that stood here until then said otherwise: it directed a reader to ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived "where item D should also be readable off an answered qualified PTP amount". That second reading is GONE — ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived is retired in place to a bare alias of ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership, so nothing in this dictionary infers item D from any other answer. UNANSWERED IS NO LONGER FALSE: leaving this field blank on a PARTNERSHIP K-1 now leaves ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership and the K-1's whole PTP surface INCOMPLETE rather than defaulting it to "not a PTP". The project owner's words are the rule: item D "should be a user input, no default needed", and an unanswered one is "2. Genuinely unanswered".
WHAT IT SELECTS, and it is the whole reason this field exists rather than a return-level amount: it routes this K-1's box 20 code Z section 199A amount (../writableQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss) to the QUALIFIED PTP INCOME half of Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28. An unchecked K-1's code Z amount is per-business QBI, which this dictionary takes through qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses instead, so it is not read here.
AND IT NOW SELECTS THE SECTION 469 REGIME TOO. This sentence previously read that item D was NOT wired into section 469 and that answering it moved no Schedule E value; that is no longer true and the correction rides with the fill that made it false. A checked box, on a K-1 whose items are PASSIVE, now routes this K-1 through ../appliesPtpSection469 into the per-PTP regime of IRC 469(k): ../passiveNet contributes nothing to the Form 8582 pool and an overall gain is nonpassive income on Schedule E line 28 column (k). See ../ptpSection469Net. On a K-1 whose participation is answered-true the flag still moves no section 469 value, because the regime is gated on ../lossIsPassive. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box D (Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)).

Fact.Name: Item D, read from the checkbox — INCOMPLETE when a partnership K-1 has not answered it
Fact.Description:
Whether this K-1's item D is checked. TWO arms and NO catch-all, which is the whole of what changed on 2026-08-22: the ANSWER (../writableIsPubliclyTradedPartnership) when it is answered, FALSE on an S-corporation K-1 because that form has no item D to answer, and INCOMPLETE otherwise.
WHAT THIS FACT USED TO DO, kept because the removal is the point rather than a detail: it was named "Item D, complete-safe" and its second arm was a bare True/False catch-all defaulting an unanswered item D to FALSE, justified in its own authority comment as "this repo's complete-safety convention". The project owner ended that on 2026-08-22 — item D "should be a user input, no default needed", and an unanswered one is "2. Genuinely unanswered". A FALSE default is an ASSERTION that the partnership is not publicly traded, made on the filer's behalf, and it is wrong in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction on a real PTP: it releases the K-1 from the per-PTP §469(k) regime so a PTP loss nets against other activities' passive income, and it withholds the §199A qualified-PTP routing of an answered box 20 code Z amount. Nothing on the return showed either. Failing closed makes the application ask.
THE sCORP ARM IS NOT A DEFAULT, and the distinction is the reason it is allowed to exist beside a no-default rule: it is a FORM-KIND fact. Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) has no publicly-traded checkbox anywhere on it — its Part I item D is "Corporation’s total number of shares" — so there is no answer to be missing, and the string "publicly traded" does not occur in the form at all. §469(k)(2) defines a publicly traded partnership as a PARTNERSHIP, so an S corporation is outside the definition by its entity kind. This arm therefore states a fact about the FORM, not a guess about the filer.
WHAT THE sCORP ARM DOES NOT SAY, stated because the shorter claim is tempting and wrong: it does NOT say that an S-corporation shareholder cannot have qualified PTP income. They can — the corporation holds the PTP units and passes the income through, and the shareholder instructions say so at box 17 Code V ("qualified publicly traded partnership (PTP) income from your S corporation"). What the arm says is that THIS K-1, the 1120-S one, has no item D to answer, because item D is a Form 1065 checkbox. The §199A route this dictionary models is the 1065 box 20 code Z one, and it has no box 17 code V intake at all — so an S-corporation shareholder with genuine qualified PTP income cannot enter it here, and ../hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD refuses the attempt rather than routing a 1065 field entered on a 1120-S K-1. NAMED GAP; it pre-dates this unit and belongs to a box-17 code V intake, not to item D.
IT REQUIRES AN ANSWERED entityType, deliberately. The arm is All(IsComplete(../entityType), Equal(../entityType, sCorp)). The IsComplete guard is what makes that arm resolve at all: without it, Equal() over an unanswered Enum is Incomplete and the whole Switch would hang on every K-1 that never recorded its entity type. WITH it the arm is Complete FALSE there, because AllOperator returns Complete(false) as soon as ANY member is Complete-false — head OR tail; its accumulator tests every thunk, not only the first. An UNANSWERED entityType therefore falls through to Incomplete and still needs item D answered — which is the right way round: "I did not say what kind of K-1 this is" is not a statement that it is an S corporation.
THE TRUTH TABLE, and the third row is the new one: item D answered (either way) -> the answer item D unanswered, entityType answered sCorp -> FALSE item D unanswered, otherwise -> INCOMPLETE (NEW 2026-08-22)
WHAT GOES INCOMPLETE WITH IT on a partnership K-1 whose item D is unanswered, measured rather than guessed (the full list is in the unit's commit body): ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived (a bare alias of this fact since the same unit), ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner and through it ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption and ../lossIsPassive, ../appliesPtpSection469 and the whole §469(k) per-PTP chain, and — ONLY when the K-1 answers a box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount — ../reportsQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, ../hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD and the /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD chain above it. The confinement is real and is worth stating: on a K-1 with NO §179 election and NO code Z amount, ../section179OnPtp, ../reportsQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss and ../hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD all resolve Complete FALSE, because each tests IsComplete on the answer that would matter BEFORE it reads item D.
AND THE REST OF THE CHAIN COMES OUT AS PLACEHOLDER NUMBERS, NOT AS INCOMPLETE — the sentence above says "goes Incomplete" and that is true only of the facts it names. Everything below ../appliesPtpSection469 is Switch-shaped, and a Switch whose matching Case is reached with the accumulated completeness already false returns its value asPlaceholder: ../passiveNet, ../ptpCurrentYearNet, ../partIINonpassivePart, /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome, /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi and /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction all resolve to Placeholder FIGURES. A Placeholder exposes its value exactly like a Complete one — only .complete differs. THAT IS WHY THIS UNIT ALSO SHIPS A FLOW MEMBER: ../itemDUnanswered aggregates into /formK1sItemDIsComplete, which joins flow:/flowIncomplete's All. Without it, neither return-level gate saw the missing answer — flow:/flowIsKnockedOut carries a Placeholder of False beneath its Any and reads false, and /flowIncomplete had no /formK1s member — so the fail-closed posture failed OPEN and the return looked finished.

Fact.Name: Item D is still unanswered on this K-1 (interview-completeness flag)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when this K-1 item has neither answered the printed item D checkbox (../writableIsPubliclyTradedPartnership) nor recorded an entity type of sCorp, which is the one case where item D is settled without being asked. It is the per-item half of /formK1sItemDIsComplete, which is a member of flow:/flowIncomplete.
WHY IT EXISTS, and it is a correction to what this unit first shipped. Removing item D's FALSE default made ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership INCOMPLETE on an unanswered partnership K-1 — but incompleteness does NOT propagate as a bare Incomplete through the Schedule E chain. Most of the chain is Switch-shaped, and a Switch whose matching Case is reached with the accumulated completeness already false returns its value asPlaceholder: /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome, /taxableIncomeBeforeQbi and /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction all come out as PLACEHOLDER NUMBERS. A Placeholder exposes its value exactly like a Complete one — only .complete differs — and NEITHER return-level gate saw it: flow:/flowIsKnockedOut carries a Placeholder of False beneath its Any, and flow:/flowIncomplete had no /formK1s member at all. So the fail-closed posture failed OPEN: the return looked finished and carried numbers computed from an answer the filer never gave. This flag, and the aggregate above it, are what close that.
IT IS NOT A REFUSAL, deliberately. An unanswered item D is an UNFINISHED INTERVIEW, not a return this dictionary cannot compute, so the remedy is a /flowIncomplete member — the same shape as every other section's IsDone/IsComplete fact — and not a knockout. Nothing here carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue and no new guard was added.
COMPLETE ON EVERY INPUT, which is the whole requirement on a completeness flag: the first disjunct is an IsComplete, which always resolves; the second is All(IsComplete(../entityType), Equal(...)), and All() returns Complete(false) as soon as ANY member is Complete-false, so an unanswered ../entityType makes that disjunct Complete FALSE rather than Incomplete. An Any() of two Complete operands is Complete, and Not() of a Complete is Complete. This fact can therefore never be Incomplete or Placeholder, and neither can the aggregate that counts it.

Fact.Name: Every K-1 has settled item D (flow:/flowIncomplete member)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when no /formK1s item still needs its item D answered — Count(/formK1s/*/itemDUnanswered) is zero — and TRUE on a return that claims no K-1 income at all. It is a MEMBER of flow:/flowIncomplete's All, so a return holding a partnership K-1 whose item D is blank reports itself UNFINISHED instead of filing on Placeholder numbers.
WHY A /flowIncomplete MEMBER AND NOT A KNOCKOUT, stated because the choice is the whole design and the other one was available: a blank item D is a question the interview has not asked yet, not a contradiction the graph cannot resolve. A knockout says "this return cannot be filed"; this says "this return is not finished". The one refusal in this area, /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD, keeps its own narrower job — an ANSWERED qualified PTP amount beside an item D answered FALSE — and is untouched by this fact.
WHAT IT CATCHES THAT NOTHING ELSE DID. flow:/flowIncomplete's All had no /formK1s member of any kind, and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut carries a Placeholder of False beneath its Any, so an unanswered item D produced Placeholder numbers on Schedule E and through to /qualifiedBusinessIncomeDeduction while BOTH return-level gates read exactly as they do on a finished, un-refused return. That is the "Placeholder tail" class the interest:/flowKnockoutHasBonds allowlist row already names.
COMPLETE ON EVERY INPUT: ../itemDUnanswered is Complete on every input by construction, Count() over a vector of Complete booleans is Complete (and is 0 on an empty collection), and the /claimsK1Income arm keeps a return with no K-1 intake out of the collection entirely. So this member can never itself be the thing that makes flow:/flowIncomplete unresolvable.

Fact.Name: Item D, derived — RETIRED IN PLACE 2026-08-22; now a bare alias of the checkbox
Fact.Description:
RETIRED IN PLACE. This fact is now ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership and nothing else. It reads no other answer, it cannot disagree with the checkbox, and it exists only so that its two readers and the allowlists, ledgers and baseline rows that name it do not have to move.
WHAT IT USED TO BE, kept verbatim in substance because the retirement is only legible against it: Any(../isPubliclyTradedPartnership, IsComplete(../writableQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss)) — item D read from EITHER the printed checkbox OR an ANSWERED box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount. Its own Description disclosed the price — a NAMED GAP in which a code-Z-without-item-D K-1 was a PTP for §199A and a non-PTP for §469(k), a named gap — and the participation presumption then had to argue, at ../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner, for reading the RAW checkbox so the presumption and the §469(k) regime would turn on together.
WHY IT IS RETIRED RATHER THAN KEPT. The project owner ruled on 2026-08-22 that this fact and ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership are "the same thing and should be a user input, no default needed". Once item D has no default there is nothing for a second reading to be safer than: the derivation's whole purpose was to rescue an amount that the FALSE default would otherwise have dropped silently, and a fact that now fails closed does not drop it silently — it refuses (item D answered false) or it does not compute (item D unanswered). THAT GAP CLOSES BY CONSTRUCTION: there are no longer two readings of item D to disagree.
WHY IT IS NOT DELETED, so the choice is not mistaken for an oversight: deleting a fact owes four allowlists plus a reviewed regeneration of the completeness-probe baseline (corrections #9), and it moves every conformance-baseline row that names the path. Retiring in place is the route the records contract names first, and it is the same route this module took for the /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD chain — which this unit has just brought back to life, which is itself the argument for keeping retired paths addressable.
ITS TWO READERS ARE LEFT POINTING AT IT and both now read the checkbox through it: ../reportsQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss (and through it ../qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28) and ../hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD. Moving them to the alias would be a no-op on values and would cost the diff, so it is not done.
COMPLETENESS: it is now exactly as complete as ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership — Complete on an answered item D, Complete FALSE on an sCorp K-1, INCOMPLETE on an unanswered partnership K-1.

Fact.Name: Qualified PTP income or (loss) from this PTP (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 20, code Z)
Fact.Description:
The QUALIFIED PTP income or (loss) this publicly traded partnership reported to the partner in the box 20 code Z section 199A statement — Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28's PTP half, for THIS K-1. Answer it only on a K-1 whose item D is checked (../writableIsPubliclyTradedPartnership); a code Z amount from a partnership that is not a PTP is per-business QBI and belongs to qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses instead. Answering it WITHOUT checking item D is not refused and not dropped: an answered amount here is itself one of the two signals that establish item D (../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived), so the amount routes. OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss downstream.
SIGN — THE ONE THING NOT TO "FIX". NO Min $0 limit, deliberately: this is income OR (LOSS), and "Line 6. Enter income as a positive number and losses as a negative number". The floor is Form 8995 line 8 / Form 8995-A line 30, built inside each consumer, so a qualified PTP loss stops at the REIT/PTP subtotal and can never eat the separately floored QBI component. A Min $0 here would delete the loss instead.
NOT THE SAME NUMBER AS BOX 1, which is why it is its own field rather than a derivation. Code Z reports the partner's share of QUALIFIED items only: "The amounts reported to you reflect your distributive share of items from the partnership's trade(s), business(es), or aggregation(s), and may include items that aren't includible in your calculation of the QBI deduction" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 30), and the section 199A definition excludes "any loss or deduction disallowed in determining your taxable income for the year" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 5).
WHAT IS NOT ASKED HERE, and it is a real limit on what an answer can mean: the PTP suspended-loss tracking the same instructions require — "you must track each loss or deduction from a PTP until the loss or deduction is no longer suspended" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995.pdf, page 4) — is cross-year state this single-year graph does not hold. The prior-year half of it IS asked, once and at return level, as the attested carry-IN qbi:/writableQualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear (Form 8995 line 7). interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Qualified PTP income or (loss) from this K-1, routed by item D
Fact.Description: This K-1's contribution to the qualified PTP half of Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28: the answered box 20 code Z amount when ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership, else $0. Two things it is doing at once, and the second is the router the contract for this fill named. (1) COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 when the taxpayer answered nothing, so every pre-fill /formK1s item is byte-identical. (2) ITEM-D GATED, on the DERIVED reading of item D since a K-1 with no qualified PTP amount answered and item D unchecked contributes $0, because an ordinary code Z amount is per-business QBI and belongs to qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses instead. An ANSWERED qualified PTP amount now establishes item D by itself and reaches line 6. MAY BE NEGATIVE, floor and all: the floor is the consumers' line 8 / line 30, not this node's.

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports a qualified PTP amount (existence flag)
Fact.Description:
True exactly when item D is established AND the box 20 code Z amount is ANSWERED. This is an EXISTENCE test, never a magnitude test, and that is load-bearing: the amount may be NEGATIVE, so a qualified PTP LOSS has to select the consumers' REIT/PTP arm too. It reads the RAW writable's IsComplete rather than the complete-safe alias, which always resolves. Aggregated by /hasK1QualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss into the third disjunct of qbi:/hasQualifiedReitOrPtpIntake.
ITEM D IS THE DERIVED READING, ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived rather than the raw checkbox alias ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership. The observable change is confined to one population: a K-1 that ANSWERS a qualified PTP amount with item D unchecked now routes that amount to Form 8995 line 6 instead of dropping it and blocking submission. Every other K-1 resolves identically, because the derived fact and the checkbox alias agree wherever the filer did not contradict themselves.

Fact.Name: This K-1 answers a qualified PTP amount with item D unchecked (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
LIVE AGAIN. It reads: ../writableQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss ANSWERED on a K-1 whose item D is not established. That is a REPRESENTABLE contradiction once more, and this fact fires on it.
THE TWO DAYS IT WAS DEAD, recorded rather than erased because the round trip is the lesson. Between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-22 this Description read "RETIRED IN PLACE AND NOW UNREACHABLE": item D had been made DERIVED, an answered qualified PTP amount was itself one of the two things that established it, so the two conjuncts could not hold at once and the fact was Complete FALSE on every input. The project owner then ruled that item D is a single user input with no default and no inference, ../isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived retired into the checkbox, and the contradiction became representable again. Nothing about the guard changed; what changed is the fact it reads.
THE THREE STATES IT NOW HAS, and only the first is a refusal: amount ANSWERED, item D answered FALSE -> TRUE. The refusal fires. The two answers contradict each other and only the filer can say which is right (uncheck the amount, or check item D). NOTE this includes an S-CORPORATION K-1 that answers a qualified PTP amount: ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership resolves FALSE off ../entityType, so the contradiction is complete and the return is refused. THAT IS NOT A NEW POPULATION. Up to 2026-08-20 this fact read the raw alias ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership, whose FALSE default covered an sCorp item, so an sCorp K-1 answering a qualified PTP amount refused then too; only between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-22 did it route. AND THE REASON IS NARROWER THAN "an S corporation cannot have qualified PTP income", which would be FALSE. An S corporation can hold PTP units and pass the income through: "you may be allowed a deduction of up to 20% of your net qualified business income (QBI) plus 20% of your qualified REIT dividends ... and qualified publicly traded partnership (PTP) income from your S corporation" (Shareholder's Inst. for Sch. K-1 (Form 1120-S), Code V). What this dictionary refuses is narrower and is a DATA-COMPLETENESS refusal on an unmodelled route: ../writableQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss is documented as the Schedule K-1 (FORM 1065) box 20 code Z field, and an S corporation reports its section 199A statement in box 17 code V of a 1120-S K-1, for which this dictionary has NO intake at all. So an answer there is a 1065 field filled in on a 1120-S K-1. NAMED GAP, disclosed rather than left as an implication: an S-corporation shareholder with genuine qualified PTP income has no way to enter it in this dictionary, and the right fix is a box-17 code V intake, not a wider item D. That gap PRE-DATES this unit and is neither widened nor closed by it. amount ANSWERED, item D UNANSWERED -> INCOMPLETE. It does not fire and it does not resolve. This is the fail-closed state: the filer has not yet said whether the two answers contradict each other, so the graph declines to decide. WHERE THAT IS AND IS NOT VISIBLE, measured rather than assumed, because the answer surprised this unit's own prediction: flow:/flowIsKnockedOut reads PLACEHOLDER FALSE on such a return, NOT Incomplete. Its Any() derivation IS Incomplete (Any() returns Incomplete past a non-Complete-true member), but the fact carries a Placeholder of False, and a Fact falls back to its Placeholder when its Derived does not resolve. So the flow gate looks exactly like an ordinary un-refused return, and the incompleteness is legible ONLY on the K-1's own facts — this one, /hasK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD and /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD, each Incomplete. That is stated here because a reader checking "does the return still knock out?" at the flow gate would read false and conclude wrongly. WHAT DOES CATCH IT, added in the same unit after review: the OTHER return-level gate. /formK1sItemDIsComplete is a member of flow:/flowIncomplete's All, so such a return reports itself UNFINISHED (Complete true) instead of filing on Placeholder numbers. The converse holds and matters more: a return knocked out for an UNRELATED reason still knocks out, because Any() returns Complete(true) past any number of Incomplete members, whatever item D is doing. The IsComplete conjunct is Complete-false, and All() returns Complete(false) as soon as any member is Complete(false), so an Incomplete item D cannot leak out of this fact on a K-1 with no code Z amount. That confinement is what keeps a plain box-1 K-1 out of the refusal chain.
WHY THE REFUSAL IS THE RIGHT ANSWER on the firing population, restated for the successor allowlist that now carries it: the contradiction it flags made the router (../qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss) drop the amount and UNDER-state the section 199A deduction with no visible cause (the refuse-and-flag pattern, the twin of ../hasUnassessedGuaranteedPayments). Both inputs are TAXPAYER-TRANSCRIBED from one printed page — item D is a checkbox the filer copies, and the amount's own instructions restrict it to a K-1 whose item D is checked — so a disagreement between them is a transcription error the filer can fix, not a tax question this dictionary could answer for them.

Fact.Name: This PTP is a specified service trade or business (Schedule A (Form 8995-A), Part II)
Fact.Description:
Whether the publicly traded partnership on this K-1 is a specified service trade or business (SSTB). The section 199A instructions keep PTP SSTBs on their own schedule part — "Schedule A (Form 8995-A), Part II, should be used for SSTBs that are PTPs, and Part I should be used for all other SSTBs" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8995a.pdf, page 5) — and warn that "PTP income generated by an SSTB may be limited to the applicable percentage if your taxable income is within the phase-in" range (lines 404-405; the word "range" is the first word past the cited span, lost to the page break at line 406). PER-PTP, not per-return: the return-level qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/isSstb flag is about the filer's own trades or businesses and says nothing about a partnership they merely hold units in.
WHAT ANSWERING IT TRUE DOES IN THIS DICTIONARY, stated plainly because it is an input to a COMPUTATION and not to a refusal: below the section 199A threshold no SSTB limitation applies at all and the raw amount is correct, so the flag changes nothing; at or above the threshold a TRUE answer routes this PTP's amount through Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II line 16 (qbi:/formK1s/*/sstbPtpQualifiedAmount), line 17 (qbi:/sstbPtpQualifiedAmountBeforeApplicablePercentage) and the applicable percentage at line 24 (qbi:/sstbPtpQualifiedAmountAfterApplicablePercentage), which the rebodied qbi:/qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss substitutes for the raw amount. Nothing is refused, and the FALSE default remains the one that cannot over-refuse. OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../qualifiedPtpIsSstb downstream.

Fact.Name: This PTP is an SSTB, complete-safe
Fact.Description: Whether this K-1's PTP is a specified service trade or business, defaulting to FALSE when unanswered (complete-safe alias of ../writableQualifiedPtpIsSstb). The false default is the one that CANNOT over-refuse: it withholds a knockout rather than raising one on a filer who never answered the question. The cost is disclosed: an above-threshold filer who holds an SSTB PTP and leaves this unanswered gets the unlimited amount, which over-states the deduction. That is the same shape as every other unanswered-intake default in this dictionary and is why the question has to be asked at intake, not inferred.

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports a qualified PTP amount from an SSTB PTP (Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II line 16 selector)
Fact.Description: True when this item both reports a qualified PTP amount (../reportsQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss) and declares that PTP an SSTB (../qualifiedPtpIsSstb). It is the per-item SELECTOR for Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II line 16 — it is the When of qbi:/formK1s/*/sstbPtpQualifiedAmount — and it is aggregated by /hasK1SstbQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, which gates the line 17 total and the line 24 applicable-percentage reduction. Below the section 199A threshold there is no SSTB limitation to apply, so this flag alone reduces nothing.

Fact.Name: K-1 section 179 deduction (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 12 / (Form 1120-S) box 11)
Fact.Description:
Box 12 of this partnership K-1 (box 11 on the Form 1120-S twin): the partner's or shareholder's share of the entity's section 179 expense deduction, exactly as printed. A section 179 amount is an EXPENSE ALLOWANCE the entity elected and reports as a POSITIVE figure, so the writable carries a Min $0 limit; there is no negative box 12. OPTIONAL writable; use the derived ../section179Elected downstream. No rounding at intake.
ANSWERING IT NONZERO OBLIGES THREE MORE ANSWERS, because each of the partner-level limitations reaches the section 179 deduction BY NAME and this dictionary refuses rather than approximates any of them: ../basis must be answered and large enough to absorb this deduction alongside any box-1 loss (section 704(d)/1366(d) treats section 179 as its own loss/deduction category sharing one basis pool), ../materiallyParticipated must leave the K-1 NONPASSIVE, and ../fullyAtRisk must not be answered false. Each failure raises its own knockout rather than producing a number: /knockoutK1Section179Basis, /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited. Item D checked raises /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp UNLESS ../materiallyParticipated is answered TRUE (narrowed: the PTP rules the box-12 fork points at govern only passive activities held through the PTP, so a materially participating PTP partner reaches column (j) like any other nonpassive K-1; an unanswered participation answer still refuses, per IRC 469(h)(2)), and a second electing activity anywhere on the return raises /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities. THREE claims in the paragraph above are now narrower than they read. (a) ../materiallyParticipated need not "leave the K-1 NONPASSIVE": a PASSIVE K-1's share is an ordinary passive-activity deduction and computes. (b) ../fullyAtRisk answered false no longer refuses either; the share is capped by ../atRiskAllowedSection179. (c) Item D no longer refuses on an UNANSWERED participation answer unless item G says GENERAL PARTNER — on a limited partner IRC 469(h)(2) presumes the interest passive and the share computes through the PTP step-1 chain. What still refuses from this list: an unanswered or insufficient ../basis, a second electing activity, and the general-partner-PTP cell just named.
THE SCHEDULE SE RESIDUAL SURVIVES THIS FILL UNCHANGED, restated rather than silently inherited: a general partner must reduce box 14A by the section 179 deduction before Schedule SE (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 22), and ../writableSeEarnings already discloses that reduction as unmodeled and names its direction (entering the printed 14A OVER-states SE tax and never under-states it). A box-12 intake does not change what box 14A says, so nothing here closes that gap. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 12 (Section 179 deduction), Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 11 (Section 179 deduction).

Fact.Name: K-1 section 179 deduction (box 12), complete-safe
Fact.Description: Box 12 of this K-1, defaulting to $0 when unanswered (complete-safe alias of ../writableSection179Deduction, the IsComplete-guard-per-member pattern that keeps every pre-existing /formK1s item resolving). This is the ELECTED amount the entity passed through, BEFORE any partner-level limitation; the amount that actually reaches Schedule E line 28 column (j) is ../section179ColumnJ.

Fact.Name: This K-1 passes through a section 179 election (existence flag)
Fact.Description: True exactly when this K-1's box 12 is answered AND positive. An entity that prints a literal 0 in box 12 has elected nothing, so 0 is NOT an election and raises no knockout — that boundary is pinned by the node-test pair scheduleE/k1-179-box12-zero-is-not-an-election (false) against scheduleE/k1-179-nonpassive-flows-column-j (true). Counted by /k1Section179ElectingCount, which with the rental-side count decides whether the return has more than one activity electing section 179.

Fact.Name: This K-1 elects §179 without proven basis to absorb it (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
NARROWED TO ITS UNANSWERED-BASIS ARM. True when this K-1 passes through a section 179 deduction (../electsSection179) and ../basis is UNANSWERED. Raises /hasK1Section179WithoutSufficientBasis -> /knockoutK1Section179Basis.
WHAT THIS FLAG NO LONGER DOES, and it was the whole of its population until today: it no longer fires because ../basis is merely SMALLER than ../ordinaryLoss + ../section179Elected. Its own retired text said why it had to — "This dictionary has exactly one loss class wired to ../basisAllowedLoss (../ordinaryLoss); adding a second would mean re-writing that cleanroom-verified formula to apportion ... the guard is a fence, not new math" — and that apportionment now exists: ../basisCompetingItemsTotal is the partner basis worksheet's line 15s column C, ../basisAllowedLoss its line 15a column D and ../basisAllowedSection179 its line 15i column D, all three on the printed pro rata rule reassembled at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 5 with its right-column continuation at 267-271. An insufficient basis is now COMPUTED, not refused, and the K-1's section 179 deduction reaches Schedule E column (j) at its allowed share.
WHY THE UNANSWERED ARM SURVIVES, unchanged in text and in reasoning: ../basisAllowedLoss treats an unanswered ../basis as "allow 0 loss", which is safe for a LOSS because it withholds a deduction. That default cannot be reused here — withholding is not available once a section 179 amount has to be either deducted or not, and an unanswered basis cannot show what the deduction's share of it would be. So this flag keeps the PROVE-IT-OR-REFUSE posture, exactly as ../seAssessmentSatisfied does for box 14: the taxpayer must assert what their basis is, and ANY answer is now accepted — where before only an answer big enough was. That is a data-COMPLETENESS refusal with no in-repo remedy, which is the one class REFUSAL-VERDICTS.md entitles to stand permanently, and the allowlist row moves to correct-refusal in the same commit.
COMPLETE-SAFE: false whenever nothing is elected, so every /formK1s item without a box-12 amount resolves Complete false.

Fact.Name: This K-1 elects §179 on a publicly traded partnership whose items may be passive (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when this K-1 passes through a section 179 deduction (../electsSection179) on a K-1 whose item D is checked (../isPubliclyTradedPartnership) AND material participation is not affirmatively answered — that is, ../materiallyParticipated is answered FALSE or is UNANSWERED. Raises /hasK1Section179OnPtp -> /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp.
NARROWED. It used to fire on item D alone, and its Description used to say "It fires regardless of ../materiallyParticipated, which is the point: item D decides, not participation." That reading does not survive the paragraph the box-12 fork points AT. The fork says to report the amount "following the rules for PTPs under Publicly traded partnerships, earlier", and those rules state their own scope: the partner instructions send the reader to the numbered steps to figure and report income, gains and losses from passive activities "held through each PTP you owned during the tax year". A partner who MATERIALLY PARTICIPATES holds no passive activity in that PTP, so the numbered steps have nothing to partition and the preceding box-12 sentence governs on its own terms: an amount that "isn't a passive activity deduction" is "report[ed] in column (j) of Schedule E (Form 1040), line 28". This is the SAME regime boundary ../appliesPtpSection469 already ships (item D AND ../lossIsPassive) — the fence is now drawn in one place instead of two that disagreed.
WHY UNANSWERED STAYS REFUSED, and it is the whole reason this is a narrowing rather than a retirement. ../lossIsPassive is false when ../materiallyParticipated is answered-true OR UNANSWERED, so a bare Not(../lossIsPassive) here would hand the unanswered PTP a full column (j) deduction. IRC 469(h)(2) says an interest in a limited partnership as a limited partner is not one with respect to which the taxpayer materially participates, except as regulations provide; a PTP interest is such an interest, so for a PTP specifically the module's usual "unanswered means nonpassive" default is presumptively the WRONG way round, and its error is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE (a deduction allowed in full that section 469 would limit). Refusing while the regime selection is unresolved needs no statutory argument at all: one of the two regimes the fork chooses between is not built, and nothing in the data says which applies.
WHAT STILL REFUSES, therefore, and what it is waiting on: a PTP whose items ARE passive. There the box-12 share is a passive activity deduction of that PTP and belongs INSIDE step 1's combination ("Combine any current-year income, gains, and losses, and any prior-year unallowed losses"), which ../ptpCurrentYearNet does not carry — that fact's own Description says "ONLY BOX 1 IS IN IT". Its replacement, /formK1s/*/ptpSection179InCombination, is not built. Note that this population is ALSO refused by /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited on the same facts, so the two guards overlap there deliberately; the population only THIS flag holds is the unanswered-participation PTP. BOTH claims in this paragraph are SPENT. The successor contract is DISCHARGED and ../ptpCurrentYearNet's post-section-179 twin carries the share; /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited has been removed, so the overlap it describes no longer exists and the unanswered-participation PTP is the only population this flag holds - which is what the sentence's last clause already said.
COMPLETE-SAFE: false whenever nothing is elected; ../isPubliclyTradedPartnership is itself the complete-safe alias (false when item D is unanswered); and the participation test is the IsComplete/Switch idiom rather than a Not() over an unanswered Boolean, which would resolve Incomplete rather than false.
DISCHARGED. NARROWED AGAIN, to the UNANSWERED-participation PTP alone. The paragraph above headed "WHAT STILL REFUSES, THEREFORE" named the affirmatively PASSIVE PTP and its successor contract by path; that contract is discharged and the population COMPUTES - ../ptpSection179Allowed is a term of ../ptpCurrentYearNetAfterSection179, and the post-section-179 chain reaches Schedule E column (k) through ../partIINonpassivePart, Form 4952 line 4h through ../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome and next year's carry-in through ../ptpSuspendedLossCarryOut. WHAT SURVIVES is the second population that paragraph named and exactly that: an item-D PTP whose ../materiallyParticipated is UNANSWERED, where IRC 469(h)(2) makes the module's "unanswered means nonpassive" default presumptively wrong in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction. NARROWED AGAIN, and the paragraph directly above is the one this note answers. That unit built the presumption: on an item-D PTP held as a LIMITED partner (../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner) an unanswered ../materiallyParticipated now resolves PASSIVE through ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption, ../appliesPtpSection469 is TRUE there, and the box-12 share computes through ../ptpSection179Allowed and the post-section-179 step-1 chain. So the LIMITED-partner cell no longer refuses and the arm that used to catch it returns False.
WHAT SURVIVES IS ONE CELL AND IT IS A DATA-COMPLETENESS REFUSAL, not a deferred build: an item-D PTP whose item G says GENERAL PARTNER and whose participation answer is MISSING, with a box-12 amount elected. IRC 469(h)(2) does not reach a general partner — the Form 8582 instructions carve them out by name for purposes of the material participation tests — so no presumption resolves the regime, and the box-12 fork chooses between column (j) and the PTP steps on exactly the answer that is absent. Only the taxpayer's answer resolves that regime question, which is what makes the refusal permanent rather than owed.
AND IT IS A CHOICE, NOT A NECESSITY. The same missing answer is DEFAULTED one field away: the BOX-1 leg takes the nonpassive default on this very cell and the return files, which k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-general-partner-no-box12-files-nonpassive shows at $60,000. What this flag declines is EXTENDING that taxpayer-favourable default to the section 179 share, and the divergence it protects is narrow and nameable: an overall LOSS (suspended per-PTP instead of deducted in full), Form 4952 line 4h (../ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome) and the Form 4562 line-11 business-income cone. The population is witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleE/k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-general-partner-still-refuses, and its BOUNDARY by k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-general-partner-no-box12-files-nonpassive: a general-partner PTP that elects NOTHING files, because the first arm of this Switch fires before item D is ever read.
THE CARRIER, and it is CLOSED rather than pending: a permanent data-completeness refusal belongs in scripts/test_refusal_successor_allowlist.tsv as a correct-refusal row, and that row LANDED 2026-08-22 in this unit's own review-fix commit under the lead's explicit authorisation. The row now holds the whole reasoning and the three pinning node tests.

Fact.Name: Partnership / S-corp K-1 ordinary loss magnitude (aggregate)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/ordinaryLoss), gated by /claimsK1Income (0 for no K-1). Was the scalar /k1OrdinaryLoss; now the aggregate over all K-1 items. DISPOSITION: EXPORTED as a CULMINATING fact. Re-measured on this trunk: no fact's depends_on names this path, no syndoc workbook lists it in a required VALUE_FACTS tuple, no flow gate reads it — it terminates the computation, which is what downstreamFacts asserts (js/src/TaxLogicTestCoverageReporter.ts reads the flag as `culminating`). The claim is TRUE because the value is a REAL OUTPUT rather than an engine-internal fiction: this fact's own authority cite is 2025 Schedule E line 28 column (g)/(i), a printed column on a FILED schedule, and a CollectionSum over K-1 items is the same per-item-then-total shape the printed Part II uses (line 28's rows, totalled at lines 29a/30). DENOMINATOR: of the seven aggregates in this K-1 loss-limitation ladder, five already carry Export downstreamFacts (/k1BasisSuspendedLoss, /k1AtRiskAllowedLoss, /k1AtRiskSuspendedLoss, /k1NonpassiveAllowedLoss, /k1PassiveSuspendedLoss) — every one of them equally consumer-less. This fact and /k1BasisAllowedLoss were the two that did not, which made the ladder legible to a reader outside the graph at five of its seven rungs and dark at the other two.
mef is deliberately NOT claimed (the Schedule H line): mef asserts the IRS RECEIVES the element, an e-file/MeF schema question project invariant #7 excludes and no vendored source can settle. None of the five exporting siblings claims it either. The Export changes no resolved value — it is metadata on the Fact element, absent from the manifest schema and from the baseline row shape. Witnessed by the node test already pinning this path (scheduleE/i6198-line21-k1-example, 1,600.00 cent-exact).

Fact.Name: K-1 ordinary loss allowed by the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation (aggregate)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/basisAllowedLoss), gated by /claimsK1Income. Was the scalar /k1BasisAllowedLoss. interpretation:provisional.
DISPOSITION: EXPORTED as a CULMINATING fact, and this is the one of the five whose evidence is NOT a printed form line — stated plainly rather than blurred into the others. The 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation has no IRS form of its own (unlike the 465 at-risk limitation, which prints as Form 6198): it is computed on a worksheet the partner keeps, so no printed line carries this figure and the "it names its own form line" argument that carries /k1OrdinaryLoss and /rentalSection179Deduction is unavailable here.
What decides it instead is the DIRECT TWIN, which the export disposition table missed by naming the three at-risk/nonpassive siblings: /k1BasisSuspendedLoss is the other half of THIS limitation — same 704(d)/1366(d) authority, same CollectionSum-gated-by-/claimsK1Income body, and the same absence of a printed line — and it has carried Export downstreamFacts all along. Allowed-vs-suspended is one computation split in two, so exporting the suspended half and not the allowed half was an asymmetry inside a single commit lineage with no reason behind it: a reviewer could see what the basis limitation DISALLOWED and not what it ALLOWED. Re-measured on this trunk: no fact's depends_on names this path, no syndoc VALUE_FACTS tuple lists it, no flow gate reads it, so it does terminate the computation and downstreamFacts (`culminating` in js/src/TaxLogicTestCoverageReporter.ts) is the accurate flag.
mef is deliberately NOT claimed — nothing here is transmitted, which is if anything clearer for this fact than for the other four (invariant #7). The Export changes no resolved value: metadata on the Fact element, absent from the manifest schema and from the baseline row shape. Witnessed by scheduleE/i6198-line21-k1-example (1,600.00 cent-exact, basis non-binding on that case). interpretation:provisional is unchanged by this disposition.

Fact.Name: This K-1's rental income or (loss) — Schedule K-1 boxes 2 and 3, complete safe and signed
Fact.Description:
The SIGNED net of the two RENTAL boxes of this partnership / S corporation Schedule K-1: box 2 (net rental real estate income or loss) plus box 3 (other net rental income or loss), each taken through an IsComplete Switch defaulting to $0 so an item that answered neither contributes a Complete $0 and the aggregates over this collection stay Complete. Positive is income, negative is a loss.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE QUANTITY FROM ../ordinaryIncome, and this is the whole finding: ../ordinaryIncome is Schedule K-1 BOX 1 ONLY, and every per item fact around it — ../lossIsPassive, ../materiallyParticipated, ../fullyAtRisk, ../basisAllowedLoss, ../atRiskAllowedLoss, ../passiveNet, ../partIINonpassivePart — describes the box 1 TRADE OR BUSINESS activity. Boxes 2 and 3 are a DIFFERENT activity on the same document. Until this date a partner whose K-1 reported only box 2 or box 3 reported $0 on the whole return.
ONLY THE INCOME SIDE OF THIS FACT IS WIRED, and the limit is stated rather than left to be discovered: /k1RentalRealEstateIncomeTotal (Schedule E Part II line 32) and /k1RentalRealEstatePoolIncomeTotal (the section 8582 pool) both read ../k1RentalRealEstateRentalIncome, which floors this net at zero. A box 2 or box 3 LOSS is subject to the section 704(d) / 1366(d) basis ceiling, the section 465 at risk limit and the section 469 passive limitation, and this module models all three for the box 1 activity only; deducting a rental loss here without them would allow in full a loss the statute caps, which understates tax. So the loss stays where it was — printed on the document, absent from the return, which OVERSTATES tax and is the safe direction — until either the per item limitation chain is generalised to a second activity or a refusal is authored. See the report of unit W1.

Fact.Name: This K-1's boxes 2 and 3 rental INCOME (Schedule E line 28 column (h)), floored at zero
Fact.Description: max($0, ../k1RentalRealEstateNet): the part of this K-1's boxes 2 and 3 that is INCOME. Section 469 limits passive LOSSES, not passive income, so a rental profit reported in box 2 or box 3 flows to Schedule E Part II line 28 column (h) in full, exactly as a passive box 1 profit does through ../passiveNet. The floor is what keeps the unmodelled loss side (see ../k1RentalRealEstateNet) out of every total.

Fact.Name: This K-1's boxes 2 and 3 rental income as it joins the section 8582 pool
Fact.Description:
../k1RentalRealEstateRentalIncome, except on a PUBLICLY TRADED PARTNERSHIP, where it is $0. IRC 469(k)(1) applies the passive activity rules "separately with respect to items attributable to each publicly traded partnership" and the partner instructions turn that into an instruction about this very form: "Don't report passive income, gains, or losses from a PTP on Form 8582." ../passiveNet already carries the identical leading arm for the box 1 amount and this fact mirrors it, reading the same ../appliesPtpSection469 gate.
FORM 8582 PART I LINE 2, NOT LINE 1, AND THAT IS A STATED CHOICE rather than an oversight. The aggregate over this fact joins /otherPassiveNet (line 2d, "All other passive activities") and never /passiveActiveRentalLegNet (line 1d, rental real estate WITH active participation), which is where the module's other rental legs route by an active participation flag (/rentalProperties/*/activeParticipation, and /farmRentalPassiveNetActiveLeg against /farmRentalPassiveNetOtherLeg). There is no active participation flag on a /formK1s item and none is invented here: active participation requires a bona fide management interest that IRC 469(i)(6)(C) denies to a limited partner, and the limited partner is the population that receives a box 2 or box 3 amount in the ordinary case, so line 2 is the right default. THE CORNER THIS LEAVES, disclosed rather than discovered: a GENERAL partner who does actively participate in the partnership's rental real estate activity belongs on line 1d, and while that partner's box 2 income sits on line 2d it inflates the line 4 special allowance base against OTHER line 2 losses. The direction is an understatement of tax on that narrow population. Closing it needs a per item active participation intake on /formK1s, which no printed box of Schedule K-1 supplies, so it is disclosed rather than guessed.
THE PTP AMOUNT IS NOT DROPPED FROM THE RETURN by this arm — only from the POOL. It is combined with the same PTP's box 1 amount in ../ptpCurrentYearNet (the per-PTP step 1) and reaches Schedule E Part II line 32 through that PTP's overall gain, or is absorbed by that PTP's own loss. /k1RentalRealEstateIncomeTotal sums THIS fact, so the PTP amount is counted once. What the arm prevents is a PTP's rental profit absorbing OTHER activities' passive losses, which is the thing section 469(k) forbids.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 2 and box 3 rental net is a loss that no line carries
Fact.Description: True when ../k1RentalRealEstateNet (box 2 plus box 3, complete safe, signed) is below $0. Only the income side of that net is wired; the loss is subject to the basis, at-risk and passive activity limits this module applies to the box 1 activity only, so it stays off the return. Complete false on every K-1 without a box 2 or box 3 loss.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Schedule K-1 reports a net rental loss in box 2 or box 3
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. A Schedule K-1 reports a rental real estate loss (box 2) or other rental loss (box 3). That loss is limited by your basis, the amount you have at risk and the passive activity rules, and this return cannot yet figure how much of it you can deduct. Leaving it off would overstate your tax.
Fires when a recorded K-1 has ../k1RentalRealEstateLossOffReturn true. Guarded by an IsComplete on /formK1s. A K-1 whose box 2 plus box 3 is income files; that income is already on Schedule E line 32 and in the passive pool.

Fact.Name: K-1 boxes 2 and 3 rental income, Schedule E Part II line 32 summand (aggregate)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/k1RentalRealEstatePoolIncome), gated by /claimsK1Income so a return with no K-1 resolves Complete $0 and every committed scenario is byte-identical. The FIFTH summand of /scheduleEPartIINetIncome (Schedule E line 32), beside the box 1 nonpassive parts, the pooled passive net, the pooled passive suspension and the guaranteed payments — the same shape /k1GuaranteedPayments uses for boxes 4a/4b.
ADDED. Before it, a partner whose Schedule K-1 reported rental income only in box 2 or box 3 reported $0 of it anywhere on the return: /formK1s/*/ordinaryIncome is box 1 only. Income only; the loss side of /formK1s/*/k1RentalRealEstateNet is deliberately not carried, for the reason that fact states. The summand is the PTP-gated per-item amount: a publicly traded partnership's box 2 and box 3 income is combined into /formK1s/*/ptpCurrentYearNet under the per-PTP rule and reaches line 32 through that PTP's overall gain or loss, so it is not added here a second time. For every other K-1 the per-item amount equals its box 2 and box 3 income.

Fact.Name: K-1 boxes 2 and 3 rental income entering the section 8582 pool (aggregate)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/k1RentalRealEstatePoolIncome), gated by /claimsK1Income (Complete $0 for a return with no K-1). The SIXTH term of /passiveIncomeTotal, beside the active rental, non-active rental, passive K-1, passive estate/trust and farm rental nets.
IT ADDS NO SECOND INCOME TERM TO THE RETURN, which is the same argument /farmRentalPassiveNet carries: the money reaches Schedule E line 32 once, through /k1RentalRealEstateIncomeTotal. Pool membership only raises the pool's capacity to allow OTHER activities' passive losses under section 469(d)(1), which is what a passive rental profit is for. Correspondingly this participant gets no Part VII ratable share and the /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated and /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated plugs are untouched: the allocation numerators are loss magnitudes and this participant's loss is structurally zero (the term is floored at $0 twice over).
