Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/seEarnings), gated by /claimsK1Income — the DECLARED box-14A total, complete-safe and never refused. Its job is LEGIBILITY: /k1SeEarnings (built from the negative-refusing /formK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed) goes Incomplete on a negative 14A and so cannot state the amount that caused the refusal, while this fact still can. The per-filer split retired its former second reader, the M2 MFJ knockout — an MFJ return with box-14A now computes on the spouse's own Schedule SE — so the remaining reader surface is the client-visible refusal explanation for the M1 negative-14A knockout (pinned by a node test of a negative box 14A).

Fact.Name: S-corporation K-1 farming and fishing income (box 17 code AN) (aggregate; exported, unwired)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/farmingFishingIncomeSCorp), gated by /claimsK1Income and Rounded — the S-CORPORATION leg of the farming and fishing figure Schedule E line 42 reconciles, and the exact twin of /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome, which is the partnership leg. That fact carries the full statement of why an aggregate of this shape is exported while nothing consumes it; it is not repeated here.
WHY IT IS A SEPARATE AGGREGATE AND NOT A THIRD ADDEND INSIDE THE PARTNERSHIP ONE: line 42 names four legs, and the wiring unit that eventually builds the line has to be able to say which legs the graph computed and which the filer attested. Two named per-leg aggregates can be composed by that unit; one merged figure cannot be decomposed by it. The rule against a partial fill of line 42 is what makes that distinction load-bearing rather than stylistic — line 42 stays a filer attestation until all four legs exist, so both of these aggregates are deliberately unwired today.
LEGS STILL MISSING AFTER THIS ONE: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F. Its instructions are vendored (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1041sk1.pdf, code F at line 235). That leg is NOT a fifth /formK1s entity type, and a successor who built one would misfile the income: /formK1s is the Schedule E PART II collection — /k1EntityTypeOptions' own Description says its members "flow box-1 ordinary business income identically to Schedule E Part II line 28" — while a Form 1041 K-1 is an estate or trust, Schedule E PART III line 33. The leg is a Part III SCALAR gated on /claimsEstateTrustK1, matching /writableEstateTrustK1Income. The fourth leg, Schedule F line 9, ships as scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: K-1 gross farming or fishing income (box 14 code B) (aggregate; exported, unwired)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/grossFarmingFishingIncome), gated by /claimsK1Income and Rounded — the partnership-K-1 half of the gross farming and fishing figure Schedule E line 42 reconciles.
WHAT CONSUMES IT: nothing in this dictionary. It is exported because the printed line names it and a partner with a code B entry owes the figure whether or not this graph computes anything from it — the same call form4835:/form4835GrossFarmRentalIncome made for Form 4835 line 7 on 2026-08-06 and scheduleF:/scheduleFGrossIncome made for Schedule F line 9.
THE TWO CONSUMERS IT WAS BUILT FOR, neither of which is wired here. * Schedule E line 42, whose second printed leg is this box and code. That line's per-leg computation is not built, and a partial fill is ruled out: a line 42 that computes some legs and attests the rest is a figure that looks derived and is not. Two of the four legs still have no intake at all (Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F are item collections this dictionary does not model), so line 42 keeps its whole-line filer attestation at /scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation and nothing here reaches it. * The Schedule SE Part II FARM OPTIONAL METHOD, whose line 15 gross farm income footnote names Schedule F line 9 and this box and code together. Part II is not built; Schedule SE line 4a reads /netEarningsFromSelfEmployment with no optional-method branch.
NO DOLLAR MOVES TODAY. This aggregate is complete-safe and resolves 0 on every return that answers no box 14 code B, which is every return in the corpus; its arms are witnessed by node tests rather than by scenarios. SIGN: unfloored, following its member intake — see /formK1s/*/writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome for why the Schedule SE line 15 floor proves nothing about code B on its own. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Description: ../grossFarmingFishingIncome floored at $0. Publication 505 figures gross income from farming or fishing as the total of the income (not loss) amounts, document by document, so a loss on one K-1 does not reduce another's income. Summed by /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncomeWithoutLosses.

Fact.Name: K-1 gross farming or fishing income (box 14 code B), the total of the income amounts only
Fact.Description: The sum over the recorded Schedule K-1s of ../grossFarmingFishingIncomeWithoutLoss, gated as /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome is and rounded once: the partnership K-1 term of the Form 2210 / Form 1040-ES gross farming or fishing income test, which counts income (not loss) amounts. /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome, the signed total Schedule E line 42 reconciles, is unchanged.

Fact.Name: A K-1 declares a negative box 14 code A (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when any /formK1s item declares a NEGATIVE box 14A — the "enter only the deductible amount on Schedule SE" case, which the graph cannot COMPUTE (704(d)/465/469 suspension state is not carried across years) and therefore INTAKES from the partner (/formK1s/*/writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss).
It no longer keys /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings; that is now the narrower /hasK1UndeterminableSeEarningsLoss, which fires only on a declared negative whose deductible amount is unstated or self-contradictory. This flag survives as the LEGIBILITY flag for "this return declares an SE loss at all" and as the population marker for the intake. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: A K-1 declares a box 14A loss whose deductible amount is not stated (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when ANY /formK1s item declares a NEGATIVE box 14A without a validly stated deductible amount (Count(/formK1s/*/seEarningsLossUndeterminable) > 0). Keys /knockoutK1NegativeSeEarnings.
REPLACED WHAT: the knockout previously read /hasK1NegativeSeEarnings, i.e. ANY declared negative box 14A on any K-1. A declared negative whose deductible amount the partner HAS stated computes, so the guard narrows to the sub-case nobody but the filer can resolve. /hasK1NegativeSeEarnings itself is the LEGIBILITY flag for "this return declares an SE loss at all"; the two are not the same population.
ANY, NOT EVERY: one unresolvable item makes the Schedule SE line-2 aggregate unresolvable, the same way the per-item Incomplete propagates through /primaryFilerK1SeEarnings. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a K-1 declares a negative box 14 code A (deductible amount undeterminable)
Fact.Description:
The return declares a NEGATIVE Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code A AND has not stated the deductible part of it (/hasK1UndeterminableSeEarningsLoss). The partner instructions require entering "only the DEDUCTIBLE amount" of an SE loss on Schedule SE, and deductibility turns on 704(d) basis / 465 at-risk / 469 passive suspension state this single-year graph does not hold — so the engine cannot compute it, and taking the printed loss RAW would UNDER-state SE tax whenever any part of it is suspended (the representable failure: a box-1 loss fully suspended by zero basis alongside Schedule C profit). BLOCKS SUBMISSION rather than compute a wrong (lower) tax; /formK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed independently refuses the VALUE (Result.Incomplete) — belt and suspenders.
WHAT THE FILL FREED, replacing the former "Follow-on: carrying suspended-loss state (or intaking the partner's already-limited deductible SE loss) would let this compute": the SECOND of those two successors landed. /formK1s/*/writableDeductibleSeEarningsLoss intakes the figure the printed instruction already asks the PARTNER to compute off the return, so a declared negative 14A with a stated, internally consistent deductible amount now computes.
WHAT STILL REFUSES: a declared negative box 14A whose deductible amount is UNANSWERED, or is POSITIVE, or is MORE NEGATIVE than the printed box 14A. All three are data-completeness or input-contradiction cases only the filer can resolve. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's K-1s
Fact.Description: The Schedule K-1s attributed to the primary filer (../filer). Mirrors /primaryFilerW2s.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's K-1s
Fact.Description: The Schedule K-1s attributed to the secondary (MFJ spouse) filer (../filer). Mirrors /secondaryFilerW2s. Empty on a non-MFJ return (no secondary filer to match).

Fact.Name: Primary filer's K-1 self-employment earnings ALLOWED (box 14 code A)
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/primaryFilerK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed), gated by /claimsK1Income — the box-14A total attributed to the PRIMARY filer that reaches that filer's Schedule SE line 2. MAY BE NEGATIVE: a declared negative 14A used to make the per-item seEarningsAllowed Result.Incomplete and refuse the return. It now carries the partner's stated deductible loss through, and refuses only when that figure is unstated or self-contradictory. FOUNDATION for per-filer Schedule SE: the primary filer's Schedule SE line-2 K-1 term. On every existing return (K-1 filer unanswered ⇒ defaults to primary) this equals the whole-collection sum. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's K-1 self-employment earnings ALLOWED (box 14 code A)
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/secondaryFilerK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed), gated by /claimsK1Income — the box-14A total attributed to the SECONDARY (MFJ spouse) filer. Complete-safe 0 on a non-MFJ return (no secondary filer, so /secondaryFilerK1s is empty) and 0 on every existing return (K-1 filer defaults to primary). This is the spouse's Schedule SE line-2 K-1 term: the per-filer split consumes it as scheduleSE:/secondaryFilerSeNetProfitOrLoss and measures it against the SPOUSE's own $176,100 OASDI wage base and own $400 line-4c threshold, never the primary's.

Fact.Name: K-1 self-employment earnings ALLOWED onto Schedule SE (box 14 code A) (aggregate -> line 2)
Fact.Description: The box-14A total that actually reaches scheduleSE:/netEarningsFromSelfEmployment (line 2) and scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, as the sum of the two per-filer subtotals (/primaryFilerK1SeEarnings + /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings). Value-identical to the former whole-collection CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed): every K-1's ../filer partitions it into exactly one subtotal, and on every existing return the filer defaults to primary, so /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings is 0. MAY BE NEGATIVE. This sentence formerly read "NON-NEGATIVE by construction: a declared NEGATIVE 14A makes the per-item /formK1s/*/seEarningsAllowed Result.Incomplete, which propagates through the subtotal and REFUSES the return (M1) rather than under-state SE tax" — that is now true only of the narrowed population where the partner has NOT stated the deductible part of the loss. Where they have, a signed negative aggregate reaches Schedule SE line 2, which is what "enter only the deductible amount" instructs. This AGGREGATE is read only where a return-level total is genuinely wanted (scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentEarnedIncome, the EIC Worksheet B base, which is a joint quantity); the SE-tax chain itself reads the two per-filer subtotals separately, so no spouse's earnings are ever measured against the other's wage base. interpretation:provisional. California TY2025 reads this fact through its stateSystems export (FTB 3514 CA earned income (K-1 self-employment detection)).

Fact.Name: This partnership K-1 reports a farming or fishing business (box 20 code AN)
Fact.Description: True when any box 20 code row of this K-1 reads AN. A partnership involved in a farming or fishing business reports its farming and fishing items in box 20 using code AN, which makes it a farm partnership whose box 14 code A self-employment earnings belong on Schedule SE line 1a rather than line 2. Complete false when no row reads AN.

Fact.Name: This partnership K-1 reports a farming or fishing business (box 20 code AN): this row
Fact.Description: One row of /formK1s/*/otherInformationEntries as /formK1s/*/reportsFarmingOrFishingBusiness reads it: True when this row passes the test /formK1s/*/reportsFarmingOrFishingBusiness applies to every row (code AN); otherwise False. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: This K-1's self-employment earnings from a farm partnership (Schedule SE line 1a)
Fact.Description: ../seEarningsAllowed when ../reportsFarmingOrFishingBusiness, else $0: the box 14 code A amount that Schedule SE line 1a takes from a farm partnership.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's K-1 self-employment earnings from farm partnerships (Schedule SE line 1a term)
Fact.Description: The part of /primaryFilerK1SeEarnings that comes from farm partnership K-1s (../reportsFarmingOrFishingBusiness): the K-1 term of that filer's Schedule SE line 1a. /primaryFilerK1SeEarnings less this is the line 2 K-1 term. Gated as /primaryFilerK1SeEarnings is.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer's K-1 self-employment earnings from farm partnerships (Schedule SE line 1a term)
Fact.Description: The part of /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings that comes from farm partnership K-1s: the K-1 term of the spouse's Schedule SE line 1a. Gated as /secondaryFilerK1SeEarnings is.

Fact.Name: K-1 self-employment earnings from farm partnerships (both filers)
Fact.Description: /primaryFilerK1FarmSeEarnings plus /secondaryFilerK1FarmSeEarnings: the farm partnership part of /k1SeEarnings.

Fact.Name: A K-1 reports guaranteed payments without the box-14 SE assessment (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when any /formK1s item reports guaranteed payments (box 4a/4b) with box 14 SE earnings unanswered — the combination the per-item ../guaranteedPayments REFUSES (Result.Incomplete cascading to /totalIncome). This taxpayer-level flag keeps the refusal legible rather than silent (the refuse-and-flag pattern; twin of /hasUnsupportedSection1245Disposition). Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: A K-1's capital guaranteed payment has undeterminable NII character (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when ANY /formK1s item reports a box 4b guaranteed payment for capital whose section 1411 character this dictionary cannot determine (Count(/formK1s/*/capitalGuaranteedPaymentNiitUndeterminable) > 0). Keys the first conjunct of /knockoutK1CapitalGuaranteedPaymentsNiit.
REPLACED WHAT, and why the replacement is a narrowing rather than a rewrite: the knockout previously read /k1GuaranteedPaymentsCapital > $0, i.e. the taxpayer-level box 4b total, because no partner-classification fact existed. It now reads this per-item ANY, so a return whose capital-guaranteed-payment K-1s are ALL general partners no longer refuses, while a single limited-or-unanswered capital-GP-bearing item still refuses the whole return.
ANY, NOT EVERY, and the source's own unit is why: IRC 1411 is applied to the taxpayer's aggregate net investment income, so one item whose character is unknown makes the aggregate unknown. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: Knockout: K-1 guaranteed payments for capital with NIIT exposure (undeterminable NII character)
Fact.Description:
The return reports a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 4b guaranteed payment for capital whose section 1411 character is undeterminable (/hasK1CapitalGuaranteedPaymentNiitUndeterminable) AND MAGI above the Form 8960 threshold. Whether capital GP is net investment income depends on partner classification: a general partner's box 14A carries it into SECA and IRC 1411(c)(6) excludes it, otherwise it is NII in the substitute-for-interest reading. BLOCKS SUBMISSION (refuses) rather than silently under-computing NIIT (World #1; the U-065a/U-CA1 refuse-what-8960-cannot-compute posture). Below the threshold no NIIT can exist and capital GP flows normally. AGI leg is complete-safe (an incomplete AGI contributes 0, keeping this fact Complete on partial-computation scenarios).
WHAT THE FILL FREED, replacing the former "Follow-on: a partner-type writable would free the above-threshold general-partner case": the classification IS now represented (/formK1s/*/writablePartnerIsGeneralPartner, Part II item G), so an above-threshold return whose capital-guaranteed-payment K-1s are ALL answered general partner no longer refuses.
WHAT STILL REFUSES, AND WHY IT IS NOT A BUILD GAP. Two arms survive, per item: an answered LIMITED partner, and an UNANSWERED item G. The limited arm turns on the substitute-for-interest reading of Reg. 1.1411-4(g), which is not published as an irs.gov artifact, so invariant 3 leaves this repo nothing to cite; that arm is blocked on a SOURCE this repo cannot obtain, which is a different obstacle from a build. The unanswered arm is an ordinary data-completeness refusal: only the filer can read their own item G. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Qualified PTP income or (loss) from Schedule K-1s (aggregate -> Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28)
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss), gated by /claimsK1Income (0 for no K-1). The PTP half of the one printed REIT/PTP entry, read by qbi:/qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss and through it by BOTH section 199A consumers.
MAY BE NEGATIVE and NOT ROUNDED, which is a deliberate departure from every other aggregate in this block. The others round because they land on whole-dollar Form 1040 lines; this one lands on Form 8995 line 6, whose consumers carry cents through the line-8 floor and the line-9 20% without rounding (a $1 difference in the REIT/PTP entry is observable to the cent at qbi:/qbi8995aDeductionBeforeDpad). Rounding here would silently disagree with the box-5 REIT half, which is likewise unrounded.
SUMS ACROSS PTPs, and that is not the same as netting them. Form 8995 line 6 is a single combined entry, so the return-level total is what the form asks for; the PER-PTP tracking the section 199A instructions require ("you must track each loss or deduction from a PTP until the loss or deduction is no longer suspended") is cross-year state this graph does not hold, and its prior-year half is the attested qbi:/writableQualifiedReitPtpLossCarryforwardFromPriorTaxYear. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: A K-1 reports a qualified PTP amount (the third disjunct of the REIT/PTP arm gate)
Fact.Description:
True when any /formK1s item both checks item D and answers its box 20 code Z amount (Count(/formK1s/*/reportsQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss) > 0), the collection-"any" idiom this module already uses for /hasK1NegativeSeEarnings. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.
AN EXISTENCE TEST, NOT A MAGNITUDE TEST, and the difference is the whole reason this fact exists rather than a `> $0` guard on /k1QualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss. Qualified PTP income may be a LOSS, and a filer with a qualified PTP loss and a prior-year carryforward must still reach the consumers' REIT/PTP arm — on a magnitude test they would not, and the carryforward would be silently lost. The Form 1099-DIV box-5 sibling disjunct CAN use `> $0` because box 5 carries Min $0 per payer; this one cannot.

Fact.Name: A K-1 reports a qualified PTP amount from an SSTB PTP (Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II gate)
Fact.Description: True when any /formK1s item reports a qualified PTP amount from a PTP the filer declared an SSTB (Count(/formK1s/*/reportsSstbQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss) > 0). Its consumers are qbi:/sstbPtpQualifiedAmountBeforeApplicablePercentage (the Schedule A (Form 8995-A) Part II line 17 total, which this fact gates on its own, WITHOUT the threshold), and qbi:/sstbPtpQualifiedAmountAfterApplicablePercentage plus qbi:/qualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss, which pair it with /isAboveQbiThreshold: below the threshold no SSTB limitation applies, so this flag alone reduces nothing. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: A K-1 answers a qualified PTP amount with item D unchecked (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when any /formK1s item answers its box 20 code Z qualified PTP amount without establishing item D (Count(/formK1s/*/hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD) > 0). Keys /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD so the contradiction is refused rather than resolved as a silent $0 (the refuse-and-flag pattern, the twin of /hasK1GuaranteedPaymentsWithoutSeAssessment). Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.
TWO THINGS FOLLOW THAT "Complete-safe" DOES NOT COVER ON ITS OWN. (1) Count() over a collection is INCOMPLETE if ANY member is Incomplete, so one K-1 that answers a qualified PTP amount with item D UNANSWERED makes this fact Incomplete for the whole return, not merely false. (2) The /claimsK1Income guard above still holds, so a return with no K-1 collection resolves Complete false and nothing here reaches it.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a qualified PTP amount answered on a K-1 whose item D is not checked
Fact.Description:
LIVE 2026-08-22. It was RETIRED as unreachable on 2026-08-20 by the derived-item-D fill — /formK1s/*/isPubliclyTradedPartnershipDerived read an ANSWERED qualified PTP amount as itself establishing item D, so the contradiction this guard exists to catch was not representable — and it is REACHABLE again now that item D is a single user input with no inference and no default. The two-day retirement is left on the record rather than erased; see /formK1s/*/hasQualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD for the three states the trigger now has, including the INCOMPLETE one.
ITS FLOW MEMBERSHIP IS INTACT: the Dependency on this path inside flow:/flowIsKnockedOut's Any was added at integration on 2026-08-03 and was never removed when the guard was retired, so nothing had to be re-wired to bring it back. The BlockSubmissionOnTrue below is the other half.
WHAT IT REFUSES: the return answers a Schedule K-1 box 20 code Z QUALIFIED PTP amount on a K-1 whose item D ("Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)") is not checked. Item D is what routes a code Z amount to the qualified PTP half of Form 8995 line 6 / Form 8995-A line 28, so without it the amount is dropped and the section 199A deduction is UNDER-stated with nothing on the return to show why. It BLOCKED SUBMISSION rather than resolve a wrong-looking-right $0: the two answers contradict each other and only the filer can say which is right (uncheck the amount, or check item D). The VALUE still computed — this is the /knockoutK1CapitalGuaranteedPaymentsNiit shape, a refusal without an Incomplete cascade — so the rest of the return stayed legible while the submission was barred.
"A REFUSAL WITHOUT AN INCOMPLETE CASCADE" IS CONDITIONAL, and the three-way statement is the exact one. It holds on the FIRING population — item D answered FALSE beside an answered amount, where every value computes and only the submission is barred. It does NOT hold when item D is UNANSWERED beside an answered amount: the trigger AND THIS GUARD are Incomplete there. flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is NOT — it reads PLACEHOLDER FALSE, because it carries a Placeholder of False beneath its Any. What tells the filer is the OTHER return-level gate: flow:/flowIncomplete reads Complete TRUE, through the /formK1sItemDIsComplete member.

Fact.Name: Form 4562 Part I line 2, total cost of §179 property placed in service, for the whole return
Fact.Description:
CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/section179PlacedInServiceCost), gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so a non-rental return resolves Complete 0. The §179(b)(2) phaseout base for /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit.
WHAT IS NOT IN IT, and the one place this dictionary had to choose a reading: a partner's Schedule K-1 box-12 amount does NOT enter line 2. The instruction that governs a K-1 share is printed under Form 4562 line 6's "Column (c) — Elected cost": "To report your share of a section 179 expense deduction from a partnership or an S corporation, enter 'from Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)' or 'from Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)' across columns (a) and (b)" — columns (a) and (b) are the description and the COST, and the share is entered with no cost figure at all, so it feeds line 8 (total elected cost), not line 2. The statute agrees: §179(b)(2) reduces the limit by the cost of property "PLACED IN the application during such taxable year", and the partner placed nothing in service — the partnership did, and §179(d)(8) applies subsection (b) to the partnership separately for exactly that reason.
THE CONTRARY READING IS NAMED RATHER THAN BURIED, because the partner instructions do point the other way: "Use this amount, along with the total cost of section 179 property placed in service during the year from other sources, to complete Part I of Form 4562". That sentence says the box-12 amount participates in Part I without saying which line, so it is consistent with the line-6 reading taken here and does not compel the line-2 one. NO VENDORED SOURCE SETTLES IT. The divergence is bounded and stated: the two readings differ only when the taxpayer's own placed-in-service cost is within one box-12 amount of the $4,000,000 threshold, and there the reading taken here gives the LARGER limit. That is the taxpayer-favourable direction, which is why it is argued from the printed line placement and the statute rather than chosen for its size.

Fact.Name: §179 dollar limitation for the whole return (Form 4562 Part I line 5), taxpayer level
Fact.Description:
Form 4562 Part I line 5 computed ONCE for the return rather than once per activity: max(0, $2,500,000 - max(0, /section179TotalCostPlacedInService - $4,000,000)). Line 1 is the §179(b)(1) maximum and line 4 is the §179(b)(2) reduction, and both are TAXPAYER figures — "The aggregate cost which may be taken into account under subsection (a) for any taxable year shall not exceed" the limit, and "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity."
THE ONLY CONSUMER IS THE K-1 LEG (/formK1s/*/section179ColumnJ), and that is the substantive decision this fill makes. The sizing contract this fact replaces asked the fill to re-point /rentalProperties/*/section179Deduction and /rentalSection179Deduction at an ALLOCATED share of this cap. It does not, because there is no allocation to share: i4562 says a filer with more than one activity MAY allocate, which makes the split an election no intake collects, and /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities refuses that population outright. With at most one electing activity the taxpayer-level limit and the per-element ../section179DollarLimit bind identically on the elected cost, so re-pointing would move no value and would re-body a cleanroom-verified fact for nothing.
THEY NO LONGER DIVERGE ON VALUE. When this fact landed, the per-element /rentalProperties/*/section179DollarLimit still measured its line-2 phaseout base from its OWN ../fiveYearPropertyBasis, so a return with one electing element beside a second element that placed 5-year property in service WITHOUT electing got a per-element limit that was too large above $4,000,000 of total cost — a defect the multi-elector knockout could not reach, because only one activity elected. That was closed: the per-element fact now reads /section179TotalCostPlacedInService too, so above the threshold it computes exactly the figure this fact does. The distinguisher that survives is COMPLETENESS, not arithmetic — the per-element fact is gated on ../claimsFiveYearProperty and is Incomplete for an element with no 5-year property, while this one always resolves.
THE BOUNDARY is pinned at the printed threshold on an AGGREGATE that no single element reaches: node-test scheduleE/rental-179-taxpayer-limit-aggregate-at-threshold (two elements at $2,000,000 each, this fact $2,500,000) against -above-threshold (the second element one dollar higher, this fact $2,499,999). Since that rebody both cases also pin each element's own ../section179DollarLimit at the SAME figure, which is the point of the pair rather than a loss: NEITHER element reaches $4,000,000 alone, so a per-element base would show no reduction at all, and the $1 step in a per-element row is only explicable at taxpayer level.

Fact.Name: How many rental elements elect §179 (Form 4562 Part I, the "more than one activity" test)
Fact.Description:
The number of /rentalProperties elements whose Form 4562 line-9 tentative deduction is positive (Count(/rentalProperties/*/electsSection179)), gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so a non-rental return resolves Complete 0. Half of /section179ElectingActivityCount.
COUNT COUNTS THE TRUE ITEMS, NOT THE COLLECTION SIZE, and this fact would be silently wrong the other way round: a return with two rental elements neither of which elects would read 2 and refuse. The committed multi-element fixtures pin it — node-test scheduleE/rental-179-two-elements-one-elects asserts 1 on a TWO-element collection, and a second node test asserts 0 for the K-1 twin on a TWO-item K-1 collection with no section 179 anywhere.

Fact.Name: How many K-1s pass through a §179 election
Fact.Description: The number of /formK1s items with a positive box-12 section 179 amount (Count(/formK1s/*/electsSection179)), gated on /claimsK1Income so a non-K-1 return resolves Complete 0. Half of /section179ElectingActivityCount. See the sibling /rentalSection179ElectingCount on why the true-items-not-collection-size semantics is pinned by a node test rather than assumed.

Fact.Name: How many activities on this return elect §179 (rental elements plus K-1s)
Fact.Description: /rentalSection179ElectingCount + /k1Section179ElectingCount: the number of separate businesses or activities electing section 179 on this return. Section 179(b)(1) caps the TAXPAYER ("The aggregate cost which may be taken into account under subsection (a) for any taxable year shall not exceed" the dollar limit), and section 179(d)(8) applies subsection (b) to the partnership AND to each partner, so every activity here competes for one cap. At a count of 1 there is nothing to divide and the taxpayer-level cap and the per-activity cap coincide; above 1 the division is the filer's ELECTION and is refused (/knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities). Schedule E Part III estate/trust K-1s are NOT counted: no estate/trust intake in this dictionary carries a section 179 amount.

Fact.Name: More than one activity on this return elects §179 (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when /section179ElectingActivityCount > 1. Keys /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities. Complete-safe by construction: both halves of the count resolve Complete 0 when their collection is not claimed.

Fact.Name: The taxpayer's allocation of the section 179 dollar limit among electing activities
Fact.Description:
One row per activity to which the taxpayer allocates part of the single section 179 dollar limit: the identification cell and the elected cost share. Section 179(b)(1) caps the TAXPAYER and section 179(d)(8) applies subsection (b) to the partnership and to each partner, so every electing activity on the return competes for one limit, and the Form 4562 instructions print the division as an election the filer MAY make rather than a formula. FILER SUPPLIED for that reason, and no derivation is offered: neither of the two shapes a reader might guess, pro rata by elected cost or a filer supplied ordering, is derivable from any vendored source.
RETURN LEVEL BECAUSE IT SPANS TWO COLLECTIONS. A rental element reaches its own row through /rentalProperties/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow; the K-1 arm's link is sequenced and not built here. The K-1 arm is BUILT. A K-1 reaches its own row through /formK1s/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow; see the K-1 arm block below the rental coverage test for the link, its readers, the K-1 consumed total and the combined consumed total.

Fact.Name: Which activity this section 179 allocation row belongs to
Fact.Description: The identification cell of one row of /section179AllocationByActivity: the business or activity whose Form 4562 line 12 carries this share, as the filer names it. FILER SUPPLIED. It is the row's own identity and is deliberately NOT the mechanism by which an activity finds its share; that is the typed link /rentalProperties/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow, because a free text cell cannot be matched to a collection element by this engine and a return that matched on prose would silently mis allocate on a typo.

Fact.Name: The part of the section 179 dollar limit this row allocates to its activity
Fact.Description:
The dollar share of the taxpayer's one section 179 dollar limit (/section179TaxpayerDollarLimit, Form 4562 Part I line 5) that this row allocates to its activity, the figure the instructions tell the filer to enter on that activity's own Form 4562 line 12. FILER SUPPLIED, because the printed word is "may allocate" and the split is the taxpayer's election.
IT IS A CEILING, NOT A DEDUCTION. The consuming activity still applies its elected cost, its basis and the line 11 business income limitation, so allocating more to an activity than it can use deducts nothing extra. Allocating more IN TOTAL than the cap allows is an input contradiction, reported by /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits and left to the refusal rather than clamped here.

Fact.Name: This allocation row's share, complete safe
Fact.Description: ../writableElectedCostShare when answered and $0 otherwise, so a CollectionSum over /section179AllocationByActivity resolves Complete even while a row is half answered. The idiom and the reason are /form8958ScheduleERows/*/columnBThisReturnShare's, character for character. NOT floored at $0: a negative entered share is an input contradiction the totals should show, not a value to repair.

Fact.Name: The whole of the section 179 shares the filer entered
Fact.Description: The sum of every row's ../electedCostShare over /section179AllocationByActivity, rounded so it is comparable with the whole dollar line 5 limit, and a complete safe $0 on a return that never answered the collection. This is the ENTERED total: what the filer says the allocation is. /section179RentalAllocatedShareTotal is the CONSUMED total, what the activities actually take, and the two differ exactly when a row is entered but unused or when two activities point at the same row. Both are compared with the cap by /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits.

Fact.Name: The whole of the section 179 shares the rental elements actually consume
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/section179AllocatedShare, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome so a non rental return resolves Complete $0. The CONSUMED total beside the entered total, and it is not a duplicate of it: nothing stops two rental elements naming the SAME allocation row, in which case the entered total counts that share once while the return takes it twice. Binding the cap on this figure is what makes the cap bind ONCE across the elements rather than once across the rows.

Fact.Name: Every electing rental element has a resolving allocation row
Fact.Description:
Count(/rentalProperties/*/section179AllocationCovered) is not less than /rentalSection179ElectingCount: no rental element elects section 179 without a row that says what its share is. A PARTIAL allocation is not an allocation, because an uncovered element still takes the whole taxpayer cap through ../section179DollarLimit, which is precisely the defect the refusal prevents. Count cannot exceed the electing count by construction, since ../section179AllocationCovered has ../electsSection179 as a conjunct, so "not less than" IS equality and is written this way because a GreaterThan over Ints is the comparison this dictionary already uses on these counts (/hasMultipleSection179ElectingActivities).
TYPE: Boolean, always Complete, so it is safe in the Switch When of a consumer.
THE K-1 ARM IS NOT IN IT, and the name says rental for that reason. A return on which a K-1 also elects is still refused; see the block comment above. The K-1 arm has its own twin, /section179AllocationCoversEveryElectingK1Activity, and the guard reads both; "still refused" above is superseded by that twin's Description.

Fact.Name: The section 179 allocation row this K-1's box 12 share is entered on
Fact.Description:
The item of /section179AllocationByActivity that carries this K-1's share of the taxpayer's one section 179 dollar limit: the K-1 twin of /rentalProperties/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow. FILER SUPPLIED, for the reason the rental twin gives: the split is an ELECTION ("if you have more than one business or activity, you MAY allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them"), not a formula, so neither the row nor its amount is derivable from the return's other answers, and the Form 4562 instructions themselves make the K-1 share one of the activities to allocate among ("To report your share of a section 179 expense deduction from a partnership or an S corporation, enter 'from Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)' ... across columns (a) and (b)").
WHY THE LINK POINTS THIS WAY: the allocation is return level because it spans two collections under one cap; the element that needs its own share names its row, exactly as the rental twin and qbi:/qualifiedBusinesses/*/linkedScheduleC do. UNANSWERED IS THE ORDINARY STATE and costs nothing: ../section179AllocationRowResolves is false, ../section179AllocationRowShare is $0, ../section179AllocationCovered is false, and ../section179AllocatedShare keeps the pro rata expression, so every single elector return is unchanged. On a multi elector return an electing K-1 that leaves this unanswered is the residue /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities keeps refusing.

Fact.Name: This K-1's section 179 allocation link reaches an answered share
Fact.Description:
Whether ../linkedSection179AllocationRow actually reaches a row whose share this graph can read: the link is answered AND that row's ../writableElectedCostShare is answered. Both terms are needed, for the rental twin's reason: an unanswered CollectionItem dereferences to nothing, and a row that exists with an empty amount cell would otherwise hand the K-1 a share of nothing and silently delete its deduction.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and load bearing: it is read in a Switch When by ../section179AllocatedShare, and an Incomplete in a When clears the Switch's completeness flag. Both terms are IsComplete tests over raw intake, so neither can be Incomplete. Copied from /rentalProperties/*/section179AllocationRowResolves.

Fact.Name: The share of the taxpayer's section 179 dollar limit allocated to this K-1
Fact.Description:
The amount on this K-1's allocation row when ../section179AllocationRowResolves, and $0 otherwise. Complete on every return. It is a CEILING on the K-1's section 179 deduction rather than the deduction itself: the box 12 figure, the partner's 704(d) basis, the line 11 business income limitation and the section 465 at-risk amount still bind, and a filer who allocates more to a K-1 than it can use does not thereby deduct more. It is read by ../section179AllocatedShare as the fifth operand of the allocated arm, and summed into /section179K1AllocatedShareTotal, the K-1 half of the consumed total the fits check reads.
NOT /formK1s/*/section179AllocatedShare; see the block comment above on the name. NOT FLOORED AT $0, for the rental twin's reason: the row's complete safe alias already returns $0 for an unanswered cell, and a NEGATIVE entered share is an input contradiction reported through the totals by /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits, not silently repaired here.

Fact.Name: This K-1 elects section 179 and has a resolving allocation row
Fact.Description: ../electsSection179 AND ../section179AllocationRowResolves: the per item half of /section179AllocationCoversEveryElectingK1Activity, which counts the true items of this field against /k1Section179ElectingCount. An electing K-1 with no resolving row is the case in which the allocation is PARTIAL, and a partial allocation is not an allocation: the uncovered K-1 would still take its whole pro rata share of the taxpayer cap through /k1Section179AllowedTotal, beside a rental element taking its own share of the same cap. The twin of /rentalProperties/*/section179AllocationCovered.

Fact.Name: The whole of the section 179 shares the K-1s actually consume
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/section179AllocationRowShare, gated on /claimsK1Income so a non K-1 return resolves Complete $0. The K-1 half of the CONSUMED total, beside /section179RentalAllocatedShareTotal and for the same reason that total exists: nothing stops two K-1s naming the SAME allocation row, in which case the entered total counts that share once while the return takes it twice. Read by /section179AllocatedShareTotal.

Fact.Name: The whole of the section 179 shares every electing activity actually consumes
Fact.Description: /section179RentalAllocatedShareTotal + /section179K1AllocatedShareTotal: the CONSUMED total across BOTH collections the allocation spans. This is the figure /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits holds under the smaller of the line 5 and line 11 limits; before this unit that test read the rental half alone, which was exact only because the K-1 co-elector was refused outright. It is not a duplicate of /section179AllocationEnteredShareTotal: the entered total is what the filer wrote on the rows, this is what the activities pointing at those rows take, and the two differ when a row is entered but unused or when two activities point at one row.

Fact.Name: Every electing K-1 has a resolving allocation row
Fact.Description:
Count(/formK1s/*/section179AllocationCovered) is not less than /k1Section179ElectingCount: no K-1 elects section 179 without a row that says what its share is. The K-1 twin of /section179AllocationCoversEveryElectingRentalActivity, written the same way for the same reasons (the count cannot exceed the electing count by construction, so "not less than" IS equality; a GreaterThan over Ints is the comparison this module already uses on these counts). Gated on /claimsK1Income through the electing count: a non K-1 return has an electing count of 0 and this resolves Complete true without reading the collection, which keeps the guard that reads it complete safe.
TYPE: Boolean, always Complete, so it is safe in the Switch When of a consumer. Read by /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities in place of the former "no K-1 elects" conjunct.

Fact.Name: The section 179 shares fit inside the taxpayer's one dollar limit
Fact.Description:
Whether the allocation the filer entered is arithmetically possible: the ENTERED total is not more than the Form 4562 line 5 taxpayer dollar limit AND the total the rental elements CONSUME is not more than the smaller of that line 5 limit and the line 11 business income limitation. False is an INPUT CONTRADICTION, not a computation this graph can repair, and it is the refusal that survives the allocation: a filer who allocates $2,000,000 and $1,000,000 out of a $2,500,000 limit has not made a legal election, and clamping the shares would answer for them which activity loses.
WHY LINE 11 IS IN THE CONSUMED TEST AND NOT ONLY LINE 5. "The limitations on lines 5 AND 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity." Line 5 is the one the contract names, but /rentalSection179IncomeLimit is taxpayer level in exactly the same way and each element's ../section179Deduction takes the whole of it independently; without this term two covered elements inside the dollar limit could still jointly over consume the income limit. The population where line 11 binds on a multi elector return therefore stays refused rather than being freed on a half checked cap.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, by the outer Switch. /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit and /rentalSection179IncomeLimit can both be Incomplete, on a return with a rental element that claims five year property and leaves its basis unanswered. The default arm returns FALSE there, which reads correctly: the shares are not KNOWN to fit, so the refusal stands. That return is already unfilable through the same missing answer, so the FALSE adds nothing to it.
THE CONSUMED OPERAND WIDENED 2026-09-01 (the K-1 arm): the consumed test now reads /section179AllocatedShareTotal, the rental consumed total PLUS the new /section179K1AllocatedShareTotal, so a K-1 pointing at a row consumes that row's share against the same line 5 and line 11 limits as a rental element does. "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer" is exactly why the two halves are one operand. The entered test is unchanged: the rows are one collection whichever arm points at them.

Fact.Name: Knockout: more than one activity on this return elects §179
Fact.Description:
Two or more separate activities on this return (rental elements and K-1s together) elect section 179. Section 179(b)(1) caps the TAXPAYER, not the activity, and section 179(d)(8) applies the whole of subsection (b) to the partnership and to each partner, so a single dollar limit has to be divided among them. HOW it is divided is the filer's ELECTION and not a formula: "The limitations on lines 5 and 11 apply to the taxpayer, and not to each separate business or activity. Therefore, if you have more than one business or activity, you MAY allocate your allowable section 179 expense deduction among them" (emphasis on "may" ours). No intake in this dictionary collects that allocation, and neither of the two shapes a reader might guess — pro rata by elected cost, or a filer-supplied ordering — is derivable from any vendored source. BLOCKS SUBMISSION rather than inventing one.
WHAT IT ACTUALLY FIXES, because it is not only a fence for the new K-1 leg: /rentalProperties/*/section179DollarLimit computes the full statutory cap INSIDE the rental collection, so before this knockout a return with two electing rental elements deducted up to TWICE the statutory maximum with no authority behind it. That population now refuses. WHY A COUNT OF 1 IS SAFE AND NEEDS NO RE-POINTING of the per-element chain: with exactly one electing activity there is nothing to allocate, and since the aggregate-cost rebody the taxpayer-level dollar limit and the per-element /rentalProperties/*/section179DollarLimit read the SAME line-2 aggregate, so they bind identically on the elected cost.
THAT CLAIM WAS NOT TRUE WHEN THIS KNOCKOUT LANDED, and the caveat is retired on the record rather than quietly dropped. As first written this paragraph said the two limits bind identically full stop, and its own sibling paragraph in /section179TaxpayerDollarLimit refuted it for one shape: a count of 1 with a NON-electing element that still placed 5-year property in service left the per-element limit measured against that element's own basis, hence too large above $4,000,000 of aggregate cost. The rebody moved the per-element fact onto /section179TotalCostPlacedInService, which is what makes the sentence above true now. It also moved committed rows, so the original clause "and every committed section-179 assert row keeps its value" is NOT carried forward: the per-element limit rows in scheduleE/rental-179-taxpayer-limit-aggregate-above-threshold and -phases-to-zero changed with that rebody (see its Description).
THE VALUE STILL COMPUTES (the /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD shape, no Incomplete cascade) and /formK1s/*/section179ColumnJ routes $0 while this flag is up, so the K-1 leg never adds a second full cap to a rental one.
ONE CAVEAT ON "BLOCKS SUBMISSION": membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is the other half of the wiring and is added at integration (flow.xml is outside this module).
/formK1s/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow lets an electing K-1 name its row of /section179AllocationByActivity, its row share caps the pro rata share in /formK1s/*/section179AllocatedShare, and the combined consumed total /section179AllocatedShareTotal is held under the line 5 and line 11 limits by /section179AllocationFitsTaxpayerLimits. The "no K-1 elects" conjunct is replaced by /section179AllocationCoversEveryElectingK1Activity. The sentence two paragraphs up, "column (j) routes $0 while this flag is up", is now literally true: column (j) reads THIS guard rather than /hasMultipleSection179ElectingActivities, so a freed multi elector return prints its K-1 share and a refused one prints $0. WHAT STILL REFUSES, each a data-completeness residue: an electing K-1 whose link does not resolve, a partial allocation on either arm, and shares that do not fit the limits (the contract's input contradiction). Witnesses: scheduleE/j3-179-allocation-rental-and-k1-share-the-cap and j3-179-allocation-two-electing-k1s-share-the-cap (freed), j3-179-allocation-k1-link-unresolved-stays-refused and j3-179-allocation-two-electing-k1s-one-linked-one-not-refused (residue).

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports more than one activity for at-risk purposes
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 22 (the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) "More than one activity for at-risk purposes" checkbox) and answered it YES. Complete-safe: an item that left the box blank contributes False rather than leaving the count Incomplete, which is what lets /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities resolve on every return. Counted by that fact and refused by /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities.

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports more than one activity for passive activity purposes
Fact.Description: True when THIS /formK1s item answered box 23 (the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) "More than one activity for passive activity purposes" checkbox) and answered it YES. Complete-safe, the twin of ../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities. Counted by /hasK1WithMultiplePassiveActivities and refused by /knockoutK1MultiplePassiveActivities.

Fact.Name: The attached box 22 statement: one share per at-risk activity on this K-1
Fact.Description:
THE NESTED PER ACTIVITY COLLECTION the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 22 statement carries. One item per section 465 ACTIVITY inside this K-1, each with its own portion of the box 1 ordinary loss (../*/writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare) and the partner's own amount at risk in that activity (../*/writableActivityAmountAtRisk). The grain is an ACTIVITY, which is strictly below the /formK1s grain: one /formK1s item is one Schedule K-1 document, and box 22 says that document spans several activities.
INTAKE ONLY AND UNDERIVABLE. The partner instructions say the partnership "will check this box and attach a statement" and tell the partner to "use the information in the attached statement to correctly figure your at-risk limitation". Nothing else on the return carries the split, so a fact that derived it would have invented a rule.
WHAT READS IT: ../atRiskAllowedLoss caps each activity's BASIS-ALLOWED share against that activity's OWN amount at risk and sums the results, instead of capping the whole item against the single ../amountAtRisk, whenever ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable is true. (The basis leg — ../*/activityBasisAllowedLossShare — was added 2026-08-31 by unit C5, issue 832.) When box 22 is unchecked, or the shares are unanswered, single rowed or not footing, nothing here is read and the single amount behavior is unchanged. AND SINCE 2026-09-01 THE 179 COLUMN: each share may carry ../*/writableActivitySection179Share, the activity's portion of box 12; ../atRiskAllowedSection179 caps those per activity the same way (../*/activityBasisAllowedSection179Share then ../*/activityAtRiskAllowedSection179) whenever the statement is usable, which for an electing K-1 now also requires the 179 column to foot to box 12 (../atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot). Fills the scheduleE-records:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares contract.

Fact.Name: This at-risk activity's description on the box 22 statement
Fact.Description: The attached statement's own label for ONE section 465 activity inside this K-1: the farm, the oil and gas property, the leased section 1245 property or the film that IRC 465(c)(2) treats as separate. Record only, exactly as /casualtyEvents/*/properties/*/writableDescription is for the Form 4684 property columns: nothing computed reads it, it exists so the shares can be told apart in intake and in a future printed statement.

Fact.Name: This activity's share of the K-1 box 1 ordinary loss (box 22 statement)
Fact.Description:
The MAGNITUDE of the portion of this K-1's box 1 ordinary loss the attached box 22 statement assigns to THIS activity, entered not less than zero. It is a share of ../../ordinaryLoss, the item's own loss magnitude, and ../../atRiskActivitySharesFoot refuses the return unless the shares add back to it.
A MAGNITUDE, NOT A SIGNED AMOUNT, and the choice is the module's convention: ../../ordinaryLoss is itself max(0, -../../ordinaryIncome), so the shares are stated in the same currency as the thing they foot to. THE COST IS NAMED: a statement that splits a K-1 into one activity with income and one with a loss cannot be expressed here, because the income activity has no magnitude to enter and the loss activity alone will not foot to the item's net loss. Such a statement is answered through ../writableActivitySignedShare instead, which states each row's share with its sign; a row that answers the signed field is not read from this one.

Fact.Name: This activity's signed share of the K-1 box 1 amount (box 22 statement; income positive, loss negative)
Fact.Description:
The portion of this K-1's box 1 ordinary income or (loss) the attached box 22 statement assigns to THIS activity, as a SIGNED amount: positive when the activity earned income, negative when it lost. It is the field for a MIXED-SIGN statement, one that splits a single K-1 into an activity with income and an activity with a loss, which the magnitude field ../writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare cannot hold.
EITHER FIELD PER ROW. A row that answers this field is read from it and ../writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare is not consulted for that row; a row that leaves it blank is read from the magnitude field exactly as before. Once any row carries an income share the statement must foot on the signed amounts: the income shares less the loss shares must equal ../../ordinaryIncome, the item's own signed box 1.
WHY AN INCOME ACTIVITY NEEDS NO CAP. IRC 465(d) defines the loss the at-risk rule limits as the activity's deductions in excess of that activity's own income, and the separation rules put each activity on its own Form 6198, so an activity whose line 5 is a profit has no line 21 to compute. Its income reaches Schedule E untouched; only the loss activities are capped, each against its own amount at risk. The partner still answers ../writableActivityAmountAtRisk on an income row, which the cap never reads there.

Fact.Name: This box 22 share answered its signed amount
Fact.Description: Gate: true when ../writableActivitySignedShare is answered. IsComplete is legal here: the operand is a raw Writable, so "answered" is a real question about it.

Fact.Name: This activity's share of the box 1 loss, from whichever field the row answered
Fact.Description: The loss this activity brings to the section 465 cap, as a magnitude: the negative part of ../writableActivitySignedShare when that field is answered (zero for an income activity), and ../writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare floored at zero otherwise. Every per share loss figure reads this fact rather than either writable, so a row stated in either field is capped the same way. On a statement that answers no signed share it is the magnitude field itself, which is why nothing already committed moves.

Fact.Name: This activity's share of box 1 INCOME (zero for a loss activity)
Fact.Description: The positive part of ../writableActivitySignedShare when that field is answered, and $0 otherwise. The magnitude field can only state a loss, so a row that answers only that field carries no income. This is the part of the statement the section 465 cap never reaches: IRC 465(d) nets an activity's income against that activity's own deductions and no other.

Fact.Name: The partner's amount at risk in THIS activity (465; Form 6198 line 20 per activity)
Fact.Description:
The partner's own amount at risk in ONE section 465 activity of this K-1, entered not less than zero. It is the per activity twin of ../../amountAtRisk, which this module holds as ONE amount per K-1 item; IRC 465(a)(1) measures the at-risk amount "for such activity" and IRC 465(c)(2) makes each activity separate, so on a box 22 K-1 the single amount is the wrong grain and this leaf is the right one.
THE SHARES DO NOT FOOT TO ../../amountAtRisk AND MUST NOT BE MADE TO. Form 6198 is filed per activity, so a partner with two activities has two line 20 amounts and no line that adds them; ../../amountAtRisk on a box 22 K-1 is simply not consulted once the shares are usable. Only the LOSS shares foot, and they foot to ../../ordinaryLoss.

Fact.Name: This activity's share of the K-1 box 12 section 179 deduction (box 22 statement, the 179 column)
Fact.Description:
The portion of this K-1's box 12 section 179 deduction the attached box 22 statement assigns to THIS activity, entered not less than zero. The statement splits ALL the K-1's loss items by activity, and the partner instructions name the section 179 deduction as one of the deductions the at-risk rules reach, so the 179 column is as much a part of the statement as the loss column; this is the leaf the records contract /formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySection179Share declared. The shares are a split of ../../section179Elected (box 12 as printed) and ../../atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot refuses the return unless they add back to it.
OPTIONAL PER ROW: an activity that carries none of the 179 amount leaves this blank, and the complete safe alias ../activitySection179Share reads $0 for it, so a statement whose 179 column names one activity only still foots. A K-1 that elects nothing never reads this leaf at all.

Fact.Name: This activity's 179 share, complete safe
Fact.Description: ../writableActivitySection179Share when answered and $0 otherwise, so the CollectionSum at ../../atRiskActivitySection179ShareTotal resolves Complete while a row leaves the 179 column blank. The /section179AllocationByActivity/*/electedCostShare idiom. NOT floored at $0: the writable carries the Min limit.

Fact.Name: This box 22 share answered both of its amounts
Fact.Description:
Gate: true only when the row's box 1 share is answered, in either ../writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare or ../writableActivitySignedShare, AND ../writableActivityAmountAtRisk is answered. A share that answers one and not the other cannot be capped, so ../../atRiskActivitySharesAnswered counts these and requires every row.
IsComplete IS LEGAL HERE and is not the forbidden IsComplete-on-a-complete-safe-fact: both operands are raw Writables, so "answered" is a real question about them.

Fact.Name: This activity's portion of the loss the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limit already allowed (basis worksheet line 15a column D, split by activity)
Fact.Description:
THE BASIS-ALLOWED LOSS SHARE THIS ACTIVITY BRINGS TO THE SECTION 465 GATE, i.e. the part of ../activityLossMagnitude that survived the item level 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation. It is an ALLOCATION of ../../../basisAllowedLoss across the box 22 activities, never a second derivation of the basis limit: the numerator is that one fact, the partner basis worksheet's line 15a column D, and the shares add back to it.
WHY THE SECTION 465 CAP MUST BE APPLIED TO THIS AND NOT TO THE RAW SHARE. The printed ordering is basis first, at-risk second: "After applying the basis rules, the loss you report on Schedule E may be further reduced by the at-risk rules and passive activity loss rules" (Instructions for Schedule E (2025), Basis rules for partnerships). And IRC 465(a)(2) carries forward only a loss "not allowed UNDER THIS SECTION" — dollars the basis limit disallowed are disallowed under 704(d)/1366(d), not under 465, so they must never appear in a section 465 figure. Capping the RAW loss share reported the same dollars twice, once in ../../../basisSuspendedLoss and once in the per activity 465(a)(2) sum (issue 832; measured at the 2026-08-31 landing review of unit D6). This fact is the fix.
THREE ARMS, AND THE FIRST TWO ARE WHY NOTHING MOVES ON THE COMMITTED CORPUS. (1) ../../../ordinaryLoss UNANSWERED: fall back to the raw share. ../../../ordinaryLoss derives from the raw writable ../../../ordinaryIncome, so without this arm an unanswered box 1 would drag every per share figure Incomplete; the return is refused anyway, because ../../../atRiskActivitySharesFoot's own leading arm makes the statement UNUSABLE when box 1 is unanswered. Legal IsComplete: the operand chain bottoms out on a raw Writable. (2) BASIS COVERS THE WHOLE LOSS (../../../basisAllowedLoss at or above ../../../ordinaryLoss, which for this fact means equal, since column D can never exceed column C): the share is UNTOUCHED and no division happens at all. Every committed box 22 fixture sits here — each was written with a deliberately non binding basis — and so does a box 1 INCOME K-1, where both sides are $0 and the arm keeps the division away from a zero divisor. (3) BASIS BINDS: this activity's PRO RATA portion of the allowed loss, share x allowed / total. The pro rata idiom is the printed one, taken from the same worksheet: "If basis as reported on Part II, line 14, is less than column C of line 15s, enter the pro rata amount on the corresponding line in column D." THAT RULE IS PRINTED FOR CATEGORIES OF LOSS, NOT FOR ACTIVITIES, and applying it across the activities of one category is this unit's interpretation, flagged ai-only and provisional. It is the conservative reading: a partner who could choose which activity the scarce basis lands in would put it where it is fully at risk and deduct more, and nothing printed grants that choice.
NO Round OF ITS OWN, for ../../../basisAllowedSection179's reason: rounding N pro rata shares can push their total a dollar above the basis-allowed loss they are shares of. The cents stop at ../activityAtRiskAllowedLoss, which Rounds, and ../../../atRiskAllowedLoss keeps its LesserOf(../basisAllowedLoss, ../atRiskActivityAllowedLossTotal) so an N-share rounding oversum can never reach Schedule E.
BASIS UNANSWERED is not a special arm here: ../../../basisAllowedLoss is already $0 on that return, so every share follows it to $0 — the same posture the item level chain already takes, and the return is refused by ../../../section179WithoutSufficientBasis or simply reports no deductible loss.

Fact.Name: This activity's loss allowed by its OWN amount at risk (Form 6198 line 21, per activity)
Fact.Description:
Form 6198 line 21 for ONE activity: the SMALLER of this activity's BASIS-ALLOWED share of the box 1 loss (../activityBasisAllowedLossShare) and the partner's amount at risk in this activity (../writableActivityAmountAtRisk). The same smaller-of rule ../../atRiskAllowedLoss applies to the whole item today, applied at the grain IRC 465(c)(2) prescribes.
THE OPERAND IS THE BASIS-ALLOWED SHARE, NOT THE RAW SHARE (rebodied 2026-08-31 by unit C5, issue 832). Form 6198's own line 5 is the loss after the basis limitation, and the Instructions for Schedule E say so in as many words: "After applying the basis rules, the loss you report on Schedule E may be further reduced by the at-risk rules". Reading the raw share here let the section 465 gate re-decide dollars section 704(d) had already disallowed. BYTE IDENTICAL WHERE BASIS DOES NOT BIND: ../activityBasisAllowedLossShare passes the raw share through untouched whenever ../../../basisAllowedLoss covers ../../../ordinaryLoss, which is every committed fixture.
WHY THE SEPARATENESS MATTERS AND CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM A TOTAL: two activities, one with a 1,500 loss and 500 at risk and one with a 500 loss and 5,000 at risk, allow 500 + 500 = 1,000. The whole-item cap over the same K-1 would compare a 2,000 loss with a 5,500 total and allow the entire 2,000, deducting a 1,000 loss from an activity the partner is not at risk in. The node test scheduleE/k1-box22-two-activities-separate-caps pins exactly that pair.

Fact.Name: This activity's loss suspended by its OWN amount at risk (465(a)(2) carryover, per activity)
Fact.Description:
../activityBasisAllowedLossShare less ../activityAtRiskAllowedLoss: the part of THIS activity's BASIS-ALLOWED share of the box 1 loss that its own amount at risk cannot absorb. IRC 465(a)(2) treats it as a deduction allocable to SUCH ACTIVITY in the first succeeding year, which is why it is tracked per activity here rather than only in the item level ../../atRiskSuspendedLoss. This single-year demo REPORTS the amount and applies no carryover, exactly as its item level sibling does.
IT IS MEASURED ON THE BASIS-ALLOWED SHARE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT (the fact previously subtracted from the RAW ../writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare). IRC 465(a)(2) carries forward a loss "not allowed UNDER THIS SECTION"; a dollar the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limit disallowed is not allowed under section 704(d), and it is already carried by ../../basisSuspendedLoss. Subtracting from the pre-basis share reported those dollars in BOTH carryover legs — measured on the fixture this unit adds, basis 1,000 against a 2,000 loss split 1,500/500 with 500/5,000 at risk reported 1,000 in ../../basisSuspendedLoss AND 1,000 across this per share sum. It now reports 250, the item level ../../atRiskSuspendedLoss agrees at 250, and the three legs of the 2,000 loss add up exactly: 750 deducted, 250 suspended by section 465, 1,000 suspended by section 704(d). Pinned by scheduleE/k1-box22-basis-binds-across-two-activities.
FLOORED AT $0 for a rounding reason and not a substantive one: ../activityBasisAllowedLossShare deliberately carries no Round while ../activityAtRiskAllowedLoss does, so on a pro rata share with cents the subtraction can land a fraction of a dollar below zero. It can never be materially negative — the subtrahend is a LesserOf against the same minuend — so the floor is a sign guard, not a cap.
Export and no consumer is that family's recorded posture (the form4835 twin's Description states it): a single-year engine has no succeeding return to carry into, so the figure is exported for the report surface rather than consumed. (Export added for lint_wiring, which is invisible until the manifest regenerates at integration.)

Fact.Name: This activity's portion of the K-1's section 179 share after Form 4562 Part I and the 704(d)/1366(d) basis limit (basis worksheet line 15i column D, split by activity)
Fact.Description:
THE SECTION 179 SHARE THIS ACTIVITY BRINGS TO THE SECTION 465 GATE: the part of ../activitySection179Share that survived the taxpayer level Form 4562 Part I limits and the item level 704(d)/1366(d) basis limitation. It is an ALLOCATION of ../../../section179AllocatedShare across the box 22 activities, never a second derivation of either limit: the numerator is that one fact (the pro rata share, which is ../../../basisAllowedSection179, the partner basis worksheet's line 15i column D, capped at the return's line 5 and line 11 limits and, since wave 9 stage 1, at the filer's allocation row), and the shares add back to it. The C5 shape, ../activityBasisAllowedLossShare, applied to the 179 limb, which is what the records contract made mandatory: "a section 179 apportionment that skips this repeats the basis-allowed-share defect on the deduction side".
WHY THE SECTION 465 CAP MUST BE APPLIED TO THIS AND NOT TO THE RAW 179 SHARE: the printed ordering is basis first, at-risk second ("After applying the basis rules, the loss you report on Schedule E may be further reduced by the at-risk rules"), the basis worksheet's line 15i takes the section 179 share "even if you can't deduct all of it due to limitations" and allocates column D pro rata, and IRC 465(a)(2) carries forward only a loss "not allowed UNDER THIS SECTION". Capping the raw share would report a basis disallowed dollar in both the basis leg and the per activity 465(a)(2) sum, the basis-allowed-share defect on the deduction side.
THREE ARMS. (1) The K-1 elects nothing: $0, without reading anything, so a box 22 K-1 with no box 12 amount never touches the 179 chain (../../../section179AllocatedShare would be $0 there anyway, but this arm also keeps the divisor case away). (2) NOTHING BINDS (../../../section179AllocatedShare at or above ../../../section179Elected, which for this fact means equal): the share passes through untouched and no division is evaluated. (3) SOMETHING BINDS: this activity's PRO RATA portion, share x allocated / box 12. The pro rata idiom is the worksheet's own column D rule, printed for CATEGORIES of loss; applying it across the activities of one category is the same interpretation ../activityBasisAllowedLossShare carries, flagged the same way. The divisor is box 12 as printed, strictly positive on arm 3 because arm 1 absorbed the electing nothing case.
NO Round OF ITS OWN, for ../activityBasisAllowedLossShare's reason: rounding N pro rata shares can push their total a dollar above the item's share. The cents stop at ../activityAtRiskAllowedSection179, which Rounds, and ../../../atRiskAllowedSection179 keeps a LesserOf against ../section179AllocatedShare so an N share rounding oversum can never reach Schedule E.
COMPLETENESS: ../../../section179AllocatedShare is Incomplete on exactly one population, an electing K-1 on a return whose rental five year basis is unanswered, where the whole K-1 179 chain is deliberately Incomplete already (see ../../../section179ColumnJ); this fact adds nothing to that refusal.

Fact.Name: This activity's section 179 share allowed by its OWN amount at risk (465, per activity)
Fact.Description: The SMALLER of this activity's basis allowed 179 share (../activityBasisAllowedSection179Share) and what is left of the partner's amount at risk in THIS activity once the activity's box 1 loss leg has taken its bite: max($0, ../writableActivityAmountAtRisk - ../activityAtRiskAllowedLoss). The item level ../../../atRiskAllowedSection179 applies exactly this remainder rule to the whole K-1 against the single ../../../amountAtRisk; on a box 22 K-1 that single amount is the wrong grain, IRC 465(a)(1) measures the amount at risk "for such activity", and this fact is the rule at the grain IRC 465(c)(2) prescribes. The box 1 loss first, 179 second PRIORITY is the same convention the item level fact discloses (Form 6198 prints no allocation between classes; the direction changes only which class carries the suspension, never the total allowed). Rounded to whole dollars, matching ../activityAtRiskAllowedLoss.

Fact.Name: This activity's section 179 share suspended by its OWN amount at risk (465(a)(2) carryover, per activity)
Fact.Description: ../activityBasisAllowedSection179Share less ../activityAtRiskAllowedSection179: the part of THIS activity's basis allowed 179 share that its own amount at risk cannot absorb. IRC 465(a)(2) treats it as a deduction allocable to SUCH ACTIVITY in the first succeeding year, which is why it is tracked per activity here beside the item level ../../../atRiskSuspendedSection179 (which agrees with the sum of these on a usable statement, up to rounding). Measured on the BASIS ALLOWED share, never the raw one, for ../activityAtRiskSuspendedLoss's reason: a dollar the basis limit disallowed is not "not allowed under this section". This single year model REPORTS the amount and applies no carryover. Floored at $0 as a rounding sign guard, exactly as its loss twin. Exported and read by nothing, the recorded posture of the whole carryover family.

Fact.Name: This K-1 recorded a box 22 statement with more than one activity
Fact.Description:
Gate: true only when ../atRiskActivityShares is a collection the return actually opened AND it holds MORE THAN ONE share. The IsComplete on the collection ROOT is the idiom /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities uses over /formK1s and is what keeps a return that never opened the nested collection Complete false instead of Incomplete: a CollectionSize over an absent root does not resolve Complete on the JVM.
WHY MORE THAN ONE AND NOT AT LEAST ONE. Box 22 is captioned "More than one activity for at-risk purposes", and IRC 465(c)(2) only has work to do once there are two. A single row statement contradicts the box that summoned it, so it is treated as an incomplete intake and left in the refusal residue rather than silently collapsed onto the single amount path.

Fact.Name: Every recorded box 22 share answered both of its amounts
Fact.Description: Gate: true when ../atRiskActivitySharesRecorded AND every share answered both amounts, i.e. the count of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityShareAnswered reaches the collection's own size. Count over a boolean collection counts the TRUE items, the /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities idiom, so "as many trues as rows" is "every row". Complete-safe false whenever the collection was never opened, because the leading Switch case reads ../atRiskActivitySharesRecorded and nothing else.

Fact.Name: Total of the box 22 statement's per activity loss shares
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityLossMagnitude (each row's loss, from whichever of its two fields it answered): what the attached statement says this K-1's loss activities add up to. It is compared with ../ordinaryLoss, the item's own loss magnitude, by ../atRiskActivitySharesFoot. Gated on ../atRiskActivitySharesAnswered so that an unanswered share leaves the total at a Complete $0 instead of Incomplete; the gate that consumes it never treats $0 as footing unless the item's own loss is also $0.

Fact.Name: Total of the box 22 statement's per activity INCOME shares
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityIncomeMagnitude: the box 1 income the statement assigns to its earning activities. $0 on every statement that answers no signed share, which is every statement the magnitude field alone can express. Gated like ../atRiskActivityLossShareTotal, so an unanswered share leaves it a Complete $0.

Fact.Name: The box 22 statement splits this K-1 into an earning activity and a losing activity
Fact.Description: True when the statement carries at least one income share (../atRiskActivityIncomeShareTotal above $0) AND at least one loss share (../atRiskActivityLossShareTotal above $0). Both totals are complete safe, so this is a Complete false on every return that leaves box 22 blank or answers no signed share.

Fact.Name: Sum of the per activity at-risk allowed losses, before the statement is judged usable
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedLoss gated only on every share being answered, NOT on ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable. It is the same sum as ../atRiskActivityAllowedLossTotal; it exists because ../atRiskActivitySharesMixedSignResidue must read that sum to decide usability, and reading the Usable-gated total there would be a cycle.

Fact.Name: A mixed-sign box 22 statement this module computes only in part (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when the statement is mixed sign (../atRiskActivityStatementIsMixedSign) AND any of three things holds. Each is a case where the answer is not wrong to want but the graph cannot yet carry it, so the statement is held UNUSABLE and the K-1 stays refused.
(1) AN AT-RISK CAP TURNS THE ITEM'S NET UPWARD PAST WHAT THE ROUTING CAN PRINT. The K-1's Schedule E figure on a mixed-sign statement is its income shares less its capped loss shares. Every consumer downstream of ../atRiskAllowedLoss chooses the income column or the loss column on the SIGN OF BOX 1 (../ordinaryIncome) and on a box 1 income prints box 1 itself. That is right when the capped net keeps box 1's sign and, on an income item, its amount. It is wrong when a cap bites hard enough that the capped loss total falls below BOTH the income total and the uncapped loss total: on a box 1 loss the K-1 would really report income, and on a box 1 income it would report MORE income than box 1. That is the test here: the per activity allowed sum (../atRiskActivityCappedLossSum) below both ../atRiskActivityIncomeShareTotal and ../atRiskActivityLossShareTotal.
(2) BASIS BINDS (../basisAllowedLoss below ../ordinaryLoss). The partner basis worksheet limits the NET box 1 loss, and its pro rata rule allocates that limit across categories of loss, not across a netted split of income and loss activities. Nothing vendored says how to carry a binding basis into a mixed-sign split.
(3) THE K-1 ELECTS SECTION 179 (../electsSection179). The statement's 179 column is capped against what is left of each activity's amount at risk after its loss share, and on a mixed statement an income activity's 179 share has no loss share ahead of it; that composition is not built.
Complete safe: an unanswered box 1 makes it a Complete false (that return is refused by the foot instead), and the mixed-sign flag is itself complete safe.

Fact.Name: The box 22 shares foot to this K-1's own box 1 loss
Fact.Description:
Gate: true when every share is answered AND ../atRiskActivityLossShareTotal equals ../ordinaryLoss. Equality is spelled as the two GreaterThanOrEqual comparisons rather than Equal because Equal compares the Dollar values with a raw ==, which is scale sensitive; the two sided inequality is exact and carries no scale risk.
THIS IS THE REFUSAL THAT SURVIVES. A statement whose shares do not add back to the K-1's own loss is an input CONTRADICTION: either the split or the box 1 amount is wrong, and no rule in the Code or the instructions says which. The return stays refused by /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities, which is the data-completeness residue the contract names.
THE LEADING ARM GUARDS COMPLETENESS (added 2026-08-31 at the landing — adversarial-review BLOCKER): ../ordinaryLoss derives from the RAW writable ../ordinaryIncome, so without this arm a box-22 K-1 with a fully-answered footing statement but an UNANSWERED box 1 dragged this gate, Usable, Unusable and the KNOCKOUT ITSELF Incomplete — a return the old key refused (Complete true, measured) stopped resolving its own guard. With the arm, an unanswered box 1 makes the foot FALSE, the statement UNUSABLE, and the return REFUSED, which is the honest disposition: statement recorded, loss unknown, statement not usable. A knockout guard's completeness must never depend on a raw writable.
THE SIGNED ARM. When any share carries box 1 INCOME (../atRiskActivityIncomeShareTotal above $0, possible only through ../atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySignedShare), the statement foots on SIGNED amounts: the income shares less the loss shares must equal ../ordinaryIncome. The magnitude comparison below it cannot see such a statement, since a net loss plus an income activity never equals the loss shares alone. A statement with no income share is tested exactly as before, including a box 1 income K-1 whose loss shares are all $0.

Fact.Name: Total of the box 22 statement's per activity section 179 shares
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activitySection179Share: what the attached statement says this K-1's box 12 section 179 deduction splits into. Compared with ../section179Elected by ../atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot.
