Gated on ../atRiskActivitySharesRecorded (the IsComplete guarded collection root) so a return that never opened the nested collection resolves a Complete $0; the alias inside the sum makes a blank 179 cell count $0 rather than leaving the total Incomplete.

Fact.Name: The box 22 statement's 179 column foots to this K-1's own box 12
Fact.Description:
Gate, the 179 twin of ../atRiskActivitySharesFoot: TRUE when this K-1 elects nothing (there is no 179 amount to split, so the column is inert and cannot block the statement), and otherwise true only when the statement is recorded AND ../atRiskActivitySection179ShareTotal equals ../section179Elected, box 12 as printed. Equality is the two sided GreaterThanOrEqual for the loss foot's scale reason.
THIS IS THE 179 LIMB OF THE REFUSAL THAT SURVIVES: a 179 column that does not add back to box 12 is an input CONTRADICTION, and no rule says whether the split or box 12 is wrong. It is the residue the records contract named ("shares must foot to the item's 179 amount"). The committed fixture k1-box22-section179-column-absent-stays-in-the-refusal-residue sits exactly here: its statement has no 179 column at all against a box 12 of 300, so it stays refused, now for this reason rather than for electing.
ALWAYS Complete: the first arm reads a complete safe flag, the second the IsComplete guarded Recorded gate, and the total is complete safe, so ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable, which reads this in an All, keeps its own completeness.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 22 statement can drive the per activity at-risk limit
Fact.Description:
Gate: true when box 22 is checked (../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities), the shares are recorded, answered and footing (../atRiskActivitySharesFoot, which subsumes the other two), and the statement's section 179 column foots to box 12 (../atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot, true for a K-1 that elects nothing and, for one that does, true only when the 179 column foots), and the statement is not in the mixed-sign residue (../atRiskActivitySharesMixedSignResidue, false on every statement that is not mixed sign).
WHY THE SECTION 179 TEST IS PART OF THE GATE AND NOT A SEPARATE GUARD. ../atRiskAllowedSection179 caps the K-1's section 179 share at what is left of the SINGLE ../amountAtRisk once ../atRiskAllowedLoss has taken its bite. Freeing a section 179 electing K-1 onto the per activity path without a per activity 179 column would subtract a per activity allowed loss from a whole item at-risk amount, which is not a quantity: it is exactly the mixing of grains this knockout family exists to prevent. The box 22 statement splits ALL the K-1's loss items by activity, section 179 included, so the honest answer is a per activity section 179 share on this same collection, and that is what the graph now carries: the 179 column ../atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySection179Share, its basis aware share ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityBasisAllowedSection179Share, the per activity 465 cap ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedSection179 and the sum ../atRiskActivityAllowedSection179Total that ../atRiskAllowedSection179 reads on a usable statement. The residue that remains is narrower: a 179 column that does not foot to box 12.
BOX 22 BEATS ../fullyAtRisk. When a usable statement is present the leading case of ../atRiskAllowedLoss fires whatever ../fullyAtRisk says, because a partnership that attached a per activity at-risk statement has reported a more specific fact than the partner's single yes-or-no attestation. A filer who is genuinely fully at risk in every activity records each share's amount at risk at or above its loss share and the caps are all non binding, so the answer is the same.
COMPLETE-SAFE by construction: ../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities is the FIRST conjunct and is itself complete safe, and an All whose head resolves Complete false short circuits without evaluating the rest, so a return that leaves box 22 blank never reads the nested collection.

Fact.Name: Sum of the per activity at-risk allowed section 179 shares on this K-1
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedSection179: the section 465 allowed section 179 deduction for this K-1 once each activity's BASIS ALLOWED 179 share has been capped against what is left of its OWN amount at risk. Read by the leading usable statement arm of ../atRiskAllowedSection179. Gated on ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable so the sum is a Complete $0 on every return that has no usable statement, the ../atRiskActivityAllowedLossTotal idiom.

Fact.Name: Sum of the per activity at-risk allowed losses on this K-1
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityAtRiskAllowedLoss: the section 465 allowed loss for this K-1 once each activity's BASIS-ALLOWED share has been capped against its OWN amount at risk (the basis leg was added 2026-08-31 by unit C5, issue 832; before it the cap opened on the raw loss share). Read by ../atRiskAllowedLoss's leading case. Gated on ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable so the sum is a Complete $0 on every return that has no usable statement, which is what keeps the whole family complete safe.

Fact.Name: This K-1 checked box 22 but its statement cannot drive the limit (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
The data-completeness residue: box 22 is checked (../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities) and ../atRiskActivitySharesUsable is false, i.e. the shares are missing, single rowed, half answered, not footing, or the K-1 also elects section 179. Counted by /hasK1WithUnusableAtRiskActivityShares and refused by /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities. "Or the K-1 also elects section 179" is superseded by "or the K-1 elects section 179 and the statement's 179 column does not foot to box 12" (../atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot).
Complete-safe: ../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities is the FIRST conjunct, so an item that left box 22 blank contributes Complete false without reading anything else.

Fact.Name: A recorded K-1 checked box 22 without a usable per activity statement (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when at least one recorded /formK1s item is flagged by /formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySharesUnusable. Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s COLLECTION ROOT for the reason /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities gives: a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete.
IT IS THE NARROWED KEY OF /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities, which until this unit was keyed on /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities, i.e. on the box alone. That flag KEEPS its meaning ("box 22 was checked") and its export, because it is the honest name for that population and the section 469 twin still uses the same shape; what changed is only which flag the refusal reads.

Fact.Name: A recorded K-1 covers more than one at-risk activity (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when at least one recorded /formK1s item checked box 22. Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s COLLECTION ROOT, the idiom scheduleD:/collectiblesGainFromK1RowsAnswered uses over this same collection, because a Count over a collection the return never opened does not resolve Complete; a return that never opened the collection therefore resolves Complete false. The gate is deliberately NOT /claimsK1Income: that flag is a separate Part II income claim and a return can record a K-1 document without it, in which case the checkbox would go unread. Keys /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities.

Fact.Name: A recorded K-1 covers more than one passive activity (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when at least one recorded /formK1s item checked box 23. Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s collection root for the reason its at-risk twin /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities gives. Keys /knockoutK1MultiplePassiveActivities.

Fact.Name: The attached box 23 statement: one share per passive activity on this K-1
Fact.Description:
THE NESTED PER ACTIVITY COLLECTION the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 23 statement carries. One item per section 469 ACTIVITY inside this K-1, each with its own portion of the box 1 amount (../*/writableActivityShare) and the partner's own participation answer for THAT activity (../*/writableActivityParticipation). The grain is an ACTIVITY, strictly below the /formK1s grain, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityShares twin's own words.
INTAKE ONLY AND UNDERIVABLE, for the reason ../atRiskActivityShares gives: the split lives only on the attached statement.
WHAT READS IT: ../passiveNet and ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 each take a leading case keyed on ../passiveActivitySharesUsable, replacing the single item-level classification with the per-activity one for the K-1s this statement can express. Fills the scheduleE-records:/formK1s/*/passiveActivityShares contract.

Fact.Name: This passive activity's description on the box 23 statement
Fact.Description: The attached statement's own label for ONE section 469 activity inside this K-1. Record only, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivityDescription twin: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: This activity's share of the K-1 box 1 amount (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description:
The MAGNITUDE of the portion of this K-1's box 1 amount the attached box 23 statement assigns to THIS activity, entered not less than zero. It is a share of ../../passiveActivityShareMagnitude — ../../ordinaryIncome when box 1 is income, ../../ordinaryLoss when box 1 is a loss — and ../../passiveActivitySharesFoot refuses the return unless the shares add back to it.
A MAGNITUDE, NOT A SIGNED AMOUNT, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityShares/*/ writableActivityOrdinaryLossShare convention. THE COST IS NAMED, and it is sharper here than at box 22 because section 469 (unlike section 465) classifies income as well as loss: a statement that splits a K-1 into one activity with income and one with a loss cannot be expressed by this field, and stays refused, as at box 22.

Fact.Name: The partner materially participated in THIS activity (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer MATERIALLY PARTICIPATED in THIS one section 469 activity inside the K-1 — the per-activity twin of ../../materiallyParticipated, asked once per row of the box 23 statement instead of once per K-1. UNANSWERED IS INCOMPLETE, deliberately not defaulted: see ../activityLossIsPassive and the module banner above for why a per-share default is never taken here, unlike ../../materiallyParticipated's own item-level presumption chain.

Fact.Name: This box 23 share answered its amount (participation is separately gated)
Fact.Description: True when ../writableActivityShare is answered. Deliberately NOT conjoined with ../writableActivityParticipation: the amount drives ../../passiveActivitySharesFoot (footing is an intake-completeness question, answerable without knowing yet how the activity classifies), while an unanswered participation answer is left to make ../activityLossIsPassive and everything downstream of it Incomplete on its own, per the module banner above. Counted by ../../passiveActivitySharesAnswered, the box-22 ../../atRiskActivityShares/*/activityShareAnswered pattern narrowed to the ONE amount this statement's foot check needs.

Fact.Name: This activity's own 469 classification (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description: Not() of ../writableActivityParticipation and NOTHING ELSE — no presumption, no item-level fallback. When the writable is unanswered this fact is Incomplete, and stays Incomplete through ../activityPassiveContribution and ../activityNonpassiveContribution into the item-level ../../passiveActivitySharesPassiveTotal / ../../passiveActivitySharesNonpassiveTotal sums.

Fact.Name: This activity's signed, post-465 amount (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description:
This activity's share, signed and — for a LOSS item — already reduced by the item's section 465 at-risk limit: +../writableActivityShare when the K-1 item is INCOME (../../ordinaryIncome >= 0, where 465 never applies), else this activity's PRO RATA portion of ../../atRiskAllowedLoss (the item's own basis-and-at-risk-allowed loss), negated. The divisor ../../ordinaryLoss is strictly positive whenever this branch is reached, because it is only read when the item is a loss and ../../passiveActivitySharesFoot has already required the shares to add back to it.
THE PRO RATA IDIOM IS THE PRINTED ONE box 22's ../atRiskActivityShares/*/ activityBasisAllowedLossShare already takes from the partner basis worksheet's column D rule, applied here across a DIFFERENT partition (box 23's participation split rather than box 22's at-risk split) for the SAME reason: nothing vendored allocates a partially binding item-level limit across an activity split, so this fact does — flagged ai-only and provisional, the box-22 fact's own posture. Rounding N independently rounded shares can push their total a cent above ../../atRiskAllowedLoss; the cents stop at the item-level totals below, which this unit does not further cap because no downstream consumer sums shares against a second ceiling the way ../atRiskAllowedLoss's LesserOf does for box 22 — named here as a known, precedented (interpretation:provisional) rounding residue rather than silently accepted.

Fact.Name: This activity's signed contribution to the 8582 pool, if PASSIVE (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description: ../activitySignedAmount when ../activityLossIsPassive, else $0. Incomplete when ../activityLossIsPassive is Incomplete (the per-share module banner). Summed into ../../passiveActivitySharesPassiveTotal, the leading case ../../passiveNet reads on a usable statement.

Fact.Name: This activity's signed contribution to Schedule E Part II, if NONPASSIVE (box 23 statement)
Fact.Description: $0 when ../activityLossIsPassive, else ../activitySignedAmount. Incomplete when ../activityLossIsPassive is Incomplete (the per-share module banner). Summed into ../../passiveActivitySharesNonpassiveTotal, the leading case ../../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 reads on a usable statement.

Fact.Name: This K-1's own box 1 magnitude, whichever sign it carries (box 23 foot target)
Fact.Description: ../ordinaryIncome when box 1 is income (>= 0), else ../ordinaryLoss: the SAME magnitude ../passiveActivityShareTotal must foot to, stated once so ../passiveActivitySharesFoot and ../passiveActivityShares/*/activitySignedAmount share one definition instead of repeating the sign test.

Fact.Name: This K-1 recorded a box 23 statement with more than one activity
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when ../passiveActivityShares is a collection the return actually opened AND it holds MORE THAN ONE share, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityShares-family ../atRiskActivitySharesRecorded pattern and its reasoning verbatim (box 23 is captioned "More than one activity" the same way box 22 is).

Fact.Name: Every recorded box 23 share answered its amount
Fact.Description: Gate: true when ../passiveActivitySharesRecorded AND every share answered its amount (../passiveActivityShares/*/activityShareAnswered), the box-22 ../atRiskActivitySharesAnswered pattern narrowed to the ONE field this statement's foot check needs — participation is deliberately not required here (module banner above).

Fact.Name: Total of the box 23 statement's per activity shares
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../passiveActivityShares/*/writableActivityShare: what the attached statement says this K-1's box 1 amount adds up to. Compared with ../passiveActivityShareMagnitude by ../passiveActivitySharesFoot. Gated on ../passiveActivitySharesAnswered so an unanswered share leaves the total at a Complete $0, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityLossShareTotal pattern.

Fact.Name: The box 23 shares foot to this K-1's own box 1 amount (single-signed only)
Fact.Description:
Gate: true when every share is answered AND ../passiveActivityShareTotal equals ../passiveActivityShareMagnitude — box 1 unanswered returns FALSE (the leading arm, the box-22 ../atRiskActivitySharesFoot completeness reasoning verbatim), so an unanswered box 1 makes this gate, ../passiveActivitySharesUsable and the knockout REFUSE rather than go Incomplete.
THIS IS THE REFUSAL THAT SURVIVES, and it is the SAME arithmetic that quietly also excludes the mixed-sign population named in the module banner above: a share total can equal ../passiveActivityShareMagnitude only when every entered share genuinely belongs to the item's own sign, because ../passiveActivityShareMagnitude IS whichever single-signed number the item carries. A statement that actually mixes an income activity with a loss activity either double-counts against the wrong magnitude or fails to foot — either way it stays refused here, honestly, even though this gate does not name "mixed sign" as a separate test.

Fact.Name: This K-1's box 23 statement can drive the per activity passive classification
Fact.Description:
Gate: true when box 23 is checked (../reportsMultiplePassiveActivities), the shares foot (../passiveActivitySharesFoot, which subsumes recorded/answered), this K-1 is NOT a publicly traded partnership (../isPubliclyTradedPartnership — the per-entity §469(k) regime the module banner names as unbuilt for this split), this K-1 does NOT also check box 22 (../reportsMultipleAtRiskActivities — two different partitions of one item, the module banner's un-merged-partitions residue), and this K-1 does NOT elect section 179 (../electsSection179 — the same population the box-22 179 column excluded before the 179 column extended it, unbuilt here for the same reason).
DELIBERATELY NOT CONJOINED WITH PARTICIPATION ANSWERED: a return with a footing, non-PTP, single-box, non-electing statement is Usable even while a share's participation is still unanswered, so the ROUTING (not the knockout) carries that Incompleteness, per the module banner.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: ../reportsMultiplePassiveActivities is the FIRST conjunct and is itself complete safe, so a return that leaves box 23 blank never reads anything else.

Fact.Name: Sum of the box 23 statement's per activity PASSIVE contributions
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../passiveActivityShares/*/activityPassiveContribution: this K-1's signed contribution to the 8582 pool once each activity has been classified on its own participation answer. Read by ../passiveNet's leading case. Gated on ../passiveActivitySharesUsable so the sum is a Complete $0 on every return with no usable box-23 statement, the box-22 ../atRiskActivityAllowedLossTotal idiom.

Fact.Name: Sum of the box 23 statement's per activity NONPASSIVE contributions
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of ../passiveActivityShares/*/activityNonpassiveContribution: this K-1's signed contribution to Schedule E Part II once each activity has been classified on its own participation answer. Read by ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179's leading case. Gated on ../passiveActivitySharesUsable, the twin of ../passiveActivitySharesPassiveTotal.

Fact.Name: This K-1 checked box 23 but its statement cannot drive the classification (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
The data-completeness residue: box 23 is checked (../reportsMultiplePassiveActivities) and ../passiveActivitySharesUsable is false, i.e. the shares are missing, single rowed, half answered, not footing (which subsumes the mixed-sign population, module banner above), or the K-1 is a PTP, also checks box 22, or elects section 179. Counted by /hasK1WithUnusablePassiveActivityShares and refused by /knockoutK1MultiplePassiveActivities.
Complete-safe: ../reportsMultiplePassiveActivities is the FIRST conjunct, so an item that left box 23 blank contributes Complete false without reading anything else.

Fact.Name: A recorded K-1 checked box 23 without a usable per activity statement (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when at least one recorded /formK1s item is flagged by /formK1s/*/passiveActivitySharesUnusable. Guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s COLLECTION ROOT, the box-22 /hasK1WithUnusableAtRiskActivityShares pattern.
IT IS THE NARROWED KEY OF /knockoutK1MultiplePassiveActivities, which until this unit was keyed on /hasK1WithMultiplePassiveActivities, i.e. on the box alone. That flag KEEPS its meaning and export; only which flag the refusal reads changed.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Schedule K-1 covers more than one at-risk activity
Fact.Description:
A recorded Schedule K-1 checked box 22, "More than one activity for at-risk purposes". The partnership then attaches a statement splitting the K-1 by activity, and the partner must apply the section 465 at-risk limit to each activity separately.
WHY THIS BLOCKS SUBMISSION RATHER THAN SITTING UNREAD. This module holds ONE at-risk position per K-1 item: /formK1s/*/fullyAtRisk is a single yes or no, /formK1s/*/amountAtRisk a single amount, and /formK1s/*/atRiskAllowedLoss caps the item's whole loss against that one amount. When the K-1 aggregates several activities, each with its own amount at risk, that per item cap is not the statute's cap: it lets a loss from an activity the partner is not at risk in be absorbed by another activity's at-risk amount. No intake in this dictionary collects the attached statement, and the split cannot be derived from any other answer on the return, so the population is refused rather than computed wrong. The same argument, and the same shape, as /knockoutSection179MultipleElectingActivities.
NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION: only a return that actually checks the box refuses. The flag /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities is guarded by an IsComplete on the /formK1s collection root and every per item flag is complete safe, so a return with no K-1, or with K-1s that leave box 22 blank, resolves Complete false and nothing changes.
ONE CAVEAT ON "BLOCKS SUBMISSION": membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is the other half of the wiring and lives in flow.xml, outside this module. Reported to the lead.
NARROWED 2026-08-31 FROM THE BOX TO THE MISSING STATEMENT. The paragraph above is no longer the whole truth and is kept because it is the argument this guard was built on. The successor the contract named is BUILT: /formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares is the attached statement, one nested share per section 465 activity carrying that activity's portion of the box 1 loss and the partner's own amount at risk in it, and /formK1s/*/atRiskAllowedLoss now caps each activity separately whenever that statement is usable. So "no intake in this dictionary collects the attached statement" has stopped being true, and the refusal moves off the box.
WHAT STILL REFUSES, and it is a data-completeness residue with no in-repo remedy: this guard is now keyed on /hasK1WithUnusableAtRiskActivityShares, i.e. box 22 checked AND the statement not usable. Unusable means the shares were never recorded, the statement holds a single row when the box says more than one activity, some share left an amount blank, the shares do NOT FOOT to the K-1's own box 1 loss, or the K-1 also passes through a section 179 election whose per activity split this unit did not build. The footing arm is the sharp one: shares that do not add back to the reported loss are an input CONTRADICTION and nothing in the Code or the instructions says which of the two numbers to believe. That is the residue the scheduleE-records:/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares contract names as "the refusal that should survive".
STRICTLY NARROWER, SO NOTHING MOVES: every return this guard refused before either still refuses (no shares recorded) or was newly given a way to compute. /hasK1WithMultipleAtRiskActivities keeps its own meaning and its export and is no longer read by this fact.
NARROWED AGAIN 2026-09-01: the section 179 arm is BUILT. The statement's 179 column (/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySection179Share) is apportioned on the C5 basis aware shape (../*/activityBasisAllowedSection179Share) and capped per activity against what is left of that activity's own amount at risk (../*/activityAtRiskAllowedSection179), and /formK1s/*/atRiskAllowedSection179 reads the sum on a usable statement. "Or the K-1 also passes through a section 179 election" is therefore replaced in the residue by "or the K-1 elects section 179 and the statement's 179 column does not foot to box 12" (/formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySection179SharesFoot). The 179 foot is the same input-contradiction class as the loss foot. Strictly narrower again: the committed k1-box22-section179-column-absent-stays-in-the-refusal-residue fixture, whose statement carries no 179 column against a box 12 of 300, stays refused byte for byte, now on the 179 foot; the new j3-box22-179-column-foots-and-computes-per-activity witnesses the freed cell.
NARROWED AGAIN: A MIXED-SIGN STATEMENT COMPUTES. Each share may now state its portion of box 1 as a signed amount (/formK1s/*/atRiskActivityShares/*/writableActivitySignedShare), so a statement that splits the K-1 into an earning activity and a losing activity foots on the signed box 1 and computes: the income passes untouched and each loss activity is capped against its own amount at risk. Such a statement used to fail the magnitude foot and refuse here. What stays refused of that population is /formK1s/*/atRiskActivitySharesMixedSignResidue: a cap that would push the K-1's net above what the box 1 sign routing can print, a binding basis, or a section 179 election on the mixed statement. Strictly narrower again: a statement that answers no signed share is judged exactly as before.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a Schedule K-1 covers more than one passive activity
Fact.Description:
A recorded Schedule K-1 checked box 23, "More than one activity for passive activity purposes". The partnership then attaches a statement splitting the K-1 by activity, and the partner must apply the section 469 passive activity rules to each activity separately.
WHY THIS BLOCKED SUBMISSION AT FIRST. This module used to classify participation ONCE per K-1 item: /formK1s/*/materiallyParticipated was a single yes or no, /formK1s/*/lossIsPassive followed from it, and /formK1s/*/passiveNet routed the whole item to the section 8582 pool on that one classification. A K-1 covering several activities can be material participation in one and passive in another, so a single classification either swept a nonpassive amount into the pool or kept a passive loss out of it.
NARROWED FROM THE BOX TO THE UNUSABLE STATEMENT. The successor the contract named is BUILT: /formK1s/*/passiveActivityShares is the attached statement, one nested share per section 469 activity carrying that activity's own portion of box 1 and its own participation answer, and /formK1s/*/passiveNet and /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 each take a leading case that routes per activity whenever that statement is usable. So "the split lives only in the attached statement, which no intake collects" has stopped being true, and the refusal moves off the box, the same narrowing its at-risk twin /knockoutK1MultipleAtRiskActivities already took.
WHAT STILL REFUSES, a data-completeness residue with no in-repo remedy today: this guard is now keyed on /hasK1WithUnusablePassiveActivityShares, i.e. box 23 checked AND the statement not usable. Unusable means the shares were never recorded, the statement holds a single row, some share left its amount blank, the shares do NOT FOOT to the K-1's own box 1 amount (which subsumes a MIXED-SIGN statement — one activity earning while another loses on the same K-1, since the magnitude-only share field can only foot against a single-signed target — see /formK1s/*/passiveActivityShares's own module banner), the K-1 is a publicly traded partnership (the per-entity section 469(k) regime a per-activity split does not yet fold into), the K-1 ALSO checks box 22 (a different partition of the same item; merging the two splits is an unruled call named at the 2026-08-31 D6/A3 landing), or the K-1 elects section 179 (the box-22 179 column's own earlier posture, extended here rather than re-derived). An UNANSWERED PARTICIPATION on an otherwise usable statement does NOT refuse here — /formK1s/*/passiveActivityShares/*/activityLossIsPassive lets that ONE activity's routing go Incomplete instead, so this guard stays FALSE while /formK1s/*/passiveNet and /formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179 (and everything downstream) correctly go Incomplete on that K-1 — the contract’s own instruction that an unanswered share is Incomplete, never a silent default.
STRICTLY NARROWER, SO NOTHING MOVES: every return this guard refused before either still refuses (no shares recorded, a PTP, a box-22 combo, a 179 election, or a non-footing/mixed- sign statement) or was newly given a way to compute (a footing, non-PTP, single-box, non-electing statement). /hasK1WithMultiplePassiveActivities keeps its own meaning and export and is no longer read by this fact, the at-risk twin's own posture.
ONE CAVEAT ON "BLOCKS SUBMISSION": membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut is the other half of the wiring and lives in flow.xml, outside this module. Reported to the lead.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the royalty activity's Schedule E line 21 is a LOSS
Fact.Description:
NARROWED on the owner's direction that the at-risk refusal be corrected and built. The successor shipped: /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk with /writableRoyaltyAmountAtRisk drive /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet, so a royalty loss is computed and filed on both arms. What still fires here is the one population the section 465 chain cannot serve: a filer with a loss who has not answered the attestation at all. All five consumer certifications are discharged (see the fixtures named on /royaltyAtRiskAllowedNet). The flow screen for the two intakes is the application follow-through that should land with this narrowing.
Blocks submission when the return claims a royalty (/claimsRoyaltyIncome) and the activity's net (/royaltyActivityNet - Schedule E line 4 minus the line-20 ordinary expenses minus the line-18 depletion) is BELOW ZERO. Fires on the ACTIVITY net, before the working-interest fork, so ONE guard covers both arms: the investment royalty that stays on Schedule E line 21 AND the oil-or-gas working interest that /workingInterestNetProfit routes to Schedule C line 31.
WHAT IT CLOSES, measured rather than described. Three Descriptions on this chain used to claim a net loss was excluded by design — /royaltyNetIncome ("Scoped to profit/breakeven (income greater than or equal to expenses); a net royalty loss is not modelled"), /writableRoyaltyExpenses ("Scoped so that income is greater than or equal to expenses ... a net royalty loss is not modelled") and /workingInterestNetProfit ("a working-interest LOSS is not modelled"). NOTHING GUARDED IT. Both /writableRoyaltyIncome and /writableRoyaltyExpenses are Min-0 writables with no maximum, and /royaltyActivityNet has no floor, so a fixture with royalty income 10,000 and expenses 25,000 resolved /royaltyActivityNet and /royaltyNetIncome at -15,000, carried it through /scheduleEPartINetIncome and /scheduleETotalIncome, and reduced /totalIncome by 15,000 - with /flowIsKnockedOut still Placeholder false. The working-interest twin did the same thing through /workingInterestNetProfit into scheduleC:/scheduleCNetProfit. The third claim is the worst-shaped of the three: it asserts a REFUSAL that never existed.
WHY THIS UNIT ADDS A REFUSAL IN A FILL CAMPAIGN. The alternative it replaces is not a computation, it is a silent taxpayer-favourable one: an unbounded income reduction that skips the limitation the printed form points at on the very line that produces it. Schedule E line 21 reads "Subtract line 20 from line 3 (rents) and/or 4 (royalties). If result is a (loss), see instructions to find out if you must file Form 6198" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040se.pdf, page 1), and the instruction it sends the filer to says "In most cases, you must complete Form 6198 to figure your loss if you have: * A loss from an activity carried on as a trade or business or for the production of income, and * Amounts in the activity for which you are not at risk" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040se.pdf, page 3, LEFT column of a two-column extraction). A royalty held for the production of income is squarely inside that first bullet, and the instruction forecloses the one escape a reader might reach for: the at-risk rules "do not apply to losses from an activity of holding real property placed in service before 1987 ... THE ACTIVITY OF HOLDING MINERAL PROPERTY DOES NOT QUALIFY FOR THIS EXCEPTION" (lines 172-176). This is the mineral-property refusal pattern and the 2026-08-17 sibling /knockoutRentalBuildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown: a refusal ADDED to close a silent under-report.
AND ON THE WORKING-INTEREST ARM IT IS NOT A DATA GAP AT ALL, IT IS AN UNGUARDED HOLE - the single strongest ground for this guard, added 2026-08-17 after adversarial review pointed out the fill had understated its own case. ../workingInterestNetProfit joins scheduleC at /scheduleCNetProfit (scheduleC.xml:1625), as a Dependency OUTSIDE the /scheduleCs collection, i.e. AFTER /scheduleCs/*/netProfit (scheduleC.xml:1344) has already applied /scheduleCs/*/atRiskLimitationApplies. So a working-interest loss walks straight past the section 465 machinery that module ALREADY SHIPS, in a module where the at-risk cap is live on every other business. Refusing that arm needs no argument from missing intake: the limitation exists, is built, and was being bypassed.
THE SUCCESSOR IS NAMED AND IT IS SMALL, and the reason this unit did not take it is stated rather than implied. One attestation retires this guard - the negation of the instruction's second bullet, "all amounts invested in this activity are at risk", the Schedule C line 32a checkbox in Part I clothing - because a fully-at-risk filer needs no Form 6198 and the printed line 25 ("Add ROYALTY LOSSES from line 21 and rental real estate losses from line 22", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040se.pdf, page 1) says the loss is then deductible in full, with line 22 and Form 8582 deliberately not completed for royalty properties (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040se.pdf, page 8). WHAT THE SUCCESSOR OWES BESIDES THAT BOOLEAN, and this is why the boolean alone is not the fill: shipping it CERTIFIES the negative that flows today, and four surfaces have never been checked on a negative royalty net. (a) form4952:/investmentIncome reads /royaltyNetIncome into a line printed as "GROSS income from property held for investment" - this dictionary already feeds it a NET figure, and a negative addend on a gross-income line is a different question again. (b) interest.xml keys its NIIT refusal on /royaltyNetIncome and the sign of that key decides whether a royalty LOSS frees or holds the refusal. (c) the working-interest arm rides scheduleC line 31 into Schedule SE line 2 and into QBI, neither verified on a negative. (d) Schedule E lines 24, 25 and 26 split positives from losses on the printed form and this module assembles them as one sum. (e) eitc:/belowEitcInvestmentIncomeLimit reads /royaltyNetIncome into EITC Worksheet-1 line 10 at eitc.xml:2215 - ALREADY DISCHARGED, and listed anyway so the checklist is complete: that term is wrapped in GreaterOf(..., $0) and its own comment says why ("royaltyNetIncome is scoped >= 0 today; this future-proofs a royalty-loss scope"), so a negative contributes 0 there and nothing is wrong today. FIVE consumers, one of them already safe; (a) through (d) live in modules this unit does not own.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS THE INTAKE, NOT THE SHAPE, and the earlier phrasing here ("the return carries no way to tell them apart") was softer than the tree supports. The Form-6198-simplified pattern - a fullyAtRisk / allInvestmentAtRisk attestation feeding an atRiskLimitationApplies gate - SHIPS FIVE TIMES ALREADY, three of them in this very module: /rentalProperties/*/fullyAtRisk with /rentalProperties/*/amountAtRisk, /formK1s/*/fullyAtRisk with /formK1s/*/amountAtRisk, /writableEstateTrustFullyAtRisk with /writableEstateTrustAmountAtRisk, plus scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/writableAllInvestmentAtRisk and scheduleF:/writableScheduleFAllInvestmentAtRisk. Nothing about the shape is inexpressible. What is missing is the ROYALTY-SIDE intake and the five certifications above, and it is the certifications - not the boolean - that this unit could not honestly make from outside those modules.
COMPLETE-SAFE AND ADDITIVE. Gated on /claimsRoyaltyIncome, which is itself the IsComplete pattern, and /royaltyActivityNet is Complete 0 on every return with no royalty - so this resolves Complete false everywhere it does not fire. Measured on the materialized corpus: /royaltyActivityNet takes exactly four values across 969 scenarios (0.00 x 954, 10,000.00 x 10, 8,200.00 x 4, 7,000.00 x 1) and NOT ONE is negative, so no committed scenario changes submittability.
THE UNANSWERED-MID-ENTRY STATE, pinned, and the answer is better than the question assumed. /claimsRoyaltyIncome true with /writableRoyaltyIncome and /writableRoyaltyExpenses still blank makes /royaltyActivityNet Result.Incomplete (both are bare Writables consumed directly by its Subtract), so this guard is Incomplete too. The review expected that to carry into flow:/flowIsKnockedOut, because an Any over an Incomplete member is Incomplete - MEASURED, it does not: /flowIsKnockedOut carries its own <Placeholder><False/></Placeholder>, so a consumer reads Placeholder false and the knockout screen does not flicker while the filer is still typing. The membership therefore adds NO new class of unresolvability - the same blank amounts already made /royaltyNetIncome, /scheduleEPartINetIncome, /totalIncome and /agi Incomplete before this guard existed. DUAL-WIRED, unlike its sibling /knockoutRentalBuildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown, and the difference is the classification rather than a preference: that guard carries an "n/a" revisit trigger because its intake already ships, which is lint_dual_wiring exemption 1. This one has a live trigger - the at-risk attestation does NOT exist yet - so it is a scope refusal, it owes the filer a knockout SCREEN, and flow:/flowIsKnockedOut gains it in this same commit.

Fact.Name: The royalty amounts entered cover more than one royalty property
Fact.Description: Screen question, asked when the return reports royalty income: do the royalty income, expense and depletion amounts you entered come from more than one royalty property (more than one oil, gas or mineral property, copyright, patent, or name, image and likeness right)? Schedule E reports each royalty property in its own column, and several rules apply property by property: the percentage depletion limit on the taxable income from the property, the at-risk limit on each oil and gas or geothermal property, and the working interest routing. This return holds the royalty amounts as one combined activity, so it can apply those rules to one property only. Unanswered is read as one property.

Fact.Name: Knockout: more than one royalty property where a per-property rule changes the result
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You told us your royalty amounts come from more than one royalty property, and at least one of these applies: the royalty is from an oil, gas or geothermal property (percentage depletion is limited property by property), not all of the amount invested is at risk or you have not yet said whether it is (the at-risk limit applies to each oil and gas or geothermal property separately), or the royalty is a working interest. This return combines all royalty properties into one, so it cannot apply these per-property limits correctly.
Fires only when all three hold: a royalty is claimed (/claimsRoyaltyIncome), the filer answered Yes to /writableRoyaltyHasMultipleProperties, and at least one merge-sensitive condition holds — /royaltyIsOilGasGeothermalCompleteSafe true, /royaltyIsWorkingInterest true, or /writableRoyaltyAllInvestmentAtRisk not answered true. When none of those holds (several profitable copyright or patent royalties, all amounts at risk, no percentage depletion), the combined figures equal the sum of the columns and the return files. Every operand is complete-safe, so the fact is Complete false on every return that does not answer the question.

Fact.Name: Knockout: oil or gas percentage depletion may exceed the 65 percent taxable income limit
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. Your oil or gas royalty's percentage depletion is large compared with the taxable income on this return. Percentage depletion for oil and gas cannot be more than 65 percent of your taxable income figured without the depletion, and any amount over that limit carries to next year. This return cannot yet figure that limit.
Fires when a royalty is claimed (/claimsRoyaltyIncome), the royalty is oil or gas and not a geothermal deposit (/royaltyIsGeothermal false; a geothermal deposit is outside section 613A), /royaltyPercentageDepletion is the depletion Schedule E line 18 takes (it exceeds the answered cost depletion /writableRoyaltyDepletion, $0 when unanswered), and that percentage depletion is more than 65 percent of Form 1040 line 15 taxable income (taxCalculations:/taxableIncome).
WHY LINE 15 IS A SAFE STAND-IN. The limit is measured on taxable income computed WITHOUT the depletion and without the section 199A deduction. Line 15 is computed WITH both, and taking a deduction away never lowers taxable income, so the true base is at least line 15. When the percentage depletion is at most 65 percent of line 15 the limit cannot bind and the return files with the figure it has. When it is more, the limit may bind, and the return refuses rather than guess; some of those returns would be under the true limit, the over-refusal direction. No fact here is read by line 15, so reading it does not feed back into the computation it tests.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a rental property used as a home was rented fewer than 15 days
Fact.Description:
This property does not belong on Schedule E. You used it as a home and rented it out for fewer than 15 days, so the rent is not income and the rental expenses are not deducted: the Instructions for Schedule E say not to report the rental income or deduct any rental expenses. Remove it from your rental properties. If you itemize, enter its mortgage interest and real estate taxes on Schedule A as you would for any home you own.
Fires when a rental property's ../dwellingRentedUnder15DaysAsHome is true (Count over the collection, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome). A PERMANENT guard on the answers, not deferred work: every rental property listed prints on Schedule E, and a home rented fewer than 15 days is to be left off it, so a return that lists one contradicts itself. The printed line 2 count is FAIR rental days, while section 280A(g) counts days actually rented; a unit rented 15 days or more of which fewer than 15 were at a fair rental is caught too, the safe direction.

Fact.Name: Knockout: an itemizer's rental part of mortgage interest and taxes exceeds the rents of a home also rented
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You itemize, and for a rental property you also used as a home the expenses that are always deductible (the rental part of your mortgage interest and real estate taxes, with advertising, management fees and similar costs) are more than the rents. This return cannot yet figure the loss that leaves on Schedule E.
Fires when a rental property's ../worksheet51ItemizerLossRefused is true (Count over the collection, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome). A loss from the other expenses that are always deductible alone is figured and deducted in full outside the passive activity rules (../section469j10NonpassiveNet); what stays refused is only the itemizer whose Worksheet 5-1 lines 2a and 2b push line 2e above the rents, because the unit's net is figured without the itemize election.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a home also rented carries a prior-year passive loss its own income does not use up
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. A rental property you also used as a home carries an unallowed passive loss from an earlier year, and this year's net from the property does not use all of it. The part left over is still a passive loss, and this return cannot yet carry it with your other passive activities.
Fires when a rental property's ../section469j10PriorLossNotAbsorbed is true (Count over the collection, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome). A carried loss the unit's own income covers is allowed and the return files.

Fact.Name: You confirm you will itemize deductions on this return (Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1)
Fact.Description: Asked when a rental property you also used as a home has rental expenses above its rents. The order in which those expenses are deducted depends on whether you itemize: if you itemize, the rental part of your mortgage interest and real estate taxes is deducted first, in full; if you take the standard deduction, it is deducted only up to the rents left after the direct rental expenses. We show our recommendation (/worksheet51ItemizeRecommended, figured on your income without that property). Answer Yes to itemize or No to take the standard deduction. Your answer must match the deduction the return takes; if it does not, the return is refused until you change one of them (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51ElectionDisagreesWithReturn). This is the IRC 63(e) election to itemize, signified on the return. Unanswered leaves every limited Schedule E line of the unit Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Pub. 527 Line 2b Worksheet line 8: room under the $40,000 limit
Fact.Description: $40,000 ($20,000 married filing separately) less Line 2b Worksheet line 7, floored at $0. Line 7 is line 5 less line 6, which is the filer's personal state and local income or sales taxes, personal property taxes and personal real estate taxes, including the personal part of the dwelling unit's own taxes: Schedule A line 5d as entered (scheduleA:/scheduleALine5dStateAndLocalTaxes). Schedule A line 5b carries only the personal part of the unit's real estate taxes, as the worksheet's own Note says: the return adds it (/rentalPropertiesPersonalRealEstateTaxes, figured from the intakes and day counts, not from this worksheet). Incomplete while the filing status is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Total of the Worksheet 5-1 nets of the dwelling units used as a home
Fact.Description: The CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/section280ALimitedNet ($0 for a property the worksheet does not apply to), gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome; $0 on a return with no rental property. What those units add to Schedule E line 21, and so to AGI. Read by taxCalculations:/agiWithoutSection280ADwellingUnits.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the itemize answer for a home you also rent does not match the deduction the return takes
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You told us you will itemize (or take the standard deduction) so we could figure the rental deductions of a home you also rent, but the return takes the other deduction. Change your answer, or change your deductions (for example, choose to itemize on Schedule A line 18), so they match.
Fires when some rental property's /rentalProperties/*/worksheet51Applies is true and /writableWorksheet51ElectsToItemize disagrees with taxCalculations:/wantsStandardDeduction (Yes with the standard deduction taken, or No with itemized deductions taken). Incomplete while the answer is unanswered on such a return. A sink: it reads the final choice, which nothing in the worksheet reads, so there is no cycle.

Fact.Name: Knockout: an itemizer with a home they also rent, whose SALT MAGI is above the phase-down threshold
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You itemize, you rent out a home you also use and pay real estate taxes on it, and your income is above $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately). At that income the state and local tax limit is reduced, and the IRS worksheet for the rental part of those taxes does not reduce it, so this return cannot yet figure that part.
Fires when some rental property's /rentalProperties/*/worksheet51Line2bTaxesPresent is true, /writableWorksheet51ElectsToItemize is Yes and scheduleA:/saltMagi is above $500,000 ($250,000 married filing separately). Pub. 527's Line 2b Worksheet uses the flat $40,000 ($20,000) with no phase-down, while its own What's New and IRC 164(b)(7)(B) reduce the limit above the threshold; following the worksheet there would allow more rental taxes than the statute. A sink: it reads final MAGI.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a casualty or theft loss on a home you also rent
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You had a casualty or theft loss on a home you also rent out, whose rental expenses are more than its rents. The IRS worksheet for that loss needs a separate Form 4684 figured on your income without that home, which this return cannot yet prepare.
Fires when some rental property's /rentalProperties/*/worksheet51CasualtyRefused is true (Worksheet 5-1 applies and ../writableWorksheet51CasualtyOrTheftLoss is Yes). Incomplete while that question is unanswered on a worksheet unit.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a section 179 deduction on a home you also rent
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You elected a section 179 deduction for property of a home you also rent out, whose rental expenses are more than its rents. This return cannot yet fit that deduction into the order the IRS worksheet deducts those expenses in.
Fires when some rental property's /rentalProperties/*/worksheet51Section179Refused is true (Worksheet 5-1 applies and ../electsSection179). The worksheet here reads the depreciation before section 179, which keeps the Form 4562 line 11 business income limit cycle-free.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a rental building's MACRS recovery period is undetermined
Fact.Description:
Blocks submission when the return claims Schedule E rental income and ANY element has a positive building basis whose recovery period nothing on the return decides (Count(/rentalProperties/*/buildingRecoveryPeriodUnknown) > 0). See that fact for the argument; this one is the wiring.
WHAT IT CLOSES. Pub 946's GDS table gives residential rental property 27.5 years and nonresidential real property 39. Since the nonresidential-class fill the return can express both, but the class gate is complete-safe, so SILENCE picked 27.5 — a real over-deduction on a genuinely commercial building, in the taxpayer's favour, with no refusal and no warning. It was the largest of the ten silent-wrong-answer rows that fill found precisely because it fires on an unanswered question rather than on an unusual taxpayer.
WHY A REFUSAL IS THE FILL HERE, in a campaign whose whole point is to convert refusals into computations: the owner's goal statement ends "only refuse if there is not enough input facts", and this is that case exactly. The recovery period is not derivable from anything else the return carries — not from the rent, not from the basis, not from the expenses — so there is no computation to build. The remedy is an answer, and the answer already has a home (/rentalProperties/*/writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty ships).
SO THIS IS A DATA-COMPLETENESS GUARD, not a scope limit, and its sidecar revisit_trigger says so with an "n/a" — the /primaryFilerHasIncompleteFormW2s and /flowIncomplete class, the one class REFUSAL-VERDICTS.md entitles to stand permanently. That classification is what exempts it from the dual-wiring convention (scripts/lints/lint_dual_wiring.py exemption 1): there is no knockout SCREEN to route the filer to, because there is nothing unmodelled here — the return is simply not finished. flow.xml is deliberately untouched, and no flow:/flowIsKnockedOut membership is owed at integration. Every fixture in this unit asserts /flowIsKnockedOut unchanged to pin that.
NO VALUE MOVES. ../buildingDepreciation is not touched, so line 18 resolves to the same dollar it always did on every return in the corpus; what moves is submittability. The 87 committed scenarios and the node-test fixtures that carry a buildingBasis now ANSWER the attestation (residential, which is what each of their own stories describes), so they file exactly as before and the corpus states its class instead of inheriting it.
KNOWN AND NAMED: syndoc/demo_docs' rental profiles do NOT answer it and are therefore blocked. That is not collateral damage — profile-self-rental is that fill’s own fixture half, an office condo whose basis is sized off a 27.5-year life and published under a VERIFIED 5/5 banner. It cannot truthfully answer FALSE, and answering TRUE moves its published number from 8,760 to 6,177. The fixture is outside this module's boundary (syndoc/profiles.py is the generator of record), so this unit refuses it rather than quietly re-answering it, and the fill keeps its fixture half.

Fact.Name: A K-1 elects §179 without proven basis to absorb it (refusal flag)
Fact.Description: True when any /formK1s item passes through a section 179 deduction its answered basis cannot be shown to cover (Count(/formK1s/*/section179WithoutSufficientBasis) > 0). Keys /knockoutK1Section179Basis. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a K-1 section 179 deduction with no proven basis to absorb it
Fact.Description:
The return reports a Schedule K-1 box 12 section 179 deduction on a K-1 whose adjusted basis is unanswered, or is smaller than the box-1 loss plus that deduction. Section 704(d)/1366(d) allows the partner's losses and deduction items only up to basis, and when basis is short and more than one CATEGORY competes for it the partner's instructions require a pro rata allocation across categories. This dictionary wires exactly one loss class to /formK1s/*/basisAllowedLoss and holds no apportionment; deducting the section 179 amount in full would OVER-state the deduction, and silently dropping it would UNDER-state it with nothing on the return to show why. BLOCKS SUBMISSION instead. Only the filer can supply the missing fact (their adjusted basis) or accept that the deduction does not fit.
THE VALUE STILL COMPUTES — this is the /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD shape, a refusal without an Incomplete cascade — and /formK1s/*/section179ColumnJ independently routes $0 to Schedule E column (j) whenever this flag is up, so the printed return neither claims the deduction nor pretends the question was never asked.
ONE CAVEAT ON "BLOCKS SUBMISSION": the BlockSubmissionOnTrue below is one half of the wiring; the other is membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut, which the unit that landed this could not add (flow.xml outside its module boundary) and which the integration adds. Until it lands the fixtures assert /flowIsKnockedOut Placeholder false, and this fact's own true/false pair is what pins the refusal.

Fact.Name: A K-1 elects §179 on a PTP whose items may be passive (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
True when ANY /formK1s item raises ../section179OnPtp (Count(/formK1s/*/section179OnPtp) > 0). Keys /knockoutK1Section179OnPtp. Complete-safe: false when no K-1 is claimed.
THE QUANTIFIER IS "ANY", and it is the right one: one K-1 the graph cannot route refuses the RETURN, because Schedule E line 32 is a single total. A sibling K-1 that routes cleanly does not clear it, and a sibling that refuses does not taint one that routes — the per-item flag decides per item and this fact only asks whether at least one is up. Pinned by node test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-two-k1s-one-refuses-the-return, where one PTP raises the flag and the other does not.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a section 179 deduction on a PTP K-1 whose items may be passive
Fact.Description:
The return reports a Schedule K-1 box 12 section 179 deduction on a K-1 whose item D ("Check if this is a publicly traded partnership (PTP)") is checked, and the filer has NOT answered that they materially participated. Box 12 has three destinations and item D picks the third: "if the box in item D of Schedule K-1 is checked, report this amount following the rules for PTPs under Publicly traded partnerships, earlier." Those rules apply section 469 SEPARATELY per PTP instead of through the cross-activity Form 8582 pool.
NARROWED, and the correction is worth stating in full because this Description used to assert the opposite. The per-PTP section 469 machinery is NO LONGER MISSING: /formK1s/*/ptpSection469Net ships, with its overall-gain and overall-loss routing, its carry-out and its investment-income leg. What is missing is narrower — that regime carries BOX 1 ONLY, so a box-12 section 179 share still has no place inside step 1's combination. What remains is /formK1s/*/ptpSection179InCombination, which is not built.
AND THE POPULATION SHRANK. The rules this fork points at govern income, gains and losses from passive activities "held through each PTP you owned during the tax year". A materially participating partner holds no passive activity in the PTP, so the numbered steps do not reach that K-1 and the box-12 sentence governs directly: an amount that "isn't a passive activity deduction" is reported in column (j) of Schedule E line 28. That population now COMPUTES (node test scheduleE/k1-179-ptp-material-participation-flows-column-j). Two populations still refuse: the affirmatively PASSIVE PTP, whose share belongs in the combination this dictionary cannot yet form (and which /knockoutK1Section179PassiveOrAtRiskLimited independently refuses), and the PTP whose participation question is UNANSWERED, where IRC 469(h)(2) makes the module's usual nonpassive default presumptively wrong in the taxpayer-favourable direction. Reporting either in column (j) anyway would apply the wrong section 469 regime; dropping it would UNDER-state the deduction invisibly. BLOCKS SUBMISSION instead.
THE VALUE STILL COMPUTES (the /knockoutK1QualifiedPtpAmountWithoutItemD shape, no Incomplete cascade) and /formK1s/*/section179ColumnJ routes $0 while this flag is up.
BOTH HALVES OF THE WIRING ARE IN PLACE: the BlockSubmissionOnTrue below, and membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut at dictionary/ty2025/flow.xml:578.
DISCHARGED. NARROWED TO ONE POPULATION, and the paragraph above headed "AND THE POPULATION SHRANK" is the one to read against this note. Of the two populations it says still refuse, the affirmatively PASSIVE PTP now COMPUTES: its box-12 share is a term of step 1's combination (/formK1s/*/ptpSection179Allowed into /formK1s/*/ptpCurrentYearNetAfterSection179), and the overall result reaches Schedule E column (k), Form 4952 line 4h and next year's carry-in from the post-section-179 twin. The successor contract that paragraph names, /formK1s/*/ptpSection179InCombination, is DISCHARGED.
WHAT THIS GUARD STILL REFUSES is the second population and only it: an item-D PTP whose /formK1s/*/materiallyParticipated is UNANSWERED. IRC 469(h)(2) treats no interest in a limited partnership as a limited partner as one in which the taxpayer materially participates except as regulations provide, so for a PTP the module's "unanswered means nonpassive" default is presumptively wrong and wrong in the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE direction; answering the question - either way - now files. NARROWED AGAIN TO ONE CELL, and the paragraph above is the one this note answers. The presumption is built: a LIMITED partner's item-D PTP with an unanswered participation answer is now PASSIVE (/formK1s/*/materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption), so /formK1s/*/appliesPtpSection469 is true, the box-12 share computes through the post-section-179 step-1 chain, and that cell FILES. WHAT STILL REFUSES: an item-D PTP whose item G says GENERAL PARTNER, whose participation answer is missing, and which elects a box-12 amount. That is a DATA-COMPLETENESS refusal and it is permanent — 469(h)(2) carves general partners out by name, so no presumption resolves the regime and the box-12 fork has nothing to choose on. Only the taxpayer's answer resolves it. A CHOICE AND NOT A NECESSITY, said so the verdict is not read as stronger than it is: the SAME missing answer is DEFAULTED one field away — the box-1 leg files on this very cell — and what this guard declines is extending that taxpayer-favourable default to the section 179 share, which would diverge only on an overall LOSS, on Form 4952 line 4h (/formK1s/*/ptpNonpassiveGainInInvestmentIncome) and in the Form 4562 line-11 business-income cone. Witnessed at tests/nodes/ty2025/scheduleE/k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-general-partner-still-refuses, with the elects-nothing boundary at k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-general-partner-no-box12-files-nonpassive and the freed cell at k1-ptp-participation-unanswered-limited-partner-presumed-passive. This refusal is a correct refusal. Nothing further is owed at this path.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part II total partnership / S-corporation income (line 32 -> Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 32 ("Total partnership and S corporation income or (loss). Combine lines 30 and 31"). AGGREGATE over /formK1s: line 32 = CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart) (each K-1's nonpassive income or -nonpassive-allowed-loss) + /k1PassiveNet (the pooled passive net, Form 8582) + /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated (the pooled ratable passive suspension). Gated on /claimsK1Income (0 for no K-1, so every non-K-1 scenario stays byte-identical). A NONPASSIVE K-1 profit/loss flows through partIINonpassivePart; a PASSIVE K-1 flows through the pool (income in full; a loss allowed to the extent passive income elsewhere absorbs it, the residue in /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated). The fourth summand is /k1GuaranteedPayments (boxes 4a/4b, always nonpassive col (k), complete-safe 0; Result.Incomplete — refusal — when GP lacks the box-14 SE assessment). Part II summand of Schedule E line 41 -> Schedule 1 line 5 -> Form 1040 line 8. interpretation:provisional. Result rounded to whole dollars.
Line 32 also adds the separately labelled line-28 amounts /scheduleEPartIIPriorYearBasisAtRiskLoss, /scheduleEPartIIPriorYearPassiveLossNotReportedForm8582, /scheduleEPartIIUPENonpassiveLoss, and /scheduleEPartIIUPEPassiveLoss. These rows are not /formK1s items and are never netted against current-year K-1 amounts. Passive UPE with an unanswered or Yes Form-8582 attestation remains Incomplete because the current model has no partnership/activity association to add it to the correct passive pool; see the successor below.
Line 32 also subtracts /k1PtpSection1231AllowedScheduleELossTotal: a publicly traded partnership's Schedule E loss allowed to the extent of the same partnership's box 10 net section 1231 gain, which is reported on Form 4797 (partner instructions' PTP example: 7,200 of a 12,000 loss allowed in column (g)). $0 on every return without such a PTP. Line 32 also adds /k1PtpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncomeTotal: a publicly traded partnership's Schedule E-side income against which the same partnership's passive box 10 loss is allowed on Form 4797, printed as passive income in column (h), while the nonpassive remainder stays in the K-1's partIINonpassivePart (partner instructions' PTP example: 3,500 in column (h), 4,500 in column (k)). $0 on every return without such a PTP.

Fact.Name: Has Schedule E Part III estate / trust K-1 income or loss
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports income or loss from an estate or trust on Schedule E Part III (line 33) via a beneficiary's Schedule K-1 (Form 1041). Gate for the Part III K-1 intake (twin of /writableHasK1Income and /hasScheduleERentalIncome). When true, /writableEstateTrustK1Income carries the K-1 income or (loss) and /writableEstateTrustK1MateriallyParticipated records the material-participation flag.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E Part III estate / trust K-1 income
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /writableHasEstateTrustK1 is answered AND true (IsComplete pattern, twin of /claimsK1Income). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so returns without an estate / trust K-1 still resolve and /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome is 0. Gates the Part III net so every non-K-1 scenario keeps /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome Complete-0 byte-identical.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 9 directly apportioned deductions (codes A, B and C)
Fact.Description:
The total of the box 9 "Directly apportioned deductions" rows on THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) whose printed letter code is A (depreciation), B (depletion) or C (amortization), the three codes the form's own back-of-form routing table sends to Schedule E line 33 column (c) or column (e). The box is recorded as a row list and every row of it is read, however many the K-1 lists; this fact sums a per-row part over the rows: a row contributes its amount only when the row's code AND its amount are both answered and the code is one of the three, and $0 otherwise. That makes the whole fact COMPLETE-SAFE — an item that answered no box 9 row contributes a Complete $0 and the aggregate over the collection stays Complete.
NON NEGATIVE, a magnitude. It is a DEDUCTION, so ../estateTrustK1ItemNet SUBTRACTS it; nothing adds it. A code the form does not list here (there is no other code in box 9) leaves the row at $0 rather than silently deducting an amount whose treatment is unknown.
WHY THE CODE IS TESTED AND NOT ASSUMED: box 9 is a coded row box, so a row is not always depreciation. Keying on the code is the same shape /formK1s/*/writableQualifiedPtpIncomeOrLoss uses for the partnership K-1's coded boxes.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 9 directly apportioned deductions (codes A, B and C): this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /form1041K1s/*/directlyApportionedDeductionEntries as /form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box9DirectlyApportionedDeductions reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is A or B or C, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's Schedule E Part III share, signed and complete safe
Fact.Description:
The SIGNED Schedule E Part III share this one Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) reports: box 5 (other portfolio and nonbusiness income) plus box 6 (ordinary business income) plus box 7 (net rental real estate income) plus box 8 (other rental income), LESS ../estateTrustK1Box9DirectlyApportionedDeductions. Positive is income, negative is a loss. Each of the four income boxes is taken through an IsComplete Switch defaulting to $0, so an item that answered none of them contributes a Complete $0 and the aggregate over /form1041K1s stays Complete on every return.
THE FOUR BOXES ARE EXACTLY THE ONES THE FORM ROUTES TO LINE 33, and no others. The back of Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) sends box 5 to "Schedule E, line 33, column (f)", boxes 6, 7 and 8 to "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)", and box 9 codes A, B and C to "Schedule E, line 33, column (c) or (e)". Boxes 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4a, 4b, 4c, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 are routed by that same table to OTHER forms (Form 1040 lines 2b/3a/3b, Schedule D, Schedule A, Form 6251, Schedule 1, Form 1040 line 26) and are deliberately not summed here: adding any of them would report the same money twice.
THE PASSIVE / NONPASSIVE SPLIT IS NOT MADE PER ITEM, and that is the limit this unit did not close. The form's own table says "column (d) or (f)" — the choice turns on the beneficiary's participation in the entity's activity, which no printed box of the K-1 supplies. This module still classifies the whole Part III share with the single return-level /estateTrustK1LossIsPassive, so a return holding one passive and one nonpassive estate K-1 is classified by the answer the filer gave once. That is unchanged from before this edit; what changed is only where the DOLLARS come from. Closing it needs a per item participation intake on /form1041K1s.

Fact.Name: Was any Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) Part III income or deduction box actually answered
Fact.Description:
True when at least one item of /form1041K1s has answered at least one of the boxes that make up its Schedule E Part III share: box 5, box 6, box 7, box 8, or the amount of any box 9 row (../directlyApportionedDeductionAmountAnswered, over scheduleE:/form1041K1s/*/directlyApportionedDeductionEntries). Computed as CollectionSize(Filter(/form1041K1s)) greater than 0, the whole of it inside an IsComplete Switch on the collection itself defaulting to FALSE, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete false rather than Placeholder and every Part III fact downstream stays Complete. That guard is the same IsComplete on a collection root that /scheduleELine23aTotalRents and its siblings use for /formK1s and /rentalProperties.
THIS IS THE "WAS THE SOURCE ANSWERED" PREDICATE brief rule 3 requires, and it is an IsComplete on the RAW INTAKE BOXES, never on a complete-safe alias. ../estateTrustK1ItemNet is complete-safe by construction, so IsComplete on it is always true and would silently retire the filer's attestation on every return that merely recorded an estate or trust K-1's identity boxes. The same trap is documented on /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered, which this fact mirrors.
A K-1 RECORDED FOR ITS IDENTITY BOXES ALONE DOES NOT TRIP IT: a beneficiary who typed the trust's name and EIN but no dollar box still falls back to /writableEstateTrustK1Income, which is the byte-identity guarantee for the two committed fixtures that record exactly that.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 answered the amount of a box 9 row
Fact.Description: True when at least one row of ../directlyApportionedDeductionEntries (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 9, directly apportioned deductions) has its amount answered, whatever its code. The box 9 term of /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered, the "was the source answered" predicate: an IsComplete on the RAW row amount, never on a complete safe alias. Complete false when the row table is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III estate and trust share, footed from the K-1 rows when they are answered
Fact.Description:
The SIGNED Schedule E Part III share the whole /estateTrust chain computes from: CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1ItemNet) when /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered is true, and the filer's single attestation /writableEstateTrustK1Income otherwise. Positive is income, negative is a loss.
THE ATTESTATION IS THE FALLBACK, NOT A SECOND TERM. It is never added to the rows: a beneficiary who both enters a K-1's boxes AND types a bottom line would otherwise state the same money twice, which is the defect this edit exists to remove. Every committed scenario and every pre-existing fixture reaches the fallback arm, so the corpus is byte-identical.
WHAT NOW READS IT. All five places that read /writableEstateTrustK1Income before 2026-08-30 read this fact instead: /estateTrustK1Loss (the loss magnitude that enters the section 465 at-risk step), /estateTrustNonpassivePart (twice) and /estatePassiveNet (twice). Because the rebody is at this ONE point, everything downstream is unchanged in shape — the four line-34 column totals, the staged lines 35 and 36, line 37 (/scheduleEPartIIINetIncome), the section 8582 pool membership and the line-6 MAGI decomposition all still reconstruct ONE signed share, so the printed Part III still foots: column (d) plus (f) less (c) less (e) is line 37.
MULTIPLE K-1s NOW ADD UP, which is the beneficiary-facing point: before this date the graph held one scalar and a filer with two estate or trust K-1s could not state them both.
LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. (a) The passive / nonpassive classification is still the single return-level /estateTrustK1LossIsPassive, so a return mixing a passive and a nonpassive estate K-1 is classified once — see ../estateTrustK1ItemNet. (b) The per item printed line 33 columns (c), (d), (e) and (f) (/form1041K1s/*/writableScheduleELine33ColumnCPassiveLossAllowed and its three siblings) stay PRINT ONLY and are NOT read here on purpose: column (c) is the filer's ALREADY Form 8582 limited figure, and feeding it into this module's own section 469 pool would limit it twice, the identical trap /farmRentalPassiveNet documents for the Form 4835 loss arm. A filer who fills both the boxes and the columns can therefore print a line 33 row that disagrees with the line 34 totals; that calls for a validations.xml reconciliation, which is outside this module. (c) The /claimsEstateTrustK1 gate is unchanged and still governs: a filer who records a K-1's boxes but never answers /writableHasEstateTrustK1 still resolves $0 through every gated arm of the chain. That is the status quo for this collection, disclosed rather than built over, because widening the gate would change the completeness of the Part III chain on returns this unit did not audit.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust K-1 income or (loss) (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041))
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 34 column (d)/(f) (income) or column (c)/(e) (loss): the beneficiary's share of income OR (loss) from the estate or trust K-1 (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041)). SIGNED: a positive value is income, a NEGATIVE value is a loss. Consulted only when /claimsEstateTrustK1 is true. A NONPASSIVE share (materially participated) flows to line 34b column (e) (loss) / line 34a column (f) (other income); a PASSIVE share flows to column (c) (loss) / column (d) (income). Line 35 sums the income columns (d)+(f), line 36 the loss columns (c)+(e), and line 37 combines them, so the signed figure flows to line 37 regardless of the passive/nonpassive split for INCOME; for a LOSS the split is decisive (a passive loss is suspended). Unlike a partnership / S-corp K-1 (Part II), a beneficiary's estate/trust K-1 carries NO §704(d)/§1366(d) basis ceiling at the beneficiary level (the entity computed the share), so income/loss is taken as reported on the K-1.
DEMOTED TO A FALLBACK. Nothing in the graph reads this attestation directly any more. The /estateTrust chain reads /estateTrustK1IncomeAmount, which is CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1ItemNet) when any item of /form1041K1s answered a Part III box (boxes 5, 6, 7, 8 or a box 9 amount) and THIS attestation otherwise. It is never ADDED to the rows, so a filer who both records a K-1 and types a bottom line does not state the same money twice; and because every committed scenario answers no /form1041K1s box, every one of them still resolves through this fact and the corpus is byte-identical.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust K-1 gross farming and fishing income (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F)
Fact.Description:
Box 14 code F of this beneficiary's Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), as declared: the gross farming and fishing income the fiduciary separately stated. The THIRD of the three K-1 legs Schedule E line 42 names, after the partnership box 14 code B (/formK1s/*/writableGrossFarmingFishingIncome) and the S-corporation box 17 code AN (/formK1s/*/writableFarmingFishingIncomeSCorp).
A SCALAR, NOT A FIELD ON /formK1s, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE MODELLING DECISION. Four earlier passes prescribed the opposite — "one estateOrTrust member on /k1EntityTypeOptions plus one intake field" — and building it that way would have MISFILED THE INCOME. /formK1s is the Schedule E PART II collection ("partnership / S-corporation Schedule K-1s reported on Schedule E Part II (line 28)", its own Description), and /k1EntityTypeOptions says of its members that "Both flow box-1 ordinary business income identically to Schedule E Part II line 28". An ITEM in that collection IS a line-28 claim, so a beneficiary's K-1 recorded there would route Part III income onto Part II — and no gate on this field would undo it, because the misrouting happens on the item. A Form 1041 K-1 is Schedule E PART III, line 33, which this dictionary already models as SCALARS (/writableHasEstateTrustK1, /claimsEstateTrustK1, /writableEstateTrustK1Income), with no Part III collection anywhere. This fact is the fourth scalar in that cluster and sits beside them deliberately.
WHAT THE FIGURE IS, from the instruction rather than inferred: "Code F. Gross farming and fishing income. The amount of farming and fishing income is included in box 6. This income is separately stated to help determine if you are subject to a penalty for underpayment of estimated tax. Report the amount of gross farming and fishing income on Schedule E (Form 1040), Supplemental Income and Loss, line 42."
IT IS A CARVE-OUT OF MONEY THIS GRAPH ALREADY HOLDS, which is the disclosure that matters most and which no earlier pass could make. Box 6 is "Ordinary business income", routed by the K-1's own page-2 map to "Schedule E, line 33, column (d) or (f)" — i.e. to the amount /writableEstateTrustK1Income carries. So this is NOT new money: it is a SUBSET of a Part III figure already in the graph, separately stated for one purpose. Line 42 is not a summand of line 41, so nothing double-counts today; a consumer that ever adds this to an income total rather than to a line-42 reconciliation would be double-counting, and this paragraph is the warning.
THREE PRINTED SPELLINGS, THREE FORMS, NOT SMOOTHED OVER. The 1065 instruction says "Gross farming OR fishing income", the 1120-S instruction says "Farming and fishing income" with no "gross", and this one says "Gross farming and fishing income". Each fact's Name follows its own source. Nothing downstream turns on the difference — line 42 collects all three as items of information — but a successor comparing the intakes should know the asymmetry is the IRS's and not a transcription slip.
SIGN: unfloored, for the reason the partnership twin records at length — no floor is printed at this intake, on the K-1, in its instructions, or at Schedule E line 42, and the one nearby printed floor (Schedule SE line 15) governs a different composite downstream.
ONE LIMITATION INHERITED, NOT INTRODUCED, and disclosed because Pub. 505's bullet is plural-capable ("your share of the gross farming income from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust"): the Part III scalar model collapses MULTIPLE estate/trust K-1s into one figure, so a beneficiary of two trusts adds their box 14 code F amounts by hand. That is the existing shape of /writableEstateTrustK1Income and every other Part III scalar; making Part III a collection is a restructuring unit, deliberately ruled out here.
Consulted only when /claimsEstateTrustK1 is true. UNANSWERED IS UNANSWERED — the complete-safe default lives on /estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome.
DEMOTED TO A FALLBACK. /estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome now reads CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome) whenever any item of /form1041K1s carries an answered box 14 row coded F (/estateTrustK1Box14CodeFAnswered), and THIS attestation only otherwise. It is never ADDED to the rows, so a beneficiary who both records a K-1's box 14 and types a bottom line does not state the same money twice. The plural limitation this Description recorded — that the Part III scalar model collapses several estate or trust K-1s into one figure, so a beneficiary of two trusts adds their code F amounts by hand — is now CLOSED on the rows arm: /form1041K1s is a collection and the CollectionSum adds them. It still governs the fallback arm. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 14 code F gross farm and fishing income
Fact.Description:
The total of the box 14 "Other information" rows on THIS Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) whose printed letter code is F, the code the form's own back of form routing table sends to Schedule E line 42. The box is recorded as a row list and every row of it is read, however many the K-1 lists; this fact sums a per-row part over the rows: a row contributes its amount only when the row's code AND its amount are both answered and the code is F, and $0 otherwise.
