That makes the whole fact COMPLETE SAFE, so an item that answered no box 14 row contributes a Complete $0 and the aggregate over /form1041K1s stays Complete on every return.
WHY THE CODE IS TESTED AND NOT ASSUMED: box 14 is a coded row box carrying at least the codes A (tax exempt interest), B (foreign taxes), C (qualified rehabilitation expenditures), D (basis of energy property), E (net investment income), F (this one) and G (foreign trading gross receipts), each of which the routing table sends somewhere else entirely. The first row is not always code F. A row coded anything else contributes $0 here rather than moving an amount whose destination is another form. This is the same code-keyed shape ../estateTrustK1Box9DirectlyApportionedDeductions uses for box 9.
GROSS, and NOT a summand of any income total. Schedule E line 42 is a reconciliation line the form does not combine into line 41, so this figure is an item of information: it is a carve out of money box 6 already reported, and adding it to an income total would double count.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1's box 14 code F gross farm and fishing income: this row's part
Fact.Description: One row of /form1041K1s/*/otherInformationEntries as /form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome reads it: this row's amount when the row's code is F, both the code and the amount are answered; otherwise $0. Complete on every row, because the code and amount tests open on IsComplete, so the reader over the row table is Complete once the table is answered.

Fact.Name: Was a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F slot actually answered
Fact.Description:
True when at least one item of /form1041K1s has a box 14 row whose CODE is answered and equal to F and whose AMOUNT is answered. Computed as CollectionSize(Filter(/form1041K1s)) greater than 0, the whole of it inside an IsComplete Switch on the collection itself defaulting to FALSE, so a return that never opened the estate or trust K-1 section resolves Complete false rather than Placeholder and every line 42 fact downstream stays Complete. That guard is the same IsComplete on a collection root /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered uses, and it is required because /form1041K1s is absent from almost every fixture.
THIS IS THE "WAS THE SOURCE ANSWERED" PREDICATE brief rule 3 requires for the demotion of /writableEstateTrustK1GrossFarmingFishingIncome, and it is an IsComplete on the RAW INTAKE ROWS, never on a complete safe alias. ../estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome is complete safe by construction, so IsComplete on it is always true and would silently retire the filer's attestation on every return that merely recorded an estate or trust K-1's identity boxes. The same trap is documented on /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered and /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered, which this fact mirrors.
A K-1 RECORDED WITHOUT A CODE F ROW DOES NOT TRIP IT: a beneficiary whose trust reported box 14 codes A and E only still falls back to the attestation, which is right because the trust separately stated no farm or fishing figure at all.

Fact.Name: This estate or trust K-1 has an answered box 14 code F row
Fact.Description: True when at least one row of ../otherInformationEntries (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14, other information) has its code answered as F and its amount answered (../otherInformationEntries/*/isAnsweredCodeFRow). The per K-1 term of /estateTrustK1Box14CodeFAnswered. Complete false when the row table is unanswered or empty.

Fact.Name: This Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 row is an answered code F row
Fact.Description: True when this row's code is answered as F (gross farm and fishing income) and its amount is answered; otherwise False. Read by ../../../hasAnsweredCodeFOtherInformationRow.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust K-1 gross farming and fishing income (box 14 code F), complete-safe (exported, unwired)
Fact.Description:
/writableEstateTrustK1GrossFarmingFishingIncome when the return claims an estate/trust K-1 AND the box is answered, else $0, Rounded — the estate/trust leg of the farming and fishing figure Schedule E line 42 reconciles, and the third sibling of /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome (partnership) and /k1FarmingFishingIncomeSCorp (S corporation).
FOOTED FROM THE K-1 ROWS SINCE. The first arm is CollectionSum(/form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome), taken whenever the return claims an estate or trust K-1 AND at least one item of /form1041K1s carries an answered box 14 row coded F (/estateTrustK1Box14CodeFAnswered). The filer's single attestation /writableEstateTrustK1GrossFarmingFishingIncome is the FALLBACK behind that predicate, never a second term, so a beneficiary who records the box and also types the bottom line states the money once. A beneficiary of TWO trusts can now state both code F amounts, which the scalar could not hold.
THE PARAGRAPH THIS REPLACES said there was no Part III collection and so no per item alias was needed. /form1041K1s exists (it was wired into Part III on the same date), so the per item alias now exists too and is the code keyed ../estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome, exactly the shape the partnership and S corporation legs use.
THE /claimsEstateTrustK1 GATE IS UNCHANGED and still governs BOTH arms: a filer who records a K-1's box 14 but never answers /writableHasEstateTrustK1 still resolves $0. That is the status quo for this collection, disclosed rather than built over, because widening the gate would change the completeness of facts this unit did not audit.
WHAT CONSUMES IT: /scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation, Schedule E line 42, which since 2026-08-07 adds all four printed legs. The paragraph below is the pre 2026-08-07 record of why it once consumed nothing. Schedule E line 42 stays a filer attestation (/scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation) until ALL FOUR of its legs exist, because a line that computes some legs and attests the rest is a figure that looks derived and is not . This is the LAST of the three K-1 legs; with Form 4835 line 7 already shipping as form4835:/form4835GrossFarmRentalIncome, all four now exist as computed facts and the wiring unit is unblocked. Exported so the printed line's own summand is nameable.
THE $0 DEFAULT IS SAFE FOR THE SAME REASON IT IS SAFE ON BOTH TWINS: nothing computes tax, AGI or any threshold from this figure, so a blank box 14 code F contributes 0 to a total nobody yet reads. Whoever wires line 42 inherits the question of whether a blank code F on a farming trust's K-1 should be ASKED rather than defaulted — the same open question the 1120-S leg recorded. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This Form 1041 K-1's gross farming and fishing income (box 14 code F), a loss read as $0
Fact.Description: ../estateTrustK1Box14GrossFarmingFishingIncome floored at $0: Publication 505 counts income (not loss) amounts document by document.

Fact.Name: Estate or trust K-1 gross farming and fishing income, the total of the income amounts only
Fact.Description: /estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome with each Form 1041 K-1 row floored at $0 before the sum (and the single attested figure floored at $0): the estate and trust term of the gross farming or fishing income test, which counts income (not loss) amounts.

Fact.Name: Materially participated in the estate / trust activity
Fact.Description: True when the taxpayer MATERIALLY PARTICIPATED in the estate / trust activity within the meaning of §469(h) — the activity is then NONPASSIVE (income flows to Schedule E line 34a column (f) "Other income from Schedule K-1"; a loss to line 34b column (e)); when false or unanswered the activity is PASSIVE (income to column (d), loss to column (c) — and a passive loss is limited by §469). For estate/trust INCOME the flag does NOT change the result, because line 35 sums BOTH column (d) (passive income) and column (f) (other/nonpassive income), so the income reaches line 35 / line 37 identically either way. It is decisive for a LOSS (the §469 passive-loss limitation suspends a passive loss). UNANSWERED ⇒ NONPASSIVE (the loss flows); a PASSIVE loss must EXPLICITLY set this false. interpretation:provisional (supplied as a direct taxpayer flag; the §469 material-participation tests are not modeled).

Fact.Name: Estate or trust K-1: prior-year unallowed passive loss carried into 2025
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "How much of your passive loss from this estate or trust was not allowed in earlier years and carried forward to 2025?" HELP TEXT: the prior-year unallowed loss from your 2024 Form 8582 worksheets for this activity; leave blank if none. ASKED WHEN: the estate or trust K-1 is passive (you did not materially participate). UNANSWERED POSTURE: $0. VALIDATION: not less than zero. WHAT IT FEEDS: /estatePassiveNet (Form 8582 Part V column (c)).

Fact.Name: Estate or trust K-1 prior-year unallowed passive loss (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableEstateTrustK1PriorYearUnallowedPassiveLoss when answered, floored at $0; $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust K-1 loss magnitude (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) loss)
Fact.Description: The MAGNITUDE of the current-year estate / trust K-1 loss = max(0, −/writableEstateTrustK1Income): the loss expressed as a POSITIVE amount (Schedule E line 34b columns (c)/(e)). 0 for a K-1 income share. Gated on /claimsEstateTrustK1 so a return with no estate / trust K-1 resolves Complete 0. Because it is 0 for every income case, the passive-suspended-loss fact resolves 0 there too.

Fact.Name: Fully at risk for the estate / trust activity (§465; no Form 6198 needed)
Fact.Description: True when the beneficiary is FULLY at risk for the estate/trust activity within the meaning of IRC §465 — the entire estate/trust K-1 loss survives the at-risk step (subject only to the downstream §469 passive limit). When FALSE, the simplified amount at risk (/writableEstateTrustAmountAtRisk, Form 6198 line 20) caps the deductible loss at Form 6198 line 21. When UNANSWERED, the activity is treated as FULLY AT RISK. Twin of /writableK1FullyAtRisk. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Amount at risk in the estate / trust activity (§465; Form 6198 line 20)
Fact.Description: The beneficiary's amount at risk in the estate/trust activity from the SIMPLIFIED computation (Form 6198 Part IV line 20), entered as not less than zero. Consulted ONLY when /writableEstateTrustFullyAtRisk is answered AND false; otherwise never read (may be left unanswered). Twin of /writableK1AmountAtRisk. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: The §465 at-risk limitation applies to the estate / trust loss (Form 6198 required)
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when /writableEstateTrustFullyAtRisk is answered AND false. When true OR unanswered (IsComplete false), resolves false and NO at-risk limitation applies. Inverted-IsComplete twin of /k1AtRiskLimitationApplies.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust loss allowed by the §465 at-risk limitation (Form 6198 line 21)
Fact.Description: The portion of the estate/trust K-1 loss (/estateTrustK1Loss) deductible after the §465 at-risk limitation (Form 6198 Part IV line 21): the SMALLER of the loss or the amount at risk (/writableEstateTrustAmountAtRisk) — but ONLY when the at-risk limitation applies (/estateTrustAtRiskLimitationApplies). When fully at risk OR unanswered, this equals the full estate/trust loss (the behavior, byte-identical). There is NO basis step at the beneficiary level, so at-risk is applied directly to the K-1 loss. This at-risk-allowed loss is what then flows to the §469 step (nonpassive: flows in full; passive: enters the pool).

Fact.Name: Estate / trust loss suspended by the §465 at-risk limitation (carryover, output only)
Fact.Description: The portion of the estate/trust K-1 loss DISALLOWED this year by the §465 at-risk limitation = /estateTrustK1Loss − /estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss (Form 6198 loss − line 21). Under §465(a)(2) this carries to the first succeeding year; this single-year demo REPORTS it but does not apply it to a future year. DISTINCT from the §469 passive-suspended loss. 0 whenever fully at risk, for an income share, and no K-1.

Fact.Name: The estate / trust K-1 loss is a §469 passive-activity loss (not materially participated)
Fact.Description: Gate: true only when /writableEstateTrustK1MateriallyParticipated is answered AND false — the taxpayer did NOT materially participate, so the activity is PASSIVE and the loss is subject to the §469 passive-activity-loss limitation. When the flag is true OR unanswered (IsComplete false), this resolves false and the loss is NONPASSIVE (no §469 limit — the safe default; a scenario leaving it unanswered is treated as nonpassive and the loss flows). A PASSIVE loss must EXPLICITLY set the flag false. Inverted-IsComplete pattern (twin of /k1LossIsPassive). THE TWIN HAS DIVERGED and this fact deliberately did not follow it. /formK1s/*/lossIsPassive is now Not(/formK1s/*/materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption), which applies IRC 469(h)(2)'s limited-partner presumption to an item-D PTP. There is no item D and no item G on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041), so the presumption's scope gate has nothing to read here and the estate/trust K-1 keeps the plain inverted-IsComplete default. Naming the divergence so a reader does not take "twin" as a promise the two still agree.

Fact.Name: Estate / trust K-1 loss suspended by the §469 passive-activity limitation (Form 8582 carryover)
Fact.Description: The estate / trust K-1 loss SUSPENDED this year by the §469 passive-activity-loss limitation = /estateTrustK1Loss when /estateTrustK1LossIsPassive (PASSIVE activity — not materially participated), else 0. A passive estate/trust K-1 loss does NOT qualify for the rental-real-estate $25,000 special allowance (Form 8582 Part II is rental real estate with ACTIVE participation ONLY — a beneficiary of an estate or trust cannot use it); it is allowed only against passive INCOME, and with NO passive income in scope it is FULLY suspended and carries forward (§469(b)). The authoritative suspended amount for the §469 carryforward is the ratable /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated (passive income from OTHER activities absorbs part of this loss); this isolated figure is superseded. This fact is retained for continuity and equals /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated whenever no passive income nets against it. 0 for a NONPASSIVE loss, an income share, and no K-1.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III NONPASSIVE half of line 37 (the estate/trust K-1 amount outside the §8582 pool)
Fact.Description:
The part of Schedule E Part III line 37 that is NOT the §8582 passive pool: the estate/trust K-1's nonpassive income or allowed nonpassive loss. Income (≥ 0) flows in full when the K-1 is NONPASSIVE and contributes 0 here when it is passive (it enters the pool through /estatePassiveNet instead); a NONPASSIVE loss flows as −/estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss; a PASSIVE loss is 0 here, again because the pool carries it. Gated on /claimsEstateTrustK1, so a return with no estate/trust K-1 resolves 0.
WHY IT EXISTS AS A FACT AT ALL — it was an INLINE Switch inside /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome until the §8582 MAGI Part II/III fill needed it. /section8582Magi must include the Part III NONPASSIVE amount and must NOT include the passive suspension allocation (which is the §469(d)(1) passive activity loss line 6 excludes, and which is also what closes the MAGI cycle). Part II already had a standalone nonpassive fact to depend on (/formK1s/*/partIINonpassivePart); Part III did not. The two honest options were extracting this half or duplicating the Switch inside MAGI, and duplication is how two bodies drift apart, so it is extracted.
BYTE-IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION, and the ROUNDING is the whole of that claim. The expression is the pre-extraction Switch VERBATIM, and this fact deliberately carries NO <Round>. /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome computes Round(nonpassive + estatePassiveNet + estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated) as ONE rounding of the sum; giving this fact its own Round would make that Round(Round(nonpassive) + …), which is NOT the same number in general — /estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss and the ratable /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated are not provably whole dollars, so the whole-dollar argument that licensed the ../buildingDepreciation extraction is NOT available here. Unrounded extraction keeps the single outer rounding exactly where it was.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III total estate and trust income or (loss) (line 37 → Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 37 ("Total estate and trust income or (loss). Combine lines 35 and 36"): line 35 (Add columns (d) and (f) of line 34a — the passive + other INCOME columns) plus line 36 (Add columns (c) and (e) of line 34b — the passive + nonpassive LOSS columns) combine to line 37. For a single estate / trust K-1: when the K-1 share is INCOME (/writableEstateTrustK1Income ≥ 0) line 35 = the income and line 36 = 0, so line 37 = the income (the passive/nonpassive split is immaterial — line 35 sums both column (d) and column (f)); when the share is a LOSS, line 35 = 0 and line 36 = the loss column, so line 37 = −loss when the loss is NONPASSIVE (materially participated — flows in full) or 0 when the loss is PASSIVE (not materially participated — §469-suspended absent passive income, /estateTrustK1PassiveSuspendedLoss). Resolves to 0 when no estate / trust K-1 is claimed (/claimsEstateTrustK1 false), which keeps every non-K-1 scenario byte-identical. This is the Part III contribution to Schedule E line 41 → Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 5 → Form 1040 total income — for a nonpassive loss it REDUCES total income. Entirely separate from the /rentalProperties §8582/§465 chain, the royalty net, and the Part II partnership/S-corp K-1 chain (cross-part independence). SCOPE: no beneficiary-level basis limit. A PASSIVE estate/trust K-1 now flows through the cross-activity §8582 pool: line 37 adds /estatePassiveNet + /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated to the nonpassive part, so a passive estate/trust loss is allowed to the extent passive income elsewhere absorbs it (ratably) and passive estate/trust income joins the pool to absorb other passive losses. With no other passive activity to net against. Total income is exact for every case; only the per-activity carryforward split stays pooled-ratable. Result rounded to whole dollars.
STRUCTURE CHANGE — the nonpassive half described above is no longer written inline here: it is /estateTrustNonpassivePart, lifted out VERBATIM so /section8582Magi can read the Part III nonpassive amount without depending on this fact (which would close a cycle) and without duplicating the Switch. The VALUE is unchanged. The single <Round> stays HERE, wrapping the whole sum, and the extracted fact deliberately carries none — Round(Round(nonpassive) + …) is not the same number when /estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss and the ratable /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated are not provably whole dollars. Node test magi-part3-estate-k1-nonpassive-income pins this fact and the extracted one to the same figure, which is the byte-identity check.

Fact.Name: Passive partnership / S-corp K-1 signed net entering the §8582 pool (line 2d component)
Fact.Description:
The Part II K-1s' aggregate SIGNED contribution to the cross-activity §8582 passive pool (Form 8582 Part I line 2d "other passive activities"), AFTER the §704(d)/§1366(d) basis and §465 at-risk limits and BEFORE §469. CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/passiveNet), gated by /claimsK1Income (0 for no K-1). Each PASSIVE K-1 (not materially participated) contributes its signed passiveNet (income +box1, loss −atRiskAllowedLoss); a NONPASSIVE K-1 contributes 0 (flows through Part II line 32 untouched). Was the scalar /k1PassiveNet. interpretation:provisional.
REBODIED (closure) AND THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS THE RETIRED DESCRIPTION, kept because its clean-room nominations and its Form 8582 line-2d identity still describe this path. TWO OF ITS SENTENCES ARE NO LONGER THE BODY. (1) "CollectionSum(/formK1s/*/passiveNet)" — this fact is now the ALIAS of /k1PassiveNetAfterSection179, which is that CollectionSum taken over the POST-section-179 per-item net /formK1s/*/passiveNetAfterSection179. The name did not move because FIVE facts read this path and it carries the module's Export and its clean-room nominations; the computation did. (2) "AFTER the §704(d)/§1366(d) basis and §465 at-risk limits and BEFORE §469" — still true, and now true of one more limit: the box-12 section 179 share it carries has been through Form 4562 Part I and IRC 465 as well. The §469 boundary is unchanged. BYTE-IDENTICAL WHEREVER NO K-1 ELECTS, which is every committed row and every clean-room witness above: /formK1s/*/section179PassiveActivityDeduction is a complete-safe $0 there, so the post-section-179 per-item net equals /formK1s/*/passiveNet.

Fact.Name: Passive estate / trust K-1 signed net entering the §8582 pool (line 2d component)
Fact.Description: This Part III estate/trust K-1's SIGNED contribution to the cross-activity §8582 passive pool (Form 8582 Part I line 2d). Only a PASSIVE estate/trust K-1 (not materially participated, /estateTrustK1LossIsPassive — participation-based gate, classifies income and loss alike) enters: a passive LOSS contributes −/estateTrustAtRiskAllowedLoss; passive INCOME (/writableEstateTrustK1Income ≥ 0) contributes +/writableEstateTrustK1Income; a NONPASSIVE estate/trust K-1 contributes 0 (it flows through Part III line 37 untouched). No beneficiary-level BASIS limit; the §465 at-risk limit is applied upstream — the entity computed the distributive share. Gated on /claimsEstateTrustK1.

Fact.Name: Active-participation leg net (Form 8582 Part I line 1d)
Fact.Description:
Form 8582 Part I line 1d, "Combine lines 1a, 1b, and 1c" — the SIGNED net of every activity that sits in Part IV, "rental real estate activities with active participation" = the rental real estate aggregate (/rentalActiveNet) + the Form 4835 farm rental's Part IV share (/farmRentalPassiveNetActiveLeg).
NEW 2026-08-03 (the /farmRentalPassivePoolParticipation fill), AND IT EXISTS TO END A CONFLATION. Until the farm rental could join the pool, line 1d and /rentalActiveNet were the same number, and /overallPassiveNet and /passiveActiveRentalLoss both read the rental aggregate as if it were the printed line. It is not: line 1d is a PART, and Part IV holds every actively-participated rental real estate activity, of which a Form 4835 farm rental is one when its line A is answered Yes. Naming line 1d separately keeps /rentalActiveNet meaning exactly "the Schedule E Part I rental properties" — which is what the Part I income flow (/rentalLimitedNetIncome) and the rental-only chain still need it to mean.
SIGNED. The farm term is never negative (only the profit arm joins the pool), so this is /rentalActiveNet or better, never worse.

Fact.Name: Other passive activities net (Form 8582 Part I line 2d)
Fact.Description:
Form 8582 Part I line 2d "Combine lines 2a, 2b, and 2c" — the aggregate SIGNED net of ALL non-active-participation passive activities = the non-active rental aggregate (/rentalNonActiveNet) + the passive K-1 (/k1PassiveNet) + the passive estate/trust (/estatePassiveNet). Signed. FOURTH TERM: /farmRentalPassiveNetOtherLeg, the Form 4835 farm rental's Part V share, which is its whole profit when Form 4835 line A is answered No and 0 otherwise. Part V's own second bullet is the destination — "Passive rental real estate activities that don't qualify for the special allowance" — because a farm rental WITHOUT active participation is exactly that. Never negative: only the profit arm joins the pool.
FIFTH TERM ADDED: /k1RentalRealEstatePoolIncomeTotal, the Schedule K-1 boxes 2 and 3 RENTAL income, which the partner instructions call "a passive activity amount for all partners" and which Form 8582 Part I line 2 ("All other passive activities") is the destination for. It joins here AND in /passiveIncomeTotal, exactly as the other pool participants do, so that /overallPassiveNet and therefore the Form 8582 line 6 MAGI carry the same figure the capacity total carries. Never negative: only the income side of boxes 2 and 3 is modelled, and a publicly traded partnership contributes nothing (section 469(k)).

Fact.Name: Overall passive net across ALL activities (Form 8582 Part I line 3)
Fact.Description: Form 8582 Part I line 3 "Combine lines 1d and 2d" for the FULL cross-activity pool = the active-rental aggregate (line 1d, /rentalActiveNet) + the other-passive aggregate (line 2d, /otherPassiveNet). Signed: ≥ 0 means net passive income (no §469 limitation, every passive loss is allowed); < 0 means an overall passive loss. Supersedes the rental-only /rentalOverallPassiveNet as the §469 netting base once a K-1 or estate passive activity is present; equals /rentalOverallPassiveNet when both new terms are 0. REPOINTED 2026-08-03 by the /farmRentalPassivePoolParticipation fill: the line-1d operand is now /passiveActiveRentalLegNet (the true printed line 1d) rather than /rentalActiveNet (the Schedule E Part I rental aggregate), because a Form 4835 farm rental profit can now sit in Part IV beside the rental properties. The two are equal on every return with no farm rental or with the farm rental routed to Part V, so line 3 is unchanged wherever the farm profit is 0 — and where it is not, the SAME profit reaches line 3 through the other leg. Line 3 is therefore INVARIANT under the Part IV/Part V routing; the routing moves the profit between the legs, never in or out of the combine.

Fact.Name: Total passive income across the six pool activities (§8582 pool PI)
Fact.Description:
Five terms: the sum of the POSITIVE signed nets across the pool activities = max(0, /rentalActiveNet) + max(0, /rentalNonActiveNet) + max(0, /k1PassiveNet) + max(0, /estatePassiveNet) + max(0, /farmRentalPassiveNet). The passive income available to absorb passive losses under §469(d)(1). A SIXTH TERM: max(0, /k1RentalRealEstatePoolIncomeTotal), the Schedule K-1 boxes 2 and 3 RENTAL income, which the partner instructions call "a passive activity amount for all partners". Like the farm rental term it is written as a GreaterOf for symmetry and is structurally redundant — the aggregate is already floored at 0, because only the income side of boxes 2 and 3 is modelled. NO DOUBLE COUNT WITH TOTAL INCOME: the amount reaches Schedule E line 32 once, through /k1RentalRealEstateIncomeTotal; here it only raises the pool's capacity to allow OTHER activities' losses. A PUBLICLY TRADED PARTNERSHIP contributes nothing to this term (section 469(k)), which is why the aggregate reads the PTP-gated per item fact rather than the line 32 one.
A FIFTH TERM: max(0, /farmRentalPassiveNet), the Form 4835 farm rental. It is written as a GreaterOf for symmetry with the other four and is structurally redundant — that fact is already floored at 0, because only the profit arm of Form 4835 line 32 joins the pool.
THE TERM IS ROUTING-INVARIANT, and that is the point of it sitting here rather than inside a leg. PI totals the POSITIVE activity nets; a farm rental profit is positive whether it lands in Part IV or Part V, so this addend is the same number either way. The Part IV/Part V choice bites only on the line-1d LOSS (/passiveActiveRentalLoss), which is what Form 8582 line 4 caps the special allowance against. NO DOUBLE COUNT with the leg facts: /rentalActiveNet does not contain the farm term, so the farm profit is counted once here and once in line 3. And no double count with TOTAL INCOME either — the farm profit reaches Schedule E through line 40 (/farmRentalNetIncome) and this pool membership adds no second income term; it only raises the pool's capacity to allow OTHER activities' losses.

Fact.Name: Total passive loss across the four activities (§8582 pool PL, positive)
Fact.Description: The sum of the NEGATED-negative signed nets across the four pool activities, as a POSITIVE total = max(0, −/rentalActiveNet) + max(0, −/rentalNonActiveNet) + max(0, −/k1PassiveNet) + max(0, −/estatePassiveNet). The aggregate passive loss subject to the §469 limitation.

Fact.Name: Active-participation rental loss eligible for the special allowance (positive)
Fact.Description: The active-participation rental real-estate loss as a POSITIVE amount = max(0, −/rentalActiveNet). The ONLY loss the Form 8582 Part II $25,000 special allowance can reach; caps /passiveSpecialAllowanceUsable so the special allowance never shelters a passive K-1/estate or non-active-rental loss. It is max(0, −/passiveActiveRentalLegNet), the loss on the true printed line 1d rather than on the rental aggregate. THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THE PART IV / PART V ROUTING CHANGES A DOLLAR. A Form 4835 farm rental profit routed to Part IV is Part IV column (a) income; it lands on line 1a and REDUCES the line-1d loss, which reduces line 4, which reduces the usable special allowance. Routed to Part V it leaves line 1d alone. Every other pool quantity — PI, PL, line 3 — is identical under both placements, so this fact carries the whole divergence. Node tests scheduleE/farm-rental-8582-part-iv-active-participation and farm-rental-8582-part-v-no-active-participation are that divergence pair (10,000 of total income on byte-identical inputs but for line A); the moot pair farm-rental-8582-routing-moot-active-yes / -no is the sub-population where line 1d carries no loss for the smaller-of to bite on and the two placements agree to the dollar.

Fact.Name: Active-participation rental loss eligible for the special allowance (Form 8582 Part II line 4)
Fact.Description: Form 8582 Part II line 4 = the SMALLER of the line-1d loss (the active-participation rental loss, /passiveActiveRentalLoss) and the line-3 loss (the OVERALL passive loss after netting ALL four activities, max(0, −/overallPassiveNet)). This is the amount of active-rental loss the $25k special allowance may reach — and it is NOT a pro-rata dilution of income across losses. Form 8582 nets other-passive income against other-passive losses within line 2d FIRST, then nets line 2d against line 1d at line 3; line 4 caps the special-allowance base at the smaller of the active-rental loss and that overall net loss. When the active rental is the only loss (line 2d ≥ 0) the overall loss ≤ the active loss so line 4 = the overall loss; when other-passive losses dominate, line 4 = the full active-rental loss. NOTE: the total-allowed formula min(PL, PI + min(SA, activeLoss)) is algebraically identical to min(PL, PI + min(SA, line4)) (the outer min-by-PL makes the line-4 overall-loss cap redundant), so the line-4 figure changes NO total-income value anywhere — it only makes the intermediate /passiveSpecialAllowanceUsable equal to the true Form 8582 line 9.

Fact.Name: Special allowance usable in the pool (Form 8582 Part II line 9 = smaller of line 4 or line 8)
Fact.Description: This is Form 8582 line 9 (smaller of the line-8 phased allowance and the line-4 loss). This changes NO total-income value (the total-allowed min(PL, PI + min(SA, activeLoss)) is algebraically identical to min(PL, PI + min(SA, line4)) — the outer min-by-PL makes the line-4 cap redundant for the total); it only makes this intermediate equal the true line 9. The special allowance still reaches active-participation rental real estate ONLY (§469(i) / Form 8582 Part II header).

Fact.Name: Total passive loss allowed this year across the pool (§8582)
Fact.Description: The aggregate passive loss ALLOWED for 2025 across the four-activity pool = min(/passiveLossTotal, /passiveIncomeTotal + /passiveSpecialAllowanceUsable). Passive income absorbs passive losses (§469(d)(1)); the special allowance tops up the deductible amount for the active rental loss (§469(i)); the min by PL caps the total at the losses actually present. The net passive contribution to total income is /passiveIncomeTotal − this amount.

Fact.Name: Total passive loss suspended this year across the pool (§469(b) carryforward)
Fact.Description: The aggregate passive loss DISALLOWED for 2025 across the pool = /passiveLossTotal − /passiveAllowedLossTotal. §469(b) carries it forward; this single-year demo REPORTS it (split ratably below) but does not apply it to a future year. 0 when the pool is a net passive profit or every loss is allowed.

Fact.Name: Passive K-1 loss magnitude entering the pool (positive)
Fact.Description: The passive K-1 loss as a POSITIVE amount = max(0, −/k1PassiveNet) (= /k1AtRiskAllowedLoss for a passive K-1 loss, else 0). The numerator of this activity's ratable share of the suspended total.

Fact.Name: Passive estate / trust loss magnitude entering the pool (positive)
Fact.Description: The passive estate/trust loss as a POSITIVE amount = max(0, −/estatePassiveNet) (= /estateTrustK1Loss for a passive estate/trust loss, else 0).

Fact.Name: Passive K-1 loss suspended — ratable share of the pool suspended total (Form 8582 Part VII)
Fact.Description: This passive K-1 activity's ratable share of the pool suspended total = round(/passiveSuspendedLossTotal × /k1PassiveLoss / /passiveLossTotal) when /passiveLossTotal > 0, else 0. SUPERSEDES /k1PassiveSuspendedLoss (which suspended the full passive K-1 loss in isolation) once passive income exists elsewhere to absorb part of it. When the K-1 loss is the only loss and no passive income exists, this equals the full passive K-1 loss (the behavior).

Fact.Name: Passive estate / trust loss suspended — ratable share of the pool suspended total (Form 8582 Part VII)
Fact.Description: This passive estate/trust activity's ratable share of the pool suspended total = round(/passiveSuspendedLossTotal × /estatePassiveLoss / /passiveLossTotal) when /passiveLossTotal > 0, else 0. SUPERSEDES /estateTrustK1PassiveSuspendedLoss once passive income exists elsewhere to absorb part of it.

Fact.Name: Rental passive loss suspended — pool suspended total minus the K-1 and estate shares (plug)
Fact.Description: The rental share of the pool suspended total, taken as the PLUG = /passiveSuspendedLossTotal − /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated − /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated. Assigning the rounding residual to rental keeps the three ratable shares summing to /passiveSuspendedLossTotal EXACTLY, so /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome stay cent-exact. When there is no rental this resolves 0 (the K-1/estate shares then equal the suspended total).

Fact.Name: Holds a residual interest in a REMIC (Schedule E Part IV)
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports a residual-holder share of REMIC income or loss on Schedule E Part IV. Gate for the Part IV intake, and the exact twin of /writableHasEstateTrustK1 / /writableHasK1Income / /writableHasRoyaltyIncome. When true, /writableRemicResidualNet carries the line-39 combined columns (d) + (e) figure. The instructions scope this to RESIDUAL interests only: "If you are the holder of a regular interest in a REMIC, do not use Schedule E to report the income you received. Instead, report it on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 2b" — a regular interest is ordinary interest income and reaches the return through the interest module, never through here.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E Part IV REMIC residual-holder income or loss
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /writableHasRemicResidualInterest is answered AND true (the IsComplete/Switch pattern, twin of /claimsEstateTrustK1). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every return that never entered a REMIC residual interest still resolves and /scheduleERemicResidualNet is 0. This is what keeps the fill byte-identical for every prior scenario, and it is also the fact that must appear in /scheduleEActivityPresent so the section 219(g) MAGI bound's `omitted` treatment of /scheduleETotalIncome stays exact.

Fact.Name: REMIC residual-holder combined columns (d) + (e) (Schedule E line 39 attestation)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part IV line 39: the filer's attested combination of column (d), "Taxable income (net loss) from Schedules Q, line 1b", and column (e), "Income from Schedules Q, line 3b", across every REMIC residual interest held. SIGNED: positive is income, NEGATIVE is a loss (the Part IV heading is "Income or Loss" and line 41 says "Combine"), so there is no Min 0 limit. Consulted only when /claimsRemicResidualInterest is true.
ATTESTED, NOT COMPUTED, AND THE REASON IS A SOURCE GAP RATHER THAN A DESIGN CHOICE: Schedule Q (Form 1066) is not vendored under sources/, so the per-quarter column (d)/(e) detail cannot be modelled against an authority (invariant #3). The vendored Schedule E line supports the combined figure on its own, and the instructions already direct a multi-REMIC holder to enter a COMBINED total on line 39, so the attestation is the form's own granularity rather than a simplification of it.
COLUMN (c) IS EXCLUDED BY INSTRUCTION, not by scope: "Do not include the amount shown in column (c) in the total on Schedule E, line 39." The section 860E excess inclusion that column (c) reports is a separate mechanism with its own consumers (it floors taxable income and can float Form 6251 line 4); it is not built here and must not be folded in.
DISPOSITION keep-fallback: the retirement this fact was proposed for is already half done and cannot be finished. /scheduleERemicResidualNet computes line 39 from the printed columns (d) and (e) (/remicColumnsDAndENet) whenever /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered is true, and reads this attestation only otherwise; the computed arm is NOT total, because a return may claim a residual interest and enter the combined line 39 figure without answering either printed column (the multi REMIC holder the instructions tell to "enter the combined totals of columns (d) and (e) on Schedule E, line 39" is exactly that filer), and Schedule Q (Form 1066) is still not vendored, so no other source can supply the number. The attestation therefore stays as the FALLBACK arm.

Fact.Name: The Schedule E line 38 columns (d) and (e) were answered on this return
Fact.Description:
True when the filer answered EITHER printed Part IV amount column — column (d) (/writableRemicColumnDScheduleQLine1bTaxableIncome, Schedules Q line 1b) or column (e) (/writableRemicColumnEScheduleQLine3bIncome, Schedules Q line 3b). It is the "was the source answered" predicate that lets /scheduleERemicResidualNet compute line 39 from the printed columns and keep the combined attestation /writableRemicResidualNet as the FALLBACK, which is the same shape /farmRentalNetIncome uses with form4835:/form4835IncomeLinesAnswered.
IT IS AN OR OF TWO IsCompletes ON THE INTAKES THEMSELVES, deliberately, and not an IsComplete on a complete-safe alias: an alias defaulting to $0 is always Complete, so a predicate built on one would be constantly true and would silently retire the attestation on every return. Answering only one column is enough — a residual holder with income on Schedule Q line 3b and nothing on line 1b answers exactly one box, and the other column is then a true $0 rather than an unanswered question.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 39 computed from the printed columns (d) and (e)
Fact.Description:
The line 39 combine, "Combine columns (d) and (e) only", taken from the two printed Part IV amount columns: column (d) plus column (e), each through an IsComplete Switch defaulting to $0 so a residual holder who answered only one column still gets a Complete figure. SIGNED — column (d)'s caption is "Taxable income (net loss)" and the Part IV heading is "Income or Loss", so a net loss is a negative term.
COLUMN (c) IS NOT HERE and that is the instruction, not an omission: the section 860E excess inclusion is carried by /writableRemicExcessInclusion and floors taxable income and AMTI through /scheduleERemicExcessInclusion; the form's own line 39 says "columns (d) and (e) ONLY".

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part IV total — REMIC residual-holder income or (loss) (line 39 to line 41)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 39 ("Combine columns (d) and (e) only. Enter the result here and include in the total on line 41 below"): the attested Part IV net (/writableRemicResidualNet) when /claimsRemicResidualInterest is true, else 0. The attested combine is now the FALLBACK. When the printed line 38 columns (d) and (e) are answered (/remicColumnsDAndEAnswered) this line reads /remicColumnsDAndENet, the combine the form itself prescribes. The attestation and the columns were two facts for one quantity and a filer who answered both stated the same money twice. Resolves Complete 0 on every return that claims no REMIC residual interest, which keeps every prior scenario byte-identical. MAY BE NEGATIVE. Result rounded to whole dollars.
NONPASSIVE BY INSTRUCTION: "REMIC income or loss is not income or loss from a passive activity." So this joins Schedule E line 41 (/scheduleETotalIncome) DIRECTLY, on the same nonpassive/portfolio channel as /royaltyNetIncome, and is deliberately OUTSIDE the section 8582 pool (/passiveIncomeTotal, /passiveAllowedLossTotal) and the section 465 at-risk chain. A consequence worth stating so it is not read as a miss: form8960's line 4a reads scheduleE:/passiveIncomeTotal, so a REMIC residual net does not reach net investment income through this module. Whether a residual interest is section 1411 property at all is a separate question with no vendored irs.gov authority in this repo; it is left open rather than guessed.
SCOPE, stated as the contract required: column (c)'s section 860E excess inclusion is NOT in this figure — the instructions' CAUTION forbids it on line 39. Its floor effect is no longer unbuilt: /writableRemicExcessInclusion asks for the column and /scheduleERemicExcessInclusion floors both taxCalculations:/taxableIncome and form6251:/alternativeMinimumTaxableIncome. Nothing about column (c) is refused any more — the interim knockout retired with that landing. This figure is unaffected by all of it — the two columns stay disjoint.
A SECOND ADDEND now sits outside the /claimsRemicResidualInterest gate: /k1RemicColumnDTaxableIncome, the code A "other portfolio income (loss)" amounts recorded on the Schedule K-1 items, which both the partner and the shareholder instruction books route to column (d) of Schedule E line 38. It is outside the gate because a partner whose only REMIC exposure is the pass through never answers /writableClaimsRemicResidualInterest, the same reason /k1RoyaltyIncomeTotal sits outside /claimsRoyaltyIncome on line 4. The K-1 leg fires only on a K-1 whose ../entityType is ANSWERED, so it is $0 on every committed fixture and scenario and this line is byte identical across the corpus. Consequence stated rather than hidden: on a K-1 only return line 39 prints a figure while the line 38 detail columns above it print nothing, because line 38 is filled only from the filer's own Schedules Q.

Fact.Name: REMIC excess inclusion — Schedule E Part IV column (c) (Schedules Q line 2c total)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (c), "Excess inclusion from Schedules Q, line 2c (see instructions)": the total of the amounts shown on Schedule(s) Q (Form 1066) line 2c across every REMIC residual interest held. Consulted only when /claimsRemicResidualInterest is true.
NON-NEGATIVE, unlike its sibling /writableRemicResidualNet. A section 860E excess inclusion is a floor on income, never a loss: the printed column carries no parenthetical negative field (contrast line 36, which prints one), and both instruction sentences describe it as a SMALLEST amount one is allowed to report. Hence the Min 0 limit.
ATTESTED, NOT COMPUTED, for the same source reason as the line-39 sibling: Schedule Q (Form 1066) is not vendored under sources/, so the per-quarter line-2c detail cannot be modelled against an authority (invariant #3).
DELIBERATELY NOT A SUMMAND OF ANYTHING. This amount is read by exactly one fact, /scheduleERemicExcessInclusion, which is the form in which the two section 860E floors consume it. Folding it into line 39 is forbidden by the instructions' CAUTION and would over-state total income.

Fact.Name: REMIC excess inclusion — the section 860E floor amount read by both floor sites
Fact.Description:
The Schedule E Part IV column (c) excess inclusion as the two floors consume it: the attested /writableRemicExcessInclusion when this return claims a residual interest AND answered the column, else 0. Whole dollars, NON-NEGATIVE (the writable carries the Min 0 limit).
DELIBERATELY NOT A SUMMAND OF LINE 39 OR LINE 41. This is a FLOOR, not an income item, and the instructions' CAUTION forbids folding it into line 39. Its two consumers are in other modules: taxCalculations:/taxableIncome (Form 1040 line 15) and form6251:/alternativeMinimumTaxableIncome (Form 6251 line 4). /scheduleERemicResidualNet, /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome are untouched by it.
THE IsComplete GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS NOT DECORATION. Both consumers are on the critical path of EVERY return: line 15 is the tax line and line 4 feeds the AMT. If this fact could resolve Incomplete, that Incompleteness would cascade into the taxable income of every filer who claimed a residual interest and had not yet answered the column. The All(claims, IsComplete(writable)) wrapper makes it Complete 0 instead, which is also the right tax answer: a column the filer never reported floors nothing.

Fact.Name: Has net farm rental income or (loss) from Form 4835 (Schedule E Part V)
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports net farm rental income or loss from Form 4835 on Schedule E Part V line 40. Gate for the line-40 intake, and the twin of /writableHasRemicResidualInterest / /writableHasEstateTrustK1. The Schedule E instructions define the population by a three-part test — an individual, receiving rental income based on crops or livestock produced by the tenant, who did NOT materially participate in the management or operation of the farm. A landlord who DID materially participate is on Schedule F instead and must not answer this gate true; that distinction is what keeps the amount out of self-employment earnings.

Fact.Name: Claims Schedule E Part V net farm rental income or (loss)
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /writableHasFarmRentalIncome is answered AND true (the IsComplete/Switch pattern, twin of /claimsRemicResidualInterest). Unanswered resolves Complete false, so every return that never entered a Form 4835 farm rental still resolves and /farmRentalNetIncome is 0. Also a mandatory member of /scheduleEActivityPresent — see that fact's block comment for why omitting it would break the section 219(g) MAGI upper bound.

Fact.Name: Net farm rental income or (loss) from Form 4835 (Schedule E line 40 attestation)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part V line 40: the filer's attested Form 4835 bottom line. SIGNED — positive is income, NEGATIVE is a loss ("income or (loss)") — so there is no Min 0 limit. Consulted only when /claimsFarmRentalIncome is true.
ATTESTED, NOT COMPUTED. When this fact landed (2026-07-31) no f4835 or i4835 file existed under sources/, so the Form 4835 line-by-line computation had no authority to be built against (invariant #3). Form 4835 was vendored 2026-08-03 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4835.pdf) and the computation is now buildable by a later unit; this fact remains the attestation until that unit lands. The vendored Schedule E line supports the bottom-line figure on its own, which is the granularity Schedule E itself asks for.
POST-LIMITATION ON THE LOSS SIDE ONLY — and the vendored form is now explicit about which side. Farm rental reported on Form 4835 is passive by definition (the instructions' third condition is that the landlord did NOT materially participate). Form 4835 line 32 sends a net INCOME straight to Schedule E line 40 with no limitation step at all ("If the result is income, enter it here and on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 40"); only a LOSS detours through line 34c, where the filer applies the section 469 and section 465 limits on their own Form 8582 and Form 6198 first. This module therefore takes the signed amount as entered and does NOT re-apply those limits to a loss — re-applying would double-limit — while a PROFIT reaching this fact is pre-section-469 by construction.
THE COST IS PAID, 2026-08-03. This paragraph used to read "the amount does not join this graph's own section 8582 pool (/passiveIncomeTotal), so a farm rental PROFIT does not absorb other passive losses", disclosed as taxpayer-adverse. That contract is filled: the PROFIT arm of this attestation is now the pool participant /farmRentalPassiveNet, routed to Form 8582 Part IV or Part V by the new line-A writable /writableFarmRentalActiveParticipation. The LOSS arm still stays out, and the paragraph above is why — a loss arriving here has already been through the filer's own Form 8582, so the attestation is post-limitation on that side and re-limiting would double-limit.
DISPOSITION keep-fallback: Form 4835 is now modelled and /farmRentalNetIncome reads the computed form4835 /form4835Line40Amount whenever /form4835Line40Computed is true, so the retirement candidacy was real; but the computed arm is NOT total. /form4835Line40Computed requires that Form 4835 Part I was answered (/form4835IncomeLinesAnswered) and that either line 32 is income or the post limitation line 34c loss was entered, and a return may answer /writableHasFarmRentalIncome and type its Form 4835 bottom line on Schedule E without opening Form 4835 in this graph at all - every committed node fixture that reaches line 40 through the attestation does exactly that. The attestation therefore stays as the FALLBACK arm behind the real answered-ness predicate, which is brief rule 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part V — net farm rental income or (loss) from Form 4835 (line 40 to line 41)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 40 ("Net farm rental income or (loss) from Form 4835"): the attested Form 4835 net (/writableFarmRentalNet) when /claimsFarmRentalIncome is true, else 0. Resolves Complete 0 on every return that claims no farm rental, which keeps every prior scenario byte-identical. MAY BE NEGATIVE. Result rounded to whole dollars, and combined into the line-41 grand total /scheduleETotalIncome, which flows to Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 5.
NO SELF-EMPLOYMENT TAX, which is the whole reason this line exists separately from Schedule F: the Form 4835 population is defined by NOT materially participating, so the income is not net earnings from self-employment. Nothing here is wired to scheduleSE, and that is deliberate rather than unbuilt.
SCOPE, disclosed rather than implied: (a) the PROFIT arm of this amount joins /passiveIncomeTotal as of 2026-08-03, so it absorbs other passive losses in this graph's section 8582 pool; the LOSS arm does not, because the filer's own Form 8582 already limited it and re-limiting would double-limit (the participant is /farmRentalPassiveNet; the Part IV / Part V routing is /farmRentalActiveParticipation). The amount reaching line 41 is unchanged either way — pool membership moves OTHER activities' allowed losses, never this line; (b) line 42's "Reconciliation of farming and fishing income", which line 40's text tells the filer to complete, is not computed FROM this fact and never could be — it is a GROSS figure and this is a net. It ships separately as /scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation (2026-08-03, once Form 4835 was vendored), feeds the estimated-tax farmer/fisherman rule rather than total income, and is NOT a summand of line 41. The attested net is now the FALLBACK; when Form 4835 is completed in this graph, line 40 reads the computed form4835 /form4835Line32BeforeGate — the printed line says "from Form 4835", and the form now exists to compute it.

Fact.Name: A real estate professional materially participated in the farm rental
Fact.Description: Screen specification. QUESTION: "Did you (or your spouse, the real estate professional on this return) materially participate in the operation of this farm rental under the passive activity rules?" HELP TEXT: a real estate professional's rental real estate activity in which they materially participate is not passive; its income and loss are not limited by the passive activity rules. ASKED WHEN: the return claims a Form 4835 farm rental and a filer qualifies as a real estate professional. UNANSWERED POSTURE: No (the farm rental stays in the passive pool). WHAT IT FEEDS: /farmRentalIsRealEstateProfessionalNonpassive.

Fact.Name: The farm rental is a real estate professional's nonpassive rental
Fact.Description: True when the return claims a farm rental, a filer is a real estate professional (/eitherFilerIsRealEstateProfessional), and /writableFarmRentalRealEstateProfessionalMaterialParticipation is Yes. The farm rental then contributes nothing to the Form 8582 pool (/farmRentalPassiveNet is $0); its line 40 amount is unchanged, and its profit counts in the Form 8582 line 6 modified AGI through /farmRentalNonpassiveMagiNet. The filer's own Schedule E line 43 total includes it (the attestation /writableRealEstateProfessionalRentalNetIncome).

Fact.Name: A real estate professional's farm rental profit in the Form 8582 line 6 modified AGI
Fact.Description: The farm rental profit (max($0, /farmRentalNetIncome)) when /farmRentalIsRealEstateProfessionalNonpassive, else $0. Modified AGI excludes a loss allowable by reason of section 469(c)(7) but not a profit; the profit of a passive farm rental reaches modified AGI through /overallPassiveNet, and this term keeps the nonpassive one in.

Fact.Name: Form 4835 line A — actively participated in the operation of this farm
Fact.Description:
Form 4835 line A, "Did you actively participate in the operation of this farm during 2025?" — the Yes/No box printed at the head of the form, above Part I. Consulted only when /claimsFarmRentalIncome is true and the attested line-32 figure is a PROFIT; a farm rental loss never reaches the pool, so line A cannot change a dollar on a loss return.
NOT THE SAME QUESTION AS THE MATERIAL-PARTICIPATION TEST THAT PUTS A FILER ON THIS FORM, and confusing the two is the one mistake available here. Form 4835 exists FOR the landlord who did NOT materially participate; that is its entry condition. ACTIVE participation is a weaker, separate standard used by section 469(i) to decide who may reach the $25,000 special allowance, and the form's own Specific Instructions state it: participating "in making management decisions or arranging for others to provide services (such as repairs) in a significant and bona fide sense" — approving new tenants, deciding on rental terms, approving capital or repair expenditures — with a floor that no one holding less than 10% by value of the interests in the activity actively participates. A filer can satisfy the second while failing the first, and the whole Form 4835 population does exactly that.
UNANSWERED IS SAFE AND MEANS PART IV. See /farmRentalActiveParticipation for the gate and the direction argument.

Fact.Name: The farm rental's Form 8582 leg — Part IV (active participation) or Part V
Fact.Description:
The Part IV / Part V routing switch for the Form 4835 farm rental's pool participation: true when the filer answered Form 4835 line A Yes, and true ALSO when line A is unanswered. False only on an explicit No.
THE UNANSWERED ARM IS A DELIBERATE ADVERSE DEFAULT, not the usual complete-safe zero, and it is the one judgment in this fill. Line A is a printed Yes/No box with no third state, so an unanswered box has to resolve somewhere the moment the profit joins the pool. Part V is weakly taxpayer-FAVOURABLE — routing the profit there leaves the line-1d loss intact, so Form 8582 line 4, line 9 and the total allowed loss are each at least as large as under Part IV — which makes a default of False a World-#1 under-taxation exposure. Defaulting to Part IV sits at the adverse end of the two legal placements, so it can over-tax a filer who did not actively participate and can never under-tax one who did. It is also never worse than the behaviour it replaces: with the profit outside the pool altogether, allowed loss was no larger than under Part IV, so the fill is monotone taxpayer-favourable from the status quo even on the defaulted arm.
A NON-PARTICIPATING FILER MUST ANSWER NO TO GET THE FAVOURABLE PLACEMENT, which is the cost of the default and is stated rather than hidden. The alternative — refusing to resolve until line A is answered — would make /overallPassiveNet and therefore total income Incomplete for every filer who claims Schedule E line 40 today, which is a larger harm than an over-stated allowance on the sub-population that leaves the box blank.
MOOT ON MOST RETURNS. When the return carries no active-participation rental real estate LOSS, line 1d is zero or positive under both placements, Form 8582 line 4's smaller-of has nothing to bite on, and the two legs give identical totals — witnessed by the node-test pair scheduleE/farm-rental-8582-routing-moot-active-yes / -no.
A READER WILL ASK WHY ANSWERING YES HERE DOES NOT UNLOCK THE $25,000 SPECIAL ALLOWANCE, so: it cannot, and it never needs to. /passiveSpecialAllowanceUsable stays gated on /claimsRentalActiveParticipation, which is a RENTAL-PROPERTY gate and takes no account of this answer. That is safe rather than merely conservative, because a nonzero line-1d LOSS is impossible without an actively-participating rental property: this fact's own term is ≥ 0 (profit arm only), so a negative line 1d requires /rentalActiveNet < 0, and that aggregate sums only per-property nets that CLAIM active participation — which makes /claimsRentalActiveParticipation true. The gate can therefore never zero a nonzero line 4. For a farm-rental-only filer the allowance is 0 and irrelevant in the same breath: with no rental property, line 1d is the farm profit alone, so line 4 is 0 and min(allowance, 0) is 0 either way.

Fact.Name: Farm rental signed net entering the §8582 pool — the PROFIT arm only
Fact.Description:
The Form 4835 farm rental's SIGNED contribution to the cross-activity §8582 passive pool = max(0, /farmRentalNetIncome). The fifth pool participant, beside the active rental, non-active rental, passive K-1 and passive estate/trust nets.
ONLY THE PROFIT ARM, and the vendored form is explicit about which side is which. Form 4835 line 32 reads "Net farm rental income or (loss). Subtract line 31 from line 7. If the result is income, enter it here and on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 40" — no limitation step at all, because section 469 does not limit passive INCOME. A positive Schedule E line 40 is therefore PRE-section-469 by construction and is exactly the figure Form 8582 wants. Only a LOSS detours: line 34c, "You may have to complete Form 8582 to determine your deductible loss ... In either case, enter the deductible loss here and on Schedule E (Form 1040), line 40". A loss arriving at Schedule E line 40 has ALREADY been through the filer's own Form 8582, so re-limiting it in this pool would double-limit it. The GreaterOf is that split.
THE PROFIT SIDE BELONGS ON FORM 8582 AT ALL — the point the parent fact's original scope note conceded it could not source. Form 4835's own instructions state it in a Note: "You may need to include information from Form 4835 on Form 8582 even if you have a net profit."
NO DOUBLE COUNT WITH TOTAL INCOME. The profit already flows to Schedule E line 41 through /farmRentalNetIncome (line 40). This fact does NOT add a second income term anywhere; it raises the pool's capacity to allow OTHER activities' losses, which is the whole point of the fill. Correspondingly this activity gets no Part VII ratable share and the /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated plug is untouched: the allocation numerators are loss magnitudes and this participant's loss is structurally zero.
Complete 0 on every return that claims no farm rental, because /farmRentalNetIncome is already gated on /claimsFarmRentalIncome.

Fact.Name: The farm rental's Form 8582 Part IV share (line 1a, feeding line 1d)
Fact.Description:
The farm rental's pool participation when Form 4835 line A routes it to Part IV, "rental real estate activities with active participation": /farmRentalPassiveNet when /farmRentalActiveParticipation is true, else 0. Summed into /passiveActiveRentalLegNet, the Form 8582 Part I line-1d combine. Always ≥ 0 — the profit arm is the only arm.
This and /farmRentalPassiveNetOtherLeg partition the same amount: exactly one is nonzero on any return, and their sum is /farmRentalPassiveNet. That is why Form 8582 line 3 is invariant under the routing while the line-1d loss is not.

Fact.Name: The farm rental's Form 8582 Part V share (line 2a, feeding line 2d)
Fact.Description:
The farm rental's pool participation when Form 4835 line A routes it to Part V: /farmRentalPassiveNet when /farmRentalActiveParticipation is FALSE, else 0. Summed into /otherPassiveNet, the Form 8582 Part I line-2d combine. Always ≥ 0.
THE PART V BULLET IT LANDS ON IS THE SECOND, NOT THE THIRD, and the distinction is the whole substance of the routing. Part V covers "Passive trade or business activities", "Passive rental real estate activities that don't qualify for the special allowance", and "Rental activities other than rental real estate activities". A farm rental without active participation is a passive rental REAL ESTATE activity that fails the special allowance's own qualification — the second bullet. It is not the third: Form 4835's Line 34 instructions route its filer through the "Exception for Certain Rental Real Estate Activities", which only a rental real estate activity can meet, and i8582's statement of that exception names Form 4835 line-32 losses beside Schedule E Part I rental real estate losses.

Fact.Name: Has gross farming or fishing income to reconcile on Schedule E line 42 (non-Form-4835 route)
Fact.Description:
Whether the return has gross farming or fishing income reported on a Schedule K-1 — (Form 1065) box 14 code B, (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN, or (Form 1041) box 14 code F — which Schedule E line 42 asks the filer to reconcile. ONLY the K-1 route needs this gate: a filer who claims Part V line 40 is already obliged to complete line 42 by line 40's own printed text, so /claimsFarmingFishingIncome ORs this writable with /claimsFarmRentalIncome and a line-40 filer never has to answer it.
A filer with NO farming or fishing income of any kind leaves this unanswered, which resolves Complete false through the gate below.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 42 is owed (farm rental route OR K-1 route)
Fact.Description:
Complete-safe gate for Schedule E line 42, and a DISJUNCTION rather than the single IsComplete/Switch its Part IV and Part V siblings use, because the line-42 obligation has two independent sources. (1) /claimsFarmRentalIncome: line 40 reads "Net farm rental income or (loss) from Form 4835. Also, complete line 42 below", so claiming line 40 obliges line 42 with no further question asked. (2) the IsComplete-guarded /writableHasFarmingFishingIncome, for the filer whose gross farming or fishing income arrives on a Schedule K-1 and who files no Form 4835 at all.
Both arms are complete-safe false when unanswered, so this resolves Complete false on every return that entered neither — the state in which line 42 is 0.

Fact.Name: Gross farming and fishing income (Schedule E line 42 attestation)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part V line 42: the filer's TOTAL gross farming and fishing income across the four sources the line names — Form 4835 line 7, Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code B, Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN, and Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F. GROSS, so never negative; the Min 0 limit is declared rather than implied.
ONE ATTESTATION OF THE WHOLE LINE, not a per-leg computation. Form 4835 IS vendored now (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4835.pdf), so its line 7 is a citable authority — but line 7 is itself the sum of that form's Part I lines 1 through 6, and the three K-1 legs have no intake in this graph at all (/formK1s models box 14 code A only, and neither the Form 1120-S nor the Form 1041 Schedule K-1 is modelled). Attesting a PARTIAL gross figure would be worse than attesting none, because the figure's purpose is a two-thirds TEST; attesting the whole line is exactly the addition the paper form asks the filer to perform. The per-leg computation is not built.
Consulted only when /claimsFarmingFishingIncome is true, so a return that claims line 40 and leaves this unanswered resolves line 42 INCOMPLETE — the form obliges the answer, and a defaulted 0 would misreport a printed line.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part V — reconciliation of farming and fishing income (line 42)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 42: the sum of the four printed legs, form4835:/form4835GrossFarmRentalIncome (Form 4835 line 7), /k1GrossFarmingFishingIncome (Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box 14 code B), /k1FarmingFishingIncomeSCorp (Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) box 17 code AN) and /estateTrustGrossFarmingFishingIncome (Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) box 14 code F). Each leg is complete safe, so the total is Complete on every return. The filer's whole-line attestation /writableFarmingFishingGrossIncome is a cross-check only (/scheduleELine42AttestationDiffersFromComputed). Rounded to whole dollars.
IT IS NOT A SUMMAND OF LINE 41. The form combines lines 26, 32, 37, 39 and 40 only (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040se.pdf, page 2), so a nonzero line 42 leaves /scheduleETotalIncome — and therefore Schedule 1 line 5, total income and AGI — untouched. That disjointness is why this is a node of its own and not a widening of line 40, and it is pinned by the node test scheduleE/farming-fishing-line42-gross-attested, which asserts a 52,000 line 42 alongside an 18,000 line 41.
NOTHING CONSUMES IT YET. Its consumer is the estimated-tax farmer/fisherman two-thirds rule (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040se.pdf, page 11) and no Form 2210 module exists in this dictionary; the test is not built. It is exported because Schedule E PRINTS it — a return that reaches line 42 owes the figure whether or not this graph yet computes anything from it.
NOT A MEMBER OF /scheduleEActivityPresent, deliberately: that gate tracks intakes that move line 41, and this one does not. See the block comment above.

Fact.Name: The filer's line 42 attestation disagrees with the computed four-leg total
Fact.Description:
True when the return claims line 42, the filer answered the whole-line attestation, and that figure differs from /scheduleEFarmingFishingReconciliation — the four-leg sum the graph now computes.
WHY THE ATTESTATION SURVIVES AT ALL. The line-42 fill had three possible routes, framed on the retired contract: retire the writables (needs operator approval), let the attestation OVERRIDE the computation (forbidden by that contract's own no-shadowing rule — "a figure that looks derived and is not"), or keep the computation AUTHORITATIVE and retain the attestation as a CROSS-CHECK. This is the third. It is the only route that loses nothing: a filer who already answered the whole line keeps a use for that answer, and the printed line is derived rather than transcribed.
WHAT IT IS FOR, and what it deliberately is NOT. It reports a disagreement; it does not resolve one. Nothing reads it to change a dollar, because the computed figure is the one the four printed legs support and an attestation cannot outvote its own components. Its value is diagnostic: a true here means either a leg intake is missing from the return or the filer's own addition is wrong, and both are worth surfacing.
FALSE WHEN THE ATTESTATION IS UNANSWERED, which is the ordinary case now that the legs compute — a filer who was never asked the whole-line question has nothing to disagree with. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part I total — rental real estate and royalty income (line 26)
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part I line 26 ("Total rental real estate and royalty income or (loss). Combine lines 24 and 25. … enter … on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5. Otherwise, include this amount in the total on line 41"): the Part I total = the §8582-limited net rental real-estate income (/rentalLimitedNetIncome — the rental portion of line 26 that flows to total income, a profit in full or the §8582-allowed portion of a passive loss as a negative) PLUS the net royalty income (/royaltyNetIncome — the nonpassive/portfolio royalty portion). Both addends are complete-safe (0 when no rental / no royalty), so this resolves complete for every return and equals 0 when neither Part I stream is present. This is the Part I summand of the Schedule E line-41 grand total (/scheduleETotalIncome). Result rounded to whole dollars (both addends are already whole-dollar, so the Round is a no-op). A THIRD addend, /rentalNonpassiveNet (the self-rental net rental income recharacterized NON-PASSIVE under Reg. §1.469-2(f)(6)): this profit was REMOVED from /rentalLimitedNetIncome (via the recharacterization case in activeEligibleNet / nonActiveNet) so line 26 would otherwise drop it; re-adding it here through the nonpassive channel keeps TOTAL income unchanged while the §8582 passive pool (/passiveIncomeTotal) is reduced. Complete-safe 0 when no self-rental is present.

Fact.Name: Schedule E grand total — total income or (loss) (line 41 → Schedule 1 line 5)
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 41 ("Total income or (loss). Combine lines 26, 32, 37, 39, and 40. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 5"): the single grand total that flows to Schedule 1 line 5 → Form 1040 line 8 total income. = the Part I total (/scheduleEPartINetIncome, line 26 = rental + royalty) + the Part II partnership / S-corp net (/scheduleEPartIINetIncome, line 32) + the Part III estate / trust net (/scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, line 37) + the Part IV REMIC residual-holder net (/scheduleERemicResidualNet, line 39) + the Part V net farm rental from Form 4835 (/farmRentalNetIncome, line 40). LINE 41 IS COMPLETE: line 39 (Part IV REMIC residual holdings) and line 40 (farm rental income from Form 4835) are computed, not 0-stubs. Both are now real summands — line 39 the attested Part IV combined columns (d) + (e), line 40 the attested Form 4835 bottom line — each complete-safe 0 unless claimed, so every prior scenario is byte-identical. All five lines the form names are present: line 41 = line 26 + line 32 + line 37 + line 39 + line 40. Every summand is complete-safe (0 when its part is absent), so this resolves complete for every return. This consolidates into one explicit number the four Schedule E streams that income.xml previously inlined into /totalIncome — VALUE-NEUTRAL: the sum is identical, so /totalIncome is byte-identical for every prior scenario. Result rounded to whole dollars.

Fact.Name: Any Schedule E activity is present on the return
Fact.Description: True when the return claims ANY Schedule E intake — Part I rental real estate (/claimsScheduleERentalIncome), Part I royalties (/claimsRoyaltyIncome), Part II partnership / S-corp K-1 (/claimsK1Income), Part III estate / trust K-1 (/claimsEstateTrustK1), or Part IV REMIC residual holder (/claimsRemicResidualInterest, added with the line-39 fill, 2026-07-31 — this Description previously said "the four Schedule E intakes" and the count is now open-ended on purpose, because EVERY new intake must land here). Every summand is an IsComplete-guarded gate that resolves Complete false when its writable is unanswered, so this is complete-safe false on every return that never entered a Schedule E intake — the state in which /scheduleETotalIncome is identically 0. Consumed by iraDeduction:/iraDeductionProvablyNotReducedByIncomeLimits as a REFUSAL signal (see the block comment above); it reports on no line and is NOT mef-exported.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) documents the filer received
Fact.Description: The collection of Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) documents the filer received as a beneficiary of an estate or trust, one item per printed K-1. It is the input-document twin of /formK1s (which holds the partnership and S corporation K-1s of Schedule E Part II): a Form 1041 K-1 is a different printed document with a different box layout, so it gets its own collection rather than sharing the partnership item shape. Each item carries the Part I and Part II identity boxes and the Part III boxes 1 through 14 exactly as printed. WIRED: the obligation this collection carried is discharged. Boxes 5, 6, 7, 8 and the box 9 codes A, B and C of every item now foot Schedule E Part III through /form1041K1s/*/estateTrustK1ItemNet, whose CollectionSum is /estateTrustK1IncomeAmount, the signed share the whole /estateTrust chain computes from. The return level attestation /writableEstateTrustK1Income is now the FALLBACK, taken only when no item answered any of those boxes (/estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered). A beneficiary with two estate or trust K-1s can now state them both. The item's other boxes still owe consumers of their own: box 1, 2a, 2b to Form 1040 lines 2b, 3b and 3a, boxes 3, 4a, 4b and 4c to Schedule D and its worksheets, box 10 to Schedule A line 16, box 11 to Schedule 1 and Form 6251, box 12 to Form 6251 line 2, box 13 to the payments lines and box 14 to Form 1040 line 2a, Form 4952 and Schedule E line 42.

Fact.Name: Form 1041 K-1 amended K-1 box
Fact.Description: The header checkbox "Amended K-1" on the Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) this beneficiary received, recorded with fact type Bool on the K-1 item. The statute anchor here is section 662 at SECTION level on purpose: section 662 is why this document exists at all, since it is the provision that charges a beneficiary with a share of the estate's or trust's distributable net income and so obliges the fiduciary to furnish this Schedule K-1. The box itself carries no dollar amount, so no subsection governs it. Intake only: it is a faithful record of what the payer printed, and no Form 1040 or Schedule E line reads it yet. The collection's own reconciliation obligation must land before any total consumes it. DISPOSITION reference-only: this input-document box is captured for the record and feeds no return computation by design; no consumer is owed. Fact.Name: Line 33 column (c): passive deduction or loss allowed on this estate or trust K-1

PRINT ONLY, and that is a STATED CHOICE rather than an unbuilt one.
