Fact.Name: Line 28 column (h): passive income from this Schedule K-1
Fact.Description: The positive part of ../passiveNetAfterSection179, which is this activity's Form 8582 Part V column (a) current year net income once the box 12 section 179 share is one of its passive activity deductions. The instructions for Schedule E say "If you have passive activity income, complete Part II, column (h), for that activity", and a passive activity's section 179 share is not a column (j) entry: the partner instructions route a passive share through Form 8582 instead, and ../section179ColumnJ is $0 on every passive K-1. So the post section 179 net is the figure column (h) prints. A publicly traded partnership contributes $0 here, because ../passiveNet already excludes it under section 469(k) and its overall gain is nonpassive column (k) income instead; and a nonpassive K-1 contributes $0 because ../passiveNet is $0 there. The second GreaterOf operand is /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor, the $0 constant, because the supported templates have no unary positive part. ADDED to it is ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedAgainstIncome: a publicly traded partnership whose passive box 10 loss is allowed against its own Schedule E-side income reports that much of the income as passive income here, and only the net gain portion in column (k) (the partner instructions' example prints 3,500 here beside 4,500 in column (k)); $0 on every other K-1.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (k): nonpassive income from this Schedule K-1
Fact.Description: ../partIINonpassivePart plus ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss plus ../section179ColumnJ. The three printed nonpassive columns and the graph's per K-1 nonpassive net stand in one identity: line 30 adds columns (h) and (k), line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) as the bracketed loss side, and line 32 combines them, so column (k) less column (i) less column (j) IS ../partIINonpassivePart. Columns (i) and (j) are the shipping ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss and ../section179ColumnJ, so adding those two back to the net recovers column (k) exactly and the printed row foots to line 32 by construction. Every case checks out: on nonpassive box 1 income it is the income itself, pre section 179 as the separately printed column (j) requires; on a nonpassive loss the two loss terms cancel and it is $0; on a passive K-1 all three terms are $0; and on a section 469(k) publicly traded partnership, whose column (j) is $0, it is the post section 179 overall gain, which is what scheduleE.xml says column (k) must print for that population. It is deliberately NOT a positive part of ../partIINonpassivePartBeforeSection179, which would print the pre section 179 gain there and disagree with line 32.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (i): nonpassive loss allowed from this Schedule K-1
Fact.Description: The figure Schedule E Part II line 28 column (i) prints for this K-1: ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss plus ../ptpDispositionReleasedLoss. A publicly traded partnership's overall loss released by the entire disposition of the partner's interest is a loss that is not from a passive activity, so it is a nonpassive loss allowed and prints in column (i), as any other released loss does. ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss cannot carry it: that fact feeds ../partIINonpassivePart, which the section 179 business income limitation reads, and the PTP release depends on the section 179 share, so the release is added here, in a print fact nothing else reads, and ../line28ColumnKNonpassiveIncome adds it back so the printed row foots to line 32. Non-negative, a magnitude: the printed column is a loss column. $0 on every K-1 that is not a disposed PTP and has no nonpassive loss.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (c): this K-1 is from a foreign partnership
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part II line 28 column (c) "Check if foreign partnership", one box per entity row. Nothing in the fact graph records whether a partnership is foreign: /formK1s carries the entity type (partnership or S corporation), the item D publicly traded flag, the box 1 amount and the basis and at-risk inputs, and none of them separates a domestic partnership from a foreign one. So this is an intake, not a derivation. It is a faithful record field: no Schedule E total consumes it, and the box is printed for the same reason the entity name and EIN on the same row are. IT IS ALSO THE ITEM'S FOREIGN MARKER: a Schedule K-1 (Form 8865) is issued only by a foreign partnership (Form 8865 is the return of U.S. persons with respect to certain foreign partnerships), so an item read from a Schedule K-1 (Form 8865) is written with this TRUE; no separate source-form field or collection exists.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (d): the partnership or S corporation EIN
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part II line 28 column (d) "Employer identification number", one per entity row. /formK1s/*/label is a stable human label for the item and is what column (a) prints; no fact carries the entity's EIN, so the number the IRS matches the Schedule K-1 against has to be taken as an intake. A faithful record field that no total consumes. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) item A (Partnership's employer identification number), Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) item A (Corporation's employer identification number).

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (e): a basis computation is required for this K-1
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part II line 28 column (e) "Check if basis computation is required". The form's own note fixes the trigger: a loss, a distribution, a disposition of stock, or a loan repayment from an S corporation. The graph knows only the first of those four. /formK1s/*/ordinaryIncome gives the loss case, but there is no distribution, stock disposition or shareholder loan repayment intake anywhere in the dictionary, so deriving the box from the loss alone would leave it unchecked on three of the four triggers. It is therefore a filer attestation. No total consumes it; it drives the attachment the note requires.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29a column (h) total passive income from the partnership and S corporation K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 29a, the Totals box under column (h) "Passive income from Schedule K-1": the CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/line28ColumnHPassiveIncome, the per K-1 column (h) entry the four line 28 entity rows print. Guarded on the completeness of /formK1s, so a return with no partnership or S corporation K-1 resolves Complete $0 rather than Incomplete.
IT IS A COLLECTION SUM AND NOT A POSITIVE PART OF THE POOLED NET, which is the whole reason it cannot be built at return level. /k1PassiveNet is the SIGNED aggregate: on a return with one passive K-1 earning $10,000 and another losing $4,000 the positive part of the aggregate is $6,000 while column (h) totals $10,000, and the $4,000 belongs in column (g). Summing the per item positive parts is the only expression that prints what the form prints.
Reported figure only: nothing computed reads it. The Part II amount that reaches income is /scheduleEPartIINetIncome.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29a column (k) total nonpassive income from the partnership and S corporation K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 29a, the Totals box under column (k) "Nonpassive income from Schedule K-1": the CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/line28ColumnKNonpassiveIncome, the per K-1 column (k) entry the four line 28 entity rows print. Guarded on the completeness of /formK1s, so a return with no K-1 resolves Complete $0.
WHY NOT /scheduleEPartIINetIncome or a positive part of it: column (k) is the GROSS nonpassive income before columns (i) and (j) are subtracted, and the per item leaf it sums adds those two legs back for exactly that reason. Line 30 adds columns (h) and (k), line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) as the bracketed loss, and line 32 combines them, so the column (i) and (j) amounts must appear once on the loss side rather than being netted away here.
Reported figure only: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29b column (g) total passive loss allowed on the partnership and S corporation K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 29b, the Totals box under column (g) "Passive loss allowed (attach Form 8582 if required)": /k1PassiveLoss less /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated. /k1PassiveLoss is the pooled passive K-1 loss magnitude entering the Form 8582 pool and /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated is that pool's ratable Part VII suspension for the K-1 leg, so their difference is the passive K-1 loss the section 469 limitation ALLOWS, which is what this box totals. Non negative, and printed positive because the line 31 box that adds it carries pre printed parentheses.
IT IS THE POOLED FIGURE, and the reader should not take it for the sum of the printed per row column (g) entries. The dictionary treats every passive K-1 as one activity in the pool: /k1PassiveNet is a signed aggregate, so a passive K-1 with income absorbs another passive K-1's loss inside it before the ratable allocation is taken. On a return with a single passive K-1 loss the two readings coincide. On a mixed return they do not, and the per row column (g) entries stay unbuilt for the same reason: splitting the Form 8582 Part VII allocation across items is a Multiply and a Divide the supported templates do not offer. Printed line 30 less line 31 still equals line 32 on the single activity case, and the mixed case is the open per item allocation.
PLUS THE PTP COLUMN (G) LOSS: /k1PtpSection1231AllowedScheduleELossTotal, the section 469(k) loss a publicly traded partnership's own box 10 gain allows. It never enters the Form 8582 pool, so it is added here beside the pooled figure, and it is $0 on every return without such a PTP.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29b column (j) total section 179 expense deduction from Form 4562
Fact.Description: The line 29b column (j) Totals box of Schedule E Part II: CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/section179ColumnJ, each K-1's own section 179 expense deduction as it reaches line 28 column (j). Line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) of line 29b as the bracketed loss side of line 32, so this is the column (j) addend of that total. It is NOT /k1Section179AllowedTotal: that fact is the taxpayer level Form 4562 Part I line 12 BEFORE allocation to the individual K-1s, and it stays nonzero on a passive or refused K-1 whose printed column (j) entry is zero. Gated on the completeness of /formK1s, so a return with no partnership or S corporation K-1 resolves a complete 0.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 29b column (i) total nonpassive loss allowed
Fact.Description: The line 29b column (i) Totals box of Schedule E Part II: CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/line28ColumnINonpassiveLossAllowed, each K-1's printed column (i) entry, so a disposed publicly traded partnership's released loss is in the total. Line 31 adds columns (g), (i) and (j) of line 29b. Gated on the completeness of /formK1s, so a return with no partnership or S corporation K-1 resolves a complete 0.

Fact.Name: Rental mortgage interest expense (complete safe)
Fact.Description:
WORKSHEET 5-1. When ../worksheet51Applies is true (a dwelling unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more, whose rental expenses are more than its rents), this line prints the part of the rental expense Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 allows, as named in the Derived body; otherwise it prints ../mortgageInterestRentalPart, the rental part of the whole-property intake, which is what the rest of this Description describes. The two cases are complements with no catch-all, so a unit whose worksheet test is undecided prints nothing rather than an unlimited figure.
Schedule E line 12 for THIS rental property as a total may consume it: the per property intake /rentalProperties/*/writableLine12MortgageInterestPaidToBanks when this item answered it, else 0. Fact.Name: Mortgage interest paid to banks for this rental property (Schedule E line 12)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 12 for THIS rental property: the mortgage interest paid to banks and other financial institutions on this rental real estate activity, as the filer enters it in this property column.
WIRED. The Schedule E line 20 total /rentalProperties/*/propertyTotalExpenses now carries this leaf through its complete-safe alias ../mortgageInterestExpense, so the printed column foots and the amount reaches ../propertyRawNet, /scheduleERentalNetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome. The obligation this Description used to carry is DISCHARGED. Read the alias, not this intake, from any new total. Form 1098 box 1 (Mortgage interest received from payer(s)/borrower(s)). Enter the total for the whole property, not only the rental part. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the graph deducts only the rental part: ../mortgageInterestExpense is this total times fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Physical address of this rental property (Schedule E line 1a)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 1a for THIS rental property: the physical address printed in the property column, as one line of text holding street, city, state and ZIP code. It is a label for the column, not a structured address: the return's own /address is the filer's mailing address and is a different thing.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered, and answering it neither creates nor limits a deduction.

Fact.Name: Type of property code for this rental property (Schedule E line 1b)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 1b for THIS rental property: the printed type of property code, 1 through 8, from the list the form prints below the table (1 single family residence, 2 multi family residence, 3 vacation or short term rental, 4 commercial, 5 land, 6 royalties, 7 self rental, 8 other).
Code 7 (self-rental) is READ: the Instructions for Schedule E define code 7 by the same condition ../selfRental and ../materiallyParticipatesInLessee together assert ("rent property to a trade or business in which you materially participated"), so entering code 7 makes ../recharacterizesSelfRental treat both flags as answered true even when the filer never separately answers them, and an explicit false answer on either flag does not override an entered code 7. Code 6 (royalties) on a rental property is refused (../codedAsRoyaltyProperty, /knockoutRentalPropertyCodedAsRoyalty): royalty property belongs in the royalty activity, not in rents. Every other code (1-5, 8) is RECORD ONLY: the building's recovery class is its own answer (../writableIsNonresidentialRealProperty), because the class turns on the share of rents from dwelling units, not on the printed type code.

Fact.Name: Fair rental days for this rental property (Schedule E line 2)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 2 for THIS rental property: the number of days in 2025 the property was rented at a fair rental price.
Read with ../writableLine2PersonalUseDays by ../dwellingUsedAsHome (the section 280A(d)(1) home test) and by /knockoutRentalDwellingRentedUnder15Days (the section 280A(g) rule). It is also the numerator of the section 280A(e)(1) rental use fraction (../rentalUseFairDays): the per property expense intakes are the totals for the whole property, and when the personal use days are above 0 each expense of the unit itself is multiplied by fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Personal use days for this rental property (Schedule E line 2)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 2 for THIS rental property: the number of days in 2025 the property was used personally.
Read with ../writableLine2FairRentalDays by ../dwellingUsedAsHome (the section 280A(d)(1) home test), which drives the two dwelling-unit refusals. An answer above 0 also divides the expenses: the per property expense intakes are the totals for the whole property, and each expense of the unit itself is multiplied by fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies). No vacation home limitation is computed here; a unit used as a home is refused where that limitation or the under-15-day rule would change the result.

Fact.Name: This property's expenses are divided between rental use and personal use (section 280A(e)(1))
Fact.Description: True when the Schedule E line 2 personal use days are answered and above 0: the dwelling unit was used for personal purposes on some day of the year, so only the rental part of each expense of the unit may be deducted. The per property expense intakes are the totals for the whole property, and every line that carries an expense of the unit itself is then multiplied by ../rentalUseFairDays over ../rentalUseAllocationTotalDays (fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days) and rounded to whole dollars, line by line. WHICH LINES ARE DIVIDED: line 7 cleaning and maintenance, line 9 insurance, line 12 mortgage interest, line 13 other interest, line 14 repairs, line 15 supplies, line 16 taxes, line 17 utilities, line 19 other expenses, and the computed line 18 depreciation of the building and the 5-year property (the section 179 deduction is not divided: its elected cost is already the business use cost). WHICH ARE NOT: line 5 advertising, line 6 auto and travel, line 8 commissions, line 10 legal and other professional fees and line 11 management fees, which are expenses of the rental activity alone and are deducted in full; and an answered ../depreciationOverride, which is the filer's own line 18 figure. Complete false when the personal use days are unanswered or 0, so a property with no personal use, and every return that never answers line 2, deducts exactly the amounts entered. When the personal use days are above 0 and the fair rental days are unanswered, every divided line is Incomplete: the rental part cannot be figured without them. KNOWN LIMITS: the fraction uses the two line 2 counts as entered. Pub. 527 counts a day rented at a fair price as a rental day for this division even when the owner also used the unit that day, and counts main-home days before or after renting as personal days for this division although line 2 leaves them out; a filer in either case enters the counts the division needs. The personal part of mortgage interest and taxes is not carried to Schedule A here.

Fact.Name: Fair rental days used in the section 280A(e)(1) fraction
Fact.Description: The Schedule E line 2 fair rental days, floored at 0: the numerator of the rental use fraction ../rentalUseAllocationApplies describes. Incomplete when the fair rental days are unanswered.

Fact.Name: Total days used in the section 280A(e)(1) fraction
Fact.Description: ../rentalUseFairDays plus the Schedule E line 2 personal use days: the denominator of the rental use fraction. Read only when ../rentalUseAllocationApplies is true, so the personal use days are above 0 and the denominator is never 0.

Fact.Name: This rental property was used as a home (section 280A(d)(1) personal-use test)
Fact.Description: True when both Schedule E line 2 day counts are answered and the personal use days exceed the greater of 14 days or 10 percent of the fair rental days: personal days above 14 AND ten times the personal days above the fair rental days, the same test in whole numbers. Complete false when either day count is unanswered, so no existing return moves. Read by /knockoutRentalDwellingRentedUnder15Days (through ../dwellingRentedUnder15DaysAsHome), by Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 and by the section 469(j)(10) routing (../section469j10Applies).

Fact.Name: This property was used as a home and rented fewer than 15 days (section 280A(g))
Fact.Description: True when ../dwellingUsedAsHome is true and the fair rental days on Schedule E line 2 are fewer than 15. Complete false otherwise, including when a day count is unanswered.

Fact.Name: This property is a dwelling unit to which section 280A(c)(5) applies, so section 469(j)(10) takes it out of the passive activity rules
Fact.Description: True when this property was used as a home (../dwellingUsedAsHome) and its fair rental days on Schedule E line 2 are 15 or more. Section 280A(c)(5) limits the deductions of a dwelling unit rented while the taxpayer uses it as a residence, whether or not the limit binds this year, and section 469(j)(10) then leaves any income, deduction, gain or loss allocable to that use out of the passive activity rules. The Form 8582 instructions list such a rental among the activities that are not passive. A home rented fewer than 15 days is the section 280A(g) population instead (../dwellingRentedUnder15DaysAsHome). Complete false when a day count is unanswered.

Fact.Name: A dwelling unit used as a home carries a prior-year unallowed passive loss its own income does not absorb
Fact.Description: True when ../section469j10Applies, a prior-year unallowed passive loss is answered above $0 (../priorYearUnallowedLoss), and this year's net after that loss (../netAfterPriorLoss) is below $0. Such a unit is a former passive activity: the carried loss is allowed against the unit's own income this year and the rest stays a passive loss for other passive income. This return does not split the rest back into the Form 8582 pool, so the return is refused (/knockoutRentalDwellingUsedAsHomePriorLossNotAbsorbed). When the unit's own income covers the carried loss, the unit's net after it is the nonpassive figure and the return files. Complete false when the carried loss is unanswered or $0.

Fact.Name: This dwelling unit's net leaves the Form 8582 pool for the Part I nonpassive channel
Fact.Description: True when ../section469j10Applies and the unit does not carry a prior-year unallowed passive loss its own income leaves unabsorbed (../section469j10PriorLossNotAbsorbed, refused). Read as the first test (after an entire disposition) by ../activeEligibleNet, ../nonActiveNet and ../atRiskDeductibleLossInPool, which then give $0, and by ../repAwareNonpassiveNet and ../repAwareNonpassiveMagiNet, which then carry ../section469j10NonpassiveNet to Schedule E line 26 and the Form 8582 line 6 modified adjusted gross income, the way a recharacterized self-rental profit goes.

Fact.Name: A dwelling unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more: its net outside the passive activity rules (section 469(j)(10))
Fact.Description: When ../section469j10Routes: ../netAfterPriorLoss, the unit's net after the at-risk limit (and, for a Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 unit, after the section 280A(c)(5) limit, since ../propertyRawNet is then ../section280ALimitedNet) less any prior-year unallowed passive loss the unit's own income absorbs as a former passive activity. A profit is income that no other passive loss may use; a loss (rents below the expenses that are always deductible) is deducted in full, with no Form 8582 share. $0 otherwise.

Fact.Name: The personal part of this property's real estate taxes, for Schedule A line 5b
Fact.Description: When the property's expenses are divided between rental and personal use (../rentalUseAllocationApplies): the whole-property taxes entered for Schedule E line 16 (../taxes, floored at $0) less their rental part (../taxesRentalPart, the taxes times fair rental days over the days used). Only the rental part may be deducted on Schedule E; the personal part is a state and local real estate tax deductible on Schedule A line 5b if the filer itemizes, as the Worksheet 5-1 Note says. It is taken before the Worksheet 5-1 limit, from the intakes and the day counts only, so Schedule A never reads the worksheet. $0 when there is no personal use or the taxes are unanswered. The Schedule E line 16 intake of a dwelling is read as its real estate taxes.

Fact.Name: The personal part of a home's Schedule E line 12 mortgage interest, for Schedule A line 8a
Fact.Description: When this property was used as a home (../dwellingUsedAsHome) and its expenses are divided (../rentalUseAllocationApplies): the whole-property mortgage interest paid to banks entered for Schedule E line 12 (../writableLine12MortgageInterestPaidToBanks, floored at $0) less its rental part (../mortgageInterestRentalPart). A rented home the filer used as a residence under section 280A(d)(1) can be a qualified residence, so the personal part is home mortgage interest for Schedule A line 8a (reported on Form 1098). The personal part of the mortgage interest on a property NOT used as a home is personal interest, not deductible, and is $0 here. Taken before the Worksheet 5-1 limit, from the intakes and the day counts only. $0 when the line 12 amount is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Total personal part of the rental properties' real estate taxes (Schedule A line 5b addend)
Fact.Description: The sum over the rental properties of ../realEstateTaxesPersonalPart, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome and a complete /rentalProperties; $0 otherwise. scheduleA adds it to Schedule A line 5b (and line 5d), so the filer does not enter the personal part of a rental's taxes there.

Fact.Name: Total personal part of the mortgage interest on rental properties used as a home (Schedule A line 8a addend)
Fact.Description: The sum over the rental properties of ../homeMortgageInterestPersonalPart, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome and a complete /rentalProperties; $0 otherwise. scheduleA adds it to Schedule A line 8a, so the filer does not enter the personal part of a rented home's mortgage interest there.

Fact.Name: This rented home carries personal mortgage interest that reaches Schedule A
Fact.Description: True when ../homeMortgageInterestPersonalPart is above $0. Counted by /knockoutRentalHomesMortgageInterestOnMoreThanOneSecondHome.

Fact.Name: Knockout: two or more rented homes carry personal mortgage interest
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. Two or more of your rental properties are homes you also used, and each has mortgage interest for the days you used it. Only your main home and one other home you choose can be qualified residences, and this return cannot yet ask which one you choose.
Fires when more than one rental property has ../homeWithPersonalMortgageInterest true (Count over the collection, gated on /claimsScheduleERentalIncome).

Fact.Name: An itemizer's Worksheet 5-1 line 2e exceeds the rents of a dwelling unit used as a home
Fact.Description: True when Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 applies to this unit (../worksheet51Applies), the filer confirms itemizing (/writableWorksheet51ElectsToItemize), and line 1 (the rents) is below line 2e, which for an itemizer includes the rental part of the mortgage interest (line 2a) and real estate taxes (line 2b). The unit's limited net (../section280ALimitedNet) is figured with the standard-deduction line 2e so that Schedule E line 21 and adjusted gross income never wait on the itemize election, so this itemizer's larger loss is not figured, and the return is refused (/knockoutRentalDwellingUsedAsHomeLoss). Incomplete while the election is unanswered on such a unit.

Fact.Name: Operating expenses carried over from the 2024 Worksheet 5-1 for this dwelling unit (line 4d)
Fact.Description: Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 line 4d: the operating expenses of this dwelling unit that last year's worksheet did not allow (last year's line 7a). Asked only for a unit used as a home and rented 15 days or more. Enter 0 if none. Unanswered counts as 0.

Fact.Name: Depreciation carried over from the 2024 Worksheet 5-1 for this dwelling unit (line 6c)
Fact.Description: Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 line 6c, the depreciation part only: the depreciation of this dwelling unit that last year's worksheet did not allow (last year's line 7b). A casualty or theft loss carried from last year's worksheet is not entered here; it is answered on ../writableWorksheet51CasualtyOrTheftLoss. Enter 0 if none. Unanswered counts as 0.

Fact.Name: Casualty or theft loss on this dwelling unit (Worksheet 5-1 lines 2c, 6a and 6c)
Fact.Description: Did this dwelling unit have a casualty or theft loss in 2025, or do you have a casualty or theft loss on it carried over from your 2024 Worksheet 5-1? Asked only for a unit used as a home, rented 15 days or more, whose rental expenses are more than its rents. Yes is refused (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51CasualtyLossUnbuilt): lines 2c and 6a need a worksheet version of Form 4684 figured on AGI without the unit. Unanswered leaves the unit's net Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4d, complete-safe
Fact.Description: ../writableWorksheet51Line4dOperatingCarryover floored at $0 when answered, else $0.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 6c (depreciation carryover), complete-safe
Fact.Description: ../writableWorksheet51Line6cDepreciationCarryover floored at $0 when answered, else $0.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 1: rents received
Fact.Description: This property's Schedule E line 3 amount (../scheduleELine3Income): the rents received, plus any Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to the property, which the Schedule E line 21 net of this unit also starts from.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2d: direct rental expenses
Fact.Description: The expenses of the rental activity alone, deducted in full: Schedule E line 5 advertising, line 6 auto and travel, line 8 commissions, line 10 legal and other professional fees and line 11 management fees (the lines IRC 280A(e)(1) does not divide).

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4a: rental part of the operating expenses
Fact.Description: The rental parts of Schedule E line 7 cleaning and maintenance, line 9 insurance, line 14 repairs, line 15 supplies, line 17 utilities and line 19 other expenses: the expenses of operating or maintaining the unit itself.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 6b: rental part of the depreciation
Fact.Description: ../depreciationExpenseBeforeSection179: the rental part of this year's depreciation of the unit, before any section 179 deduction (a worksheet unit that elects section 179 is refused).

Fact.Name: Rental part of all this unit's expenses and depreciation, with the Worksheet 5-1 carryovers
Fact.Description: Line 2d plus line 4a plus the rental parts of the line 12 and line 13 interest and the line 16 taxes, plus line 6b, plus the line 4d and line 6c carryovers. This is the total the worksheet's third entry question compares with the rents, and it does not depend on the itemize election: the election only moves interest and taxes between line 2 and line 4. The carryovers are counted because the limit applies to an expense carried forward exactly as to this year's.

Fact.Name: Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1 applies to this property (IRC 280A(c)(5))
Fact.Description: True when this property was used as a home (../dwellingUsedAsHome), was rented at a fair price 15 days or more, and ../worksheet51RentalExpensesTotal is more than the rents (../worksheet51Line1): the three entry questions of Worksheet 5-1. Complete false for every property not used as a home, so no other rental moves. When it is true the printed expense lines, line 21 and the Form 8582 inputs of the unit follow the worksheet.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2a: the deductible home mortgage interest from Schedule E line 12
Fact.Description: For a filer who elects to itemize (/writableWorksheet51ElectsToItemize true): the rental part of the line 12 interest (../mortgageInterestRentalPart) times the Pub. 936 debt-limit fraction Schedule A figures for all the filer's home mortgage interest (scheduleA:/scheduleAMortgageDebtLimitFractionPerThousand, Table 1 line 14 stored times 1,000), rounded to whole dollars; $0 without reading the fraction when there is no such interest. For a filer who takes the standard deduction: $0 (the interest goes to line 4b). Incomplete while the election is unanswered. THE CONTRACT: the line 12 and line 13 intakes of a dwelling unit used as a home are interest on loans secured by the unit and used to buy, build or substantially improve it, and the Schedule A average balance answers include this unit's debt, as Pub. 936 counts all home acquisition debt together.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2a: the deductible home mortgage interest from Schedule E line 13
Fact.Description: For a filer who elects to itemize (/writableWorksheet51ElectsToItemize true): the rental part of the line 13 interest (../otherInterestRentalPart) times the Pub. 936 debt-limit fraction Schedule A figures for all the filer's home mortgage interest (scheduleA:/scheduleAMortgageDebtLimitFractionPerThousand, Table 1 line 14 stored times 1,000), rounded to whole dollars; $0 without reading the fraction when there is no such interest. For a filer who takes the standard deduction: $0 (the interest goes to line 4b). Incomplete while the election is unanswered. THE CONTRACT: the line 12 and line 13 intakes of a dwelling unit used as a home are interest on loans secured by the unit and used to buy, build or substantially improve it, and the Schedule A average balance answers include this unit's debt, as Pub. 936 counts all home acquisition debt together.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2a: rental part of deductible home mortgage interest
Fact.Description: ../worksheet51Line2aLine12 plus ../worksheet51Line2aLine13.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4b: the excess mortgage interest from Schedule E line 12
Fact.Description: The rental part of the line 12 interest less the part line 2a took: all of it for a standard-deduction filer, the part above the Pub. 936 limit for an itemizer.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4b: the excess mortgage interest from Schedule E line 13
Fact.Description: The rental part of the line 13 interest less the part line 2a took: all of it for a standard-deduction filer, the part above the Pub. 936 limit for an itemizer.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2b: rental part of deductible real estate taxes
Fact.Description: For a filer who elects to itemize: the Line 2b Worksheet line 9, the smaller of the rental part of this unit's real estate taxes (../taxesRentalPart, worksheet line 6) or the room left under the $40,000 ($20,000 married filing separately) limit after the filer's personal state and local taxes (/worksheet51Line2bWorksheetLine8); $0 without reading Schedule A when the unit has no taxes. For a standard-deduction filer: $0 (the taxes go to line 4c). Incomplete while the election is unanswered. The worksheet's Step 1 test (total not more than $40,000) gives the same figure, so the worksheet is run for every itemizer. The printed worksheet has no MAGI phase-down; an itemizer whose SALT MAGI is above the phase-down threshold is refused (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51SaltPhasedownUnbuilt).

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4c: rental part of excess real estate taxes
Fact.Description: The rental part of this unit's real estate taxes less line 2b: all of it for a standard-deduction filer, the Line 2b Worksheet line 10 for an itemizer.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2c: rental part of deductible casualty and theft losses
Fact.Description: $0 once ../writableWorksheet51CasualtyOrTheftLoss is answered; Incomplete while it is unanswered. A Yes answer is refused (/knockoutRentalWorksheet51CasualtyLossUnbuilt), so $0 is the figure on every return that files.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 2e: fully deductible rental expenses
Fact.Description: Lines 2a + 2b + 2c + 2d.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 3
Fact.Description: Line 1 less line 2e; zero or less enters $0.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4e
Fact.Description: Lines 4a + 4b (both interest lines) + 4c + 4d.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f: allowable operating expenses
Fact.Description: The smaller of line 3 or line 4e.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 5
Fact.Description: Line 3 less line 4f; zero or less enters $0.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 6d
Fact.Description: Line 6a ($0: a casualty on the unit is refused) + line 6b + line 6c.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 6e: allowable depreciation
Fact.Description: The smaller of line 5 or line 6d. Printed on Schedule E line 18 for a worksheet unit.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 7a: carried over to next year
Fact.Description: Line 4e less line 4f: the amount the filer enters on next year's worksheet (line 4d). Meaningful only when ../worksheet51Applies is true.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 7b: carried over to next year
Fact.Description: Line 6d less line 6e: the amount the filer enters on next year's worksheet (line 6c). Meaningful only when ../worksheet51Applies is true.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 7 cleaning and maintenance
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 7 cleaning and maintenance: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 9 insurance
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 9 insurance: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to the line 12 mortgage interest line 4b carries
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to the line 12 mortgage interest line 4b carries: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to the line 13 interest line 4b carries
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to the line 13 interest line 4b carries: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 14 repairs
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 14 repairs: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 15 supplies
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 15 supplies: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to the line 16 taxes line 4c carries
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to the line 16 taxes line 4c carries: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 17 utilities
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 17 utilities: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to line 19 other expenses
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to line 19 other expenses: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: Worksheet 5-1 line 4f allocated to the line 4d carryover, printed on line 19
Fact.Description: The part of line 4f allocated to the line 4d carryover, printed on line 19: the smaller of that expense or what is left of line 4f after the expenses ahead of it. The allocation runs in printed Schedule E line order (lines 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19, then the line 4d carryover), one allocation Pub. 527 allows ("in any way you wish"); the allocated amounts add up to line 4f.

Fact.Name: This property's net after the section 280A(c)(5) limit (Pub. 527 Worksheet 5-1)
Fact.Description: When ../worksheet51Applies is true: line 1 less lines 2e, 4f and 6e, which is the smaller of $0 or line 1 less line 2e (when the expenses are more than the rents, lines 4f and 6e together use up all of line 3). It is figured with the standard-deduction line 2e (lines 2c and 2d), so it never reads the itemize election: an itemizer's larger line 2e gives the same $0 whenever line 1 covers it, and when it does not the itemizer is refused (../worksheet51ItemizerLossRefused). A negative figure (lines 2c and 2d above the rents) is deducted in full outside the passive activity rules (IRC 469(j)(10), ../section469j10NonpassiveNet). $0 when the worksheet does not apply (such a property's net is the ordinary body of ../propertyRawNet). Incomplete while ../writableWorksheet51CasualtyOrTheftLoss is unanswered.

Fact.Name: A Worksheet 5-1 unit with a casualty or theft loss
Fact.Description: True when ../worksheet51Applies is true and ../writableWorksheet51CasualtyOrTheftLoss is Yes. Incomplete on a worksheet unit while that question is unanswered.

Fact.Name: A Worksheet 5-1 unit that elects section 179
Fact.Description: True when ../worksheet51Applies is true and this property elects a section 179 deduction (../electsSection179).

Fact.Name: A Worksheet 5-1 unit with real estate taxes on line 2b
Fact.Description: True when ../worksheet51Applies is true and the rental part of the unit's real estate taxes is above $0: the unit whose line 2b the Line 2b Worksheet figures for an itemizer.

Fact.Name: Qualified joint venture box for this rental property (Schedule E line 2)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 2 QJV box for THIS rental property: true when the filer meets the requirements to treat the property as a qualified joint venture of spouses and elects to do so.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered, and answering it neither creates nor limits a deduction. The graph does not split this property between the two spouses: the whole column stays one activity in every computed Schedule E line, and the box only reports the election the filer made.

Fact.Name: Auto and travel expense for this rental property (Schedule E line 6)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 6 for THIS rental property: the deductible auto and travel expense of this rental real estate activity, as the filer enters it in this property column.
WIRED. The Schedule E line 20 total /rentalProperties/*/propertyTotalExpenses now carries this leaf through its complete-safe alias ../autoAndTravelExpense, so the printed column foots and the amount reaches ../propertyRawNet, /scheduleERentalNetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome. The obligation this Description used to carry is DISCHARGED. Read the alias, not this intake, from any new total. Enter the total for the whole property. This line is an expense of the rental activity alone, so it is deducted in full even when the property was also used for personal purposes (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Cleaning and maintenance expense for this rental property (Schedule E line 7)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 7 for THIS rental property: the cleaning and maintenance paid for this rental real estate activity, as the filer enters it in this property column.
WIRED. The Schedule E line 20 total /rentalProperties/*/propertyTotalExpenses now carries this leaf through its complete-safe alias ../cleaningAndMaintenanceExpense, so the printed column foots and the amount reaches ../propertyRawNet, /scheduleERentalNetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome. The obligation this Description used to carry is DISCHARGED. Read the alias, not this intake, from any new total. Enter the total for the whole property, not only the rental part. When the property was also used for personal purposes (Schedule E line 2 personal use days above 0), the graph deducts only the rental part: ../cleaningAndMaintenanceExpense is this total times fair rental days over fair rental days plus personal use days (IRC 280A(e)(1); see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Commissions for this rental property (Schedule E line 8)
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 8 for THIS rental property: the commissions paid on this rental real estate activity, as the filer enters it in this property column.
WIRED. The Schedule E line 20 total /rentalProperties/*/propertyTotalExpenses now carries this leaf through its complete-safe alias ../commissionsExpense, so the printed column foots and the amount reaches ../propertyRawNet, /scheduleERentalNetIncome, /scheduleETotalIncome and /totalIncome. The obligation this Description used to carry is DISCHARGED. Read the alias, not this intake, from any new total. Enter the total for the whole property. This line is an expense of the rental activity alone, so it is deducted in full even when the property was also used for personal purposes (see ../rentalUseAllocationApplies).

Fact.Name: Total of the per property Schedule E line 21 losses, as positive amounts
Fact.Description: The CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/rawLoss, guarded on the collection so a return with no rental property resolves Complete 0. Each summand is that property's line 21 loss as a POSITIVE magnitude, max(0, minus ../propertyRawNet). Structural helper for line 24: the signed total /scheduleERentalNetIncome plus this loss total equals the sum of the POSITIVE line 21 amounts, since a loss property contributes its negative net and the same magnitude back, and a profitable property contributes its net and 0. It reports on no line of its own.

Fact.Name: The royalty activity is not an oil or gas working interest
Fact.Description: The complement of /royaltyIsWorkingInterest: true whenever the return's single royalty activity is NOT a working (operating) interest in an oil or gas well, which is the population Schedule E Part I line 4 reports. /royaltyIsWorkingInterest is itself the complete safe gate (All of /claimsRoyaltyIncome, IsComplete and the attestation), so this resolves TRUE on every return that never answered the attestation, exactly as the module's own unanswered behaviour intends. Structural helper: it exists so /royaltyReportedOnScheduleE can be an All of two Bool facts.

Fact.Name: The royalty activity is reported on Schedule E Part I line 4
Fact.Description: True when the return claims royalty income (/claimsRoyaltyIncome) AND that royalty is not an oil or gas working interest (/royaltyIsNotWorkingInterest). This is the gate the Schedule E line 4 population needs: the Instructions for Schedule E exclude operating interests from line 4 in terms, and scheduleE.xml already routes a working interest off Schedule E and onto Schedule C through /workingInterestNetProfit, leaving /royaltyNetIncome at 0. Nothing computed changes with this fact; it decides only whether a royalty figure prints in Part I.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to the Schedule E royalty activity
Fact.Description: The portion of Form 4797 Part IV line 35 recapture attributable to a deduction taken for this return-level Schedule E royalty activity. The filer allocates the recapture here when the deduction was taken on Schedule E line 4; the amount is a destination for the Form 4797 reconciliation, not a recomputation of the recapture. A royalty is a single activity in this dictionary, so one allocation amount is the correct grain.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to the Schedule E royalty activity
Fact.Description: The answered royalty allocation when the return claims royalty income, otherwise $0. This raw destination is included in form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal even while the return's allocation gate is false; the gate then refuses rather than dropping an unconfirmed recapture. The separate ../royaltyForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg carries the amount into the royalty activity only after Form 4797 confirms the allocation.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture carried to the Schedule E royalty activity
Fact.Description: The royalty allocation carried into the royalty activity only when the royalty is reported on Schedule E and form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated is TRUE. An unanswered or mismatched allocation contributes $0 here; the Form 4797 refusal flag keeps the return Incomplete, so no recapture silently disappears.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture allocated to Schedule E destinations
Fact.Description: The sum of /rentalProperties/*/form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated when Schedule E rental income is claimed plus /royaltyForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated for the return-level royalty activity. This is the complete Schedule E destination term in form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal. Each carried destination leg separately requires form4797:/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated to be TRUE.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 23a: total line-3 amounts for all rental properties
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 23a, the total of every amount printed on line 3: the CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/scheduleELine3Income, guarded on the collection so a return with no rental property resolves Complete 0 rather than Incomplete. This totals exactly what the form shows, because column n of line 3 prints /rentalProperties/[n]/scheduleELine3Income (the printed column axis for this form is /rentalProperties, dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv). Reported figure only: no computed Schedule E line reads it, and the aggregate that flows to income is /scheduleERentalNetIncome.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 23b: total royalties received for all royalty properties
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 23b: the gross royalty income the return reports on line 4, /writableRoyaltyIncome, when the royalty is reported on Schedule E at all (/royaltyReportedOnScheduleE), else 0. Two states make it 0: no royalty is claimed, and an oil or gas working interest, whose net scheduleE.xml routes to Schedule C through /workingInterestNetProfit and which the line 4 instruction excludes from the line in terms. scheduleE.xml models ONE return level royalty activity, so this return level total is exact even while the three line 4 COLUMN boxes stay unmapped for want of a royalty column axis. Reported figure only: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 23c: total mortgage interest reported on line 12
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 23c: the total of all amounts reported on line 12 for all properties. Sums the complete safe ../mortgageInterestExpense over /rentalProperties, so a property that never answered line 12 contributes 0 rather than making the total Incomplete, and resolves 0 for a return with no rental properties. This is a true total of what line 12 prints: it does not depend on the line 20 rewiring the line 12 intake owes.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 23d: total depreciation or depletion for all properties
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 23d, the total of every amount printed on line 18: the CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/depreciationExpense, guarded on the collection so a return with no rental property resolves Complete 0. It totals exactly the printed line 18 cells, because column n of line 18 already prints /rentalProperties/[n]/depreciationExpense and the printed column axis for this form is /rentalProperties (dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv). SCOPE, stated rather than left silent: the royalty activity has no printed column here, and its line 18 depletion is not separately held by the graph (the greater of cost and percentage depletion is computed inside the rounded /royaltyActivityNet, so recovering it by subtraction would carry a rounding residue). A royalty return therefore shows only the rental depreciation on this line, which is what its printed line 18 cells show. Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 23e: total expenses for all properties
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 23e, the total of every amount printed on line 20: the CollectionSum of /rentalProperties/*/propertyTotalExpenses, guarded on the collection so a return with no rental property resolves Complete 0. It totals exactly the printed line 20 cells, because column n of line 20 already prints /rentalProperties/[n]/propertyTotalExpenses and the printed column axis for this form is /rentalProperties (dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv). SCOPE, stated rather than left silent: the royalty activity has no printed column here, and its line 20 total is not separately held by the graph (/writableRoyaltyExpenses excludes depletion by design and the depletion term lives inside the rounded /royaltyActivityNet), so a royalty return shows only the rental totals on this line, which is what its printed line 20 cells show. Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 25: the royalty loss from line 21, as a positive amount
Fact.Description:
The royalty half of Schedule E line 25 ("Losses. Add royalty losses from line 21 and rental real estate losses from line 22"), as a POSITIVE magnitude: the negative of /royaltyNetIncome when that is a loss, and $0 otherwise. It is the POST-fork, section 465 allowed figure, which is what line 25 prints: $0 for a working interest activity (whose net is routed to Schedule C and whose /royaltyNetIncome is $0 by the fork) and, for an investment royalty, the loss the at-risk rules ALLOW rather than the raw loss - the suspended remainder is carried out on /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss and never printed on this line. DISTINCT from /royaltyRawLoss, which is the PRE-limitation, PRE-fork magnitude that Form 6198 line 5 wants.
Schedule E lines 24, 25 and 26 split positives from losses on the printed form and this module assembles them as one sum; this is checked on a negative royalty net. It was not safe: /scheduleELine24Income added /royaltyNetIncome raw, so a royalty loss would have made line 24 - an income-only line - print a NEGATIVE, and line 25 would have printed $0 instead of the loss. This fact is the cancelling term that fixes both, exactly as /rentalRawLossTotal cancels the rental negatives inside the same sum. Complete-safe $0 on every return with no royalty loss, so no committed scenario moves. Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 24: income, the positive line 21 amounts added
Fact.Description:
Schedule E line 24: the positive amounts shown on line 21, added, with no losses included. It is /scheduleERentalNetIncome (the signed CollectionSum of the per property line 21 nets) plus /rentalRawLossTotal (the same properties' loss magnitudes, which cancels every negative summand) plus /royaltyNetIncome plus /scheduleELine25RoyaltyLoss (the royalty loss magnitude, which cancels the royalty negative the same way). Including the royalty net is what makes line 24 minus line 25 equal the line 26 total /scheduleEPartINetIncome, which carries the royalty net. Reported figure only.
CORRECTED 2026-08-30. The sentence this replaces read "The royalty term belongs here and is never negative: scheduleE.xml refuses a net royalty loss through /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss and resolves /royaltyNetIncome to 0 for an oil or gas working interest, whose net is routed to Schedule C." The second half is still true; the first half stopped being true the moment the section 465 at-risk gate made a royalty loss fileable. Without the new cancelling term a royalty loss of $4,000 would have printed line 24 = -4,000 on a line the form defines as income only, and line 25 = 24 minus 26 = 0 instead of 4,000. With it, line 24 = 0, line 25 = 4,000 and line 26 = -4,000, which is what the printed form says. NO COMMITTED SCENARIO MOVES: the new term is $0 on every return whose royalty net is not a loss, and no committed scenario carries one.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 25: total losses, printed as a positive amount
Fact.Description: Schedule E line 25: the royalty losses from line 21 and the rental real estate losses from line 22, added, printed inside the line's parentheses as a positive total. The form defines line 26 as lines 24 and 25 combined, so this is line 24 (/scheduleELine24Income) minus line 26 (/scheduleEPartINetIncome), and it is exact rather than a restatement: what line 26 carries for a loss property is precisely the loss the Form 8582 and Form 6198 chain ALLOWS, which is what line 22 prints and line 25 totals. On the published examples it reproduces the allowed loss (Pub 527 active participation example, 4,000; the i8582 line 9 example, 25,000 of a 42,000 loss). A ROYALTY LOSS NOW CONTRIBUTES, corrected 2026-08-30: the sentence this replaces read "A royalty loss never contributes: scheduleE.xml refuses one through /knockoutRoyaltyActivityLoss", and the section 465 at-risk gate built that day makes a royalty loss fileable, so the line prints it. The arithmetic needed no change here - /scheduleELine24Income gained the cancelling term /scheduleELine25RoyaltyLoss, and this subtraction then recovers the royalty loss automatically alongside the rental losses. What line 25 prints for the royalty is the at-risk ALLOWED loss; the section 465 suspended remainder leaves on /royaltyAtRiskSuspendedLoss and is not printed on the schedule. Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 27 answered No
Fact.Description: The complement of /writableScheduleELine27PriorYearOrUnreimbursedLoss, the writable that carries the line 27 question: is the return reporting a loss not allowed in a prior year because of the at-risk or basis limitations, a prior year unallowed passive activity loss that was not reported on Form 8582, or unreimbursed partnership expenses? This fact is TRUE exactly when that answer is No, and it is what the line 27 No box prints. Mirrors /scheduleHLine27IsNo and /scheduleFDidNotMateriallyParticipate: one writable carries the question and a Not carries the second printed box, so the two boxes cannot both be checked and neither is checked while the question is unanswered. The writable is authored for this same form, which prints the Yes box from it.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 30: the line 29a column (h) and column (k) income totals added
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 30 ("Add columns (h) and (k) of line 29a"): the passive income total /k1Line29aColumnHPassiveIncomeTotal plus the nonpassive income total /k1Line29aColumnKNonpassiveIncomeTotal. Both operands are guarded on /formK1s, so line 30 resolves Complete $0 on a return with no partnership or S corporation K-1.
Reported figure only: line 32 (/scheduleEPartIINetIncome) is computed from the per K-1 chain rather than from lines 30 and 31, and nothing reads this fact.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 31: the line 29b column (g), (i) and (j) loss totals added
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 31 ("Add columns (g), (i), and (j) of line 29b"): the allowed passive loss total /k1Line29bColumnGPassiveLossAllowedTotal plus the column (i) total /k1Line29bColumnINonpassiveLossAllowedTotal (which carries a disposed publicly traded partnership's released loss) plus the section 179 total /k1Line29bSection179ColumnJTotal. NON NEGATIVE, a magnitude: the printed box carries pre printed parentheses, so the figure entered there is the size of the loss and the parentheses supply the sign, exactly as the sibling column (i) box takes the non negative /k1Line29bColumnINonpassiveLossAllowedTotal.
THE COLUMN (G) OPERAND IS POOLED, so this total inherits the caveat that fact's Description states: on a return whose passive K-1s include both income and loss, the pooled allowed loss is not the sum of the per row column (g) entries, which stay unbuilt. Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34a column (d) total passive income from the estate and trust K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 34a, the Totals box under column (d) "Passive income from Schedule K-1": the positive part of /estatePassiveNet, this estate or trust interest's signed contribution to the section 8582 pool. A passive share that is income lands here; a passive share that is a loss lands in column (c) and a nonpassive share contributes nothing here at all, because /estatePassiveNet is $0 for it. The positive part needs the staged $0 constant /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor as the second GreaterOf operand.
scheduleE.xml reduces the whole of Part III to a single SIGNED share (/estateTrustK1IncomeAmount), so exactly one side of the Part III split can be non zero on any return. The four column totals therefore reconstruct that signed share exactly: (d) plus (f) less (c) less (e) is /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, which is what the staged lines 35 and 36 already compute from it. The share is now FOOTED FROM THE K-1 ROWS — CollectionSum over /form1041K1s of each K-1's boxes 5, 6, 7 and 8 less its box 9 codes A, B and C — with the old return level attestation as the fallback. Several K-1s may now be stated; they NET into the one signed share before the split, so this reconstruction identity is unchanged and the printed page still foots.
Reported figure only: line 37 (/scheduleEPartIIINetIncome) is computed from the share rather than from these boxes.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34a column (f) total other income from the estate and trust K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 34a, the Totals box under column (f) "Other income from Schedule K-1": the positive part of /estateTrustNonpassivePart, the NONPASSIVE half of the Part III line 37 amount. A nonpassive share that is income lands here; a nonpassive share that is a loss lands in column (e) and a passive share contributes nothing here, because /estateTrustNonpassivePart is $0 for it. The positive part needs the staged $0 constant /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor as the second GreaterOf operand.
scheduleE.xml reduces the whole of Part III to a single SIGNED share (/estateTrustK1IncomeAmount), so exactly one side of the Part III split can be non zero on any return. The four column totals therefore reconstruct that signed share exactly: (d) plus (f) less (c) less (e) is /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, which is what the staged lines 35 and 36 already compute from it. The share is now FOOTED FROM THE K-1 ROWS — CollectionSum over /form1041K1s of each K-1's boxes 5, 6, 7 and 8 less its box 9 codes A, B and C — with the old return level attestation as the fallback. Several K-1s may now be stated; they NET into the one signed share before the split, so this reconstruction identity is unchanged and the printed page still foots.
Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34b column (c) total passive deduction or loss allowed on the estate and trust K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 34b, the Totals box under column (c) "Passive deduction or loss allowed (attach Form 8582 if required)": /estatePassiveLoss less /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated. /estatePassiveLoss is the passive estate or trust loss magnitude entering the section 8582 pool and /estatePassiveSuspendedAllocated is that pool's ratable Part VII suspension for the estate leg, so their difference is the passive loss the section 469 limitation ALLOWS. NON NEGATIVE, a magnitude: the line 36 box that adds it carries pre printed parentheses.
EXACT HERE, unlike its Part II twin: the graph reduces Part III to ONE signed share, so there is no second estate activity left inside the aggregate whose income could absorb this loss before the allocation is taken. When several K-1 rows are stated they net into that one share FIRST, at /estateTrustK1IncomeAmount, so a second entity's income does absorb a first entity's loss — which is what section 469 does inside a single passive pool anyway, and the identity this box relies on is untouched.
