The four column totals therefore reconstruct that signed share exactly: (d) plus (f) less (c) less (e) is /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, which is what the staged lines 35 and 36 already compute from it. The share is now FOOTED FROM THE K-1 ROWS — CollectionSum over /form1041K1s of each K-1's boxes 5, 6, 7 and 8 less its box 9 codes A, B and C — with the old return level attestation as the fallback. Several K-1s may now be stated; they NET into the one signed share before the split, so this reconstruction identity is unchanged and the printed page still foots.
Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 34b column (e) total nonpassive deduction or loss from the estate and trust K-1s
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part III line 34b, the Totals box under column (e) "Deduction or loss from Schedule K-1": the positive part of /scheduleELine34bColumnENonpassiveLossNegated, which is minus /estateTrustNonpassivePart. A NONPASSIVE share that is a loss prints its magnitude here; a nonpassive share that is income, and any passive share, leave the box at $0. NON NEGATIVE, a magnitude: the line 36 box that adds it carries pre printed parentheses, exactly as the staged /scheduleELine36EstateTrustLossColumns is written.
scheduleE.xml reduces the whole of Part III to a single SIGNED share (/estateTrustK1IncomeAmount), so exactly one side of the Part III split can be non zero on any return. The four column totals therefore reconstruct that signed share exactly: (d) plus (f) less (c) less (e) is /scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, which is what the staged lines 35 and 36 already compute from it. The share is now FOOTED FROM THE K-1 ROWS — CollectionSum over /form1041K1s of each K-1's boxes 5, 6, 7 and 8 less its box 9 codes A, B and C — with the old return level attestation as the fallback. Several K-1s may now be stated; they NET into the one signed share before the split, so this reconstruction identity is unchanged and the printed page still foots.
Reported figure only.

Fact.Name: The estate and trust NONPASSIVE half of Part III with its sign flipped, the operand of the column (e) total
Fact.Description:
Zero less /estateTrustNonpassivePart: the sign flipped Part III nonpassive half. It exists only as the first operand of /scheduleELine34bColumnEDeductionOrLossTotal, which floors it at zero to recover the column (e) loss magnitude from the signed nonpassive half. The supported templates have no unary negation and no unary positive part, so the pair is Subtract(0, x) then GreaterOf(that, 0); the minuend is the staged $0 constant /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor because dollar_subtract takes fact paths, not literals.
IT IS NOT A PRINTED FIGURE and it is NEGATIVE whenever the estate or trust nonpassive half is income. Nothing but the column (e) total reads it.

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III line 35, the estate and trust INCOME columns (d) plus (f) of line 34a
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part III line 35 ("Add columns (d) and (f) of line 34a"): column (d) "Passive income from Schedule K-1" plus column (f) "Other income from Schedule K-1", the two INCOME columns of the Part III totals row. The graph reduces the whole of Part III to a single SIGNED share (/estateTrustK1IncomeAmount, footed from the /form1041K1s rows, or the filer's attestation when no row answers a Part III box), so exactly one side of the Part III split can be non-zero on any return: an income share puts its whole amount on line 35 and leaves line 36 at zero (the passive / nonpassive split is immaterial, since line 35 sums both column (d) and column (f)), and a loss share leaves line 35 at zero. Line 35 is therefore the positive part of line 37, GreaterOf(/scheduleEPartIIINetIncome, $0). It is taken off the ROUNDED line-37 fact rather than off the unrounded /estateTrustNonpassivePart and /estatePassiveNet halves precisely so that line 35 minus line 36 reproduces line 37 to the cent, which is the printed form's own invariant ("Combine lines 35 and 36").

Fact.Name: Schedule E Part III line 36, the estate and trust LOSS columns (c) plus (e) of line 34b
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part III line 36 ("Add columns (c) and (e) of line 34b"): column (c) "Passive deduction or loss allowed" plus column (e) "Deduction or loss from Schedule K-1", the two LOSS columns of the Part III totals row. NON-NEGATIVE, a magnitude: the printed box carries pre-printed parentheses, so the figure entered there is the size of the loss and the parentheses supply the sign, exactly as the sibling Part II column (i) box takes the non-negative /k1NonpassiveAllowedLoss. Computed as line 35 minus line 37, which is max(0, -line 37): for the single modelled estate or trust K-1 an income share gives 0 here, a NONPASSIVE loss gives the section 465 at-risk allowed loss and a PASSIVE loss gives the section 469 allowed part after the Form 8582 pool. Line 35 minus this fact is line 37 to the cent, the printed form's "Combine lines 35 and 36".

Fact.Name: Schedule E question A answered No
Fact.Description:
The No box of Schedule E Part I question A: the complement of /writableScheduleEMadePaymentsRequiring1099, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked and neither can contradict the other. Answered only when question A itself is answered.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered.

Fact.Name: Schedule E question B answered No
Fact.Description:
The No box of Schedule E Part I question B: the complement of /writableScheduleEWillFileRequired1099s, so exactly one of the two printed boxes is checked and neither can contradict the other. Answered only when question B itself is answered, which the form asks only of a filer who answered question A Yes.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered.

Fact.Name: Zero dollars, the floor that separates a Schedule E income column total from a loss column total
Fact.Description: A $0 Dollar constant. Schedule E splits one signed Part total across an INCOME line and a LOSS line printed in parentheses (Part III line 35 "Add columns (d) and (f) of line 34a" against line 36 "Add columns (c) and (e) of line 34b"), and recovering either half from the signed total is a floor at zero. The fourteen supported templates have no unary positive part: GreaterOf needs two Dollar FACT PATHS, and there is no zero-valued Dollar fact anywhere in dictionary/manifest/facts-manifest.json to name as the second one. This fact is that second path and nothing else. It resolves Complete $0 on every return, depends on nothing, and is read only by /scheduleELine35EstateTrustIncomeColumns.

Fact.Name: Real estate professional reconciliation, Schedule E Part V line 43
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part V line 43: the net income or (loss) the filer reported anywhere on Form 1040, 1040-SR or 1040-NR from all rental real estate activities in which they materially participated under the passive activity loss rules. It includes the deductible loss of a Form 4835 farm rental in which a real estate professional materially participated, which Form 4835 line 34c also sends to Schedule E line 40. SIGNED, so no Min 0 limit: the printed line says "net income or (loss)". Owed only by a real estate professional, whom the 2025 Instructions for Schedule E define by the more-than-half and 750-hour tests and then direct: "If you were a real estate professional for 2025, complete Schedule E, line 43." An ATTESTATION, not a computation, for two reasons the form itself gives: the figure is gathered from ANYWHERE on the 1040 rather than from Schedule E, and this graph has no real-estate-professional concept to decide which rental activities qualify. NOT a summand of anything: line 41 combines lines 26, 32, 37, 39 and 40 only, so a line 43 figure leaves /scheduleETotalIncome, Schedule 1 line 5 and total income untouched, exactly as line 42 does.

Fact.Name: REMIC column (d) taxable income (net loss) from Schedules Q line 1b, Schedule E line 38
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (d) "Taxable income (net loss) from Schedules Q, line 1b": the total of the amounts shown on the filer's Schedule(s) Q (Form 1066) line 1b across every REMIC residual interest held. SIGNED, because the caption names a net loss and the Part IV heading is "Income or Loss".
INTAKE AND NOT A DERIVATION: Schedule Q (Form 1066) is not vendored under sources/, so the per quarter detail behind the column cannot be modelled; the printed Schedule E caption is authority for what the box means, which is what an intake needs.
WIRED. /scheduleERemicResidualNet (Schedule E line 39) now COMBINES this column with its twin through /remicColumnsDAndENet whenever either column is answered, and the combined attestation /writableRemicResidualNet is the fallback behind /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered for a return that claims a residual interest without answering the columns. The double statement of the same money is over and the obligation is DISCHARGED. Column (c), the section 860E excess inclusion, stays out of the line 39 combine by instruction and is carried by /writableRemicExcessInclusion.

Fact.Name: REMIC column (e) income from Schedules Q line 3b, Schedule E line 38
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (e) "Income from Schedules Q, line 3b": the total of the amounts shown on the filer's Schedule(s) Q (Form 1066) line 3b across every REMIC residual interest held.
INTAKE AND NOT A DERIVATION: Schedule Q (Form 1066) is not vendored under sources/, so the detail behind the column cannot be modelled; the printed Schedule E caption is authority for what the box means.
WIRED. /scheduleERemicResidualNet (Schedule E line 39) now COMBINES this column with its twin through /remicColumnsDAndENet whenever either column is answered, and the combined attestation /writableRemicResidualNet is the fallback behind /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered for a return that claims a residual interest without answering the columns. The double statement of the same money is over and the obligation is DISCHARGED. Column (c), the section 860E excess inclusion, stays out of the line 39 combine by instruction and is carried by /writableRemicExcessInclusion.

Fact.Name: REMIC employer identification number, Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (b)
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (b) "Employer identification number": the EIN of the REMIC in which the filer holds the residual interest. Printing intake only, consulted when /claimsRemicResidualInterest is true. Part IV prints exactly ONE entity row on the 2025 form and the graph already models the residual holding at return level, so this is a return level EIN beside /writableRemicEntityName rather than a collection leaf. It feeds no computation.

Fact.Name: REMIC name, Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (a)
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part IV line 38 column (a) "Name": the name of the REMIC in which the filer holds the residual interest. Printing intake only, consulted when /claimsRemicResidualInterest is true. Part IV prints exactly ONE entity row on the 2025 form, and the graph already models the residual holding at return level (/writableHasRemicResidualInterest, /writableRemicResidualNet, /writableRemicExcessInclusion), so this is a return-level String rather than a collection leaf. It feeds no computation: the Part IV dollars reach line 41 through /scheduleERemicResidualNet and the section 860E floor through /scheduleERemicExcessInclusion, and neither reads a name.

Fact.Name: Description of the other expenses listed on Schedule E line 19
Fact.Description:
The one printed description box on Schedule E line 19, Other (list). The form prints a single label box for the whole Part I expense table, not one per column, so this fact is return level, exactly as /writableScheduleELine1bOtherPropertyTypeDescription is for the line 1b code list. It labels the per property line 19 amounts (/rentalProperties/*/writableLine19OtherExpense).
LABEL ONLY, and it can never be anything else: this is a String, so no Dollar total can ever carry it. The line 20 obligation recorded here belonged to the AMOUNTS it labels (/rentalProperties/*/writableLine19OtherExpense), and those were wired into the line 20 total on 2026-08-30; this box keeps printing the list of what they are.

Fact.Name: Description for type of property code 8, other (Schedule E line 1b)
Fact.Description:
The one printed description box under the Schedule E type of property list, filled when a property column carries code 8, other. The form prints a single box for the whole Part I table, not one per column, so this fact is return level: a filer with two columns of code 8 describes them in this one box.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered, and answering it neither creates nor limits a deduction.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 27: prior year disallowed loss or unreimbursed partnership expenses
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 27: true when the filer reports a loss not allowed in a prior year under the at risk or basis limitations, a prior year unallowed passive activity loss that was not reported on Form 8582, or unreimbursed partnership expenses. The printed Yes box is checked from this fact; the printed No box is its complement and takes a bool_not over this fact, the treatment questions A and B already have.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: it routes the filer to the instructions and no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered.
S332 (2026-09-12): the two record-only sentences above describe pre-S332 behavior and are superseded for Part II line-28 supplemental rows. This answer now gates those rows. When a K-1 is reported, an unanswered line 27 leaves them Incomplete; No makes their amounts zero, and Yes requires each amount and any applicable UPE routing answer. Without a current K-1, Yes still enables the prior-year/UPE rows (for example, a released carry-in); otherwise those supplemental rows remain disabled.

Fact.Name: Prior-year basis or at-risk loss deductible this year (Schedule E line 28 PYA)
Fact.Description: The positive dollar amount of a prior-year partnership or S-corporation loss that is now deductible because the basis or at-risk limitation no longer disallows it. Enter the amount separately from current-year K-1 amounts; the graph subtracts it into Schedule E line 28 column (i) and labels the row PYA. Ask only after Schedule E line 27 is Yes. Enter 0.00 if line 27 is Yes for another category and no basis/at-risk PYA is deductible. This writable does not itself decide basis, at-risk, or passive limitations.

Fact.Name: Prior-year passive loss not reported on Form 8582 (Schedule E line 28 PYA)
Fact.Description: The positive dollar amount of a prior-year passive partnership or S-corporation loss that is deductible this year but was not reported on Form 8582 in the prior year. Enter it on a separate Schedule E line 28 row in column (g); the graph labels the row PYA and subtracts the amount from line 32. Do not enter a loss already reported on Form 8582. Ask only after Schedule E line 27 is Yes. Enter 0.00 if line 27 is Yes for another category and no such PYA is deductible.

Fact.Name: Unreimbursed partnership expenses paid by the partner (Schedule E line 28)
Fact.Description: The positive dollar amount of ordinary and necessary partnership expenses the filer paid and was not reimbursed for. Only the expenses the partnership agreement required the partner to pay can be deducted. Ask after Schedule E line 27 is Yes. Enter 0.00 if line 27 is Yes for a prior-year loss but there are no unreimbursed partnership expenses. When this amount is positive, the graph requires the agreement, passive-activity, and (for passive activity) Form 8582 routing answers before determining a line-28 amount.

Fact.Name: Partnership agreement requires these unreimbursed expenses
Fact.Description: Whether the partnership agreement required the partner to pay the unreimbursed ordinary and necessary expenses entered on this Schedule E line-28 intake. Asked only when /writableScheduleEUPEAmount is positive. An unanswered answer leaves the UPE deduction Incomplete; expenses not required by the partnership agreement are not deducted here.

Fact.Name: These unreimbursed partnership expenses are from a passive activity
Fact.Description: Whether the agreement-required unreimbursed partnership expenses are from a passive activity. Asked only when the amount is positive, the partnership agreement required payment, and the filer confirms that all expenses in this one amount share the same passive/nonpassive status. If expenses have mixed status, the classification answer below must be No and the line-28 result remains Incomplete until the intake is split. A nonpassive UPE is separately deducted in column (i). A passive UPE requires the Form 8582 filing answer below to determine whether it is separately reported in column (g). Unanswered leaves the applicable line-28 route Incomplete.

Fact.Name: All expenses in this UPE amount share the same passive status
Fact.Description: Filer attestation that the full unreimbursed-partnership-expense amount above comes from activities that are all passive or all nonpassive. Asked only when the positive amount is required by the partnership agreement. Yes allows the following passive/nonpassive answer to route the whole amount. No means the aggregate mixes passive and nonpassive activities, which this single-amount intake cannot split; the line-28 UPE result remains Incomplete until each category is supplied separately. This attestation does not associate an amount with a particular partnership or activity for Form 8582.

Fact.Name: UPE amount has a single passive-status classification
Fact.Description: Complete only when the filer confirms the whole UPE amount comes from activities that share one passive/nonpassive status. False means the amount mixes statuses and this scalar intake cannot route it safely. UPE line-28 outputs stay Incomplete for that amount.

Fact.Name: Required to file Form 8582
Fact.Description: Filer attestation: whether the filer is required to file Form 8582 for this return. Asked only when a positive unreimbursed partnership expense is required by the partnership agreement and comes from a passive activity. This answer does not re-derive the Form 8582 filing exceptions. No selects Schedule E line 28 column (g). Yes means the expense must instead be incorporated into its partnership activity's Form 8582 computation; until the UPE can be attributed to a specific passive partnership/activity in that computation, the Schedule E line-28 result remains Incomplete and the return cannot silently omit or separately deduct it.

Fact.Name: Schedule E line 27 says a separate PYA or UPE row may apply
Fact.Description: Line-28 PYA/UPE rows are in scope when line 27 is Yes. Line 27 is an OPTIONAL intake: a return that has not answered it — including a return with a current K-1 — keeps the Part-II supplemental rows inactive and resolves exactly as it did before those rows existed. The answer is read IsComplete-first with an explicit absent arm, so a new intake cannot leave a pre-existing return Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (i): deductible prior-year basis or at-risk loss
Fact.Description: The positive carry-in entered on /writableScheduleEPriorYearBasisAtRiskLoss, made negative for Schedule E line 28 column (i). It is never netted against a current-year K-1. The separately printed row is labelled PYA. If line 27 is No, this amount is zero; if line 27 is Yes, an unanswered amount remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (g): deductible prior-year passive loss not reported on Form 8582
Fact.Description: The positive carry-in entered on /writableScheduleEPriorYearPassiveLossNotOnForm8582, made negative for Schedule E line 28 column (g). It remains a separate row labelled PYA. If line 27 is No, this amount is zero; if line 27 is Yes, an unanswered amount remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (i): agreement-required nonpassive UPE
Fact.Description: Agreement-required unreimbursed partnership expenses from a nonpassive activity, made negative for the separate Schedule E line 28 column (i) row labelled UPE. If the UPE amount is zero or the partnership agreement did not require payment, this is zero. A positive amount with an unanswered agreement or activity classification remains Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (g): agreement-required passive UPE not subject to Form 8582
Fact.Description: Agreement-required unreimbursed partnership expenses from a passive activity, made negative for the separate Schedule E line 28 column (g) row labelled UPE only when the filer attests that Form 8582 is not required. If Form 8582 is required, the amount belongs in that partnership activity's Form 8582 computation, not as a separate line-28 deduction. The current graph has no partnership/activity association for this UPE; the required-Yes and unanswered attestation paths therefore remain Incomplete rather than using the expense twice or silently dropping it. A zero amount or UPE not required by the agreement is zero and needs no routing answers.

Fact.Name: Printed label for the basis/at-risk prior-year-loss row
Fact.Description: The Schedule E line-28 column (a) label printed on the separate row for the prior-year basis or at-risk loss amount.

Fact.Name: Printed label for the prior-year passive-loss row
Fact.Description: The Schedule E line-28 column (a) label printed on the separate row for a prior-year passive loss not reported on Form 8582.

Fact.Name: Printed label for the UPE row
Fact.Description: The Schedule E line-28 column (a) label printed on the separate unreimbursed partnership expenses row.

Fact.Name: Schedule E question A: payments requiring a Form 1099
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part I question A: true when the filer made payments in 2025 that would require filing one or more Forms 1099 for the rental real estate and royalty activities reported in Part I. The printed Yes box is checked from this fact; the printed No box is its complement and stays unmapped until the candidate templates gain a boolean negation.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered, and answering it neither creates nor limits a deduction.

Fact.Name: Schedule E question B: the required Forms 1099 were or will be filed
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part I question B: true when the filer did file or will file the Forms 1099 that question A says are required. The form asks it only of a filer who answered question A Yes, so this fact stands on its own and is left unanswered when question A is No. The printed Yes box is checked from this fact; the printed No box is its complement and stays unmapped until the candidate templates gain a boolean negation.
RECORD ONLY. Nothing in the fact graph reads this attestation: no computed Schedule E line moves when it is answered, and answering it neither creates nor limits a deduction.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (b): P for a partnership, S for an S corporation
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part II line 28 column (b) prints one letter per entity row: P when the Schedule K-1 came from a partnership and S when it came from an S corporation. The entity is already recorded on the item as ../entityType, a writable Enum over /k1EntityTypeOptions whose two options are partnership and sCorp, so nothing new is asked of the filer here. What the column needs is the printed CODE rather than the option name, and that is exactly what this Switch of Equal cases produces. An unanswered entityType prints the empty string, which is the right behaviour for a faithful record field the form leaves blank when the type was never recorded. The statute anchor is IRC 702 at section level because the P half of the column is the partner distributive share Part II reports; the S half rests on the twin provision IRC 1366, the pro rata share rule for an S corporation shareholder, and both sections are named in the authority of /k1EntityTypeOptions and /formK1s/*/entityType themselves. Reported figure only: nothing computed reads it.

Fact.Name: This K-1 passive activity loss magnitude entering the Form 8582 pool
Fact.Description: The positive part of the negated post section 179 passive net, that is max(0, minus ../passiveNetAfterSection179): this Schedule K-1 own passive LOSS as a positive amount, the Form 8582 Part V column (b) figure for the activity. It is the numerator of the Part VII ratable allocation below and the gross amount column (g) reduces to its allowed part. Taking it from ../passiveNetAfterSection179 rather than from the older ../passiveSuspendedLoss is deliberate and matters in two populations: a section 469(k) publicly traded partnership contributes $0 here, because ../passiveNet already excludes it from the cross activity pool and its overall result is a Part II nonpassive column (k) figure instead, while ../passiveSuspendedLoss still carries the whole at risk allowed loss for it; and a passive K-1 that elects a box 12 section 179 amount carries that deduction inside its pool net, which ../passiveSuspendedLoss does not see. The second GreaterOf operand is /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor, the $0 constant, because the supported templates have no unary positive part.

Fact.Name: Line 28 column (g): passive loss allowed for this Schedule K-1
Fact.Description:
Schedule E Part II line 28 column (g) for this entity row: this K-1 passive activity loss (../line28ColumnGPassiveLoss) less the part of it the section 469 limitation disallows (../line28ColumnGSuspendedShare). Printed as a positive amount, because the line 31 box that adds column (g) carries pre printed parentheses. It is $0 on a nonpassive K-1, on a section 469(k) publicly traded partnership and on a passive K-1 whose net is income, since the gross loss is $0 in all three. NOT READ BY /k1Line29bColumnGPassiveLossAllowedTotal, AND THAT IS A STATED CHOICE AS OF RATHER THAN A PENDING REWIRE: that staged line 29b total is the POOLED figure /k1PassiveLoss less /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated, not the sum of these rows. The two readings coincide on the ordinary return where the passive K-1s are all losses, and they part company on a return where one passive K-1 earns income and another loses, because the dictionary nets the K-1 leg into a single signed /k1PassiveNet before the pool allocation while Form 8582 treats each K-1 as its own activity; the ratable rounding of these per item shares can also leave a residual, since there is no per item plug of the kind /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated gives the three legs. WHY THE POOLED FIGURE KEEPS THE LINE AND THESE ROWS DO NOT. Re-pointing the line 29b total at a CollectionSum of these rows would change /scheduleEPartIINetIncome, Schedule 1 line 5 and total income on exactly the mixed passive return where the two readings differ, and it would need a residual plug to stay cent exact against /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated; the section 469 pool that produced the suspension is itself computed from the single signed /k1PassiveNet, so the per item shares are an allocation OF the pooled answer and cannot outvote it without rebuilding the Part II passive chain per activity. That is a unit of its own. The consequence, disclosed rather than left to be found: on a return holding one profitable and one loss making passive K-1, printed line 31 does not foot to the printed column (g) rows above it. Closing it needs either the per activity Part II rebody or a validations.xml reconciliation, both outside this module.
A PUBLICLY TRADED PARTNERSHIP ROW adds ../ptpSection1231AllowedScheduleELoss: the part of its section 469(k) loss that its own box 10 net section 1231 gain allows ("report $7,200 of the losses as a passive loss in column (g)"). It is $0 on every other row.

Fact.Name: Zero less this K-1 post section 179 passive net, the operand of the column (g) loss magnitude
Fact.Description: Zero less ../passiveNetAfterSection179: the sign flipped per K-1 Form 8582 pool contribution. It exists only as the first operand of ../line28ColumnGPassiveLoss, which floors it at zero to recover this activity passive LOSS magnitude from the signed net, the mirror image of the promoted ../line28ColumnHPassiveIncome, which floors the same signed net the other way to recover the column (h) income. The supported templates have no unary negation and no unary positive part, so the pair is Subtract(0, x) then GreaterOf(that, 0), exactly as /scheduleELine34bColumnENonpassiveLossNegated does for Part III; the minuend is the staged $0 constant /scheduleEZeroDollarFloor because dollar_subtract takes fact paths, not literals. IT IS NOT A PRINTED FIGURE and it is NEGATIVE whenever this K-1 passive net is income.

Fact.Name: This K-1 ratable share of the K-1 leg unallowed passive loss (Form 8582 Part VII)
Fact.Description: This Schedule K-1 share of the passive loss the section 469 limitation DISALLOWS = round(/k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated times ../line28ColumnGPassiveLoss divided by /k1PassiveLoss), $0 when /k1PassiveLoss is unanswered or zero. It is the Form 8582 Part VII Allocation of Unallowed Losses ratio taken one level down from where scheduleE.xml already takes it: /k1PassiveSuspendedAllocated is itself round(/passiveSuspendedLossTotal times /k1PassiveLoss divided by /passiveLossTotal), the K-1 leg share of the whole pool suspension, so the operands here mirror that fact exactly, with the leg total /k1PassiveLoss as the denominator and this item own loss as the numerator. Rounding is the same Round the module applies to its own allocation. Not a printed figure of its own; it exists to be subtracted in ../line28ColumnGPassiveLossAllowed.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) amended K-1 box
Fact.Description: The header checkbox "Amended K-1" on the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) this partner received, recorded with fact type Bool on the K-1 item. The statute anchor here is section 702 at SECTION level on purpose: section 702 is why this document exists at all, since it is the provision that charges each partner with a distributive share of the partnership's items and so obliges the partnership to furnish this Schedule K-1. The box itself carries no distributive share amount, so no subsection governs it. Intake only: it is a faithful record of what the partnership printed on the document, and no Form 1040 or Schedule E line reads it yet. It is a new item leaf on the EXISTING /formK1s collection (the partnership and S corporation Schedule K-1 collection that Schedule E Part II line 28 already reads), so no collection is authored here. DISPOSITION reference-only: this input-document box is captured for the record and feeds no return computation by design; no consumer is owed. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box final-amended (Final K-1 / Amended K-1 checkboxes). Shared leaf: the Amended K-1 checkbox on Form 1120-S uses this same Boolean fact as the Form 1065 Amended K-1 checkbox. Shared leaf: Schedule K-1 (Form 8865), Amended K-1, uses this same fact (a Form 8865 K-1 is a partnership K-1 item on /formK1s).

Fact.Name: Form 1065 K-1 box 10 amount is from a passive activity (Form 4797 line 2 admission test)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Is the net section 1231 loss in box 10 of this Schedule K-1 from a PASSIVE activity?" HELP TEXT: "An activity is passive if you did not materially participate in it, and rental activities are generally passive whether you participated or not. The box 10 amount can come from a different activity than the box 1 trade or business, which is why we ask about it separately. If you are not sure, the partnership's statement attached to the K-1 identifies the activity the box 10 amount came from." WHY IT IS ASKED: the Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), box 10, admit BOTH signs on Form 4797 line 2 - "If the amount is either (a) a loss that isn't from a passive activity or (b) a gain, report it in column (g) of Form 4797, line 2" - and send the passive loss elsewhere: "If the amount is a loss from a passive activity, see Passive Loss Limitations in the Instructions for Form 4797" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1065sk1.pdf, page 16). ASKED WHEN: this K-1's box 10 (../writableK1065Box10NetSection1231Gain) is answered and is NEGATIVE. One answer per K-1. A GAIN needs no answer - the instructions admit it either way - and neither does an unanswered box 10. WHY IT IS NOT DERIVED: ../materiallyParticipated classifies the BOX 1 trade or business activity, and a box 10 amount may come from a different activity of the same partnership or from a rental. Reading the box-1 answer here would be a guess wearing a derivation's clothes. A RELATED PRESUMPTION THIS QUESTION DOES NOT CONSULT: IRC 469(h)(2) treats no interest in a limited partnership held AS a limited partner as one with respect to which the taxpayer materially participates, except as regulations provide (26 U.S.C. 469, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section469&num=0&edition=2024). This dictionary already reads that as a PRESUMPTION for box 1 participation on a publicly traded partnership interest held as a limited partner (../ptpInterestHeldAsLimitedPartner, ../materiallyParticipatedAfterPresumption): an UNANSWERED box 1 participation question there defaults to passive rather than this module's usual nonpassive default, rebuttable only by satisfying participation test 1, 5 or 6. So a limited partner on such a K-1 is presumptively passive on box 1 whenever that question is left blank. THIS QUESTION DOES NOT READ THAT PRESUMPTION, for the same reason it does not read ../materiallyParticipated directly: the presumption classifies the box 1 activity, and the box 10 amount may be a different activity of the same partnership. A limited partner whose box 1 participation the presumption treats as passive can still truthfully answer NO here if the box 10 loss comes from a different, nonpassive activity, and this dictionary does not check the two answers against each other either way. UNANSWERED: REFUSED. form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 has no arm for a negative box 10 with this question unanswered, so it resolves Result.Incomplete and the return refuses; form4797:/hasUnansweredScheduleK1Box10Passivity makes that refusal legible. That is the deliberate replacement for the silent $0 this leaf used to take, which cost a partner with a genuinely nonpassive section 1231 loss BOTH the deduction and the entry into the section 1231(c) recapture pool that would shelter a later year's gain. VALIDATION: Boolean, Yes / No. No default, no Min or Max. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 -> Form 4797 line 2 -> line 7, the section 1231 netting, and from there Schedule D or Form 4797 line 11. ANSWERING YES keeps the loss at $0 on Form 4797. That $0 is NOT because Form 8582 or its section 469 pool is unmodelled here - scheduleE builds a full section 469 pipeline on this same /formK1s collection (../lossIsPassive, ../nonpassiveAllowedLoss, ../passiveSuspendedLoss, ../line28ColumnGSuspendedShare, /section8582Magi) for the K-1's activity loss. It is because this box 10 amount is not wired onto that pool, so a genuinely passive box 10 loss is DROPPED for the year rather than suspended into a future one the way an activity loss answered YES here would be.

Fact.Name: Form 1065 K-1 box 10 net section 1231 gain (loss)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "What is the net section 1231 gain (loss) reported in box 10 of this Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)?" (Box 9 on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S), "Net section 1231 gain (loss)" - the same leaf records both, because scheduleE records both entity types on the one /formK1s collection.) HELP TEXT: "Enter the amount exactly as the partnership or S corporation reported it - a negative number for a loss. This can be a different activity than the one reported in box 1 or box 2; if you are not sure, the partnership's attached statement identifies the activity it came from." WHY IT IS ASKED: intake only, a faithful record of what the entity printed on the document. It is a new item leaf on the EXISTING /formK1s collection (the partnership and S corporation Schedule K-1 collection Schedule E Part II line 28 already reads), so no collection is authored here. ASKED WHEN: on every recorded Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S), one answer per K-1. Blank is the common case; most K-1s carry no box 10/9 amount. UNANSWERED: DEFAULTED to $0, but not on this leaf itself - the raw leaf is Incomplete when unanswered, and form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797's own first Switch arm reads that Incomplete and supplies $0, which keeps the CollectionSum over /formK1s Complete for a K-1 that never reports this box. VALIDATION: Dollar, no Min or Max - the box can be a gain or a loss. A NEGATIVE answer makes the sibling ../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity REQUIRED; the two belong on one screen. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: form4797:/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797, which admits a GAIN in full whatever the activity, admits a LOSS in full when ../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity is answered NO, holds a PASSIVE loss at $0, and REFUSES the return when a NEGATIVE answer's passivity question is unanswered - into form4797:/form4797Line2Section1231FromScheduleK1, Form 4797 line 2 and line 7 (the section 1231 netting), and from there Schedule D or Form 4797 line 11. Shared leaf: Schedule K-1 (Form 8865), box 10, uses this same fact (a Form 8865 K-1 is a partnership K-1 item on /formK1s).

Fact.Name: This K-1 reports a box 10 net section 1231 loss answered as from a passive activity
Fact.Description:
True when ../writableK1065Box10NetSection1231Gain is answered and below $0 and ../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity is answered Yes. That loss is held at $0 on Form 4797 line 2 and is not a member of this module's Form 8582 pool, so no part of it is allowed this year. Complete false on every K-1 without a negative box 10 or without a Yes.
FALSE on a K-1 under the section 469(k) per-PTP regime (../appliesPtpSection469): a publicly traded partnership's passive items are never reported on Form 8582, so the pool this flag describes does not reach that loss. It is combined with the same PTP's other items instead (../ptpSection469NetWithSection1231), and its allowed part reaches Form 4797 through ../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedOnForm4797. When the regime is undecided (item D unanswered) the flag keeps its general answer.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a passive box 10 section 1231 loss that the passive activity rules could partly allow
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. A Schedule K-1 reports a net section 1231 loss in box 10 (box 9 on Form 1120-S) from a passive activity, and your return also has passive income or claims active participation in a rental. Part or all of that loss may be allowed this year through Form 8582, and this return cannot yet figure that amount.
Fires when a recorded K-1 has ../k1PassiveSection1231LossNotPooled true AND the pool could allow part of it: /passiveIncomeTotal above $0 (other passive income absorbs passive losses under IRC 469(d)(1)) or /claimsRentalActiveParticipation (the special allowance). When neither holds the whole loss would be suspended this year, the $0 on Form 4797 line 2 is the current-year answer, and the return files. Guarded by an IsComplete on /formK1s.

Fact.Description: Part III box 22, the checkbox saying the K-1 reports more than one activity for at-risk purposes on the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) this partner received, recorded with fact type Bool on the K-1 item. The box points the partner at an attached statement and carries no distributive share amount, so the anchor stays at section 702 at SECTION level: section 702 is why this document exists at all, since it is the provision that charges each partner with a distributive share of the partnership's items and so obliges the partnership to furnish this Schedule K-1. It is NOT /formK1s/*/fullyAtRisk or /formK1s/*/amountAtRisk: those record the partner's own section 465 at-risk position, while this box records only that the partnership split the K-1 across several activities. The printed cell carries a percentage followed by a percent sign, so it is recorded as a String rather than an Int: the form accepts fractional percentages and the printed value is transcribed as it appears. The statute anchor here is section 702 at SECTION level on purpose: section 702 is why this document exists at all, since it is the provision that charges each partner with a distributive share of the partnership's items and so obliges the partnership to furnish this Schedule K-1. The box itself carries no distributive share amount, so no subsection governs it. Intake only: it is a faithful record of what the partnership printed on the document, and no Form 1040 or Schedule E line reads it yet. It is a new item leaf on the EXISTING /formK1s collection (the partnership and S corporation Schedule K-1 collection that Schedule E Part II line 28 already reads), so no collection is authored here. Fact.Name: Total of the per property Form 6198 line 21 deductible rental losses
Fact.Description: /rentalRawLossTotal less /rentalAtRiskSuspendedLoss: the total of the per property at risk ALLOWED losses, the figure that actually enters Form 8582 for the rental leg. Both operands are existing collection sums over the same items, /rentalProperties/*/rawLoss and /rentalProperties/*/atRiskSuspendedLoss, and the per property identity ../atRiskDeductibleLoss equals ../rawLoss less ../atRiskSuspendedLoss holds item by item, so this difference is exactly the collection sum of ../atRiskDeductibleLoss and is not an approximation of it. It exists to be the denominator of the per property ratable allocation the line 22 column needs; the raw loss total would be the wrong denominator, because a property whose section 465 amount at risk binds sends only part of its line 21 loss to Form 8582. Reported figure only: nothing printed reads it.

Fact.Name: Line 22: deductible rental real estate loss for this property after the Form 8582 limitation
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part I line 22 for this property column: the at risk allowed loss (../atRiskDeductibleLoss, Form 6198 line 21) less this property ratable share of the rental leg unallowed passive loss (../line22SuspendedShare). Printed as a positive amount inside the pre printed parentheses the line carries. $0 for a profitable property, since its at risk allowed loss is $0. On the published i8582 line 9 example, a single property with a 42,000 loss whose special allowance is capped at 25,000, it prints 25,000, which is what line 25 totals and what line 26 carries. PRINT ONLY UNTIL /scheduleELine25Losses CONSUMES IT: that staged total is computed as line 24 less line 26 rather than by adding these columns, so it stays exact while the per property split is provisional. The two agree on the ordinary return; they can differ by the ratable rounding residual, because no per property plug exists, and this column can even go negative on a property whose answered ../priorYearUnallowedLoss pushes the rental leg suspension above the current year at risk allowed loss, the Form 8582 Worksheets 4 to 7 per activity allocation scheduleE.xml still records as deferred on /rentalLimitedNetIncome.

Fact.Name: This property ratable share of the rental leg unallowed passive loss (Form 8582 Part VII)
Fact.Description: This rental property share of the passive loss the section 469 limitation DISALLOWS = round(/rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated times ../atRiskDeductibleLoss divided by /rentalAtRiskDeductibleLossTotal), $0 when that total is unanswered or zero. /rentalPassiveSuspendedAllocated is the rental leg share of the pool suspended total that /rentalLimitedNetIncome already adds back, so it is the aggregate this splits, and the Form 8582 Part VII ratio is this activity loss over the total loss. The numerator is the AT RISK allowed loss rather than the raw line 21 loss because section 465 is applied on Form 6198 before Form 8582 sees the activity, and the denominator is the matching total, so the ratios sum to one. Rounding is the same Round the module applies to its own Part VII allocations. Not a printed figure of its own.

Fact.Name: Line 4: royalties received for this Part I property column
Fact.Description: Schedule E Part I line 4 for this property column, the gross royalties received. Schedule E prints royalties in the SAME A, B and C property columns as the rents on line 3, and type of property code 6 on line 1b is Royalties, so a royalty activity occupies one of the three Part I columns exactly as a rental property does. scheduleE.xml instead models ONE return level royalty activity, /writableRoyaltyIncome feeding /royaltyActivityNet and /royaltyNetIncome, which no index of /rentalProperties can address, so the printed column has no fact behind it. This is that per column intake, a Dollar with a zero floor because gross royalties received are never negative. PRINT ONLY UNTIL /royaltyActivityNet CONSUMES IT: the return level royalty chain still owns every computed royalty figure, so this leaf is deliberately NOT summed into the staged /scheduleELine23bTotalRoyalties or into line 24, line 25 and line 26, and a filer who answered both would otherwise be counted twice.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 allocation rows
Fact.Description: The rows Form 8958 line 8, Rents, royalties, partnerships, estates, trusts, prints: one item per rent, royalty, partnership, estate or trust item the separate returns allocate, each item carrying the row description, the column A total and the column B and column C shares. The form prints these rows on separate lines and the instructions require columns B and C together to equal column A. FILER SUPPLIED, because the graph holds only the return level figure scheduleE:/scheduleETotalIncome and no per row community allocation for this class. The rows stay FILER SUPPLIED. RECONCILED: /form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal now adds every column B and column C cell the form prints for this return, by both routes, and /form8958ScheduleELine8DoesNotFootToScheduleETotal reports when that sum differs from /scheduleETotalIncome, the figure column A of the first printed row carries. THE ALLOCATION ITSELF IS STILL FILER SUPPLIED, and that is a refusal with a reason rather than an omission. The eight shipping per collection allocation facts all switch on a PER ITEM community income character flag (dividendReports:/dividendReports/*/isCommunityIncome and its four siblings), and no such flag exists on /rentalProperties, /formK1s or /form1041K1s, so there is nothing for a derivation to switch on. Nor can the adjustment land where the dividend twin lands: dividendReports:/communityPropertyOrdinaryDividendsAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded is a term of income:/ordinaryDividends, a Form 1040 line, whereas /scheduleETotalIncome is simultaneously Schedule E line 41, which must keep footing to lines 26, 32, 37, 39 and 40, and Form 8958 line 8 column A itself, which is by definition the total BEFORE allocation. An adjustment inside it would contradict the very cell this row prints. MERGE: the three return-level scalars that printed row 0 (/writableForm8958ScheduleEEntityName, ThisReturnShare, SpouseShare) were deleted; row 0 is item [0] of this collection and the register maps it so. /form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal and /form8958ScheduleELine8Answered now read only the collection.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row column A total amount
Fact.Description: Form 8958 line 8 column A for this row, the total amount before allocation. One item of /form8958ScheduleERows, the collection behind the printed rows of line 8. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph holds no per row community allocation for this class, only the return level figure /scheduleETotalIncome. Not read by any total. Item [0] of this collection IS the first printed line 8 row — the register prints its description and its column B and column C cells — but that row's column A prints /scheduleETotalIncome, the Schedule E line 41 total, and never this cell; this cell prints only for items [1] and [2]. So a CollectionSum of these cells leaves out the figure the first row actually prints and is not comparable with the Schedule E total. See /form8958ScheduleELine8DoesNotFootToScheduleETotal for the identity that IS checkable. Not floored at zero, because a negative amount allocates a negative share.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row column B share allocated to this return's taxpayer
Fact.Description: Form 8958 line 8 column B for this row, the part allocated to this return's taxpayer. One item of /form8958ScheduleERows, the collection behind the printed rows of line 8. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph holds no per row community allocation for this class, only the return level figure /scheduleETotalIncome. CONSUMED through the complete safe alias ../columnBThisReturnShare into /form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal, the reconciliation against /scheduleETotalIncome. It still moves no dollar of tax; see that fact for why the allocation cannot yet be derived. Not floored at zero, because a negative amount allocates a negative share.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row column C share allocated to the spouse or RDP
Fact.Description: Form 8958 line 8 column C for this row, the part allocated to the spouse or RDP. One item of /form8958ScheduleERows, the collection behind the printed rows of line 8. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph holds no per row community allocation for this class, only the return level figure /scheduleETotalIncome. CONSUMED through the complete safe alias ../columnCSpouseShare into /form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal, the reconciliation against /scheduleETotalIncome. It still moves no dollar of tax; see that fact for why the allocation cannot yet be derived. Not floored at zero, because a negative amount allocates a negative share.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row description
Fact.Description: the identification cell Form 8958 line 8 prints at the left of the row. One item of /form8958ScheduleERows, the collection behind the printed rows of line 8. FILER SUPPLIED: the graph holds no per row community allocation for this class, only the return level figure /scheduleETotalIncome.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row column B share, complete safe
Fact.Description: The column B share this Form 8958 line 8 row allocates to this return's taxpayer, read complete safe: ../writableColumnBThisReturnShare when answered and $0 otherwise. Not floored, because a loss allocates a negative share. Its only consumer is the reconciliation /form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal, which needs every item of the collection to resolve before a CollectionSum over it can be Complete.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8 row column C share, complete safe
Fact.Description: The column C share this Form 8958 line 8 row allocates to the spouse or RDP, read complete safe: ../writableColumnCSpouseShare when answered and $0 otherwise. The sibling of ../columnBThisReturnShare, character for character.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 8, the whole of columns B and C across every printed row
Fact.Description:
The sum of every column B and every column C amount Form 8958 line 8 prints for this return: a guarded CollectionSum of ../columnBThisReturnShare and ../columnCSpouseShare over /form8958ScheduleERows, whose items [0], [1] and [2] the print configuration wires to the first, second and third printed rows; an item past the third is summed though it is not printed. Rounded, so it is comparable with /scheduleETotalIncome, which is a whole dollar line.
ONE SOURCE. Every printed column B and column C cell of line 8 is an item of /form8958ScheduleERows, so a sum over the collection covers the whole printed page.
COMPLETE SAFE. Each CollectionSum sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the collection root, the same guard /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered uses for /form1041K1s, because /form8958ScheduleERows is absent from almost every fixture and a CollectionSum over a collection the return never opened is not Complete.
IT MOVES NO DOLLAR. Nothing computes tax, AGI or any threshold from this figure; it exists so /form8958ScheduleELine8DoesNotFootToScheduleETotal can say whether the printed allocation adds up.

Fact.Name: Did this return answer any Form 8958 line 8 allocation cell
Fact.Description:
True when at least one column B or column C cell of Form 8958 line 8 is answered, on any item of /form8958ScheduleERows, the collection whose first three items the print configuration wires to the three printed rows.
IsComplete ON THE RAW WRITABLES, never on the complete safe aliases. ../columnBThisReturnShare and ../columnCSpouseShare are always Complete by construction, so testing them would make this predicate vacuously true on every return and turn the reconciliation below into a false alarm on returns that never opened Form 8958. The trap is the one /remicColumnsDAndEAnswered and /estateTrustK1PartIIIRowsAnswered document.
The collection leg sits inside an IsComplete Switch on the collection root and the whole fact resolves Complete FALSE on a return that never opened the section.

Fact.Name: The Form 8958 line 8 allocation does not add back to Schedule E line 41
Fact.Description:
True when this return answered any Form 8958 line 8 allocation cell (/form8958ScheduleELine8Answered) AND the whole of columns B and C (/form8958ScheduleELine8AllocatedTotal) differs from /scheduleETotalIncome, the Schedule E line 41 grand total that the same form prints in column A of the first line 8 row (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8958/en/configuration.yml line 136, field f1_90).
THIS IS THE COLLECTION'S OWN STATED OBLIGATION, DISCHARGED AS A DIAGNOSTIC. /form8958ScheduleERows carried the sentence "PRINT ONLY until /scheduleETotalIncome reconciles to the sum of these rows' column A", and the form's own instruction is the rule: "amounts in columns B and C. Together, columns B and C should" / "equal column A." Column A of the first printed row IS /scheduleETotalIncome, so the identity the graph can actually check is B plus C against the Schedule E total, and that is what this fact checks.
WHY NOT AGAINST THE ROWS' OWN COLUMN A. A CollectionSum of /form8958ScheduleERows/*/writableColumnATotal is NOT comparable with /scheduleETotalIncome, because the printed row [0] takes its column A from /scheduleETotalIncome itself, not from item [0]'s own writableColumnATotal, which is never printed. Item [0] IS the first printed row for its description and its column B and column C cells, but that row's column A is the Schedule E line 41 total, so the rows' own column A cells and the Schedule E total are still not comparable. Comparing them would report a disagreement on every return whose first row states the Schedule E total in column A, which is every return this form prints. The per row column A cells stay a filer record.
IT REPORTS A DISAGREEMENT AND DOES NOT RESOLVE ONE, exactly like /scheduleELine42AttestationDiffersFromComputed, whose shape it copies. Nothing reads it to change a dollar, because these cells are filer typed and an allocation the graph cannot derive must not be allowed to move AGI on a typo. What it buys is that a Form 8958 line 8 that does not add up is now visible rather than silently printed.
FALSE ON EVERY RETURN THAT NEVER OPENED THE SECTION, and Complete there.

Fact.Name: Form 1065 K-1 item G limited partner or other LLC member checkbox
Fact.Description: Part II item G, the SECOND of its two printed checkboxes, "Limited partner or other LLC member", on the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) this partner received, recorded with fact type Bool on the K-1 item: true when the partnership checked it. The first checkbox, "General partner or LLC member-manager", is ../writablePartnerIsGeneralPartner. One Bool per printed checkbox (INPUT-FORMS.md section c): the filer transcribes what the partnership printed, including neither box or both. Unanswered is complete-safe. Intake only: no Form 1040 or Schedule E line reads it; the limited-partner presumption and the box 4b net investment income arm key on ../partnerIsGeneralPartner, which reads only the first checkbox, and reconciling the two printed boxes into that answer is a named successor, never a silent switch. Exported so a state module that reads the partner type does so by module-qualified path. Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) box G (Limited partner or other LLC member).

One Bool per printed checkbox (INPUT-FORMS.md section c): the filer transcribes what the partnership printed, including neither box or both. Unanswered is complete-safe. Fact.Name: Form 1065 K-1 box 4c total guaranteed payments
Fact.Description: Part III box 4c, total guaranteed payments, on the Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) this partner received, recorded with fact type Dollar on the K-1 item, as printed. The partnership prints it as the total of boxes 4a and 4b (Partner's Instructions for Schedule K-1 (Form 1065), Box 4c). The return does not read it: ../guaranteedPayments adds boxes 4a (../writableGuaranteedPaymentsServices) and 4b (../writableGuaranteedPaymentsCapital) itself, and this leaf is never made a term of that sum. A printed 4c that disagrees with 4a plus 4b is a reconciliation for a named successor, never a silent switch. Unanswered is complete-safe. Fact.Name: Form 8865 K-1 item A2 reference ID number
