Fact.Name: Supported straight-line building recovery methods
Fact.Description: Closed method set for an existing, unchanged MACRS straight-line building schedule. Not a method-change election. Land and 15-year land improvements are not buildings and must not be entered here.

Fact.Name: Building recovery method on the depreciation schedule
Fact.Description: Select the actual unchanged, formula-based MACRS straight-line method for this building from its depreciation records. Do not switch an existing percentage-table schedule to this route: continuing that schedule requires the applicable table or a separately calculated override. Selection activates the dated calculation and requires the original in-service date, original depreciable basis, prior allowed-or-allowable depreciation, and current disposition answer. Do not select a new method merely to obtain a deduction. This route excludes basis-changing transactions, general asset accounts, short tax years, and changes of use or method requiring a remaining-life calculation. Use the separately supported depreciation override for a professionally computed amount in those cases.

Fact.Name: Original building placed-in-service date
Fact.Description: Actual original date this depreciable building was ready and available for the rental use represented by this unchanged schedule. Not the purchase date unless it is also the in-service date. A new owner starts that owner's own depreciable schedule. Do not reset the date on an existing schedule. Dates before 1987 require a different depreciation system.

Fact.Name: Building depreciation allowed or allowable before 2025
Fact.Description: Cumulative depreciation allowed or allowable on this same building basis through the end of 2024. Enter an explicit zero for a building first placed in service in 2025. This is a remaining-basis ceiling, not a deduction to add to current depreciation. It must be between zero and the original depreciable building basis.

Fact.Name: Building disposed of or retired in 2025
Fact.Description: Answer Yes if this building was disposed of or permanently retired from income-producing use in 2025; otherwise answer No. Yes requires the actual disposition/retirement date. Depreciation recapture and gain or loss are calculated separately on the applicable disposition forms.

Fact.Name: Building disposition or permanent retirement date
Fact.Description: Actual 2025 date of disposition or permanent retirement from rental use. Required only when the 2025 disposition answer is Yes. The mid-month convention applies; a date before the in-service date is invalid.

Fact.Name: 1993 nonresidential transition rule applies
Fact.Description: Required for either nonresidential GDS method when property was placed in service May 13 through December 31, 1993. Yes selects the 31.5-year transition; No is needed for the ordinary 39-year method. Answer Yes only if purchase or construction was under a binding contract in effect before May 13, 1993, or construction began before that date, as described in Pub. 946. No does not authorize a 31.5-year schedule.

Fact.Name: Unchanged standard building schedule confirmed
Fact.Description: Confirm this is a calendar-year, unchanged formula-based straight-line MACRS building schedule with one original basis and recovery period. A schedule previously using IRS percentage tables is NOT supported by this route; answer No for that history and use a separately calculated override. The confirmation does not authorize a change from percentage tables to formulas. No change-of-use/method adjustment, carryover-basis transaction, short year, general asset account, tax-exempt-use lease extension, or separate improvement is being folded into this basis. An ADS residential 30-year schedule for pre-2018 property is excluded here because the transition to ADS can require a remaining-adjusted-basis calculation. An unsupported situation stays incomplete, rather than assuming a new original-cost schedule.

Fact.Name: A dated building method was selected
Fact.Description: Whether a valid method enum was answered. An unanswered selection retains the legacy two-class computation; any answered selection requires the dated route to resolve.

Fact.Name: Building recovery period in whole months
Fact.Description: 330, 378, 360, 468, or 480 months according to the selected building method; never 180 months for land improvements.

Fact.Name: Building method matches the supported date range
Fact.Description: Checks the ordinary MACRS date ranges, including the 1993 31.5-year GDS transition. Pre-2018 residential ADS-to-30-year conversions are not implemented by simply substituting a new divisor. A selected unsupported vintage remains distinguishable from an unanswered selection.

Fact.Name: Original in-service midpoint relative to 2025
Fact.Description: Two half-month units per month: 24*(original year - 2025) + 2*original month - 1. January 2025 is 1, December is 23. A negative number is a prior-year midpoint.

Fact.Name: End of the building recovery interval
Fact.Description: The original in-service midpoint plus twice the original recovery period in months. Depreciation cannot continue after the recovery interval.

Fact.Name: 2025 depreciation interval ending point
Fact.Description: 24 at December 31 for a building held all year; otherwise the 2025 disposition-month midpoint. A missing or invalid required disposition date does not become a full-year deduction.

Fact.Name: Selected building calculation is within its supported domain
Fact.Description: Requires the unchanged-schedule confirmation, a supported method/date, a 1987-2025 in-service date, and a nonnegative cumulative depreciation balance not above basis. A 2025 in-service date requires zero prior depreciation. Missing operands propagate incomplete.

Fact.Name: Recovery interval starting point within 2025
Fact.Description: The later of January 1 and the original in-service midpoint, expressed in half-months.

Fact.Name: Half-months of recovery in 2025
Fact.Description: Length of the intersection of the original recovery interval, the 2025 calendar year, and the period ending at the disposition midpoint; floor zero. A building placed in service and disposed of in the same year is excluded from MACRS depreciation under Pub. 946, regardless of month.

Fact.Name: Building basis remaining for depreciation
Fact.Description: Original depreciable basis less depreciation allowed or allowable through 2024, floored at zero. The validity predicate separately rejects a carry-in above the original basis.

Fact.Name: Dated building depreciation before whole-dollar rounding
Fact.Description: Formula-based straight-line MACRS only. In the placement year, original basis times the allowed half-months divided by twice the original recovery months; same-year placement/disposal is zero. In later years, use basis unrecovered through 2024 and the recovery period remaining at January 1, 2025. The annual rate is one over the remaining years, capped at 100 percent; a disposition before recovery ends applies the mid-month in-service fraction. If the final recovery midpoint is in 2025 and the building is held through it under the applicable convention, deduct the entire unrecovered basis. A recovery period ended before 2025 gives zero, not an automatic catch-up for earlier errors. All calculations are capped at remaining allowed-or-allowable basis and retain cents until the separate whole-dollar step. Percentage-table histories and method changes are excluded by the required confirmation.

Fact.Name: Dated straight-line building depreciation for 2025
Fact.Description: Round the dated, remaining-basis-capped depreciation to whole dollars under the existing Schedule E convention. The unrounded companion is the accounting-basis amount; the filed rounded figure can differ by less than one dollar. This is a formula calculation, not every rounded optional IRS percentage-table cell.

Fact.Name: Filer who performed the personal services
Fact.Description: Identify whose own services are recorded. Spousal services are not combined for the 750-hour and more-than-half qualification tests.

Fact.Name: Personal service records for real-estate-professional qualification
Fact.Description: When testing qualification, record every personal-service segment in ALL trades or businesses during 2025, including non-real-estate and nonqualifying employee services. Use nonoverlapping segments, actual minutes, and the performer's identity. A segment must have uniform real-property-business, material-participation, and employee/ownership status. Do not include investor activity that is not qualifying personal services. The total denominator is calculated from these records, so the interviewer must obtain a complete log, not only favorable real-estate hours.

Fact.Name: All 2025 trade-or-business service time was recorded
Fact.Description: Answer Yes only after all personal-service minutes in all trades or businesses for the primary filer and, on a joint return, the spouse are recorded without overlap. No or unanswered leaves a requested qualification unresolved; an empty unrequested collection never creates a professional claim.

Fact.Name: Person who performed this service segment
Fact.Description: The primary filer or spouse who personally performed the services. Do not attribute one spouse's time to the other.

Fact.Name: Minutes of personal services in this segment
Fact.Description: Actual minutes of personal services performed in a trade or business during 2025. All segments for a filer together cannot exceed the minutes in the calendar year. Exactly 750 hours is 45,000 minutes and does not satisfy the more-than-750-hour test.

Fact.Name: Services are in a qualifying real-property trade or business
Fact.Description: Yes for a real-property development, redevelopment, construction, reconstruction, acquisition, conversion, rental, operation, management, leasing, or brokerage trade or business within section 469(c)(7)(C). Otherwise No. Nonqualifying trade-or-business minutes remain in the total denominator.

Fact.Name: Performer materially participates in this real-property business
Fact.Description: Required for a real-property-business segment. Apply the material-participation rules to the business; qualifying as a real estate professional does not itself establish material participation in each rental activity. Spousal participation may be considered for material participation, but the minutes entered remain only the performer's own.

Fact.Name: Services were performed as an employee
Fact.Description: Required for materially participated real-property-business services. Employee time is excluded from the qualification numerator unless the performer meets the more-than-5-percent owner exception. It stays in the all-business denominator.

Fact.Name: Employee is a more-than-5-percent owner of the employer
Fact.Description: Required only for an employee segment. Yes only when the performer owned or was considered to own MORE THAN 5 percent of the employer's outstanding stock, voting stock, or capital or profits interest under the applicable owner rule. Exactly 5 percent is No.

Fact.Name: Qualifying own real-property-business minutes
Fact.Description: Exclude a non-real-property business, a business not materially participated in, and employee work without the ownership exception. Missing required status answers remain incomplete. All excluded minutes still belong in the total personal-service denominator.

Fact.Name: A service log requests qualification testing
Fact.Description: An entered nonempty service-log collection starts qualification review. No collection or an explicitly empty collection creates no claim. A started review requires the complete-log confirmation before qualification can be determined.

Fact.Name: Primary filer AllServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Select this performer's own minutes; the other performer contributes zero. An unidentified performer is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Primary filer total AllServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Sum the performer-specific service segments without adding the spouse's services.

Fact.Name: Primary filer QualifyingServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Select this performer's own minutes; the other performer contributes zero. An unidentified performer is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Primary filer total QualifyingServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Sum the performer-specific service segments without adding the spouse's services.

Fact.Name: Primary filer meets real-estate-professional qualification
Fact.Description: True only when this filer independently exceeds 750 hours AND performs more than half of all trade-or-business personal services in qualifying real-property businesses. Exactly either threshold fails. A missing required log answer stays incomplete. The secondary-filer result is used only on a joint return. This does not by itself classify any particular rental as nonpassive.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer AllServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Select this performer's own minutes; the other performer contributes zero. An unidentified performer is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer total AllServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Sum the performer-specific service segments without adding the spouse's services.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer QualifyingServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Select this performer's own minutes; the other performer contributes zero. An unidentified performer is incomplete.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer total QualifyingServiceMinutes
Fact.Description: Sum the performer-specific service segments without adding the spouse's services.

Fact.Name: Secondary filer meets real-estate-professional qualification
Fact.Description: True only when this filer independently exceeds 750 hours AND performs more than half of all trade-or-business personal services in qualifying real-property businesses. Exactly either threshold fails. A missing required log answer stays incomplete. The secondary-filer result is used only on a joint return. This does not by itself classify any particular rental as nonpassive.

Fact.Name: At least one filer independently qualifies as a real estate professional
Fact.Description: On a joint return either spouse may independently satisfy both tests; their minutes cannot be combined to reach a threshold. Particular rental activities still require material participation.

Fact.Name: Material participation in this rental activity
Fact.Description: Required when using the real-estate-professional activity calculation. Determine material participation under the applicable tests, including spousal participation and any valid grouping election. The qualification service log alone does not prove this answer.

Fact.Name: Qualified professional materially participates in this rental
Fact.Description: The section 469(c)(7) rental exception requires both independently established professional qualification and material participation in this activity. The allocation is now wired through ../repRoutingApplies, which additionally requires three boundary attestations before a property leaves the passive pool.

Fact.Name: Positive current-year at-risk-adjusted activity net
Fact.Description: Zero for a current loss, otherwise the current at-risk-adjusted net available to absorb this activity's prior passive loss.

Fact.Name: Prior passive loss offset against this activity's current net income
Fact.Description: For a now-nonpassive professional rental, offset prior-year unallowed passive loss only up to positive current-year at-risk-adjusted net income from this same activity. Enter prior-year loss explicitly, including zero. Remaining prior losses stay passive and are not released merely by qualification.

Fact.Name: Professional rental nonpassive net after its own prior passive offset
Fact.Description: Current at-risk-adjusted net less the same-activity prior passive loss offset. A current loss remains nonpassive; it must not be combined with remaining prior passive losses and deducted wholesale. WIRED. This amount is what ../repAwareNonpassiveNet carries into /rentalNonpassiveNet and therefore into Schedule E line 26, and what ../repRoutingNiitNet carries into Form 8960 line 4c when the activity is not a section 162 trade or business. It reaches both only through ../repRoutingApplies, so nothing moves on a return that does not claim the section 469(c)(7) exception.

Fact.Name: Prior passive loss remaining in the passive system
Fact.Description: Prior unallowed loss minus the amount offset against current net income of this same activity. This remainder still needs the ordinary passive-income/special-allowance or qualifying-disposition rules. This is NOT a current nonpassive deduction or an automatic disposition release. For a routed property this remainder is the ONLY thing left in ../activeEligibleNet / ../nonActiveNet, carried there negated by ../repRoutingActivePassiveRemainder and ../repRoutingNonactivePassiveRemainder, so it stays inside the ordinary Form 8582 pool exactly as section 469(f)(1)(C) requires.

Fact.Name: Each rental real estate interest is its own activity
Fact.Description: True only when every rental property on this return is its own section 469 activity. That is the default for a qualified professional: each interest in rental real estate is a separate activity unless the filer elects under Regulations section 1.469-9(g) to treat all of them as one. This dictionary holds no activity-level allocation across a grouping election, so a false answer leaves the professional-rental routing unresolved rather than routing on an activity boundary it cannot compute. Read only on a property that has already reached the professional-rental branch; a return with no service log never reads it.

Fact.Name: No personal use of this dwelling unit
Fact.Description: True only when no part of this property was used personally in a way that brings section 280A(c)(5) into play. Section 469(j)(10) takes the income, deduction, gain or loss allocable to such use out of the passive-activity system entirely, and this dictionary derives no section 280A day-count allocation from the Schedule E line 2 entries, so a false answer leaves the professional-rental routing unresolved. This is a bound on what the routing can compute, not a condition of section 469(c)(7) eligibility.

Fact.Name: No separately reported disposition item belongs to this activity
Fact.Description: True only when this property has no Form 4797 or other separately reported disposition gain or loss that would have to be combined with its current net before the prior passive loss is offset. Section 469(f)(1)(A) offsets the unused deduction against the income from the same activity, and a disposition item reported on another form is part of that income; this dictionary makes no cross-form attribution, so a false answer leaves the routing unresolved. This is a bound on what the routing can compute, not a condition of section 469(c)(7) eligibility.

Fact.Name: This professional rental is a section 162 trade or business
Fact.Description: Whether this rental real estate activity is a trade or business within the meaning of section 162. Qualifying as a real estate professional and materially participating do not by themselves establish it, and the answer decides only whether the current net stays in net investment income: a section 162 rental is derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business and leaves net investment income, while a rental that is not a section 162 business keeps its signed net there. An unanswered box is not a no and is not a yes; the net investment income leg stays unresolved until the filer answers, because either default would move the tax silently in one direction.

Fact.Name: Professional-rental routing is in force for this property
Fact.Description: True when this return requests qualification testing, the property reaches the professional-rental branch (../repRentalNonpassiveApplies), and the three boundary attestations are all true. Complete FALSE on every return that answers no service log, which is the whole existing population, and false again whenever the branch itself is false — so the routing is additive and changes nothing for a return that does not claim the section 469(c)(7) exception. When the branch is true and any boundary answer is missing or false the fact is deliberately UNRESOLVED and every consumer below refuses with it: there is no catch-all arm that would hand back the pre-routing number as a provisional value.

Fact.Name: A professional rental answered No to one of the three routing boundary questions
Fact.Description: True when a service log requests qualification testing (/repQualificationRequested), this property reaches the professional-rental branch (../repRentalNonpassiveApplies), and at least one boundary question is answered No: /writableRepRentalActivitiesAreSeparate (a grouping election), ../writableRepNoPersonalUseOfThisProperty (personal use of a dwelling unit), or ../writableRepHasNoSeparatelyReportedDispositionItems (a disposition item reported on another form). ../repRoutingApplies has no answer for those properties. An unanswered boundary question is a prompt, not this flag. Complete false on every return without a service log.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a real estate professional's rental is grouped, used personally, or has a separately reported disposition
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You qualify as a real estate professional and materially participate in a rental, but that rental is grouped with your other rentals as one activity, part of it was used personally, or it has a sale or other disposition reported on another form. This return cannot yet figure the professional-rental treatment in those cases.
Fires when any recorded rental property has ../repRoutingBoundaryAnsweredNo true. Guarded by an IsComplete on /rentalProperties. It names the refusal that the unresolved ../repRoutingApplies already enforces for those three answers.

Fact.Name: One of the six exceptions makes this property not a rental activity
Fact.Description: Screen question for each rental property: does any of these apply? (1) The average period of customer use is 7 days or less. (2) The average period of customer use is 30 days or less and you provide significant personal services with the rentals. (3) You provide extraordinary personal services with the rentals. (4) The rental is incidental to a nonrental activity. (5) You customarily make the property available during defined business hours for nonexclusive use by various customers. (6) You provide the property for use in a nonrental activity of a partnership, S corporation or joint venture in your capacity as an owner. When one applies, the activity is not a rental activity for the passive activity rules, and this return cannot yet treat it that way. Unanswered is read as No.

Fact.Name: You provided significant services to the renters of this property
Fact.Description: Screen question for each rental property: did you provide significant services to the renters, such as maid service? Heat and light, cleaning of public areas, trash collection and similar services do not count. A rental with significant services is reported on Schedule C, not Schedule E, and this return cannot yet move it there. Unanswered is read as No.

Fact.Name: This property answered Yes to a rental-activity exception or to significant services
Fact.Description: True when ../writableRentalActivityExceptionApplies or ../writableRentalSignificantServicesProvided is answered Yes. Complete false when both are unanswered or No.

Fact.Name: Knockout: a property is not a rental activity, or its services put it on Schedule C
Fact.Description:
We can't file this return yet. You told us that one of your properties is rented for short stays or with services, or meets another exception that makes it not a rental activity, or that you provide significant services such as maid service to its renters. Those properties are treated differently from an ordinary rental (a different passive activity test, or Schedule C with self-employment tax), and this return cannot figure them yet.
Fires when any recorded rental property has ../rentalActivityClassificationUnbuilt true. Guarded by an IsComplete on /rentalProperties. Never fires on an unanswered question.

Fact.Name: Active-participation passive bucket under professional-rental routing
Fact.Description: What is left in the active-participation passive bucket once the current net has been routed out: the negative of ../repPriorPassiveLossStillSubjectToSection469, which section 469(f)(1)(C) keeps arising from a passive activity, and nothing else. Zero for a property that does not claim active participation, whose remainder belongs to the non-active bucket instead. The current-year net is NOT here; it is in ../repAwareNonpassiveNet.

Fact.Name: Non-active passive bucket under professional-rental routing
Fact.Description: The complement of ../repRoutingActivePassiveRemainder: the negative of ../repPriorPassiveLossStillSubjectToSection469 for a property that does NOT claim active participation, zero for one that does. Section 469(f)(1)(C) is the authority for the remainder staying passive; nothing releases it here.

Fact.Name: Per-property Part I nonpassive net, professional rental or self-rental
Fact.Description: The amount this property contributes to the Schedule E Part I NONPASSIVE channel. Under professional-rental routing it is ../repCurrentNonpassiveNetAfterOwnPriorLoss, the current at-risk-allowed net after this same activity's own prior passive offset, which is SIGNED: a professional rental LOSS is nonpassive and is not limited by section 469. Otherwise it is the pre-existing self-rental recharacterized net. The two are ALTERNATIVES, never addends, so a property that is both a self-rental and a routed professional rental is counted once.

Fact.Name: Per-property nonpassive contribution to Form 8582 line 6 modified AGI
Fact.Description: The same per-property nonpassive amount as ../repAwareNonpassiveNet, except that a routed professional rental LOSS is floored at zero. Form 8582 line 6 excludes any rental real estate loss allowed to a real estate professional from modified AGI, and the statutory list behind that bullet excludes any loss allowable by reason of subsection (c)(7); a professional rental PROFIT is not excluded and stays. Nothing else about the line 6 build changes: the overall passive-income floor, the social security exclusion and the eligible adjustment subtotal are untouched.

Fact.Name: Rental nonpassive component of Form 8582 line 6 modified AGI
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/repAwareNonpassiveMagiNet), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome exactly as /rentalNonpassiveNet is, so it is a complete-safe zero for a non-rental return. This is what /section8582Magi reads in place of /rentalNonpassiveNet: identical to it for every return that does not route a professional rental, and lower by the excluded professional-rental loss for one that does.

Fact.Name: Per-property net investment income contribution of a routed professional rental
Fact.Description: Zero when this property is not routed, and zero when it is routed and the filer has established that the activity is a section 162 trade or business — such rent is derived in the ordinary course of a trade or business and is outside net investment income. When the routed activity is NOT a section 162 business the signed current net stays in net investment income, which is what the Form 8960 instructions say in terms: qualifying as a real estate professional does not by itself make the rental a trade or business, and the rental income is included in the tax when it is not one. The section 162 answer has no default here: unanswered leaves this fact unresolved, because a yes and a no move the tax in opposite directions.

Fact.Name: Professional-rental addend of Form 8960 line 4c
Fact.Description: CollectionSum(/rentalProperties/*/repRoutingNiitNet), gated by /claimsScheduleERentalIncome exactly as /rentalNonpassiveNet is, so it is a complete-safe zero for a non-rental return and for every return that routes no professional rental. It is a fourth addend of Form 8960 line 4c, not a replacement for any of the three that are there: the routed net has already LEFT the section 469 passive component that line 4c reads, because ../activeEligibleNet and ../nonActiveNet now carry only the prior passive remainder, so adding it here restores it exactly once for the rentals the statute keeps inside net investment income.
